Translation from 2026-10-15; the original has changed since.

Business rules

Each rule has a statement, where it lives (file:line), and the test that covers it. If you change a rule, update the line here in the same change — that's what .docmap.yml requires with block severity.

They all live in apps/api/src/domain/, which is pure: no IO, no framework, no database. That's why each one has a fast, deterministic unit test.

Business context​

Brabo executes engineering work through AI agents. Two forces shape virtually every rule here:

The agent is not trustworthy by construction. It's a language model: it can hallucinate, get stuck in a loop, or request something destructive. The rules exist so the possible damage is bounded by structure, not by prompt quality.

Spend is real and continuous. Every turn consumes a paid token. Budget, ceiling, and metering aren't administrative conveniences — they're what stops an agent loop from turning into a loss.

Actors​

actorwho it isauthority
Userthe person. Roles: viewer, developer, maintainer, ownerfinal decision on any action with external effect; merge is theirs exclusively
Agentlong-running process with a role (Creative, PO, Architect, Dev, Infra, QA, SecOps, Psychologist, Anamnesis)proposes; never decides alone what policy doesn't allow
Systemapi and engineenforces policy, records the event, measures cost

The vocabulary is in the glossary.

Session​

RN-001 — The session has five states and closed transitions​

created → active → closing → closed, with closed_abnormally reachable from any non-terminal state. From closing there's never a way back to active, and terminal states have no exit.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/sessions/session-state-machine.ts:29
  • Test: test/domain/sessions/session-state-machine.spec.ts
  • Edge case: closing is a transient state. A session stuck there means the drain started and didn't complete — there's an alert for that, see the runbook.

RN-002 — Every session event is immutable and seq is dense​

There's never an UPDATE on session_events. seq is unique per session (unique(session_id, seq)) and has no gaps: it starts at 1 and is contiguous.

  • Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/sessions.ts (table session_events)
  • Test: verified on restore — docker/backup/restore.sh fails if count(*) ≠ max(seq) − min(seq) + 1 or min(seq) ≠ 1
  • Why: it's what makes the Psychologist's evidence traceable and the backup verifiable. State that needs to change lives in its own table, alongside.

RN-097 — The session's kind is creation intent; execution stays an event​

The session is born consultiva (consultative) or criativa (creative), chosen by whoever opens it and recorded in sessions.kind. consultiva is just conversation; criativa is the one that produces — it opens ideation with the Creative agent and is the only one that enters execution. The kind never changes: there's no route that swaps it.

The risk in this rule isn't the field, it's the second source of truth. The product already knew how to say whether a session is executing, and knew it through another path: findActiveExecutionSession looks for the active session that carries the execution.activated event (it's what makes reactivation land on the session where the dev agents already are, finding #11 of the first dogfooding). The two coexist under a rule that keeps them from fighting:

  • kind classifies creation INTENT. A criativa session that never activated execution is not the current execution session, and the event-based derivation keeps not looking at kind — if it started to, every open creative session would become a candidate to receive the dev agents.
  • The event classifies execution STATE, as always.
  • execution.activated on a consultiva session is an ERROR (409), never silent conversion. This is the point that decides which of the two sources wins: letting the event promote the kind would be exactly having them write over each other.

The guard lives in the funnel — AppendSessionEventUseCase — not in ActivateExecutionUseCase, because both paths that write an event (the user's route and the engine's /internal/*) go through it. The extra session read is only paid when the event is the execution one. The refusal happens before incrementSeq: a refused attempt can't consume seq, or RN-002 would break.

The column's DEFAULT is consultiva — the kind that can do less: a row arriving through a path that doesn't go through the route (migration, maintenance SQL) doesn't earn the right to execute. The migration's backfill does the opposite and is deliberate, by the 0033 reasoning: at the moment it runs, every session predates the distinction, and some are sessions where dev agents are working — waking them up as consultiva would make reactivating an in-progress project fail without anyone having decided anything.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/sessions/session-kind.ts:50 (podeAtivarExecucao), apps/api/src/db/schema/sessions.ts:68 (the column), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/sessions/append-session-event.use-case.ts:53 (the guard)
  • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/sessions/session-kind-e-nome.spec.ts
  • Origin: ADR 0061

RN-098 — The session name adds to the hashtag, never replaces it​

The session can receive a friendly name (sessions.name, optional), at creation or later, via PATCH /projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId. The label shown on screen is composite: <name> · #<first 8 characters of the id>. With no name, it degrades to the hashtag alone.

The hashtag never disappears, and the reason is operational: it's what gets pasted into a URL, a command, or a conversation, and a name chosen by a person isn't unique — two sessions named "Checkout" are normal. A blank name (or whitespace only) counts as absence, both on creation and on renaming: writing '' would turn the label into " · #a1b2c3d4", worse than the hashtag alone. null in the PATCH body is the way to undo.

Renaming is not a session event. The event log is what the session lived through, and the name is a navigation label, changed as many times as desired — N renaming events would push exactly what matters out of the 200-event tail.

  • Where: apps/web/src/lib/session-label.ts:61 (rotuloDaSessao), apps/api/src/application/ports/session-repository.port.ts:52 (rename). Reachable both from inside the session (apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx:439, handleRename) and from the project's list, without needing to open the session first (apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSessionsTab.tsx:101, handleRenomear) — both screens call the same renameSession and the same rotuloDaSessao.
  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/session-label.test.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/sessions/session-kind-e-nome.spec.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSessionsTab.test.tsx
  • Origin: ADR 0061

RN-104 — The tab derives from the recorded kind, and creates in that kind​

The project has two session tabs — Creative and Chat — and each one is a kind: it lists the sessions whose sessions.kind is its own, and its CTA creates in that kind, without asking again. There's no third tab listing both together.

The kind was already immutable (RN-097), and that's what makes it a legitimate navigation coordinate instead of a saved filter: a session never switches tabs. The tab reads the recorded field — it doesn't derive the kind from any event, for the same reason as RN-097: execution.activated classifies execution STATE, and a tab that looked at it would move on its own.

Two consequences the rule fixes, and which aren't screen detail:

  • The kind choice leaves the form. It used to live in a radio-button fieldset, and now it happens the moment the person clicks the tab. Keeping both would offer the chance to create a session that contradicts the place you're standing in. What's left in the form is the name, which stays optional (RN-098).
  • One action, one place at a time. "Start ideation" still exists — it's what brings the Creative agent into the session, and from there on the owner's key starts being spent (RN-058); no one steps in alone. What changed is where it lives: inside the invite while the invite is on screen, and in the topbar when it isn't. The invite used to POINT to the topbar ("use Start ideation, at the top of the screen"), which is the literal version of the problem that originated RN-097 — the action in one place and the explanation in another. The topbar can't simply lose the button: it's possible to type into a creative session without ever having called the Creative agent, and then the invite leaves the scene.

The three screens honor the three states of RN-088, with error before empty: the filtered list is empty in both cases, and saying "no ideation yet" after a 429 would be lying about what happened.

The Chat's deep-link key stays sessions, not chat. That's what makes an old bookmarked ?tab=sessions link open the Chat with the tab marked in the tab bar — resolving the old key as an alias only in the panel would leave the tab bar with no selection at all, because Tabs compares active to key, and whoever writes active receives the raw key from validateSearch.

  • Where: apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.ts:95 (both entries), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSessionsTab.tsx:114 (the filter by recorded kind) and :98 (the CTA creating in the tab's kind), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx:716 (conviteVisivel, the one question the topbar and the invite share)
  • Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSessionsTab.test.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.test.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.sessao.test.tsx
  • Edge case: a project with no session of that kind shows the empty state OF THAT KIND, even when it has sessions of the other kind — that's information, not an error.
  • Origin: ADR 0061

RN-123 — Creative session with no active Creative agent: the first message ALSO activates it​

In a kind: 'criativa' session (RN-097) with no agent.activated yet, sending the first message through the composer activates the Creative agent first (waiting for activation to finish) and only then delivers that message to it through the real path (sendAgentMessage — history, system prompt, emit_artifact tool). Before this rule, whoever typed without clicking "Start ideation" fell into a generic SSE chat with no history and no business rules: it was NOT the real Creative agent, and the conversation recorded nothing in the domain.

The "Start ideation" click still exists (RN-104) — it's still what triggers activation when the person prefers the explicit gesture, and it's from it that the owner's key (RN-058) starts being spent on either of the two paths. What changed is that the FIRST MESSAGE now also counts as that gesture: no one should need a separate click before talking to whoever the screen already invited them to talk to.

  • Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx:678 (handleSend)
  • Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.ideacao-automatica.test.tsx
  • Edge case: a consultiva session has no Creative agent — the rule doesn't apply, and the generic SSE path stays the right one for it.

RN-119 — The session's ACTIVE agent is the one with the most recent agent.activated — never a fixed chain​

SessionPage decides two things from the SAME agent: who the composer's message goes to, and which agent the topbar resolves the displayed model from (the full cascade session→agent→area→project→workspace, the same one RunLlmTurnUseCase uses to actually run the turn). The two questions used to have DIFFERENT answers before this rule: routing used a fixed precedence chain (architect > po > creative, based on historical EXISTENCE — "has already activated once", which never "turned off"), and the displayed model didn't even know who was active — the model-binding route received no agent at all and always fell back to the Creative agent's fixed fallback (herdarModeloDeStart), even after a handoff to the PO, Architect, or Dev Lead.

The single definition: the ACTIVE agent is the one with the most RECENT agent.activated (by seq), among the conversational agents of the chat flow (Creative, PO, Architect, Dev Lead). Infra Lead is left out: agent_command_controller.ex (engine) only has a message route for po/dev-lead/arquiteto (plus Creative, as the last clause's implicit fallback) — Infra never had message wired, only start. Sending a message to "infra" today would silently fall through to the Creative agent; treating it as the composer's active agent would reopen that trap instead of closing one.

Superseded in part by RN-631 (AT-251): "most recent agent.activated wins" was itself an implicit default recipient, and an invisible one. The composer's recipient is now CHOSEN by the person (a "To" selector listing the agents already in the session) and the topbar model follows that recipient. What survives from this rule is the half about the model: the binding route receives the agent, never falls back silently.

  • Where: apps/web/src/lib/session-destinatario.ts:272 (useDestinatarioDoChat, since RN-631), apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts:1124 (getSessionModelBinding, the agentId), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/llm/model-bindings.controller.ts:166 (getSessionBinding, @Query('agentId'))
  • Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.destinatario-do-chat.test.tsx (formerly SessionPage.agente-mais-recente.test.tsx), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.modelo-do-agente-ativo.test.tsx, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/resolve-model-binding.use-case.spec.ts
  • Edge case: Infra Lead doesn't participate in composer routing nor in the "active agent" definition — it's proactive (Phase 4), not conversational through the composer.

RN-120 — The session's event poll pauses during an in-progress turn​

useSessionEvents fetched events every few seconds with NO awareness of an in-progress turn. If the poll landed DURING a turn (common — turns usually last longer than the interval), it brought already-persisted chat.message/agent.response, which rendered ALONGSIDE the optimistic/streaming state still on screen: the same message, twice.

The fix pauses only the TIMER (refetchInterval) while streaming is true — the query stays enabled, so the explicit invalidation that already fires at the end of the turn (finalizarTurnoDoAgente) keeps fetching fresh data at the right time. pausarPoll is an OPTIONAL parameter, default false: the hook's other consumers (Overview, Code, Provisioning, AdoptionPlan) have no conversational turn in progress and stay as they were.

  • Where: apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts:221 (useSessionEvents), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx:277 (eventsQuery)
  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/hooks.pausar-poll.test.tsx
  • Edge case: pausing the timer isn't disabling the query — explicit invalidation keeps working, and the fix depends on it to never miss data.

RN-122 — The "Stop" button cancels the turn FOR REAL, killing the task holding the LLM call​

Until now there was no cancellation anywhere. The root was structural: agent_command_controller.ex handled the user's message with GenServer.call(pid, {:user_message, texto}, ...) — SYNCHRONOUS — and the entire turn (tool loop + SSE call to the LLM) ran INSIDE handle_call. The agent's process stayed blocked until the turn finished and handled NO other message in the meantime — not even a future cancel command.

The fix: the turn handle_call/handle_cast of the four conversational agents (Creative, PO, Architect, Dev Lead) spawns a Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 (Engine.Agents.TurnoAssincrono, new, shared by all four) with the heavy work and returns {:noreply, state} — the reply to the original GenServer.call is DEFERRED until the task finishes (GenServer.reply/2, fired when {ref, resultado} arrives at handle_info). Since the agent process STOPS being blocked, a new handle_cast(:cancel, state) arrives and is handled while the turn runs: Task.shutdown/2 in :brutal_kill mode kills the task, which drops the HTTP (SSE) connection it holds with the api — that's what makes cancellation actually save tokens, not just stop rendering on the client. The original from receives {:error, :cancelado}, and a TERMINAL agent.error is recorded with origin "politica" (policy — the same origin as budget/credential/binding — cancelling is a user decision to stop spending tokens, not a fifth value in ADR 0020's closed vocabulary) — without it, GetSessionPendingWorkUseCase would see agent.activated with no subsequent agent.response/agent.error, and the session would stay hung on the pending-work signal.

Two competing messages to the same agent (the user sends again while a turn is already running) never spawn a second task: TurnoAssincrono.iniciar/3 replies {:error, :turno_em_andamento} (turn in progress) right away.

Revised by RN-578 (ADR 0163): the reply to the original GenServer.call is no longer deferred until the task finishes — it goes out on ACCEPTANCE, as soon as the task is up, and cancelling answers nobody (the caller already has :ok). {:error, :turno_em_andamento} stopped being discarded by the controller: it is a named 409 and a durable agent.error.

  • Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/turno_assincrono.ex (the mechanism), apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/{criativo,po,arquiteto,dev_lead}_server.ex (the four turn handle_call/handle_cast), apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/agent_command_controller.ex:361 (cancel/2), apps/engine/lib/engine_web/router.ex (POST /internal/sessions/:sessionId/agent/cancel), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/cancel-agent-turn.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/agents/agents.controller.ts (POST /projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/agents/:agent/cancel), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (handleCancel, "Stop" button in the composer)
  • Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/turno_assincrono_test.exs (the task dies FOR REAL — Process.alive?/1 before and after — not just "stopped importing the result"), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/agents/cancel-agent-turn.use-case.spec.ts
  • Edge case: cancelling with no turn in progress is an idempotent NO-OP — there's no task to kill nor pending from to reply to. Cancellation does NOT undo a side effect that already ran BEFORE the task died (e.g., a tool that had already been dispatched and recorded its event) — it only interrupts what hasn't happened yet.
  • Origin: this session's investigation; no dedicated ADR (a concurrency pattern change INSIDE the harness, not a layer/database boundary).

RN-142 — Confirming readiness with NO business rule at all is refused by the engine, not just hidden in the UI​

Before, clicking "I'm ready to produce" — or calling the route directly — ALWAYS created the product_brief and offered the handoff to the PO, even in a conversation where zero business rules had been captured. business_rule_refs(state) already existed in criativo_server.ex, but only to POPULATE the brief's "rules" field — never as a blocking condition. In the UI, SessionPage.tsx disabled the button only during streaming, without checking the rule count.

The real guarantee had to live on the server, not on the screen: whoever calls the route directly (or a future client that isn't this frontend) can't punch through the guardrail just because the button is drawn disabled. CriativoServer.handle_call(:confirm_readiness, ...) now checks business_rule_refs(state) BEFORE spawning the Engine.Agents.TurnoAssincrono Task (RN-122) — empty, it refuses right there, without running the consolidation turn, without a product_brief, without a handoff.

The refusal doesn't turn into an HTTP 4xx: agent_command_controller.ex#readiness/2 IGNORES this GenServer.call's return and always answers 202, the same pattern message/2 already uses since RN-122 ("this response is just the acknowledgment" — the real outcome lives in the event log). That's why the refusal is narrated as a DURABLE agent.error (RN-059), with origin "politica" (policy — it's a product decision, not an infra/model/turn failure) — and a message explaining why; the session thread already knows how to render this event type (lerFalhaDeTurno, the same red bubble as any other turn failure).

The complementary UX, in SessionPage.tsx: the button is born disabled (with a title explaining why) while events has no artifact.business_rule — the SAME source that already feeds the "Business rules" panel (ContextAside), with no second read that could diverge from the first.

  • Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/criativo_server.ex (handle_call(:confirm_readiness, ...), emit_falha_sem_regra/1), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (hasBusinessRule, the "I'm ready to produce" button)
  • Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/criativo_server_test.exs ("readiness: refuses when NO business rule was captured" — no turn, no brief, no handoff; the refusal narrated with origin "politica"), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.readiness-exige-regra.test.tsx (button disabled with no rule, enabled with 1+)
  • Edge case: the session already had readiness.confirmed recorded by the api BEFORE signaling the engine (ConfirmReadinessUseCase) — that doesn't change: it's the record of the user's CLICK, a fact that happened independent of the engine accepting or refusing afterward.
  • Origin: code investigation confirming a user report — no ADR (new guardrail on an already-existing flow, no layer/database boundary change).

Action approval​

The heart of the system. Every action with an external effect is born as a proposed_action.

RN-003 — The action has six states, and denied is terminal​

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/action-state-machine.ts:36
  • Test: test/domain/actions/action-state-machine.spec.ts
  • Edge case: an approved action that executed becomes executed, not still approved. Counting approvals by status = 'approved' gives the wrong number — the correct criterion is decided_by IS NOT NULL.

RN-004 — The decision is evaluated in three stages, and deny wins immediately​

Order: (a) IAM → (b) agent_autonomy → (c) permissions.json. Each stage can only raise permissiveness; a silent stage never lowers the previous one. deny at any stage returns immediately.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts:118
  • Test: test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts (10 KB — the largest in the domain)

RN-005 — Minimum role per action type​

Before any policy, IAM: each ActionType requires a minimum effective role. Without it, deny with an explicit reason.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts:110 (MIN_ROLE_FOR_ACTION_TYPE)
  • Test: test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts

RN-006 — Ceiling: merge into a protected branch is never auto-approvable​

dev, qa, rc, and main are protected. A git_merge targeting one of them is downgraded from auto_approve to require_approval after all the policy has run. Neither agent_autonomy nor permissions.json can promote it.

rc stays on the list even after the step left the policy (ADR 0030) and the bootstrap stopped creating it (RN-029). This list decides what the lock refuses, and repositories bootstrapped by earlier versions still have the branch: protecting one that doesn't exist costs nothing; unprotecting one that exists costs dearly.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts:498 (isProtectedBranch, the merge lock ceiling) + protected-branches.ts:4
  • Test: test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts
  • Origin: ADR 0011 §1
  • Note: the equivalent protection on the platform (GitHub/GitLab) diverges between providers and isn't the gate — see ADR 0028.

RN-007 — Ceiling: an instruction patch is never auto-approvable​

Changing an agent's instruction always requires a human decision. The feature's value is in the human seeing the diff; auto-approving would be the agent rewriting itself.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts:168
  • Test: test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts
  • Origin: ADR 0016 §8

RN-008 — Command matching is by pattern, not substring​

permissions.json matches a terminal command by structured pattern, with the command properly tokenized — not by includes().

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/command-matcher.ts
  • Test: test/domain/actions/command-matcher.spec.ts

Backlog​

RN-009 — The story has four states, and done is terminal​

draft → ready → in_progress → done. Rework is allowed: ready → draft and in_progress → ready.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/backlog/story-state-machine.ts:27
  • Test: test/domain/backlog/story-state-machine.spec.ts

RN-010 — draft → ready requires four things, validated in the domain​

For a story to become ready it needs, all of them:

  1. dod not empty — Definition of Done
  2. dor not empty — Definition of Ready
  3. at least 1 functional requirement (rf)
  4. at least 1 linked business rule (businessRuleIds)

The error names exactly what's missing, not a generic "invalid".

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/backlog/story-readiness.ts:39
  • Test: test/domain/backlog/story-readiness.spec.ts
  • Origin: ADR 0009 §3
  • Why: it's what stops the PO from dumping a vague story into the dev queue.

RN-011 — Business rule with no story is a finding, not an error​

Rule→story coverage is computed, and what has no story shows up as pending — information, not a failure.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/backlog/coverage.ts
  • Test: test/domain/backlog/coverage.spec.ts

RN-012 — A module removed from module_map demotes the story​

A story linked to a module that ceased to exist goes back to draft, with a backlog.story_demoted event.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/architecture/module-resolution.ts; the event is emitted in application/use-cases/architecture/create-module-map.use-case.ts:73
  • Test: test/domain/architecture/module-resolution.spec.ts

RN-013 — The module graph cannot have a cycle​

PR Gates​

RN-014 — The gate order is immutable and awaiting_user is terminal​

awaiting_qa → awaiting_secops → awaiting_user. Approving QA never skips straight to the user. changes_requested sends it back to the dev on the same branch, with no new PR.

  • Where: apps/api/src/domain/execution/pr-gate-state-machine.ts:24
  • Test: test/domain/execution/pr-gate-state-machine.spec.ts
  • Origin: ADR 0013 §1
  • Edge case: awaiting_user is terminal by design — the system never merges (RN-006).

RN-015 — Cycle K: the correction ceiling is finite and inherited​

Every gate return consumes a lap. Once the ceiling is exhausted, the task is blocked with a reason, instead of spinning forever. A subagent created by parallelization inherits the base agent's ceiling.

Since Phase 8b the ceiling also applies to the QA AREA, with no code change: QaLeadServer is the only caller of record_gate_verdict, so one gate round — no matter how many specializations it consulted underneath — still consumes exactly ONE lap. See RN-036.

  • Where: DEFAULT_MAX_GATE_CORRECTIONS = 3 in apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/record-gate-verdict.use-case.ts:21; applied in activate-execution.use-case.ts:89 and, in the engine, in qa_lead_server.ex:268 and secops_agent_server.ex:142
  • Test: apps/engine/test/engine/gates/qa_automacao_agent_test.exs (the specialization returns {:blocked, ...} without calling the api) and qa_lead_server_test.exs (the Lead NEVER calls record_gate_verdict in that case — that's what stops the correction from being burned)
  • Origin: ADR 0017 §4

RN-016 — The gate's verdict prevails over the task's statement​

If the task description says one thing and the gate's verdict says another, the verdict wins.

Since Phase 8b, "the verdict" can come from two specializations — the rule doesn't change: each one prevails over the task WITHIN what it evaluates (Automation over test coverage; Performance/Security over performance NFRs and code findings). QaLead.consolidar/1 doesn't arbitrate between them and the task: any changes_requested from any of them already fails the whole thing (see RN-036).

  • Where: prompt for each specialization in apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/qa_automacao_agent.ex and qa_performance_seguranca_agent.ex
  • Origin: ADR 0020 §9

RN-036 — QA becomes an area: the Lead consolidates without changing the gate's contract​

The Automation specialization (Phase 4a's QAAgent) always delegates; Performance/Security only when the story has a pertinent performance NFR (Engine.Gates.QaLead.rnf_de_performance?/1 — a keyword heuristic, not NLP). The decision NOT to delegate is always recorded — a dispensed delegation with a justification, never silence.

Consolidation: approved only if ALL delegations that ran approved; any changes_requested fails the whole thing, with itens (items) from the specialization(s) that requested changes, each item prefixed with the label of whoever raised it ("[QA de Automação] ...") — that's how the origin is traced WITHOUT changing itens from string[] to another shape. Delegation failure (any origin — infra, modelo, codigo, politica) NEVER becomes changes_requested: the Lead blocks the task with the real origin (RN-015).

The qa_verdict that reaches the api is the SAME artifact and goes through the SAME route as always (RecordGateVerdictUseCase, nextGateStatus) — neither of the two changed. What the api learns about the area lives only in the delegation.completed/delegation.failed/ delegation.dispensed events, which the specialization and the Lead record separately.

  • Test: apps/engine/test/engine/gates/qa_lead_test.exs (the pure decision tree), qa_lead_server_test.exs (the wiring: decision → delegation → recording → consolidation → the SAME call as always), and — the proof that the contract didn't change — record-gate-verdict.use-case.spec.ts, pr-gate-state-machine.spec.ts and record-infra-gate-verdict.use-case.spec.ts pass with no change at all

On the apps/web side (Phase 8d): the team panel groups qa/ qa-automacao/qa-performance-seguranca as lead + collapsible specializations, the PR timeline expands the consolidated verdict into its internals (ProjectApprovalsTab.tsx, PrGateTimeline.tsx), and the feed narrates delegation.* — see apps/web/src/lib/agents.ts (AREAS/areaFor).

RN-054 — External handoff addresses the area's lead or an agent with no area — never a subagent​

Whoever talks to an area from outside talks to the lead. A handoff addressed to a subagent (qa-automacao, qa-performance-seguranca, infra-workflows) is refused with a typed error that names the lead the caller should have addressed — refusing without saying the right path would just trade a hierarchy breach for a stuck agent.

The refusal happens before the INSERT. Refusing afterward would leave a ghost handoff in the table and a handoff.offered — an immutable event — asserting an offer the policy doesn't allow.

Internal delegation (lead → subagent) does not go through here: it's private to the area, has its own table (delegations) and its own path (RecordDelegationUseCase). The rule is about the area's external boundary, not about what happens inside it.

ADR 0038 called for this validation, naming the place — CreateHandoffUseCase is the only one in the system that writes toAgent — and it had never been implemented (finding #12 of the first dogfooding). The engine's offer_handoff passed to_agent through as a free string, so until now nothing stopped an agent from breaching the hierarchy.

Area, lead, and members have ONE source since PHASE 18: apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts. The list used to be hand-written in three places (api, web, engine) and the test only compared api against web — the engine silently diverged. Now apps/web/src/lib/agent-areas.generated.ts and apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/areas.ex are produced by pnpm --filter api gerar:areas, and the test fails what's stale on disk. Since AT-046 the same generator also writes SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS (RN-440) into the web file — and only there, since the engine has no reader for it. The list is still the CATALOG; agent_areas is the per-project STATE (RN-094), and the two answer different questions.

  • Origin: ADR 0038, closed from finding #12 of the first dogfooding

RN-037 — Infra becomes an area: Workflows generates CI per provider, Lead consolidates into a single PR​

Second instance of the ADR 0038 model, after the QA area (RN-036) — with one structural difference: the Infra area's two delegations ALWAYS run (Dockerfiles/compose by the Lead itself — "delegates to itself"; CI pipeline by the Workflows subagent), never is one dispensed. Workflows decides the pipeline format from the context's gitProvider (GetInfraContextUseCase, read from project_repositories.provider — not from GitProvider capabilities, which are the SAME for GitHub and GitLab): "gitlab" generates .gitlab-ci.yml; any other value ("github", "local", or unknown) generates .github/workflows/ci.yml. Each file goes through validate_infra_file before finishing — hadolint for Dockerfile, actionlint for GitHub Actions workflow (ADR 0039; .gitlab-ci.yml has no local validation, a documented gap, not a half-solution).

Consolidation: the two delegates' files are merged by path (Workflows' wins on collision) into a SINGLE PR — the mechanism to propose the PR (propose_infra_pr) changes from "the tool calls the api directly" to "the tool signals the Lead, which consolidates and calls once" — the open_infra_pr the api receives is the SAME as always, byte for byte (ExecuteInfraPrUseCase untouched). Failure of any delegate (origin infra/modelo/codigo/politica) NEVER opens a partial PR — the same rule as RN-036, one level up again.

Each delegate (even the Lead, on itself) is tracked as a delegations row — reused exactly as RN-036 left it, with ONE correction: the task_id column became NULLABLE (the Infra area delegates on the SESSION, with no backlog task behind an infra PR), and the route POST /internal/sessions/:sessionId/delegations stopped being nested under /tasks/:taskId — taskId now goes in the body, optional. Cycle K and budget have no dedicated column in the Infra area (the original InfraAgent never had per-task budget, and this work didn't introduce one).

RN-140 — A gate cycle that dies mid-way resumes on its own, with no manual intervention​

QaLeadServer/SecOpsAgentServer are restart: :temporary, and the gate's intermediate transitions (DevAgentServer.correct/3, Dispatcher.run_secops/2) are direct in-memory calls — made AFTER record_gate_verdict has already durably advanced gate_status on the api. A crash between the two used to trap the PR forever in awaiting_qa/awaiting_secops: nothing knew that step had been left pending, and no engine restart fixed it — ADR 0057 itself already declared suspension in {:awaiting, ...} as a known limit, and investigating again found that the window between a recorded verdict and a dispatch call is, in practice, easier to hit.

gate_states (schema engine, key {project_id, task_id, gate}) records the in-flight cycle at the SAME points where the transitions already happened — "in_progress" before any subagent/scanner runs, "dispatch_pending" right after record_gate_verdict returns correct/run_secops and before the in-process call. Engine.Gates.GateRescuer scans rows stuck for more than 15 minutes (configurable, GATE_RESCUE_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS) — generous on purpose, because a QA subagent's ToolLoop legitimately runs up to TOOL_LOOP_MAX_ITERATIONS_GATE (60) iterations, and a short threshold would rescue (and duplicate) a cycle that's merely slow — and resumes: "in_progress" restarts the whole area (no surgical resumption of ctx, which doesn't survive a restart, the same choice as the dev agent); "dispatch_pending" resends exactly the lost call. Called on boot and by an Oban tick self-rescheduled every 5 minutes (GATE_RESCUE_INTERVAL_SECONDS), Engine.Workers.GateRescueSchedulerWorker — the same idiom as ModelSyncSchedulerWorker/AnamneseSchedulerWorker.

Two guards against duplicating work: a process alive ON THE SAME node (Registry.lookup) is never disturbed, and the staleness threshold covers what the local guard doesn't reach (remote replica — Registry is local to the node, the same caveat as Engine.Dev.Wake since ADR 0045). The worst outcome of a residual race is duplicated, cheap work — the api rejects a second record_gate_verdict for a gate that no longer owns gate_status (nextGateStatus), and DevAgentServer.correct/3 is already idempotent via a state guard since ADR 0052 — never inconsistent data.

  • Test: apps/engine/test/engine/gates/gate_rescuer_test.exs — kills a real QaLeadServer with the cycle in flight (DynamicSupervisor.terminate_child/2, the durable row surviving the process) and proves GateRescuer.run/0 reconnects the area on its own up to a real outcome; the scenario in the statement (lost run_secops) and the lost correct return, both with REAL process and dispatch, no FakeGateDispatcher; and the two guards (a live local process isn't disturbed; a recent row isn't touched)
  • Origin: ADR 0067, which extends ADR 0057

Projects panel​

RN-039 — Project status dot: risk always beats inactivity​

The dashboard sidebar shows a health dot per project, derived from three independent signals: budget (the same 70%/90% thresholds as RN-018), blocked task (tasks.blocked), and recent activity (7 days). Colors: green = healthy and active; amber = budget ≥70%; red = budget ≥90% or blocked task; gray = no activity in the last 7 days. When a risk signal (amber/red) and the inactivity signal (gray) apply at the same time, the risk one wins — an overrun, stalled project is still something to look at, not something to hide behind "no activity".

  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/project-status.test.ts

RN-088 — Load failure is said on screen; 429 is not retried​

Every screen that loads data from the api distinguishes three states, never two: loading (skeleton), error (the message the api sent, with the trace_id and a try-again button), and empty (the empty-list text). if (!dado) return null collapses the three, and the observed outcome was the worst possible: with the api rate-limiting with 429, the main area of /projects/:id was completely blank — no message, no error, no skeleton — and the reason existed only in the console. On the dashboard it was worse than blank: !projects was also true on error, so the screen invited you to create the first project of a workspace that could have twenty.

It's RN-059 on the other end of the wire: failure never becomes an empty response. Whoever fails, says so.

The sentence is the api's, extracted by mensagemDaApi — the same function the mutation path already used in toasts. A generic text of ours doesn't know the difference between "rate limit exceeded, try again shortly" (wait) and "access denied" (waiting won't help).

The other side of the same rule is not answering the limit with more traffic. 4xx is not retried: 429 is literally the server telling you to stop, and 401 has already been renewed once inside request(). And polling stops when the query errors — it comes back on window focus, on remount, or on the button. Before, there were three retries per failure added to ~25 polls of 3 to 5 seconds that didn't know how to stop: a real session accumulated 1128 429 errors against a limit of 300 requests per minute per user (RateLimitGuard), and the loop kept the sliding window from recovering. 5xx and network failure keep the three attempts, where repeating is the right reaction.

  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/query-policy.test.ts; apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPage.test.tsx (429 becomes a message with the api's sentence; 403 shows the 403's reason; loading is not an error); apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.test.tsx (error on the list doesn't become "no project yet"); apps/web/src/routes/Shell.test.tsx (the sidebar says so instead of staying empty)
  • Origin: real navigation on /projects/:id with 1128 429 errors in the console

Project name is not unique — nothing in the domain prevents it. When two or more projects in the list have the same name, each of them shows in the sidebar the abbreviated id and the creation date (#a1b2c3d4 · 07/08 14:32), both already present in the project payload. Projects with a unique name show nothing: the caption on every row would be noise in the place with the least space on screen.

Concrete origin: a validation run created twenty projects called validacao-real, and the twenty sidebar rows were visually identical.

RN-090 — The dashboard reads the workspace, not one project at a time​

The card grid and the sidebar dots are fed by one request per cycle — GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-summary —, and the number of requests doesn't grow with the number of projects.

The card shows git provider, provisioning status, budget, agent chips, and last activity; the sidebar shows the status dot and the unread counter. All of that came from seven POLLED queries per project, which made 23 projects cost 3,824 requests per minute against a limit of 300 (RateLimitGuard) — the screen knocked itself down with 429 before finishing loading. RN-088 made the app stop insisting when that happens; this one reduces the request.

Two boundaries the rule fixes, which are not implementation detail:

  • The api answers facts, not a roster. roster brings what happened in the event log (execution activated, modules, gate already opened, delegated subagents, infra accepted). Who is area lead, which icon each agent has, and how members become a chip remain the web's — and the PRESENCE rule is a single one (rosterFromFacts), shared with the team panel, so that a new agent doesn't appear in one place and go missing in the other.
  • The bell drawer only fetches when open. It was, until RN-091, the only read that was still one request per project — the "where I stopped reading" cutoff is a seq kept in the browser (read-state), which the server doesn't know. Today the browser sends that cutoff, and the drawer is also a single request.

Accepted and desired side effect: gatesEverOpened and delegatedSubagents now cover the ENTIRE session. The client derived from the last 200 events and lost chips in long sessions (see ADR 0021) — the text of deriveAgentRoster always said "has opened at some point".

  • Origin: dashboard of 23 projects measured in the browser — 3,824 req/min before, 12 after

RN-091 — The browser sends where it stopped reading; the bell is one request​

With the notifications drawer open, its content comes from one request per cycle — POST /workspaces/:workspaceId/unread-events — and the number of requests doesn't grow with the number of projects.

It's the missing half of RN-090. That one brought the dashboard down from 3,824 to 12 req/min, but the bell kept fetching one project at a time: 23 projects with the drawer open measured 286 req/min against the limit of 300 (RateLimitGuard). It passed, and vanished with one more project.

The obstacle, and why this is the way out. There's no "mark as read" on the server, on purpose: the cutoff is a per-project seq kept in each browser's localStorage (read-state). There were two ways out, and the difference between them is PRODUCT:

  • stop repolling while the drawer is open changes how current what the user sees is — refused, nobody asked for that trade;
  • the browser sending the project → afterSeq map returns exactly the same data at the same cadence. It's pure batching: nothing changes for whoever looks at the screen, neither freshness nor content.

It's a POST that mutates nothing, and the api answers 200 (never 201) to say so. The verb was chosen for being the only one with a BODY: there are dozens of pairs, and in a query string that becomes a long URL — which proxies truncate — besides putting the user's project id in access logs, against the rule of not passing personal data through query strings.

Three semantic guarantees the route fixes, because batching reads with different cutoffs is where the easy mistake lives:

  • an empty map returns empty, without touching the database. "I asked nothing" is not "give me everything";
  • each project respects ITS cutoff — seq strictly greater than its own;
  • the 50-event ceiling is per project, the same one GET .../events applies without limit. A limit on the whole response would let the noisy project eat the quiet ones' quota.

A cursor pointing to a project of another workspace is ignored, not refused: it comes from the caller's local storage and may be a leftover from an old workspace.

  • Test: apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.fanout.test.tsx (with the drawer OPEN: one request, and 30 projects cost the same as 3); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts (the number of database queries doesn't grow with N; empty map, per-project cutoff, per-project ceiling, and workspace isolation)
  • Origin: measured residual of RN-090 — 286 req/min with the drawer open on a 23-project workspace

RN-099 — Activity paginates the past without repolling what doesn't change​

The Overview's Activity column shows a window of 100 events anchored at the session's tail, and goes down into the past page by page. Each page uses the afterSeq/nextCursor that GET /projects/:p/sessions/:s/events already returns: no new route, no new parameter.

Two questions, two queries. useSessionEvents answers "how is it now" — the last 200 under polling — and feeds the team panel, the tree timeline, the execution section, and the Approvals tab. None of them paginates. Activity's answers "what happened", and it was the only one asking that question with the other one's answer: 200 items at once, with no beginning or end, and still not reaching the start of a long session.

The anchor is the tail, not the start of the session. The endpoint paginates FORWARD, and there's no beforeSeq — inventing one would be a new contract. But opening the feed at event #1 of a session with thousands delivers the wrong screen: whoever opens Activity wants what just happened. So the first page is the same latest read the screen already does, with the same queryKey (React Query serves both with ONE fetch), and each click goes down a fixed window with afterSeq.

What pagination can't cost. One request per poll cycle — the same as before, and the savings of RN-090/RN-091 don't regress. Three pieces guarantee that:

  • the tail is the query the screen already had, shared by queryKey;
  • the first click does not become a request: the latest read brings 200 and the window shows 100, so revealing what was already paid for comes before asking again;
  • an old page is a closed seq window over immutable events (there's never an UPDATE on an event table): staleTime: Infinity and no refetchInterval. A poll there would be paying N requests to receive N identical responses.

The count is honest about what it knows. The filters by agent and by type run over the loaded page, not over the session — so the UI says N of M loaded, not "N results". Taking the filter to the server would give the true total and touch the event repository; it's not for this phase, and saying the wrong total would be worse than saying less.

The three states of RN-088 apply here: error before empty — the column said "no activity" when the api had refused.

  • Where: apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts (useSessionEventHistory, EVENTOS_POR_PAGINA), apps/web/src/components/ActivityFeed.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectOverviewTab.tsx, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/session-event.repository.ts (listPaginated, already existing)
  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/session-history.test.tsx (opens at the tail; the first click costs no request; the next paginates with contiguous afterSeq; the loop ends at the start of the session; mounted together with the current state, the tail is ONE fetch; an old page doesn't repoll); apps/web/src/components/ActivityFeed.test.tsx (the "N of M loaded" follows the filter; without the pagination props nothing changes)
  • Origin: user request on the first real navigation — "Activity in the Overview tab must be paginated, so it isn't infinite"

RN-100 — The bell's order is SQL's, not the front end's​

The notifications drawer shows events from most recent to oldest, and when a project has more unread than the 50 ceiling the ones that appear are the NEWEST.

The ordering is the database's out of necessity, not taste. The query cuts at 50 per project with a window function (row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY seq DESC)), and it's what decides which 50 events survive — not just in what order they come out. With ASC, the 50 oldest survived, and a .sort() on the client would sort by recency precisely the window the query had already chosen wrongly: in a project with 300 unread, the 251st event would appear as "the most recent". That's why there's no sorting at all in the front-end path, and the comment in the component says there can't be.

The consequence, and why the read cutoff didn't change. The cutoff is a per-project seq in localStorage, and there's no mark-as-read endpoint, by decision recorded in RN-091. A seq cutoff marks a prefix; the drawer now shows a suffix. Marking as read "the 50 displayed" is inexpressible without a set of reads per event — a new table, out of scope. The only two expressible cutoffs remain "nothing" and "everything up to now".

The way out wasn't changing the semantics (it keeps advancing to the last seq, exactly as before), it was to stop hiding what that advance swallows:

  • each project shows the total unread, not the window size, and declares how many were left out (+ N older);
  • the button now says what it does — mark the N as read — when there's something outside the window;
  • the missing number comes from subtraction, not a request: latestSeq minus the cutoff already comes in the workspace summary (RN-090).

Since the cutoff's semantics didn't change, there's no ADR for this rule: what changed was which window the query chooses and what the drawer declares about it.

  • Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts (unreadEventsForWorkspace), apps/api/src/application/ports/projects-summary-repository.port.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/iam.response.dto.ts (ProjectUnreadEventsResponseDto), apps/web/src/lib/notifications.ts (useNotificationGroups), apps/web/src/components/NotificationBell.tsx
  • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts ("with more unread than the ceiling, the MOST RECENT come back, from new to old" — asserts the SET before the order); apps/web/src/components/NotificationBell.test.tsx (renders in the order received, without reordering; the counter is the total; the button says how many it marks); apps/web/src/lib/notifications.test.tsx (what was left out of the window comes out by subtraction, without a second request); apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.fanout.test.tsx (the drawer is still ONE request)
  • Origin: user request on the first real navigation — "Bell and notifications must always sort by last modified date descending to the oldest"

RN-118 — The team tree exposes execution detail per milestone, and opens the "last 5"​

AgentTimelineTree/timeline-tree.ts (PHASE 14b) already grouped the event log by agent, but with three gaps: the criterion for opening a branch was only active/stopped (unrelated to how many agents existed), the header counter was the TOTAL of milestones (never "what's new"), and tool.call/ tool.result/agent.response became a milestone showing only the tool name — args, result, and iteration, which the event log already records, never reached the screen.

Default opening becomes "the 5 agents with the most recent activity (highest seq of the last milestone)", with active keeping priority over recency — they don't add up: since montarArvore already sorts actives first and, within each group, from most recent to oldest, the two criteria collapse into a single slice (ramosAbertosPorPadrao, the first max(number of actives, 5) branches). More than 5 actives: all open, with no cutoff.

The novelty counter per agent uses the SAME mechanism as the bell (read-state.ts, localStorage), granular by projectId:agentId instead of only projectId — there was no "last seen" at that granularity before. A collapsed branch with a milestone seq greater than that agent's last seen shows the NOVELTY count in place of the total; opening the branch (automatically or manually) marks as seen up to the most recent seq.

Expandable detail is per MILESTONE, not per branch — only tool.call, tool.result, and agent.response (EVENTOS_EXPANSIVEIS) become an individual button, because only they carry a payload worth expanding. The visual grouping by ITERATION uses iteration from the agent.response payload when it exists (ToolLoop — tool.call/tool.result inherit the iteration of the response that dispatched them, because in the ToolLoop they are emitted AFTER it); agents outside the ToolLoop (PO, Criativo, with no iteration in the payload) get their OWN counter per agent, incremented on each response — inference by seq proximity, not a new field in the event log.

  • Where: apps/web/src/lib/timeline-tree.ts (Marco.iteracao, Marco.eventType, Marco.payload, ramosAbertosPorPadrao, marcoExpansivel), apps/web/src/components/AgentTimelineTree.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/read-state.ts (getAgentLastSeenSeq/ setAgentLastSeenSeq)
  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/timeline-tree.test.ts (grouping by real and inferred iteration, ramosAbertosPorPadrao with active/recency/no cutoff), apps/web/src/components/AgentTimelineTree.test.tsx (default opening, novelty counter appearing/disappearing, milestone expanding with args/result/iteration)
  • Origin: user request — gaps confirmed by investigation of the existing PHASE 14b component; no ADR, same "unseen" semantics as the bell, only a new granularity

RN-096 — Every decision says in plain language what happens; the raw payload is born collapsed​

Every proposed_action type has a sentence in Portuguese describing the effect of approving, and it is the first visible thing on the card — before any detail, on the three screens where a decision is asked for (the Approvals queue, the card inside the session chat, and the Insights tab). The raw payload remains accessible, inside a collapse that is born closed, and is never dumped on the screen.

What existed was a dump. Every type without its own visual body fell into an Object.entries(payload).map(([k, v]) => k + ': ' + JSON.stringify(v)), always open. Whoever opened the queue read worktree: /workspaces/dev-api, coAuthor: Brabo User <user@brabo.dev>, and proposto: 4 — and had to deduce what would happen if they clicked Approve. Approval that requires deduction is approval given on autopilot, and the whole product rests on the user being the final authority.

The sentence degrades, and that's what makes it reliable. None of them assumes that a payload key exists: with an empty payload the sentence is still a true sentence, just less specific ("Records a commit in the project's repository."). The payload comes from the engine and from ten different use cases, and none of them promises a format — a sentence that only works with the right fixture is a sentence that breaks on the first real approval.

A type the web doesn't know yet is not a theoretical case. The web's ActionType union has already fallen behind twice: first with the three Gitflow bootstrap types, and again with parallelize/raise_max_parallel, which came in during PHASE 14d. The compiler doesn't catch it: the canonical list is in apps/api, which the web doesn't import. Hence two things at once — the card degrades (neutral verb

  • "see details", with the payload collapsed, instead of the undefined in the icon map that took down the whole React tree), and the test reads the backend's decide.ts and fails when a type comes in without a sentence.

The open/closed default is derived, not configured. The rule is a single one — it opens what is still waiting for a decision from whoever is looking: in the chat, a pending action; in the queue, never (there are N cards, and N open details are the same wall of text); in Insights, a proposed hypothesis. And the RAW payload doesn't open in any variant. The project consequence is that ApprovalCard gained no new mandatory prop: the default comes from variant and status, which already existed.

Verb and sentence come from a single module, consumed by the three screens. The Psicólogo's hypothesis literally uses the instruction_patch verb instead of a parallel vocabulary — and its sentence says what accept really does (queues it for the Anamnese, which may propose the adjustment, which still comes for approval), never "the instruction will be changed".

write_file had a sentence, but no body. It was born outside COM_CORPO_PROPRIO: the sentence showed only the path, and the detail fell into the same collapsed raw-JSON dump this RN exists to avoid — so a write that genuinely asked for approval (outside the dev- prefix, or a path outside the agent's scope) required one more click to see the content. It entered COM_CORPO_PROPRIO with its own body: path and a preview of the content (up to 25 lines/4,000 characters, with a truncation notice — never the entire file, same rule as the raw payload), open by default in the chat while pending, like terminal.

An empty payload is not an absent payload. command (terminal) or path/content (write_file) arriving as an empty string — a malformed tool call from the model, not a rendering bug — degraded into a $ prompt or a blank preview, which the user read as a screen defect. The two bodies now distinguish the two cases and show "the model did not produce a valid X for this action" instead of a blank.

  • Where: apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.ts (VERBO_DA_ACAO, fraseDaAcao, descreverAcao, descreverHipotese), consumed by apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx (Approvals + session chat, COM_CORPO_PROPRIO, previewConteudo for the write_file content) and apps/web/src/components/HypothesisCard.tsx (Insights); collapse via the Disclosure of apps/web/src/components/ui/Disclosure.tsx
  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.test.ts (reads ACTION_TYPES from apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts and requires verb + sentence for each type, with an empty payload); apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.test.tsx (frase e colapso — payload collapsed in both variants, readable JSON on opening, an unknown type doesn't take the screen down, write_file with its own body open by default and preview truncation, empty command/path/content showing the fallback message); apps/web/src/components/HypothesisCard.test.tsx (frase e colapso)
  • Origin: PHASE 19 of program 16–26, from the request "today reading is very hard" on the first real navigation after the database reset

RN-121 — Dev agent and QA are "executors": their own tab, outside the "Agent team"​

The Overview's "Agent team" grid and "Team timeline" mixed Criativo/PO/Arquiteto/Infra with dev-<module> and QA (lead + qa-automacao/qa-performance-seguranca) — seven, eight agents in the same grid, without distinguishing who CREATES/DECIDES from who IMPLEMENTS/VERIFIES. The Executors tab isolates the last two, with the SAME rendering as the Overview (AgentCard, the area grid — extracted to AgentTeamGrid.tsx — and AgentTimelineTree), never a reinvented card.

The separation rule is a single function, isExecutorGroup/ isExecutorAgentId (lib/agent-status.ts): dev-lead/dev-<any module> and the entire qa area (lead + sub-specialties) are executors; the rest isn't. BOTH screens filter the SAME groupRosterByArea with that function — the Overview with !isExecutorGroup, Executors with isExecutorGroup — so an agent can't appear in both nor vanish from both: it's always exactly one side.

The tree doesn't duplicate: each tab filters the EVENTS before passing them to AgentTimelineTree (by whether actor.id belongs to the set of executors), so a dev agent's branch appears only in Executors, never also in the Overview. The Activity column (ActivityFeed, RN-099/100) was NOT filtered — it answers "what happened" in the whole session, dev/QA included, and the component's own per-agent filter already lists everyone who spoke; only the grid and the "who is doing what" tree change place.

RN-125 — Handoff acceptance is INLINE in the thread, with a CTA for the Dev Lead pointing to Executors​

The "X passed the baton to Y" divider that already existed in the timeline (handoff.offered) becomes an actionable card — with the accept button embedded — whenever it represents the current pending offer (the same one offeredHandoff already resolved for the topbar button). Which event becomes the card is decided by PAIR, not by id. The handoff.offered payload carries only toAgent; the fromAgent is the event's actor (RN-054 already used that reading for the divider text). Without the handoff id in the event, "this is the current offer" is answered by finding the most RECENT handoff.offered (highest seq) with the SAME fromAgent/toAgent pair as offeredHandoff — which prevents reopening an accept invite that an older offer for the same pair has already resolved (accepted, declined, or superseded by a new offer).

The card for the Dev Lead gets a second link, "Follow the execution in Executors", to the tab that already exists (RN-121) — it's the start of EXECUTION, and whoever accepts needs to know where to look afterwards. The other offers (PO, Arquiteto…) don't get the link: their session remains the place to follow along itself, there's no "elsewhere to look".

RN-131 — Three races confirmed LIVE in the session thread: invite over the history, anxious indicator, and a turn stuck in handleReadiness​

Three defects found by actually navigating SessionPage.tsx in Chrome, not by test — and all three were race conditions or an incomplete criterion disguised as a product decision.

1. conversaComecou became "ANY event exists", not "a chat.message/agent.response exists". The previous criterion (finding G) was born so as not to confuse the git bootstrap cards with conversation, but had the opposite effect: a session created by git-bootstrap (commit/branch actions already approved, zero chat.message) showed the invite on top of them, and the same happened — much more seriously — in the session that execution activation uses, with dozens of real events (tool.call, tool.result, task events) and no chat.message/agent.response: the invite covered the entire execution history. A new session is the only one with no event at all — that's the right question.

2. conviteVisivel waits for useSessionEvents to finish loading. With a cold cache (page reload), session could arrive while events was still [] — the default of data?.items, indistinguishable from "truly empty session" until the first fetch resolved. Without the !eventsQuery.isPending gate, the invite flickered over sessions with a large history.

3. The "thinking" indicator (bubble with the 3 dots) only turns on after 5s with no text arriving. Before, it turned on the instant streaming/statusAgent became truthy — visual noise on most turns, which answer in under a second. A useEffect arms a setTimeout(…, 5000) when the turn starts with no text yet, and disarms it (via cleanup) as soon as the first delta arrives or the turn ends before the deadline. Real text (streamingText) still appears immediately, never waits for the timer — only the empty indicator gained patience.

4. handleReadiness got the same safety net that handleSend already had. confirmReadiness is, like sendAgentMessage, a synchronous GenServer.call in the engine (up to 120s) — and the Phoenix channel may not have finished connecting (ticket + join, RN-108) when the turn ends, losing the agent.done broadcast forever. handleSend already called finalizarTurnoDoAgente() as soon as the synchronous call resolved, regardless of whether the channel had delivered the event; handleReadiness had been left out of that fix, and without it the agent's bubble stayed stuck empty (streaming: true, no text) until the page reloaded.

  • Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (conversaComecou, conviteVisivel, the pensandoVisivel useEffect right below agenteExibido, and the success block of handleReadiness)
  • Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.convite-so-em-sessao-vazia.test.tsx (an empty session shows the invite; a session with git-bootstrap events or with dozens of tool.call/tool.result hides it; eventsQuery.isPending holds the invite until the first fetch resolves), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.pista-e-status.test.tsx (finding B — the indicator doesn't appear before 5s, appears after, disappears on the first delta, and never appears when the turn ends before the deadline), and apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.readiness-turno-preso.test.tsx (confirmReadiness resolving without onAgentDone reconciles the state the same way SessionPage.turno-preso.test.tsx already proves for handleSend)
  • Origin: LIVE investigation of the product in Chrome — all three reproduced manually before the fix.

RN-136 — The actionable handoff card in the chat only considers those who CONVERSE on this screen​

Since ADR 0185 (RN-658) the Criativo→PO handoff that "I'm ready" requested is born and accepted in the same call, on behalf of whoever clicked — its accept card only appears when that acceptance doesn't fit (a session predating the ADR, a brief that didn't come from the click) or failed. The filter below doesn't change.

OfferInfraHandoffUseCase offers the handoff to Infra and, in the SAME confirmation, offers it to the Dev Lead right after (PHASE 14d) — two separate calls, the Infra one first. handoffs (what SessionPage.tsx reads from useHandoffs) comes sorted by createdAt ASC (DrizzleHandoffRepository#findBySession), and the offeredHandoff that decides which card becomes "actionable" resolved with a plain .find() — always the oldest offered. Since the Infra Lead isn't conversational (it isn't in AGENTES_DE_CHAT, and is never accepted by this screen), the Dev Lead's card would only become actionable after someone accepted the Infra one in a place this screen doesn't show — in practice, never: the user only saw "accept handoff from Infra" and the invite for the Dev Lead stayed invisible behind it.

The filter restricts offeredHandoff to handoffs addressed to an agent of AGENTES_DE_CHAT. The handoff to Infra is still narrated in the thread — its handoff.offered becomes a silent divider, like any offer that isn't "the current one" — only the card with a button now ignores it: Infra never had (nor needs to have) a way to be accepted from here.

RN-137 — "Activate execution" has an inline shortcut on the Dev Lead card, without lowering the role requirement​

The accept card of the handoff to the Dev Lead gained an "Activate execution" button next to the "Follow the execution in Executors" link — a shortcut for those who already know what they want, without going through the conversation. It calls the SAME activateExecution that the Overview uses, now with sessionId (the open chat session) as originSessionId — without this the session that brought the Dev Lead stayed active forever, even with execution (in a SEPARATE session) having already taken off through this shortcut (RN-135).

The route still requires maintainer — DELIBERATELY not aligned with the developer that already suffices to accept the handoff on the same card. Whoever activates becomes the session.createdBy of the execution session, and that's the role that ProposeActionUseCase resolves (ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject) as the EFFECTIVE one of every git_commit/git_push/pr_open the dev agents propose from then on — it's the same reason that already justified the maintainer of the Overview button (ExecutionController#activate). Lowering the requirement here would silently invert that resolution: every PR the execution opened would go from auto_approve to require_approval whenever whoever clicked was developer, without anyone having decided that. Whoever isn't maintainer receives the api's real sentence ("Papel insuficiente para esta ação", via mensagemDaApi) instead of a generic error.

No client-side module_map gate: when this card exists, the Arquiteto has already defined it — it's the artifact that precedes the handoff offer to the Dev Lead —, so replicating the Overview's disabled={!hasModuleMap} would lock the button for nothing. The rare case (inconsistent session) falls into the same catch that handles 403/other errors.

RN-138 — An agent's messages collapse after it passes the baton​

The chat timeline showed everything always expanded, without grouping by author — in a long session with Criativo, PO, and Arquiteto taking turns, the history of those who already left the scene competed for space with whoever is speaking now. Each timeline entry gained an agentId (the actor.id of whoever generated it, when it's an agent — agent.response, agent.error, epic/story created by the PO, approval card); user entries and those that mark a TRANSITION (handoff, story promotion) are left without agentId on purpose, because they're cut points by nature.

A CONSECUTIVE sequence of the same agentId becomes a collapsible header (the design system's Disclosure, closed by default — agent name + count, reopens with one click) when both conditions hold:

  1. the agent has already passed the baton — there's a handoff from it (fromAgent) with status: 'accepted' (the same truth the event log's handoff.accepted records, without needing to rebuild by joining events); and
  2. none of its actions is pending — the check is by actor.id across ALL the session's actions, not only those in the current sequence: an open approval race can't stay hidden behind a click at ANY point of the thread.

A sequence of 1 entry never collapses — "So-and-so · 1 message" in place of the message itself gains nothing. Any entry without agentId, or from a different agent, breaks the current sequence exactly as a change of agent does — it only groups what is really consecutive.

  • Origin: code investigation + live test in Chrome — collapse request, with AgentTimelineTree/timeline-tree.ts as the reference of FORM (group by agent, name + count, open/closed), adapted to the chat's heterogeneous interleaved timeline

RN-028 — Capability decides, not the provider's name​

An unsupported operation (branch protection on the local provider) is declared in capabilities and rejected with GitNotSupportedError — never a silent failure.

And the criterion for declaring is still proof: a capability is only true when the suite exercises it on that provider; without proof, it's declared false and degrades (same criterion as ADRs 0041/0042).

RN-029 — The Gitflow bootstrap is idempotent and resumable​

Five steps; each one checks before acting and can be resumed from the point where it failed. skip is success, not error.

There used to be six. The sixth created the rc branch, a rung that ADR 0030 removed from the policy — the bootstrap kept creating, protecting, and documenting in the user's repository a ladder the product had already abandoned (finding #3 of the first dogfooding). The value create_rc_branch remains in the bootstrap_step enum: old rows reference it, and a step that really happened isn't erased from history.

Credentials​

The user's LLM key and git token live in the same table (user_credentials), under the same envelope encryption. This section applies to both.

RN-055 — A credential is always encrypted and saved; verifying is a separate action, with three answers​

Registration doesn't judge the credential: it encrypts and saves, even if the provider would refuse it. Verifying is an explicit action on the already saved credential — the api decrypts, calls the provider, and returns only the verdict. The plain text never comes back in any response, not in pieces, not in the refusal reason.

It used to be the opposite: registration tested before persisting and refused to save (ADR 0004, extended to LLM keys in Phase 11a). The real failure mode was the opposite of what was predicted — since the field is write-only and the screen never redisplays what was typed, a refusal left the user with no credential and without the text to fix it.

The verdict has three values, and the third is mandatory:

when
okthe provider accepted
recusadothe provider rejected — carries its reason
nao_suportadothere's no verified test endpoint (ollama, anthropic, openai)

Without nao_suportado, a provider whose tester is a NO-OP would come back ok and the screen would assert a verification that never happened. It's the capability rule of ADR 0041 applied here: only what was proven is declared. That's why the port declares supports() — the silence of test() alone is ambiguous.

A bad key is not an HTTP exception: the use case catches LLMCredentialConnectionTestFailedError/GitCredentialConnectionTestFailedError and returns a result, with 200. The only exception is when there's no credential for (user, provider) — 404, because then there's nothing to test.

  • Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/credentials/test-stored-credential.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/upsert-user-credential.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/git/register-git-credential.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/ports/llm-credential-connection-tester.port.ts (supports)
  • Test: test/application/use-cases/credentials/test-stored-credential.use-case.spec.ts (the three results, the git×LLM dispatch, the 404, and the absence of the secret in the response); test/application/use-cases/llm/upsert-user-credential.use-case.spec.ts and test/application/use-cases/git/register-git-credential.use-case.spec.ts (the unconditional save, which is the inversion)
  • Origin: ADR 0050

PROGRAM 28 — Wave 4, front G2: indexing pipeline and hybrid search for Chat RAG (RN-231..238, ADR 0080)​

RN-231 — ChunkRepository gains DELETE and both halves of hybrid search​

The Wave 3 port (RN-226) only covered basic write/read. Wave 4 added deleteByScope/deleteBySession (for idempotent reindexing by full rebuild — delete and recreate, never UPDATE) and searchByVector/searchByLexicalQuery (the two halves of hybrid search, each an independent query, taking advantage of the index built for it — HNSW or GIN). deleteByScope is typed Exclude<ChunkScope, 'session'>: deleting session for a whole project would delete sessions that aren't being reindexed now, so a session is only deleted by deleteBySession.

When the e-mail returned by the provider matches an already registered account, the link only happens if the provider marks that e-mail as verified (emailVerified: true) — GitHub via GET /user/emails, GitLab via confirmed_at. A typed but unverified e-mail is not proof of identity: anyone can register someone else's e-mail at an OAuth provider. Accepting the link without that check would open account takeover — whoever already has alguem@empresa.com on Brabo didn't ask for someone else's GitHub, with that address only TYPED, to inherit the account. The refusal is 403, and no link is saved.

RN-274's e-mail verification protects an account that already exists; when there's no matching account, there's nothing to protect, only a new account to be born. Requiring a verified e-mail in that case would make the common path more expensive (most GitHub users have a verified e-mail, but not all, and refusing the login for that would be friction with no corresponding security gain) without reducing any risk — the worst case is a new account with an unproven e-mail, the same risk that password registration already implicitly accepts until the click on the verification link.

Provisioning by social login writes one row in users and NONE in auth_credentials — the same pair the Keycloak migration already left for "account without a password yet" (see RN-032 and migracao-keycloak.spec.ts). LoginUseCase and ResetPasswordUseCase already handle that state; no second "pending password" mechanism was needed for social login.

RN-279 — Linking by verified e-mail also verifies the existing account's e-mail​

When an account registered by password (and never verified) is linked to a social identity whose e-mail the provider marks as verified, the account gets emailVerifiedAt filled in as a side effect. The provider has just proven, through an independent path, exactly what clicking the verification link would prove — it makes no sense for the account to remain blocked from password login (RN-032) after proving possession of the e-mail through another equally strong path.

A social identity linked to an account with auth_credentials.disabled_at filled in is refused with 403, both on direct login (already known identity) and on the attempt to link. Disabling an account can't be bypassed by switching the sign-in method.
