RN-418 — Git external effect and privileged command (sudo/doas) become an absolute ceiling, never deny​

Revised by RN-713 (AT-385, 10/02): with automatic mode (the wildcard on auto_approve), push and PR are auto-approved.

Revised by RN-689 (AT-347, owner's decision of 10/01): the ceiling below also applies to the TYPED actions git_push and pr_open, which until then only had the minimum role and were born auto_approved by the wildcard, by a specific rule, or by permissions.json. The rest of this entry still holds.

Revises RN-106 by a GLOBAL and explicit decision of the product owner: git push, PR opening, deploy (the same prefix detection RN-106 already had), and sudo/doas (new — matched by VERB in comandoPrivilegiadoNoComando, scanning all segments of the command) stop being an unconditional deny and become an ABSOLUTE CEILING — unconditional require_approval, in the SAME final block and SAME code pattern as the other ceilings (protected merge, instruction_patch, parallelize/raise_max_parallel, path scope): current.policy === 'auto_approve' → overridden. The condition that makes this safe — without which the ceiling would be decorative — is the half that closes "always allow" AT THE SOURCE: ApproveAlwaysActionUseCase/patternsForAction refuse to write a pattern into allow for a terminal action with a git external effect or a privileged command. The specific instance can still be approved through the normal flow (ApproveActionUseCase); only the click that would write a pattern forever is refused, with a clear message. It's the same argument the original RN-106 used to justify deny — resolved at the source, no longer blocking the symptom.

RN-419 — The local runner authenticates with a single-use ticket, scoped to project and role​

POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket (role developer+, refuses if workspaceMode !== 'local') and POST /projects/:projectId/terminal-ticket (role viewer+, any mode) are the two public routes that issue the ticket to the right client — the runner asks for the first, the web asks for the second. RN-420 — An agent command routed to the runner goes through the SAME approval pipeline; PTY is a user action, audited​

REVISED by RN-423 (ADR 0104): the condition to route is no longer binary. workspace_mode == "local" became execution_mode == "runner" AND non-null workspace_verified_at AND runner connected — missing any of the THREE, the command is explicitly REFUSED, never falling into the System.cmd/bind-mount of mounted (which doesn't exist for a runner project, with no bind-mount at all). The rest of this entry — the usual approval pipeline, PTY as a user action — still holds as is.

Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor decides to route a command to the runner (instead of the usual System.cmd, inside the container) AFTER the normal pipeline (decide()/proposed_action) has already approved — routing is only a choice of DESTINATION for the same already authorized command, never a second execution path escaping the policy (which keeps the absolute ceilings of RN-418 applying the same, sudo/git included). Condition to route (history, see revision above): workspace_mode == "local" AND runner connected (Engine.Runners.Registry.connected?/1) — without either of the two, the usual behavior continues (System.cmd in the container via bind-mount, ADR 0072 becomes the FALLBACK, never removed).

Interactive PTY is DIFFERENT: it's an action of the authenticated USER typing in the terminal of their own machine, not the agent's — that's why it does NOT go through proposed_action. But it needs to leave a trace: pty_open/pty_close coming from the web emit terminal.session.started/terminal.session.ended in the event log (addressed to the project's most recent session, ProjectSession.latest_id/1, the same mechanism the Anamnese already uses to narrate something project-scoped). A real finding during consolidation: with no runner connected, the web needs an EXPLICIT pty_error back — discarding the request with only a log on the server would leave the tab stuck in "loading" forever, never reaching the "no runner" state the screen already knew how to show.

Automatic personal workspace on sign-up (RN-410)​

Found while navigating the product after a database reset: the dashboard's "New project"/"+" button did NOTHING, with no error at all. The root cause was in two layers. The visible one: Dashboard.tsx only opens the NewProjectWizard when useCurrentWorkspace() finds a workspace (list[0]?.workspace from GET /workspaces); with none, the click has nowhere to go. The deep one: RegisterUseCase created user and credential but NEVER a workspace, and the same held for SocialLoginCallbackUseCase in the branch that provisions a new account — EVERY new sign-up, by password or by social login, hit that wall. It just hadn't shown up before because db/seed.ts always creates a workspace along with the demo data, and no product screen calls createWorkspace (the route, the use case, and the HTTP client exist — they just have no caller at all in the UI).

RN-410 — Every NEW account is born with a personal workspace, in the SAME transaction as the account​

RegisterUseCase (e-mail/password registration) and SocialLoginCallbackUseCase (provisioning a new account via social login) create the workspace and add the user as owner — the same create/addMember pair that CreateWorkspaceUseCase already uses — inside the SAME transaction that already creates user and credential. It isn't a second call to the use case: that one opens its OWN transaction, and the point is that a user without a workspace never exists if something fails midway.

Name and slug come from ONE pure function, nomeESlugDoWorkspacePessoal(nome, email, userId) (apps/api/src/domain/auth/personal-workspace.ts), reused by both creation points — so the rule doesn't diverge in two files, the same reason behind normalizarEmail/exigirSenhaValida living in the domain. The name uses the given nome (social login uses the provider's login), with the e-mail's local-part as a fallback when there's no name — it never invents either. The slug is kebab-case of the same text, ALWAYS suffixed with userId.slice(0, 8) (same pattern as extraDevAgentId/workspaceDirName/session label): workspaces.slug is UNIQUE in the database and nothing in the product does retry-on-conflict, so two sign-ups with an equal name or local-part would collide without the suffix. A name or e-mail with NO alphanumeric character degrades to the literal workspace-<8 chars>, never to an empty string.

  • Test: apps/api/test/domain/auth/personal-workspace.spec.ts (name with/without nome, fallback to the e-mail's local-part, accent/uppercase becoming ASCII kebab-case, workspace-<id> fallback with no alphanumeric character at all, slug always unique thanks to the suffix); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/register.use-case.spec.ts (a new account gets a workspace with the user as owner, a duplicate e-mail doesn't create a second); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/ social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts (same proof in the branch that provisions a new account via social login)

ADR 0072 (RN-169/RN-170) and ADR 0103 (RN-419/RN-420) never talked to each other: the runner reused the same workspace_mode == 'local' flag without any bind-mount, so really using the runner still required going through the MOUNTED FOLDER validation. ADR 0104 reconciles the two. Migration 0048 recreates the enum (project_workspace_mode → project_execution_mode, local → mounted) in a single transaction — ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE can't be referenced in the same transaction where it was added — and adds workspace_verified_at (nullable).

RN-421 — execution_mode has THREE values: container/mounted/runner​

projects.workspace_mode (two values) became projects.execution_mode (three): container (DEFAULT, unchanged), mounted (the old local, RENAMED — same behavior, same disk validation on creation), and runner (NEW: a user folder without bind-mount, confirmed by the brabo-runner CLI). The database CHECK became (execution_mode <> 'container') = (workspace_path IS NOT NULL) — it covers both non- container modes with the SAME condition, with no explicit OR per value.

projectScopeRoot/Project.workspace_dir_name (api and engine) derive the root by the SAME rule in both non-container modes: the user's path is the root, distinguished from the managed folder name by the leading slash. What changes between mounted and runner isn't WHERE the root is — it's WHEN/WHO confirms that it really exists (RN-422/RN-423).

RN-423 — The runner CONFIRMS the path; without confirmation, the command is refused — it never falls into the container​

The runner is the source of truth for a runner project's path, not what was typed in the wizard. Right after the Phoenix channel connects (terminal:<projectId>, :runner role), apps/runner/src/index.ts pushes workspace_confirm with the --dir it received on the command line. The engine passes it on (Engine.Sessions.EngineApiClient.confirm_workspace/4) to POST /internal/projects/:projectId/workspace-verification (ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase), which:

  1. Refuses with 400 if the project isn't in runner mode;
  2. Revalidates the path with the SAME lexical predicate as creation (RN-422) — even coming from the runner, system root and overlap with Brabo remain forbidden;
  3. OVERWRITES workspacePath with the normalized path and writes workspaceVerifiedAt = now() — without requiring equality with what was typed at creation: the runner rules;
  4. Is IDEMPOTENT — reconnecting reporting the SAME path rewrites nothing (changed: false); a DIFFERENT path rewrites, because the runner remains the source of truth at each reconnection;
  5. With no session in the project yet (ProjectSession.latest_id/1 returns nil): the UPDATE happens all the same, only the project.workspace_verified event (and the evidence for the workspace-verificado gate) is absent — the SAME degradation that pty_open/pty_close already accept (RN-108/RN-420). An accepted and declared gap, not a silent one.

Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 gained FOUR outputs, not two: runner with workspace_verified_at: nil refuses (:recusar_nao_verificado); verified runner without a connected runner refuses (:recusar_runner_desconectado); verified and connected runner routes (:rotear_runner); any other mode follows the usual path (:caminho_de_sempre). The two refusals NEVER fall into System.cmd — a runner project has no bind-mount, and "falling to the usual path" would be executing blindly in a folder the engine's process doesn't see. The same refusal applies in the race (Registry said connected at the start of run/3, but the runner dropped before the dispatch answered).

RN-424 — A PAT authenticates ONLY runner-ticket, by construction — never dual-auth with JWT on that route​

A Personal Access Token (brb_…) never authorizes any route other than POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket. The guarantee isn't an if that a new route could forget to check: it's structural. @RequirePatAuth() marks the handler with IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY; JwtAuthGuard (the global APP_GUARD) checks that metadata BEFORE trying JWT verify() and returns true without validating anything — the same bypass shape that IS_PUBLIC_KEY and IS_SERVICE_ROUTE_KEY already use. PatAuthGuard, applied only to that handler via @UseGuards(), is what actually authenticates: it extracts the bearer, refuses (401) any value not starting with brb_ without querying the repository — it never tries to validate as JWT on that route, and no other route accepts brb_… as a bearer.

After PatAuthGuard populates request.user, RolesGuard/ ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase keep running, unchanged — belt and suspenders: if the PAT's owner loses sufficient role in the project through the normal path (ProjectMember/workspace), the token stops authorizing even without having been explicitly revoked.

The alternative considered and refused: the global JwtAuthGuard recognizing the brb_ prefix and populating request.user directly, for ANY route. That would authorize the PAT for everything the user's role allows in the rest of the api — the "only asks for a runner ticket" scope would become decorative.

RN-425 — PAT validation collapses nonexistent/revoked/expired into a single answer; wrong scope is 403; last_used_at is never throttled​

PersonalAccessTokenRepository.validarEUsar(hash) is ONE query: UPDATE personal_access_tokens SET last_used_at = now() WHERE token_hash = $1 AND revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()) RETURNING id, user_id, project_id. Zero rows returns null, and the guard answers 401 for "doesn't exist", "revoked", and "expired" with the SAME message — whoever presents a stolen or expired token doesn't find out which of the three is the reason (same pattern as AccountTokenRepository.consumir()).

Incorrect project scope is a DIFFERENT category: if the project_id returned by the query doesn't match the route's :projectId, it's 403, not 401 — the token really authenticated, it just has no right to THIS project.

last_used_at is updated UNCONDITIONALLY, in the SAME validation query — never with a throttle (e.g. "only if last_used_at is NULL or older than 5 minutes") in the same WHERE. A throttle there is a real bug: a PAT presented twice in under 5 minutes would fall out of the WHERE the second time (because last_used_at would be "too fresh"), and the query would return zero rows for a valid token — rejecting a legitimate reconnection with 401. The runner's retry loop reconnects in seconds, not minutes. The cost of not throttling is a one-row UPDATE by unique index per call — irrelevant in the real worst case (up to 10 attempts in a row, the runner's ceiling).

  • Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/personal-access-token.repository.ts (validarEUsar), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts
  • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/personal-access-token.repository.spec.ts (nonexistent/revoked/expired → null; "toca last_used_at sempre que válido, sem throttle" — regression of the bug above), apps/api/test/interfaces/pat-auth.guard.spec.ts (wrong scope → 403, not 401)
  • Architectural decision: ADR 0105

RN-426 — Listing/revoking a PAT is scoped to the user's OWN tokens, in the query's WHERE — no cross-user admin in this wave​

ListPersonalAccessTokensUseCase/RevokePersonalAccessTokenUseCase filter by userId inside the SQL query (WHERE user_id = $1 AND ...), never fetching everything and filtering afterwards in memory. Each user only sees and only revokes their OWN tokens — including within a project where they're maintainer.

revogar(id, userId, motivo) is IDEMPOTENT: if the UPDATE (with the same WHERE user_id = $1) finds no row because it was already revoked, a second tie-breaking query returns the row (revoking again isn't an error); if it finds none because the token doesn't exist OR doesn't belong to the calling user, it returns null — the SAME answer (404 in the controller) for both cases, so as not to leak the existence of someone else's token through the status code.

Closed by RN-427: a maintainer revoking another user's PAT — the incident response case (a dismissed dev with a leaking token) — which this section declared out of scope left the backlog and is implemented. This ruler (self-revocation, scope by userId) didn't change at all.

  • Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/list-personal-access-tokens.use-case.ts (ListPersonalAccessTokensUseCase), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-personal-access-token.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/personal-access-token.repository.ts (listarDoUsuarioNoProjeto, revogar)
  • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/list-personal-access-tokens.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-personal-access-token.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/personal-access-token.repository.spec.ts (revoking another user's token → null)
  • Architectural decision: ADR 0105

RN-427 — A maintainer revokes the PAT of ANY user of the project, scoped by project_id — incident response​

An extension of RN-426's model, not a new architecture decision: the same pattern already used to close RN-407 (PO reading product metrics) over an already decided model, with no ADR of its own. It closes the cut that ADR 0105 declared "outside this wave" — real incident response (a dismissed dev with a leaking token), where waiting for the user themselves to revoke isn't an option.

ListPersonalAccessTokensAsMaintainerUseCase/ RevokePersonalAccessTokenAsMaintainerUseCase are NEW use cases, on SEPARATE routes (GET .../personal-access-tokens/all, DELETE .../personal-access-tokens/:tokenId/admin, both @RequireRole('maintainer')) — never an if inside the self-service handlers, the same principle already used in the rest of the product for authorization by level (OfferInfraHandoffUseCase). The self-revocation route (RN-426) doesn't change at all.

listarDoProjeto brings ALL of the project's tokens — with no userId filter — with an innerJoin on users for the owner's e-mail, the same pattern the project members listing already uses: without the e-mail, a maintainer seeing "revoke whose token?" would only have a raw UUID, and the item's very reason (incident response) asks to know WHO the owner is.

revogarComoMaintainer(id, projectId, motivo) is the same idempotent design as revogar() — a conditional UPDATE followed by a tie-breaking SELECT when the UPDATE finds no row —, but the WHERE compares project_id, never user_id: a maintainer revokes any owner WITHIN their project, never a token of another project. With no row at all (the token doesn't exist OR belongs to another project), it returns null — the SAME answer (404) for both cases, the same discipline of not leaking existence that RN-426 already applied.

RN-428 — The story promotion carousel survives the event window​

promocoesPendentes/the PO's promotion carousel (RN-148) no longer depends on a scan over the window of the last 200 events of useSessionEvents. The source of content/count is useBacklog (Story.proposedReady, per session, complete and without a window) — in a long session, backlog.story_promotion_proposed leaves the window while the story is still really pending, and before this the carousel shrank (or vanished) silently. The same class of bug that RN-180 already fixed for ContextAside.

When the story isn't in the loaded backlog (query hasn't answered yet), it degrades story by story to the usual window scan. The anchoring in the timeline still comes from the event within the window when it exists; if the event that opened the batch has already left the window, the carousel anchors at the TOP of the visible stretch instead of vanishing — never hiding a real state because of a read cutoff.

RN-429 — Local folder navigation is a pure relay through the Runner, never the api enumerating the container​

The terminal:<projectId> channel gains two events, in the SAME relay design as the PTY: fs_list_dir/fs_home_dir (:web asks, the engine relays DIRECTLY to the registered runner's pid, immediate error when there's no connected runner — it never waits for a response that won't come) and fs_list_dir_reply/fs_home_dir_reply (:runner answers, a broadcast filtered only to :web, correlated by a client-generated ref). The api does NOT gain any new route — it still doesn't enumerate the filesystem, the argument ADR 0072 had already fixed against a folder picker still stands. apps/runner/src/guard.ts (which restricts the cwd of an already approved command to the project root) on purpose does NOT apply to navigation — listing a directory is a free read on the user's machine, with the privileges they already have, and an entry without permission is skipped, it doesn't abort the whole listing.

Declared gap: the channel's ticket is issued PER already existing PROJECT — on the project creation screen (NewProjectWizard.tsx), the project is only born on confirmation, so FolderBrowserModal receives projectId: null there and shows the declared state instead of trying an impossible connection; the free text field remains the manual path, as before.

The prs tab resolves the defect of ProjectApprovalsTab.tsx, which scoped the "PRs in review" section to usePendingActions(projectId, latestSession?.id) — a pending review from a previous session disappeared as soon as a new session was born. RN-432 — The language preference comes in the login/refresh payload, never in an extra call​

Revised by RN-891: the column also accepts ru and zh-Hans, and the web's default went from en to pt-BR (ADR 0216).

Local runner terminal stuck at "Opening terminal..." forever (RN-433)​

Found testing a new project in runner mode (ADR 0103/0104) and opening Code → Dev → Terminal: the screen never left the loading skeleton, and the console showed socket do terminal com erro/socket do terminal fechado in a loop, with growing backoff until stabilizing at ~5-6s — the pattern of the phoenix.js DEFAULT backoff.

RN-433 — The terminal socket gives up after a timeout, the ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL default is reachable BY THE BROWSER, and the endpoint doesn't duplicate the path​

Three stacked defects. The first two were found investigating the symptom; the THIRD only showed up after fixing the first two — without them, the browser never reached the engine to reveal the path bug underneath. Fixing only one leaves the others standing:

  1. ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL (RN-419) never had any default in docker/docker-compose.yml — only ENGINE_URL (http://engine:4000, a hostname that ONLY resolves inside the Compose network). The code's fallback (process.env.ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL ?? process.env.ENGINE_URL ?? …, request-runner-ticket.use-case.ts) silently fell to the wrong value, and the browser tried to open a WebSocket against a hostname it never resolves. docker/docker-compose.yml gained ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL: ${ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:4000} in the api service — the SAME default VITE_ENGINE_URL already uses in the web service, for the same reason.
  2. Even with the right URL, a transport that NEVER opens (engine down, firewall, a wrong future reconfiguration) had no ceiling at all: apps/web/src/lib/terminal-channel.ts never passed reconnectAfterMs to the Socket, so phoenix.js fell into its DEFAULT backoff and kept trying to reconnect on its own forever — the module's own docblock already declared the intent of "no automatic reconnection" (same ruler as session-channel.ts/RN-108), but it was never fulfilled in practice. Without onError/onClose calling handlers.onErro, TerminalPanel stayed stuck in 'carregando' (RN-088 — every screen distinguishes loading/error/ empty — silently violated). Fixed with reconnectAfterMs returning a value that practically never fires (24h, same pattern as session-channel.ts) and an OWN 8s timeout (TIMEOUT_CONEXAO_MS): if onOpen doesn't fire before that, the module calls handlers.onErro with an actionable message and disconnects.
  3. The defect that actually prevented the connection, masked by the two above: terminal-channel.ts concatenated '/runner/websocket' to an engineWsUrl the api already returns READY — ws://host:porta/runner (engineWsUrlPublico()) —, and phoenix.js's OWN Socket also appends /websocket by itself in the constructor (this.endPoint = ${endPoint}/websocket). The result hit the engine as GET /runner/runner/websocket/websocket, which Phoenix.Router.NoRouteError refuses — confirmed in the engine's log (docker logs brabo-engine-1) during the end-to-end verification of this fix. apps/runner/src/channel.ts (the CLI side) already did it right — it passes engineWsUrl straight to the Socket, without touching it — and the terminal-channel.ts test never caught it because the mock of getTerminalTicket used an engineWsUrl (http://engine.local, without /runner) that doesn't reflect the api's real contract; fixed along with it. Fix: terminal-channel.ts now uses engineWsUrl (only with the defensive .replace(/^http/, 'ws')) directly, without concatenating any path.

Verified END TO END against exp001 (runner mode, without a real brabo-runner connected): before the fix, the tab spun forever; after, the engine's log shows CONNECTED TO EngineWeb.RunnerSocket → JOINED terminal:<projectId> → pty_resize descartado — sem runner conectado, and the screen shows RunnerOnboardingPanel with the brabo-runner command in under 1s — never item 2's 8s timeout, which remains as a safety net for the case of the engine being genuinely down.

  • Where: docker/docker-compose.yml, .env.example, apps/web/src/lib/terminal-channel.ts
  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/terminal-channel.test.ts (a socket that never opens calls onErro within the timeout, without phoenix's automatic reconnection; the mock's engineWsUrl fixed to reflect the real contract — already with /runner, without /websocket — and the happy path assertion now requires the URL used in the Socket EQUAL to the ticket's engineWsUrl, with no concatenation)
  • ADR: none — a bug fix restoring the behavior that ADR 0103/0104 and the module's own docblock already declared as intent
  • Origin: found manually testing a new project in runner mode; item 3 only showed up when verifying the fix of items 1/2 end to end in the browser against the real engine

RN-434 — On Linux, the local runner's --dir is only accepted inside the user's $HOME​

The brabo-runner CLI (runner mode, ADR 0103/0104) only validated that --dir exists and is a folder — with no restriction at all on WHERE that folder could be in the file system. lerArgumentos() (apps/runner/src/index.ts) now calls validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux(dir, process.platform, homedir()) (apps/runner/src/guard.ts) right after the existence check: on Linux (process.platform === 'linux'), --dir is only accepted inside os.homedir() — the $HOME itself or any subfolder of it; a path outside that tree (/etc, /root, /, or even another account in /home) is refused with process.exit(2) and a message explaining the reason and showing the expected home. Outside Linux (macOS, Windows) the behavior doesn't change — the restriction is Linux-only.

The check reuses dentroDoEscopo/semBarraFinal, the same path comparison primitives that validarCwdDentroDaRaiz already uses in the same module, but is deliberately simpler than it: no realpath nor TOCTOU/symlink protection, because it doesn't protect against a malicious SERVER (that's the role of validarCwdDentroDaRaiz, exercised on each exec) — it's a STARTUP check of the local CLI itself, guiding the user who typed a wrong path when bringing up the runner.

  • Where: apps/runner/src/guard.ts (DirForaDoHomeError/validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux), apps/runner/src/index.ts (lerArgumentos)
  • Test: apps/runner/src/guard.spec.ts (describe('validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux', …) — accepts the home itself and a subfolder of it on Linux, refuses a path outside home and another account inside /home on Linux, and confirms the restriction does NOT apply outside Linux)
  • ADR: 0104 (additive extension — the runner was already declared "source of truth of the path"; this rule only narrows what it accepts as --dir on Linux)
  • Origin: explicit request from the product owner, during a real project creation test (an attempt to point --dir at a path outside home, /home/dev/exp001, which didn't exist on the machine — it led to the decision to lock paths outside $HOME on Linux)

RN-435 — A nonexistent local runner --dir is created, not refused​

The brabo-runner CLI (runner mode, ADR 0103/0104) refused with process.exit(2) any --dir that didn't yet exist on disk — the project folder had to be created manually before bringing up the CLI. garantirDiretorio() (apps/runner/src/guard.ts) now creates the folder automatically (mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })) when it doesn't exist, and lerArgumentos() (apps/runner/src/index.ts) calls that function RIGHT AFTER validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux (RN-434) — the ORDER is the rule: the $HOME check works on a path that doesn't exist yet (only resolve(), without touching disk), so it runs first and keeps refusing --dir outside home on Linux even when it doesn't exist yet, BEFORE any creation attempt — creating first would reopen the hole that RN-434 had just closed. --dir pointing to an already existing FILE remains a real error (DirNaoEUmaPastaError, process.exit(2), without trying to create anything) — this CLI never overwrites a file silently. A failure in the creation itself (permission denied, disk full, etc.) also refuses (NaoConsegiuCriarDiretorioError), with the original error's message embedded.

  • Where: apps/runner/src/guard.ts (garantirDiretorio/DirNaoEUmaPastaError/NaoConsegiuCriarDiretorioError), apps/runner/src/index.ts (lerArgumentos)
  • Test: apps/runner/src/guard.spec.ts (describe('garantirDiretorio', …) — does nothing when the folder already exists, creates recursively when it doesn't, refuses without creating when the path already exists and is a file, and wraps a mkdir failure in NaoConsegiuCriarDiretorioError; and one more case in describe('validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux', …) proving that a --dir outside home and NOT YET EXISTING stays refused, confirming that the order of the two checks opens no hole)
  • ADR: 0104 (additive extension — it doesn't change the design of the runner as source of truth of the path, it only reduces the friction of bringing up a new project)
  • Origin: product owner's request, upon noticing that the folder of a new project in runner mode didn't exist on the machine and needed to be created manually before running the CLI — the same scenario that motivated RN-434 (nonexistent /home/dev/exp001), now solved by creating the folder instead of just refusing

RN-453 — A relative local runner --dir resolves against INIT_CWD, not against pnpm's rebased cwd​

resolve(dirBruto) in lerArgumentos() resolved a relative --dir against process.cwd() — correct when the CLI runs directly (standalone binary, npm install -g @brabo/runner), but WRONG in the only invocation path that exists today without a real npm publication (a real finding, ADR 0106/backlog): pnpm --filter runner start REBASES process.cwd() to the PACKAGE's folder (apps/runner), not the folder from which the user typed the command. pnpm --filter runner start -- --dir ../exp001, run from ~/dev/brabo, created ~/dev/brabo/apps/exp001 instead of ~/dev/exp001 — silently, with no error, because RN-435 already makes a nonexistent --dir get created instead of refused.

resolverDir() (apps/runner/src/guard.ts) resolves against INIT_CWD when present — the variable that npm/pnpm ALWAYS defines with the original invocation folder, existing only when the process is born from a package.json script — and falls back to process.cwd() when absent (direct binary, where it's already the right folder). Node's resolve() already ignores the base when dirBruto is absolute, so an absolute path (the case documented in the README) doesn't change behavior.

  • Where: apps/runner/src/guard.ts (resolverDir), apps/runner/src/index.ts (lerArgumentos)
  • Test: apps/runner/src/guard.spec.ts (describe('resolverDir', …) — relative against INIT_CWD when present, falls back to the process's cwd when absent, absolute ignores both bases)
  • ADR: 0104 (additive extension, same category as RN-435 — it reduces invocation friction, it doesn't change the runner as source of truth of the path)
  • Origin: found in real use, running pnpm --filter runner start -- dir ../exp001 from inside the monorepo checkout — the only invocation path available today, because @brabo/runner hasn't really been published on npm yet (NPM_TOKEN pending, see ADR 0106's backlog)

The Runner's folder explorer becomes three columns, and creating a runner project no longer waits for the final step (RN-436/436)​

Two changes requested by the product owner after testing the creation of a real project: (1) the existing folder browser (FolderBrowserModal) was a simple list with a breadcrumb, when the visual reference he sent (a GNOME Files/GTK-style picker, with three columns) already existed as a ready design handoff to adapt; (2) "Browse folder..." didn't work on the project's CREATION SCREEN — only after it was created — because the Runner channel's ticket (ADR 0107) is anchored to a projectId that, until this fix, was only born on confirmation.

RN-436 — FolderBrowserModal becomes a three-column explorer: shortcuts, a list where one click selects/double click enters, and a details panel​

The single-list layout became three columns inside the Modal size="full": shortcuts (Home folder, which calls diretorioInicial(); Root, /), the central list with breadcrumb, and a details panel on the right. The protocol (FsEntrada, in apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts) only has { nome, isDir } — no size nor modification date — and wasn't extended (it would touch apps/engine/apps/runner, outside the scope of this delivery); the details panel only shows what can be derived client-side: name, type, and the item count when the displayed item is the ALREADY OPEN folder (never of a merely selected folder, which would require an extra call to the runner).

The TWO gestures that were previously fused into a single click (which already navigated into the folder) were separated: one click now only SELECTS (highlights the item and updates the details panel) and a double click ENTERS. The final button ("Use this folder", renamed from "Select this folder" — the folderBrowserModal.select key of pt-BR/en changed along with it) uses the selected item when there is one (selected.kind === 'dir' ? join(path, selected.name) : path) or the currently open folder when there's none. The list stopped filtering files — the whole listing appears now, with files rendered as <div aria-disabled> instead of <button>: visually dimmed and with no gesture at all, because only folders remain navigable/selectable.

  • Where: apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.tsx, FolderBrowserModal.module.css, apps/web/src/locales/{pt-BR,en}/terminal.json
  • Test: apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.test.tsx — a single click selects without calling listarDiretorio again; a double click navigates; a file appears in the list but isn't reachable by getByRole('button'); "Home folder"/"Root" shortcuts; and "Use this folder" uses the selected one when there is one, otherwise the open folder
  • ADR: none — a UI redesign over a component that already existed, with no protocol change nor data boundary change (ADR 0107 still describes the mechanism behind it)
  • Origin: product owner's request, after testing the creation of a real project and finding the folder browser not much like a real file explorer — a visual reference sent by him (three-column picker, GNOME Files/GTK style)

RN-437 — In runner mode, "Browse folder..." creates the project IN ADVANCE, and the final confirmation reuses it by identity SNAPSHOT​

ADR 0107 had already declared this gap in its own Consequences section: with no project yet, the channel's ticket (RN-429) has nothing to anchor to, and "Browse folder..." always fell into the "available after the project exists" state — even in runner mode, where creation does NOT depend on validating disk (ADR 0104, item 2). Closed by ADR 0108: NewProjectWizard.tsx (handleProcurarPasta) calls createProject when clicking "Browse folder..." when modoDeWorkspace === 'runner' — using the already typed path, or a lexically valid and clearly provisional placeholder (/workspace-a-confirmar) when the field is still empty, never blocking the click. mounted mode doesn't change: it keeps projectId={null} until confirmation, because there disk validation runs on creation and creating early with an empty path would return RN-422's refusal at a moment when the user hasn't even thought about a path yet.

An identity SNAPSHOT ({ name, externalId, adotando } — never caminhoLocal, whose refinement is the PURPOSE of browsing) decides when to reuse: clicking "Browse folder..." again with the identity intact reopens the modal with the SAME project, without creating another; changing the name (or going back and swapping the repository to adopt) invalidates the snapshot, and the next browse creates a new project. handleConfirm applies the same ruler — it reuses the project already created when browsing when the snapshot still matches, and only calls createProject when there's nothing to reuse. montarPayloadDeCriacao, a pure function extracted from what used to live only inside handleConfirm, is reused by both paths.

The button's prerequisite is stated BEFORE the click (AT-214): in this mode the list comes from the local agent, so without a brabo-runner running and connected to the newly created project the modal can only show the wait and the onboarding. The screen now says so in TEXT below the field (aviso-procurar-runner, ADR 0064 — never a tooltip), with the command brabo-runner --project <id> --dir <pasta> and the alternative that depends on nothing: typing the path in the field, which the runner confirms on connecting. The mechanism (the early creation, the transport through the local agent) didn't change.

  • Where: apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx (handleProcurarPasta, handleConfirm, montarPayloadDeCriacao, snapshotDeIdentidade/mesmaIdentidade)
  • Test: apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx, describe navegação de pasta antecipada no modo Runner — creates the project and opens the modal with the real id; uses the placeholder when the field is empty; clicking again without changing anything doesn't create another; changing the name invalidates the snapshot and creates a different project; handleConfirm reuses instead of duplicating. The preexisting test "'Procurar pasta...' mostra o estado declarado" (mounted mode) stays green, unchanged — it proves the scope didn't leak
  • ADR: 0108 — a structural change (WHEN a project comes to exist in the creation flow), with the accepted side effect of an orphan "not provisioned" project when the wizard is closed without finishing (the SAME state that any interrupted creation already produces today, not a new regression)
  • Origin: product owner's request, after testing the creation of a real project in Runner mode and not being able to browse folders before confirming — the gap ADR 0107 had already declared and postponed

RN-438 — fs-browser-channel.ts had the SAME duplicated-path bug that RN-433 had already fixed in its sibling terminal-channel.ts​

Found while verifying RN-437 end to end in Chrome, against the real engine: the modal opened with the right projectId, but the connection dropped immediately with "The connection to the runner dropped — close and reopen to try again." instead of showing RunnerOnboardingPanel. apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts concatenated '/runner/websocket' to an engineWsUrl the api already returns READY (ws://host:porta/runner, from engineWsUrlPublico()) — the same phoenix.js Socket also appends /websocket on its own in the constructor, and the result hit the engine as GET /runner/runner/websocket/websocket, which Phoenix.Router.NoRouteError refuses. It's EXACTLY item 3 of RN-433, only in the SIBLING module — the fix there had never been replicated here, and no suite caught it because this module had no test at all until now (its own docblock said, incorrectly, that terminal-channel.test.ts covered it "indirectly"). Fix: the same line as RN-433 — engineWsUrl.replace(/^http/, 'ws'), without concatenating any path.

Verified END TO END against a real runner project (owner logged in, teste-navegacao, created by RN-437): before the fix, the modal fell straight into the connection error; after, it shows RunnerOnboardingPanel with the command brabo-runner --project <id-real> --dir <pasta> in under 2s — the expected result without a real runner connected.

  • Test: apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.test.ts (new — the module had no test of its own at all until this fix). The happy path confirms socket.url === engineWsUrl without concatenation; plus diretorioInicial/listarDiretorio roundtrip, failure fetching the ticket, and idempotent fechar()
  • ADR: none — it restores the behavior that ADR 0103/0107 and RN-433 already declared as intent, only in a module the previous fix didn't reach

RN-439 — POST .../runner-ticket authenticates AND authorizes in the SAME guard; RolesGuard (global) abstains on an @RequirePatAuth() route​

POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket answered 403 "Não autenticado" for EVERY PAT, even a valid one, freshly issued, scoped to the right project — found in a LIVE verification of brabo-runner connecting to a real project, never by an automated test. Root cause: JwtAuthGuard and RolesGuard are the two APP_GUARDs — GLOBAL — and a global guard ALWAYS runs BEFORE a route's LOCAL guard (@UseGuards), regardless of the order of the decorators in the controller. JwtAuthGuard already knew how to abstain on this route (the IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY bypass already existed, without populating request.user, counting on PatAuthGuard to authenticate afterwards); RolesGuard didn't, and refused every call with request.user still empty — PatAuthGuard never got to run. The controller's comment described the order backwards ("RolesGuard runs AFTER PatAuthGuard"), and it never was so.

The fix followed the SAME pattern JwtAuthGuard already used for this problem: RolesGuard gained the twin bypass (IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY → returns true without checking request.user), delegating the entire authorization to whoever becomes the ONLY guard running after request.user is populated on this route — PatAuthGuard itself, which now also reads @RequireRole (via Reflector) and resolves the effective role (ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject), refusing with the SAME message RolesGuard would use ("Papel insuficiente para esta ação"). The logic is duplicated between the two guards ON PURPOSE — RolesGuard lives in iam, PatAuthGuard lives in auth, and a cross dependency just to reuse ~10 lines wouldn't be worth it.

A SECOND defect was hidden behind the first, and only showed up when the integration test started exercising the two guards TOGETHER: PatAuthGuard compared the RAW token directly against personal_access_tokens.token_hash in validarEUsar — which always expects the HASH (hashDeToken, HMAC-SHA256+ pepper, the same one TokenFactory/IssuePersonalAccessTokenUseCase use to write). Fixed to this.tokens.validarEUsar(hashDeToken(token)). While RolesGuard refused everything before, this second bug never got to manifest — fixing only the first would have swapped an always-403 for an always-401, and the runner would still never really connect.

  • Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/roles.guard.ts (the IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY bypass); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts (authorization by role + token hash); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-http.module.ts (IamUseCasesModule imported, for the ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase that PatAuthGuard now needs); comment fixed in apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-tickets.controller.ts
  • Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/pat-auth.guard.spec.ts (authorization by role in isolation + token hash); apps/api/test/interfaces/roles.guard.spec.ts (IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY bypass); apps/api/test/interfaces/http/runner/runner-tickets.guards.integration.spec.ts (NEW — brings up JwtAuthGuard+RolesGuard+PatAuthGuard in a real Nest, with supertest, in the SAME relative order as AppModule: it's the test that was missing, because each guard was only exercised in isolation before this). Also verified LIVE: brabo-runner really connected to a real runner project with a PAT issued after the fix
  • ADR: 0105 — a bug fix in the implementation of the decision already made there (PAT authenticates this route), not a new decision
  • Origin: found running brabo-runner for real against a real project and isolating with curl directly — never by an automated test, because no suite exercised RolesGuard and PatAuthGuard in the same request

RN-443 — Area budget is ADDITIVE to the project/session ones, never a cascade; only maintainer changes the ceiling​

Closes the "budget per area" item of ADR 0038's cut, open since PHASE 8. agent_areas gains budget_micros (nullable — null is NO CEILING, the default) and spent_micros (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0), mirroring exactly max_parallel: same row, same decision owner, same AgentAreaRepository. It's not the model binding cascade of ADR 0064 (session > agent > area > project > workspace, "the most specific wins") — the two mechanisms use the word "area" and have nothing else in common. The area budget is a THIRD independent ceiling alongside the project and session ones that already existed: CheckBudgetGateUseCase.execute now resolves the agentId's area (via areaDo, a pure function, without touching the database unless it finds a match) and checks all three in parallel — any one blocked already refuses the call, with no hierarchy among them.

RecordLlmUsageUseCase increments the actor's area spent_micros WHENEVER it belongs to one (lead or member — areaDo returns an area for both), with or without a configured budget_micros: the area's real spend becomes visible even before anyone configures a ceiling. An actor without an area (user in the chat, agent outside any area) records nothing — it isn't a silent omission, it's the correct behavior when there's nothing to increment.

SetAreaBudgetUseCase requires maintainer (same ruler as SetAreaMaxParallelUseCase — changing how much the product can spend without asking), converts dollar→micro-USD in the controller (same convention as BudgetsController) and emits no domain event (project config, with no session to record into — the same reasoning already recorded in SetAreaMaxParallelUseCase). null CLEARS the ceiling — a required field that accepts null as a valid value (ValidateIf, not IsOptional), the same pattern as RenameSessionDto.

  • Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/agents.ts (agentAreas, columns budgetMicros/spentMicros and the two CHECKs); apps/api/src/domain/llm/area-budget.ts (isAreaBudgetExceeded); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/check-budget-gate.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/record-llm-usage.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/set-area-budget.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-area.repository.ts (setBudget/incrementSpent); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/execution/execution.controller.ts (PUT agent-areas/:key/budget); apps/web/src/routes/settings/BudgetSection.tsx
  • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/check-budget-gate.use-case.spec.ts (describe budget de área — aditivo, não cascata: an exceeded area blocks with project/session OK and vice versa, no ceiling never blocks, an agent without an area isn't affected); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/record-llm-usage.use-case.spec.ts (describe gasto por área: increments for the member and the lead, does nothing harmful without an area, adds up with no ceiling configured); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/execution/set-area-budget.use-case.spec.ts (writes, clears with null, refuses negative/NaN/Infinity, zero is valid); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-area.repository.spec.ts (setBudget/incrementSpent, atomicity under concurrency)
  • ADR: 0110
  • Origin: backlog item approved by the product owner in an explicit planning session — docs/explanation/backlog.md, "Older backlog" table

RN-440 — addressableAgents() is the CLOSED catalog of the manual handoff, stricter than assertHandoffTargetAllowed​

Manual handoff to an agent of choice (backlog, ADR 0109): assertHandoffTargetAllowed (ADR 0038) only refuses an area SUBAGENT — an agent citing "abc" as a target would pass through it without error, because an AGENT only cites targets it already knows from its own instruction. That stops being true when whoever chooses is a HUMAN, in a <select> fed by a client that may diverge from the backend. addressableAgents() (apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts) is the CLOSED catalog — area leads (AGENT_AREAS.map(a => a.lead)) ∪ SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS (criativo, po, arquiteto, ux-designer, staff) — and RequestManualHandoffUseCase refuses with 400 any toAgent outside it, BEFORE calling CreateHandoffUseCase.

SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS is its OWN list, not derived from the apps/web/src/lib/agents.ts roster (which also lists gate agents and the Psicólogo/Anamnese, none addressable by handoff). The direction of the derivation is from the api to the web: since AT-046 the web's copy is no longer a MANUAL mirror and comes out of the SAME generator as the areas (pnpm --filter api gerar:areas, Phase 18), in apps/web/src/lib/agent-areas.generated.ts, which agents.ts only reexports. agent-areas.spec.ts fails when the disk diverges from what the generator produces, and the generated list comes out as const satisfies readonly AgentKey[] — a name the web's roster doesn't know breaks the web's build. The engine does NOT receive the list (there's no consumer there). Even with both copies locked, what decides what's accepted is still RequestManualHandoffUseCase.

RN-441 — POST .../sessions/:sessionId/handoffs requires developer; a manual handoff is born offered, with no new state​

The only path to write toAgent is still CreateHandoffUseCase (ADR 0038) — not a second mechanism. RequestManualHandoffUseCase resolves fromAgent on its own (the session's most RECENT agent.activated, via SessionEventRepository.listByTypeInSession — the same criterion as activeAgent in SessionPage.tsx, finding 9-fix; a session with no agent activated yet falls to the "usuario" sentinel, never a guessed name) and calls CreateHandoffUseCase.execute passing actor: {kind: 'user', id: userId} — CreateHandoffInput gained the optional field actor?: Actor for that, with default {kind:'agent', id: fromAgent} preserving the usual behavior for the internal caller (the engine). The handoff is born offered, the SAME way as an automatic one, and the already existing accept card (offeredHandoff/handleAcceptHandoff in SessionPage.tsx) picks it up on its own on the next useHandoffs poll — with NO change to the accept path. (It didn't pick it up, and nobody saw it until AT-253: the card matched the offer by ACTOR, and the manual one's actor is the person. Fixed in RN-631, which matches by handoffId.)

The route (POST projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/handoffs) requires the developer role, the same as handoffs/:handoffId/accept (RN-136: those who CONVERSE on this screen). ux-designer and staff entered AGENTES_DE_CHAT (SessionPage.tsx) in the same change — the two message/2 clauses already existed in agent_command_controller.ex (ADR 0087/0088), verified by reading BEFORE writing any web line, and neither of them had a human path to itself.

RN-447 — Converting the execution_mode of an EXISTING project refuses (409) while any of the project's dev agents is not idle​

ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase (PUT .../execution-mode, role maintainer) reads engine.dev_agent_states DIRECTLY (cross-schema, same physical database — the same path as RN-409) by project_id, across ALL of the project's sessions, not only the most recent one. Any status other than idle (working/blocked/idle_tripped/awaiting_gate/ awaiting_approval) refuses the conversion: Engine.Dev.DevAgentServer does NOT re-resolve the worktree on its own — workspace_root is captured ONCE, at the worktree's creation, and swapping the column underneath it would leave the agent writing in a scope that permissions.json and the terminal policy (ADR 0055) have already abandoned. The decision is to REFUSE and explain (same "refuse and teach" pattern as RN-088/RN-422) — never to drain or force the migration of a live agent.

idle_tripped counts as ACTIVE here, unlike RN-409 (which excludes it from onlineAgentCount): the two questions are different — "is someone watching this agent work now" (RN-409) versus "is there a scope pointer that would become stale" (here). An agent with the circuit breaker tripped still has workspace_root captured, waiting for human unblocking — it isn't "idle" for conversion purposes, even though it isn't "online" for counting purposes.

The same (mode, path) as today is a NO-OP: the dev agent check doesn't even run — resubmitting the form without changing anything shouldn't cost a sweep of active agents.

  • Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/ports/dev-agent-activity.port.ts; apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/dev-agent-activity.repository.ts
  • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.spec.ts (refuses with an active dev agent, writing nothing; a no-op doesn't check); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/dev-agent-activity.repository.spec.ts (idle doesn't count, everything else counts, isolation between projects)

  • Origin: a fix recorded in docs/explanation/backlog.md during the implementation of Wave 1 of the runner (ADR 0104), closed in this Wave 2

RN-448 — permissions.json is RELOCATED on conversion — the content never changes, only the path​

PermissionsFileStore.move(from, to) reads the file at the OLD location (projectScopeRoot(localAntiga)), writes the SAME content at the NEW location, and deletes the old one (best-effort — if it no longer exists, there's nothing to delete). The content (allow/deny/ask patterns) carries neither path nor mode inside it, so there's nothing to REWRITE, only to move. from === to (no effective root changed) is a no-op.

Confirmed by reading projectScopeRoot (project-workspaces-root.ts): for mounted/runner the root IS the workspacePath, treated as a path INSIDE THE API'S CONTAINER — in runner, that was already true BEFORE this delivery (with no bind-mount, the file lives in a folder that only coincides in STRING with the user's real folder, disconnected from it). The conversion doesn't change that existing property, it only relocates it consistently — with no special case for runner besides using move() like any other pair.

  • Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/permissions-file-store.port.ts (move); apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/fs-permissions-file-store.ts
  • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/fs-permissions-file-store.spec.ts (content survives and is deleted from the origin; an origin without a file writes empty without throwing; from === to is a no-op)
  • ADR: 0111

RN-449 — Leaving container, the container lifecycle is ended (removed) BEFORE the column changes​

ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase calls RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase (ADR 0081) to take the project_containers row to removed — via stopped first when it's running (container-lifecycle.ts has no direct running -> removed edge) — BEFORE writing the new execution_mode. The order is mandatory: RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase refuses (400) any transition in a project that isn't in execution_mode = 'container' AT THE MOMENT of the call, so calling it after swapping the column would always fail. With no container row (a project that never provisioned), no transition is triggered.

Entering container from mounted/runner does NOT auto-provision anything — the Arquiteto's image gate (RN-105) and the normal lifecycle apply from then on, as for any container project — never a shortcut that skips the gate because the project "already had code somewhere".

  • Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.ts (removerContainerSeExistir)
  • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.spec.ts (running goes through stopped; provisioning goes directly; with no row, no transition; entering container never triggers a transition)
  • ADR: 0111

RN-450 — workspaceVerifiedAt resets on EVERY real conversion, even going back to runner with the "same" path​

It only makes sense in execution_mode: 'runner' (RN-423): a timestamp proving that a CONNECTED runner confirmed the path on the real host. Any conversion that actually changes the (mode, path) pair — including one that lands in runner again with a seemingly equal path — resets the field, forcing a NEW confirmation: the old timestamp attests a verification that happened under a DIFFERENT pair, and carrying it forward would assert a confirmation that never happened for the new state. The no-op (RN-447) is the only exception — nothing changes, so nothing resets.

  • Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.ts
  • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.spec.ts (runner -> container resets; no-op preserves)
  • ADR: 0111

RN-451 — The standalone binary smoke runs the real SUBPROCESS, never a mock​

The same discipline pattern that smoke-dist.mjs (ADR 0106) already applies to the dist/index.cjs published to npm now also applies to dist-bin/brabo-runner-<platform>-<arch>[.exe] (ADR 0112): no suite proves that a PACKAGED artifact works by reading its source code — only by executing the real artifact, as a subprocess, and observing real output. scripts/smoke-bin.mjs runs the COMPILED binary (never node src/index.ts nor any non-compiled form) with --self-test-pty — an internal flag, not documented in uso() — which resolves node-pty exactly as production does and spawns a real PTY via GerenciadorDePty, writing to and reading from it. Only the line node-pty carregado com sucesso + SELF_TEST_PTY_OK: in the real process's stdout counts as proof; no mock of node-pty nor of child_process is acceptable for this specific test, because what it exists to prove is precisely that the embedded native .node (with { type: 'file' }, native-pty-embed.generated.ts) loads and works INSIDE the binary — mocking any piece of the path would erase the only thing the test needs to prove.

  • Where: apps/runner/scripts/smoke-bin.mjs; apps/runner/src/index.ts (rodarAutoTestePty, the implementation of --self-test-pty)
  • Test: smoke-bin.mjs itself — there's no unit test that replaces it, on purpose (it's the same design as smoke-dist.mjs, which also has no unit counterpart)
  • ADR: 0112
  • Origin: explicit requirement from the product owner for this backlog item ("no mocking")

RN-452 — node-pty resolved by injection, not static import — and the gap this opened in the npm smoke was closed in the same commit​

pty.ts stopped doing a static import * as nodePty from 'node-pty' at the top of the module — it now receives the already resolved module by injection in the constructor of GerenciadorDePty, resolved once in main() (src/index.ts) via native-pty-loader.ts#carregarNodePty(). The change exists for the standalone binary (ADR 0112): the compiled path needs to extract the embedded files to a real directory BEFORE resolving node-pty, which requires an asynchronous call — incompatible with a hoisted static import. Outside the compiled binary, the behavior is identical to before (await import('node-pty'), resolved from the node_modules of whoever installed the package).

The gap the change opened, closed in the SAME commit: ADR 0106 already recorded that the static import of node-pty, being hoisted before any argument parsing, made smoke-dist.mjs prove that the native binding loaded just by IMPORTING dist/index.cjs — even on the uso() path (zero arguments), which never reaches main(). Moving the resolution into main() silently broke that guarantee, because smoke-dist.mjs only exercised the uso() path. smoke-dist.mjs gained a third check — it runs the CLI with valid arguments (but without real api/engine on the other side) and waits for the line node-pty carregado com sucesso on stdout before killing the process — closing the gap the change itself opened, instead of leaving it as a silent loss of coverage.

  • Where: apps/runner/src/pty.ts (GerenciadorDePty, injection of NodePtyModule); apps/runner/src/native-pty-loader.ts (carregarNodePty); apps/runner/src/index.ts (main, resolves once); apps/runner/scripts/smoke-dist.mjs (third check, verificarNodePtyCarrega)
  • Test: apps/runner/scripts/smoke-dist.mjs (npm/tsup path) and apps/runner/scripts/smoke-bin.mjs (binary path, RN-451) — the only two places that exercise the really packaged artifact, no unit test replaces them
  • ADR: 0112
  • Origin: a technical need of the standalone binary; the gap in the npm smoke was found by an audit of the change itself, not by a real run reporting failure

RN-454 — The Insights tab knows the Psicólogo is paused BEFORE the user runs into the 503​

Found by USE: the Insights tab, with zero hypotheses, showed "No hypotheses yet — the Psicólogo analyzes each closed session" even with PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED=false — the same sentence that appears when the Psicólogo is ACTIVE and just hasn't run yet. The two situations are indistinguishable by the text, which is the same class of defect RN-088/RN-107 already closed for other screens: a state that exists and that the product knows, but doesn't show.

RN-117 already covered discovering the pause, but only on the CLICK of "Reanalyze" (503 → PsychologistDisabledError) — and that button only exists in the analyses strip, which only appears when runs.length > 0. A session with no hypothesis at all never gets near it, so the pause was invisible precisely on the empty screen.

GET /internal/psychologist/status (engine, PsychologistCommandController.status/2) is a pure read of PsychologistWorker.enabled?/0 — WITH NO side effect, unlike /reanalyze, which creates a job when enabled. The api exposes GET /projects/:projectId/psychologist/status (GetPsychologistStatusUseCase, role:viewer) on top of that — the project in the URL only for consistency with the sibling routes (hypotheses, psychologist/analyses); the flag itself is GLOBAL, as RN-117 already records. ProjectInsightsTab.tsx consumes that read (usePsychologistStatus) and chooses the empty state's sentence by it: paused shows "The Psicólogo is paused — no session is analyzed until it's reactivated" (insights.projectInsightsTab.emptyPaused); otherwise, it keeps the original sentence, which IS honest when the feature is indeed active. The persistent warning (pausedNotice) and the "Reanalyze" buttons also now reflect that proactive read, and not only the useState discovered by the 503 — which still exists, as reinforcement, for the rare case of the flag changing IN FLIGHT between the status read and the click.

Presentation rule (history): agruparNarracoesDoTurno, a new pure pass that runs AFTER afundarDesfechos (RN-172) in the same useMemo — within the same turno+autor, consecutive agent.responses become a compact Disclosure ("Turn steps · N"), leaving only the last one intact and outside it. turno === 0 (the sentinel prologue of turnoDoSeq) is left OUT of the grouping, on purpose — it isn't a real turn, and old fixtures stack agent.response without a turn boundary to test another mechanism (RN-138/RN-177). An agent-agnostic function (it only reads turno/autor), afundarDesfechos itself doesn't change.

RN-464 — The runner's device key: self-service registration/revocation; NO maintainer view in this round (declared cut)​

Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): the browser flow was RETIRED, and POST .../runner-device-keys left with it — together with RegisterRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase and its test, cited below as they were. runner_device_keys keeps only the PUBLIC Ed25519 key of a runner device — generated in the browser, never the private one. POST/DELETE .../runner-device-keys require the minimum role developer and are authenticated by the normal SESSION JWT (unlike runner-ticket: whoever calls here is the already logged-in browser registering its own device, not the runner running without a session). RegisterRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase validates only the minimal SHAPE of the JWK (kty:"OKP", crv:"Ed25519", x present) — the deep validation (whether it's really a valid Ed25519 point) is left to jose.importJWK at the moment of use, in RN-465. RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase is IDEMPOTENT and scoped to the calling userId — the same design as revogar() of RN-426 — and returns 404 both for a nonexistent key and for another user's key, the same discipline of not leaking existence.

Declared asymmetry with the PAT: unlike RN-427 (a maintainer revokes the PAT of ANY user of the project, incident response), the device key does NOT have an equivalent maintainer route today — only self-revocation. The docblock of RunnerDeviceKeysController declares this explicitly as a cut of this round, not forgetfulness: extending the same pattern of RN-427 to device keys is direct future work, if it comes to be requested.

RN-465 — POST .../runner-ticket accepts a PAT OR a device key (Ed25519, TTL ≤60s) — a second form of DEVICE credential, never dual-auth with the session JWT (RN-439's distinction)​

Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): nothing of this RN changed in the guard — PatAuthGuard still accepts the JWT of a PROJECT key, and that's why a runner configured through the browser before ADR 0203 doesn't break. What no longer exists is creating a NEW project key: the browser no longer generates the pair.

PatAuthGuard gained a second path, next to the unchanged PAT (brb_...): a bearer in compact JWT format (three segments) is treated as a device key. The guard reads the header's kid (without verifying the signature yet), fetches the corresponding ACTIVE public key in runner_device_keys, and only then verifies the EdDSA signature with jose.importJWK/jwtVerify. Short and MANDATORY TTL: exp - iat can't exceed 60s — checked against the token's SIGNED life, not against "now", closing the replay window of a leaked JWT from the moment it was signed. The userId/projectId used to authorize always come from the record saved in the database, never from a JWT claim — the token only needs to prove possession of the private key, never to state who the owner is. projectId is checked TWICE (the JWT's claim against the route, and the key's registered project against the route) — the same 401 vs 403 discipline the PAT path already uses: a token/key valid for the WRONG project is a different category from an invalid token/key. The runner signs that JWT in assinarTicketComChaveDeDispositivo (apps/runner/src/auth.ts), with the private JWK already LOADED in memory — never reading a file there, preserving the "no file I/O" guarantee of auth.ts (whoever reads the file is RN-466's separate module).

This does NOT reopen RN-439: RN-439 closed the guarantee that runner-ticket never accepts the LOGIN JWT as a credential — it still stands. The device key is a DIFFERENT JWT, self-signed by the runner itself with a key whose private part the api never saw, with no user sub at all — only a second way of proving "I am the device of such user in this project", as scoped as the PAT it complements. Accepting the session JWT here would make RolesGuard/@RequireRole authorize that user for everything their role allows in the rest of the api, blowing past the runner:project:<id> scope — exactly what RN-439 prevented.

"Needs you" panel (RN-467)​

RN-467 — The panel of the five decision queues NEVER sums and NEVER executes: it separates by queue and forwards to the decision​

The "Needs you" chip, at the top of the project, opens a panel with the project's FIVE decision queues — action approvals, PR merges, story promotions, architecture pending items, and Psicólogo hypotheses. Two guarantees define it, and neither of them is aesthetic:

It never sums. Each queue has its OWN header and count, and there's no project total anywhere: neither in the panel, nor in the chip that opens it — the chip announces PRESENCE (a dot, temAlgoEsperando, boolean by signature) and never quantity. It's the same product decision that already keeps the five rail counters separate (ADR 0126): summing erases WHICH queue is asking for attention, which is precisely the question of whoever opens the panel. montarFilas returns the five in the declared order of urgency (ORDEM_DAS_FILAS) and doesn't export a total function — the absence is the mechanism, not an oversight.

The only dedupe that exists is by IDENTITY, never between queues: the SAME git_merge proposed_action arrives through both hooks (usePendingActions is the session's and doesn't filter by type; useProjectPendingActions is project-wide) and would appear twice in the same list, under two titles. It stays in the most specific group (prs).

It never executes. The two actionable queues in the panel (aprovacoes, prs) render the SAME ApprovalCard as the Approvals tab (a single variant since AT-322, with the detail collapsed), and the buttons call the same decision endpoints — the panel is a SHORTCUT to the decision, never a substitute for it. That matters especially for git_merge: a merge into a protected branch is downgraded to require_approval UNCONDITIONALLY (apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts), a ceiling that neither agent_autonomy nor permissions.json lift, and nothing in the panel touches that path. onActivateAutoMode is OMITTED on both cards on purpose: turning on "auto mode" (RN-153) is changing the agent's POLICY, not deciding the action that's in front of you — whoever wants that decides in the Approvals tab, where the workspace role is already checked. The other three queues have no decision card outside their context and therefore LEAD to the tab where the decision lives.

The architecture pending item has no date of its own — none, in any field (ArchitecturePendency): it's a view DERIVED from crossing story and module_map, recomputed on every read and never recorded. The panel BORROWS the related story's date and SAYS it borrowed it ("story updated 18 min ago", dataEmprestada); without the story in the loaded backlog, it shows "no date" and sorts the item at the END of the queue. In no case an invented instant: rendering "now" would make the most urgent line of the screen the one least known about, with nothing exposing the lie. Adding a column and a migration in the api would solve it for real and is a separate decision, outside this one's scope.

  • Where: apps/web/src/lib/precisa-de-voce.ts:108 (ORDEM_DAS_FILAS), :117 (FILAS_ACIONAVEIS), :139 (montarFilas — the dedupe by identity and the date borrowing), :245 (temAlgoEsperando); apps/web/src/components/PainelPrecisaDeVoce.tsx:246-248 (role="dialog", aria-modal, label) and :279-284 (group per queue, with its count); apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPage.tsx:120 (builds the queues from the five hooks the rail counters already use)

Environment state on screen (RN-468)​

RN-468 — An environment signal says what it KNOWS: workspaceVerifiedAt is a record of confirmation, never a guarantee that the runner is alive​

The product shows environment state in two places, and the slice of each is the rule: the login screen shows only what's true WITHOUT identity, and the project Overview shows what's only true WITH it.

Pre-login, the slice is imposed by the data's scope, not by aesthetic choice. What remains are the two /health endpoints — public in both services on purpose (@Public() in the api; "Sem auth de propósito" in router.ex), the same ones StatusPage already consumes without a session. Runner presence is keyed by {user_id, project_id} (runner_device_keys) and the model list is projects/:projectId/models with role viewer: before login neither subject exists, so the screen declares the absence ("Runner and local models depend on your account and a project") instead of omitting it — omitting it would make the platform look like it doesn't have what it has. The two /health keep the THREE states separate (RN-088 applied to an environment signal): checking… is not no response, and neither of them is responding. The probe has a CEILING (6s): an api that accepts the connection and never answers would leave the line at "checking…" forever, which is honest for half a second and a lie by omission after ten.

And the form never waits for the probe. The state is local to the block, which is a SIBLING of the card — an api that's down changes a text and doesn't delay or hide a pixel of the login. That matters exactly at the moment the api goes down, which is when someone most needs the screen to at least OPEN.

Post-login, the rule is about what the data does NOT assert. The runner signal comes from projects.workspace_verified_at — the stamp ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase writes when a runner connects and confirms the folder (RN-423), and the SAME field the engine uses as a gate (TerminalExecutor refuses a command in a runner project with the field null). It is not a heartbeat, for two independent reasons: there's no process being observed, and reconnecting reporting the same path doesn't rewrite the stamp (an explicit decision of the use case), so that not even the date is "the last time the runner showed up". The screen says "folder confirmed on <date>" with the caveat of what that isn't, and never "up", "online", nor a green dot — the tone is neutro, and green there would read as a liveness guarantee the data doesn't support. What knows about NOW is the terminal's socket, in the Code tab (TerminalPanel/RunnerOnboardingPanel), and the caveat points there. The same discipline RN-467 used when borrowing the story's updatedAt.

The runner line only exists in a project in runner mode: in the other two the field is null by definition (the mode conversion resets it, RN-450) and a "never confirmed" line there would be an invented absence.

RN-469 — Saving a section is N calls, and the screen never asserts an outcome it didn't get​

In the Settings sections whose rows are a SCALAR setting per key (Parallelism per area and Spend ceiling per area, both per agent_areas), the save button is ONE, the section's, and not one per row. Saving triggers one call per dirty row — PUT .../areas/:key/max-parallel and .../budget are per-AREA endpoints, there's no transactional endpoint for "write these N ceilings", and this product didn't invent one. The consequence is that the outcome of a click can be partial, and the rule is about what the screen can say then.

The calls are in SERIES, in the screen's order, and one failure doesn't interrupt the following ones. In series because the failure report names rows and needs to come out in the order the person sees them. Without interrupting because whoever clicked asked for the N: aborting on the first refusal would leave rows with no attempt at all, and the screen wouldn't be able to distinguish "the api refused" from "it didn't even try".

The outcome is per ROW, and that's what the UI shows. Only the draft the api CONFIRMED is discarded; what failed stays in the field, with what the person typed, and the section stays marked as unsaved by exactly those rows — clicking Save again tries only them. The three outcomes are distinct and none disguises itself as another: all passed → success; none passed → the message the API gave, never a count; some passed → a warning saying how many out of how many and naming the ones left. "Saved" and "not saved" would both be a lie in the third case, and it's the one this RN exists to protect.

The section declares HOW MANY rows are pending before the click. One button per section says "Save" the same with one dirty row and with five; the count ("2 unsaved changes in this section") is the counterpart of having swapped N buttons for one. Dirty is a comparison by interpreted value, not by text: 20 and 20.0 are the same ceiling, and comparing strings would send a call the api treats as a no-op. An invalid draft counts as dirty and replaces the count with the message explaining the block — two numbers about the same set would be noise, and whoever has an invalid value needs what locks the button.

Where the rule does NOT apply, and why. A section whose control is a choice of a NAMED value (Story promotion, Models per agent, Model per area, role in Members) saves on onChange, with no button, and stays that way: the confirmation exists for a TYPED field, where saving on each key press would send 1 on the way to 12. What that sentence measures is whose value it is: it applies to the control that writes its OWN value, and doesn't reach a selector whose value is the ARGUMENT of an action over other rows — see RN-476, which is the exception and says why. And Credentials keeps a button per row despite also having drafts per key: the credential is write-only (ADR 0050) and never comes back from the server, so there's no value to compare against to decide "dirty"; the row's button alternates between "Save" and "Replace" depending on whether that provider already has a key; and it shares the card with "Test" and "Remove", which are irreducibly the row's.
