RN-476 — Applying a model to ALL agents: one value, N calls, and a button even though the value is named​

The Models per agent table has one row per agent and a selector in each one. Choosing the same model for the 17 meant going through the 17 rows, and the cost of that isn't time: it's that nobody checks 17 dropdowns and the screen has no way to say whether one was left behind. The section gains a bar ABOVE the table — a selector and a button — that applies ONE model to all agents at once.

The action writes at the AGENT level, on the 17 rows — not on the project. The two readings of "one model for all" exist and produce different states: writing on the project and deleting the agent and area bindings would make the 17 INHERIT, and that's the cascade's own idiom. It wasn't the one chosen, for two concrete prices: PUT projects/:id/model-binding and the area endpoints require maintainer, while the agent binding requires developer — the same person who can change row by row would no longer be able to do it all at once —, and the project binding is also the SESSION's default, which RN-040 leaves free on purpose. The choice has a declared price: the 17 rows now diverge, with origin agent in the Origin column, and going back to inheriting remains row by row.

There's a button, even though the value is NAMED. The ruler of RN-469 says a choice of a named value saves on onChange, and it still applies to EACH ROW's selector, which writes its own value. The bar's selector isn't configuration of anything: it's the argument of the action next to it. Applying on onChange would make an exploratory click on a dropdown rewrite 17 rows the person wasn't editing, and undoing that is 17 clicks. The button NAMES how many rows it will reach, because that number is the consequence.

The outcome follows RN-469 entirely, and that's the reason the bar invents nothing. One call per agent, in SERIES, in the screen's order, without aborting on the first refusal — aborting would leave 16 rows with no attempt and the screen wouldn't distinguish "refused" from "didn't even try". The three outcomes don't disguise themselves: all passed → success naming the model; none passed → the api's message, never a count; some passed → a warning with how many out of how many, naming the ones left by the agent's NAME, which is what the person reads in the first column. Only the rows the api CONFIRMED are reread: invalidating the 17 would erase from the screen the difference the partial report just counted.

The gate is the ENDPOINT's, and the endpoint is the same as the row controls'. developer, through PUT projects/:projectId/agent-bindings/:agentSlug — not the neighboring area section's maintainer (RN-102). The button is inert for whoever doesn't reach it, and the reason is said ONCE, in TEXT, in the section's caption, together with the other two actions that are inert: title on a disabled element doesn't open in Chromium (ADR 0064). The selector's "fit for agents" filter opens CHECKED, as in the row picker and for the same reason (RN-040) — with more force here, because a chat-only model chosen in the bar wouldn't produce one 422, but 17, and the partial report would count the same refusal seventeen times.

The Members section respects the role, and the role is the project's EFFECTIVE one (RN-471)​

RN-471 — Role in the Members section: maintainer, and derived from the project's row over the workspace's​

MembersSection checked no role at all. The section's THREE actions — invite, change someone's role, and remove — appeared active for everyone, viewer included, and the api refused with 403. Two of them didn't even get to say so: handleRoleChange and handleRemove had no try/catch and were called from an onChange/onClick, so every refusal became an unhandled promise rejection — silence on screen and noise in the console, the same class of defect that RN-102 closed in the models table. Removing a member silently is the worst of the three: it's a consequential action with no way back through the screen, because restoring requires the UUID the removed row took with it.

The minimum is maintainer, and it's the ENDPOINT's. The three paths require the same (projects.controller.ts), and GET requires viewer — that's why whoever doesn't edit still sees the whole table:

actionendpointrole
invitePOST :projectId/membersmaintainer
change rolePOST :projectId/members (upsert)maintainer
removeDELETE :projectId/members/:userIdmaintainer
see the tableGET :projectId/membersviewer

Copying the models section's gate (developer, and correct there) would offer the three controls here to those the api refuses. It's the SECOND section in a row whose minimum differs from its neighbor: the ruler is still the endpoint, never the screen next door.

The role is the PROJECT's EFFECTIVE one — and this CLOSES the gap RN-102 declared, it doesn't repeat it. There the screen reads the WORKSPACE role while what authorizes is ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject, and closing that would require a per-project role query the web doesn't have. It's the SAME gap here, seen from the other side: this section ALREADY makes that query. listProjectMembers is findMemberRole for everyone at once, and userIdDaSessao() (the access token's sub) says which row belongs to whoever is looking. The composition is literally the use case's — projectRole ?? workspaceRole —, not a second source of role invented only on this screen. While the list hasn't arrived the role is ABSENT, not the workspace's: without it there's no way to know whether an own row exists, and erring on the side of disabling is fixed by reloading.

The override applies in BOTH directions, and FOUR places said otherwise. forProject returns the project_members row when it exists, without comparing with the workspace. So setting viewer here really downgrades — even a workspace owner, who afterwards can only be restored by someone with maintainer. The code never did the opposite, and resolve-effective-role.use-case.spec.ts itself fixes this ("papel de projeto sobrepõe o de workspace"). Where the false promise was:

placewhat it saidstatus
description of POST :projectId/members"the EFFECTIVE role is the higher of this one and what the person already has in the workspace"; "associating someone as viewer here doesn't downgrade a workspace owner"not fixed — it's an api change
description of AddMemberDto.rolethe same "higher of" sentencenot fixed — it's an api change
summary of GET :projectId/members"with their effective role"; "includes whoever inherits access from the workspace"not fixed — it's an api change
apps/web/src/lib/roles.ts:3"Papel efetivo nunca é rebaixado"fixed here

The three in the api stay declared and aren't touched in passing: the descriptions propagate to api-types.generated.ts. The web one is WORSE than the other three and was therefore fixed along with it — the api ones at least live in an OpenAPI description, while that one was in the module that roleAtLeast and ROLE_ORDER export, that is, in the code the next person of this family of fixes will open and edit, reading the wrong rule before anything else. The linear hierarchy declared on the same line remains valid — it's the order roleAtLeast compares, and it didn't change. The screen, in turn, SAYS what holds, instead of letting the Select be read as a harmless suggestion.

The CONTROL disappears, never the INFORMATION (ADR 0064). Whoever doesn't have maintainer keeps reading each member's role in the dimmed Select itself — it's the table's central information, and swapping it for text would hide the state along with the action. The reason is said ONCE, in text, in the caption: title on a disabled element doesn't open in Chromium, and one line per member would repeat a fact about WHO IS LOOKING on top of each person on the list.

The table is a SLICE, and declares it (RN-180). listMembers is an innerJoin on project_members: whoever reaches the project only through the workspace doesn't appear in any row, although the GET summary promises "includes whoever inherits access from the workspace". That data is NOT within the client's reach — no web query lists workspace members with role —, so the caption says the list omits, instead of letting it be read as "everyone who has access". It's the remaining gap, and it's declared, not handled.

None of this is a security boundary: what refuses is still RolesGuard.

Invite keeps the fixed hint, and it's a decision. The other two actions use mensagemDaApi because their userId came from the list and exists — what remains is 403 and network, and the api's sentence is the most useful information there is. In the invite the userId is TYPED, and the reachable error is pointing to a nonexistent user: a well-formed UUID passes @IsUUID(), blows the FK project_members.user_id → users.id, none of the global filters handles it, and Nest answers the default 500. mensagemDaApi would return "Internal server error", worse than the hint — its padrao only applies to an error that isn't an ApiError. Uniformizing the form would worsen the content on the box's most likely path.

The two downgrade ceilings in project_members (RN-472)​

RN-472 — Nobody downgrades the workspace owner, and nobody downgrades themselves​

RN-471 recorded that ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject is projectRole ?? workspaceRole — the project row OVERRIDES the workspace one, in both directions. What it didn't keep is the consequence: AddProjectMemberUseCase was a one-line passthrough to the upsert, and neither of the two write paths looked at WHO the target is. Any maintainer could (a) downgrade the workspace owner to viewer in a project, taking the owner out of their own project, and (b) downgrade themselves with no way to undo it, because undoing is the same route, which requires maintainer.

The override STAYS in both directions. forProject doesn't change. Restricting someone in a sensitive project (workspace developer → viewer in project X) is a deliberate capability, and "the higher of the two" would eliminate it — the resolve-effective-role.use-case.spec.ts fixes the upward half since Phase 1. What comes in are TWO ceilings, and only them:

ceilingwhat it refusesstatus
1a role below owner for whoever is the WORKSPACE owner403
2a role below what the CALLER has today, when the target is themselves403

The owner is workspace_members.role, never workspaces.created_by. Both exist in db/schema/iam.ts and they're not the same thing: created_by is a historical fact, and it's the role that authorization uses in all the rest of the system (forWorkspace is workspaces.findMemberRole; created_by doesn't appear in any authorization path). Reading created_by would shield the creator who has already transferred ownership and leave uncovered the current owner who created nothing — the hole the ceiling exists to close.

Ceiling 2 is "themselves", with no threshold — not "below maintainer". The version with a threshold would copy a number from the controller's @RequireRole into the domain and would age silently if the route changed its minimum. The price, declared: the owner who wanted to set themselves as maintainer in their own project (a reversible move) is also refused, and now needs another maintainer. Raising one's own role isn't a downgrade and still passes.

The ceilings live in the USE CASE, with the rule in the domain — not in RolesGuard. The guard authorizes the CALLER against the route's @RequireRole and doesn't see the body (dto.role) nor the target (dto.userId); the two ceilings are about the TARGET and about the actor↔target relation. The SHAPE is that of domain/actions/decide.ts (RN-154/RN-418): a pure function, the message next to the condition, with no configuration key. What doesn't carry over is the outcome — there the ceiling becomes require_approval over an agent's proposed_action, here the call is already human and synchronous and there's no queue to send it to.

403, not 409 nor 400: it's an authorization refusal — the caller has the route's role and doesn't have authority for this move. Waiting changes nothing (it isn't a state conflict) and the body is valid (the same body with another target would pass).

What the ceilings do NOT cover, and remains possible: downgrading another maintainer who isn't a workspace owner; self-downgrade through REMOVAL — RemoveProjectMemberUseCase got no ceiling, and removing one's own row drops the effective role to the workspace role, which is benign when the workspace holds it and irreversible when it doesn't (maintainer only through the project row, viewer in the workspace); self-PROMOTION, which was already possible before; and downgrading the owner IN THE WORKSPACE (POST workspaces/:workspaceId/members still has no ceiling). The two removal cases are FIXED in tests, including the open one.

The screen is left for later, and the refusal shows up. MembersSection computes ceiling 2 on its own, but not ceiling 1: listProjectMembers returns the role of the PROJECT ROW, and the target's workspace role isn't within the client's reach. Half a gate would be a Select honest about one refusal and silent about the other — the second source of role RN-471 writes against. Meanwhile, handleRoleChange already shows mensagemDaApi(erro, …) in a toast (RN-471), and it's the api's sentence that says which ceiling was hit.

The folder comes first, and the binary isn't a blocker (RN-473/474)​

RN-473 — Runner configuration through the browser starts with the FOLDER, and the binary's failure never discards what has already been configured​

Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): the flow this RN orders was REMOVED — runner-bootstrap.ts and its test were removed with the browser flow. What survives of it is the ruler of the human step stated BEFORE, which the panel applies to the installer's command.

The flow of RN-464..466 ran in the order key → registration → binary → folder (configurarPastaAutomaticamente, apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts). The four steps don't carry the same risk: the binary download is the ONLY one that depends on a release published on GitHub (RunnerReleasesController, a proxy of releases/latest), and with the current release having no asset for any platform it returns 502. The exception went up before showDirectoryPicker, so the folder picker never got to open — the button looked inert and the folder was unreachable, with the whole configuration lost because of the most fragile step.

The order becomes folder → config → key → registration → private key → binary, and the last step is best-effort:

stepdoes failure take down the flow?why
1. showDirectoryPickeryeswithout a folder there's nowhere to write anything. Cancelling (AbortError/NotAllowedError) is NOT a failure — it goes back to the initial state, with no alert
2. brabo-runner.config.jsonyesit's half of the pair RN-466 reads
3. Ed25519 pair + registerRunnerDeviceKey + …device-key.jwk.jsonyesa private key on disk with no counterpart on the server doesn't authenticate; that's why registration comes BEFORE writing, and the two are adjacent
4. binarynoreturns falhaDoBinario filled in; the final instruction becomes npm install -g @brabo/runner && brabo-runner

The alternative path works with no flag at all precisely because steps 2 and 3 have already run: the CLI reads both files from the cwd (RN-466). It's one of the THREE distribution paths the CLAUDE.md declares, and the only one that depends on neither the release nor a monorepo checkout. baixarKitManual (outside Chromium) follows the same ruler by inverting the order of the two downloads: the kit comes out first, the binary last.

The terminal step is human, and the screen never pretends otherwise. A web page doesn't execute a binary on anyone's machine, and the File System Access API doesn't preserve the execute bit — hence the chmod +x remaining in the command. What the product does is shrink that step to ONE line copyable with one click; no UI text says "automatic installation".

And it's announced BEFORE the click, not only after. The sentence explaining the step existed from the start, but was rendered only in the SUCCESS state — after the person chose the folder, waited for the key registration and the binary download. Whoever clicks a button called "Configure folder automatically" and only then finds out they still need to open a terminal was surprised, even without any sentence having lied: announcing at the end is the latest possible moment to still not be pretense. Now there's a warning in the initial state, next to the button, and the one at the end STAYS — the two say different things (one warns that the step will come, the other explains why it exists). The button's label did not change: it speaks of the FOLDER, which is indeed configured automatically, and changing it would describe worse what it does.

The final command says which folder to run in, when it can assert which one it is. The instruction said "inside the chosen folder, run: …" without ever saying where that folder is — the File System Access API exposes only the basename (dirHandle.name), never the absolute path. The path exists on the other side: it's the projects.workspace_path the person typed when creating the project. When its basename matches the chosen folder, the instruction gets a cd <caminho> && prefix; when it does NOT match, it comes out without a prefix — nothing forces the person to choose in the picker the same folder they typed, and a cd to the wrong place would be the screen asserting what it doesn't know. The basename is the most that can be proven from here, and the rare case where it coincides for different folders fails LOUD (cd doesn't find the path, or ./brabo-runner isn't there), never silently — which is the ruler that decides whether a heuristic may come in. The manual kit (fallback outside Chromium) does not get the prefix, and it isn't forgetfulness: there the files land in the downloads folder, and cd would send you where they aren't yet.

Declared gap: closing the tab between step 3 and the end leaves an orphan device key in the project. It's inert — the corresponding private key only existed in that tab's memory, and without it the key authenticates nothing — but today it's invisible: RunnerDeviceKeysController has POST and DELETE, and no LISTING route, so there's no screen where to revoke it. Redoing the flow registers a new key, which works. A listing is direct work on the DELETE that already exists, when requested.

RN-474 — After the instruction, the screen WAITS for the runner: three states, a ceiling, and the path that holds is the one the runner reported​

Configuring the folder and showing the command left the person not knowing whether it had worked. The fourth step is a wait that resolves on its own (apps/web/src/components/EsperaDoRunner.tsx), mounted by RunnerOnboardingPanel as soon as the configuration ends — on both paths (folder written and kit downloaded).

The mechanism is what already existed. The signal is project.workspaceVerifiedAt, the stamp ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase writes when the runner connects (RN-423) and which the engine uses as a GATE (terminal_executor.ex refuses to execute in a runner project with null workspace_verified_at) — the product's own definition of "this project has a runner". It's the same data that AmbienteDoProjeto already reads (RN-468), under the same cache key ['project', id] the whole page maintains. The alternative considered was probing connectFsBrowserChannel (whose error 'Nenhum runner conectado' FolderBrowserModal detects): it knows about NOW, which is stronger, but the channel writes erroDeConexao permanently per instance, so each probe would cost a NEW ticket + socket — dozens over the wait — and it still wouldn't answer the second half of what the screen must say: WHICH path the runner reported.

Confirmed is the stamp CHANGING, never "existing". The wait takes a baseline on the first GET and compares against it. Without that, a project already confirmed before would be announced as freshly connected the instant the screen opened.

The three states don't collapse, and none is eternal (RN-088, RN-468):

The kid is the link, and the refusal has a name (RN-475)​

RN-475 — The private JWK written by the browser carries the registration's kid; and the CLI distinguishes "there's no key" from "there's a key and it doesn't work"​

Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): the BROWSER half left with the flow (and the e2e that proved it in a Chromium); the stamped kid still applies to the key created in the terminal (device-key finish --id, RN-551), and the CLI half — absent × refused — remains intact.

The automatic mode of ADR 0118 (RN-464..466) never authenticated a single time since it was born. The two halves of this RN are the defect and what hid it.

The kid isn't decoration — it's the only link between the two sides. The id that POST projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys returns identifies the runner_device_keys record that keeps the PUBLIC key. It needs to reach disk INSIDE the private JWK, in the kid field (RFC 7517), because that's how the whole chain carries it: lerChaveDeDispositivo only PASSES ON jwk.kid (it never invents nor derives an id), assinarTicketComChaveDeDispositivo puts it in the protected header of the ticket JWT, and PatAuthGuard uses exactly that kid to find the public key and verify the signature (RN-465).

The browser discarded the return of registerRunnerDeviceKey on BOTH paths (configurarPastaAutomaticamente and baixarKitManual), and crypto.subtle.exportKey exports the RAW JWK, with no kid at all. The producer wrote a file the consumer always refuses — and the defect was invisible from both sides: each function was correct on its own. The proof is in the database: the keys registered by the flow had null last_used_at, all of them.

The fix is structural, not one line: step 3 of RN-473 (export the public key, register, export the private key) becomes ONE function (registrarChaveEExportarPrivada), with the id flowing inside it. Discarding it again now requires deleting code, not forgetting an assignment. The kid goes only in the PRIVATE key: the public one doesn't carry it, because it's its registration that produces it.

The refusal has a name. lerChaveDeDispositivo returns null without throwing — on purpose, and that doesn't change: the absence of the files is the NORMAL path of whoever runs with --project/--dir/--token. But null answered two different questions, and the CLI printed the SAME uso() block — which talks about flags and doesn't mention the file — both for "you configured nothing" and for "your folder is configured and the key doesn't work". A person with a perfect brabo-runner.config.json was sent to investigate precisely the side that was right.

statewho answersCLI output
ausentenormal paththe uso() block, unchanged
json-invalidorefusalexplicacaoDaChaveRecusada — names the file, the reason, and the two ways out (rewrite the folder through the browser, or --token meanwhile)
sem-kidrefusallikewise, naming the missing field and what it's for
validafollows the flow—

estadoDaChaveDeDispositivo and explicacaoDaChaveRecusada live in device-key.ts because they talk about the FILE; what to DO with the refusal (exit, with which code, with or without the usage block) remains index.ts's, as the module's docblock already said. The type of explicacaoDaChaveRecusada excludes ausente and valida: there's no explanation for the normal case nor for success, and a vague text covering the four states would be the same defect again.

What let it through: the web test asserted that the file had been OPENED (getFileHandle called with the right name), never what was INSIDE it. A test that proves the creation of a file without proving its content lets anything be written. The double now ties name → content, and the two old assertions gained the missing half.

RN-477 — Provisioning that fails SAYS it failed, and the wait for it has a ceiling​

Repository provisioning runs entirely inside the POST — there's no worker nor queue behind it (the OpenAPI description that promised "continues in the background" was wrong and was fixed). A failure, therefore, has already happened when the response arrives. This RN is about the screen never asserting "provisioning" about work that has already ended badly.

Every failure becomes a DURABLE state, and there were two paths that didn't. The first is step.check(), which was outside every try/catch in the BootstrapRunner and does network IO: a 401 from an expired token, a 403, or a timeout went up without touching the row, which stayed pending with lastError: NULL. The second is the refusal in createRepo, which happens before the row exists — repo_bootstraps is only born after the provider confirms the repository, so the project was left with ZERO rows. Now the first writes status: 'failed' + lastError in a single place (the step's catch) and emits bootstrap.step_failed; and the second is read by the status endpoint from the failed git_repo_create proposed_action.

The creation failure does NOT invent a step. failedStep stays null: the repository never came to exist, so none of the six Gitflow steps was attempted, and naming one to fill in the sentence would be swapping a silence for wrong information. The screen has its own title for that case, without {{step}}.

The screen shows the reason and offers a way out. The empty-bodied .catch(() => {}) of ProvisioningPage — whose comment asserted that "the failure appears via bootstrapQuery", which was false on both paths above — now keeps the api's message and displays it. The "Try again" button no longer depends on status === 'provision_failed': it also appears when the POST refused, which is precisely when there's no failure status to depend on.

The wait has a CEILING and three states that don't collapse, exactly like RN-474 and for the same reason: the 1s poll was infinite. After 3 minutes without converging, the screen says it stopped following, declares that this doesn't prove failure (provisioning runs inside the request, and a slow provider may still be working) and offers "look again" — which rearms the wait without triggering a second POST, because a second POST would create one more bootstrap session.

The dashboard card knows. The read model queries the failed git_repo_create actions together with the bootstrap rows, so a project that failed before a cursor existed no longer appears without any badge — and the click once again leads to the provisioning screen, which only redirected on provision_failed.

  • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/git/provision-repository.use-case.spec.ts (a failure in CHECK becomes failed with reason and event; a failure to CREATE leaves no row but the status reports it, with null failedStep), apps/api/test/domain/git/repo-bootstrap-status.spec.ts (no row with a creation failure; with a row the old failure is ignored; pure pending), apps/web/src/routes/ProvisioningPage.test.tsx (the reason appears; the retry exists without provision_failed; the wait stops and says what it doesn't know; a title without a step doesn't invent one)

RN-478 — permissions.json lives where the api REACHES, the terminal scope points to the HOST​

The project root had one derivation (projectScopeRoot) and two consumers with opposite needs. That was right while the two modes with a user folder were bind-mount; it stopped being so when runner mode was born (RN-423, ADR 0104), because it's deliberately without bind-mount.

consumerneedswhy
terminal scope (ADR 0055)the host's paththat's where the command runs — on the user's machine, through the runner
permissions.json (the api reads and writes)a path the api reachesit writes it from inside its container

They're two derivations, and both live in the same file — the source remains single, what split was the question. projectScopeRoot stays unchanged; permissionsFilePath is new and diverges from it at a single point: in runner mode the file goes to <PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT>/<workspace_dir_name>/permissions.json, the managed root, keyed by the name RN-109 freezes at creation. container and mounted don't change — in mounted the folder is a bind-mount, and moving the file would break projects that already have it on disk with no gain.

Why the managed root and not the user's disk, given the code is there: permissions.json is policy, not project code. Who reads it is the api; the runner never reads it (it receives an already approved command) and the engine doesn't touch it at any point — all mentions of it in apps/engine/lib are comments. Keeping it on the user's machine would make it editable by whoever it restricts, and unreadable precisely when the runner is disconnected, which is when the decision needs to remain valid.

What this fixed. Execution activation is the first write of the file, and it did mkdir -p of a host path inside the api's container: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/home/<usuario>' → 500. The read degraded silently (ENOENT → EMPTY_PERMISSIONS_FILE), and that's why the bigger effect slipped through unseen: in a runner project the permissions.json never existed, and decide() always fell to require_approval because of a file that wasn't there.

Declared cost: for a runner project, the policy file no longer lives next to the code — whoever looks for it in the project folder won't find it.

A typed refusal, and 400 instead of 500. The derivation's two throw new Error(...) become LocalizacaoDeProjetoInvalidaError, in the mold of CaminhoLocalInvalidoError: a readable motivo in pt-BR, and ActivateExecutionUseCase maps it to 400. An incoherent project row (the (mode, path) pair only becomes invalid by being written outside creation) now says what to fix instead of becoming a body-less 500. The Overview screen now shows that message — it printed the constant "Could not activate execution" while the twin button in the session chat already used mensagemDaApi: same button, two diagnoses.

The gap that REMAINS, declared: the engine has the same defect and it wasn't fixed here. Engine.Actions.Workspace.ensure!/4 does File.mkdir_p!(workspace_dir(project_id)), which in a runner project is the host's path — the dev agent's working tree has nowhere to be born. It doesn't become a 500 (the rescue of ensure_remoto/2 returns {:error, …}), it becomes a dev agent that doesn't work. Fixing it in isolation would be materializing a worktree on the host through a path that container execution replaces; what changes now is only the message, which names the cause instead of passing on a raw "permission denied".

  • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts (permissionsFilePath in the three modes; and the non-regression of projectScopeRoot still returning the host's path in runner/mounted — unifying the two back would break ADR 0055), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/execution/activate-execution.use-case.spec.ts (with the REAL FsPermissionsFileStore: the file lands in the managed root and the host folder stays untouched; an incoherent row becomes a 400 that teaches), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectOverviewTab.test.tsx (the api's message on screen), apps/engine/test/engine/actions/workspace_runner_test.exs (the failure names the cause in a runner project, and passes intact in the other modes)

RN-485 — The container broker doesn't accept a specification: it receives a project and COMPOSES​

The broker (apps/broker) is the only process of the product with access to a Docker daemon on the server. The rule that makes it non-arbitrary isn't an allowlist: it's the shape of the input.

It receives projectId and one of the five operations — nothing else. The five are those of the DockerPort of ADR 0128 (start, stop, remove, inspect, exec), and a sixth is a product decision with an ADR, never one more parameter. start, stop, and remove have an EMPTY body; exec takes a command and cwd, and nothing else.

The specification is read from the api and COMPOSED here. The broker calls GET /internal/projects/:projectId/container-spec, which returns the project's identity, execution mode, and the Arquiteto's current image decision. Image, network, resources, and the single mount come from there. There's no field where one writes privileged, cap_add, network: host, or a free -v — because there's no field. If the specification traveled in the body, the containment of a root-equivalent process on the host would depend on the CALLER being correct, and containment that depends on the caller isn't containment.

It revalidates what the api returned, and the two validations aren't the same. validarDecisaoDeImagem (api) asks "is this architecture decision reviewable?" — it requires rationale, refuses latest, applies RECURSOS_MAXIMOS, and returns the refusal to the MODEL through the tool-result (RN-061). especificacaoValidada (broker) asks "can I hand this to the daemon?" — it's the PARSE of an untrusted JSON into the closed type. The ceilings here are the BROKER's, the last resort it never exceeds wherever the request comes from; today the numbers coincide with the api's on purpose, and if one day they diverge the smaller wins without anything breaking, because neither of the two claims to be the other. One check exists only on this side: an image reference starting with - would be read by the CLI as a FLAG, and execFile without a shell solves COMMAND injection, not ARGUMENT injection.

The api sends no PATH at all. The -v of a docker run is resolved by the DAEMON, against the HOST's filesystem — a path from inside the api's container would make the daemon create and mount an EMPTY folder, with the dev agent working in a directory with no code and nothing indicating why. The broker composes the path with PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT, ITS configuration, plus the workspaceDirName frozen at creation (RN-109). Without that variable, start REFUSES naming it; the other four operations keep working. Refusing is the rule: guessing would produce the empty mount silently.

A mounted/runner project is refused with 409, because their folder lives on the user's machine and the broker's host doesn't see it — there, whoever brings up the container is the runner. It's the same policy RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase already applies in the api, stated where the broker can state it.

Nothing triggers a startup. There's no loop, no queue, no container_start proposed_action: the broker acts when called, and the only caller that exists today does a READ. External effect still requires approval.

  • Where: apps/broker/src/operacoes.ts (the five, and the composition in especificacaoDoProjeto), apps/broker/src/servidor.ts (the closed list of routes and the status table), packages/docker-port/src/spec-de-container.ts (the parse and the ceilings), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/obter-spec-de-container.use-case.ts (what the api returns, and the path it doesn't return), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-containers.controller.ts
  • Test: apps/broker/src/servidor.spec.ts (image, network, resources, and mount sent in the body are IGNORED; an artifact with an image starting with - is 422 and nothing is touched; a sixth operation is 404; a cwd outside /work is refused, including /workspace; without PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT the start refuses saying which variable is missing), packages/docker-port/src/spec-de-container.spec.ts (the parse field by field), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/spec-e-observacao-de-container.use-case.spec.ts (the api returns no path at all, nor rationale), apps/api/test/infrastructure/http-clients/container-broker.client.spec.ts (start sends an empty body)
  • ADR: 0130

RN-486 — REGISTERED state and OBSERVED state never merge, and "didn't look" has its own reason​

project_containers keeps what was REGISTERED. The daemon answers what is OBSERVED. Before the broker the table had no way to lie (container_id was always NULL); now it has, and the read says so instead of hiding it.

The lifecycle route returns both, separately. A container killed from outside appears as registered running and observed exited, and that's how it has to appear. The reconciliation is ON READ, not a background daemon.

observado: null alone isn't an answer. It means two different things, and naoObservado is what separates them: null there means the observation HAPPENED and came back empty — the positive statement "I looked and there's no container" —, while broker-nao-configurado, broker-sem-resposta, and broker-recusou mean it wasn't possible to look, each with a different fix. Inheriting the registered state in those three cases is exactly what RN-468 forbids: an environment signal says what it KNOWS, and a proxy doesn't become a guarantee.

No broker refusal takes down the read. The registered lifecycle is legitimate information on its own and existed before the broker; losing it because the broker is down would trade data we have for data we don't.

Declared gap: an orphan container of a project that never had a lifecycle row doesn't appear on that route — it reads the registered first. What finds orphans is the sweep by brabo.managed=true, and the page that consumes it doesn't exist yet.

RN-479 — Every hybrid search writes a row in rag_searches, with FROZEN weights; and telemetry never takes down the search​

apps/api/src/domain/rag/rag-search-limits.ts declares, in its own comment, that none of the four hybrid search numbers (the two weights, the threshold, and the number of candidates) comes from calibration with real data. It didn't because there was no way to: the search left no trace at all — neither a table row nor an event. Calibrating without measuring would be trading one guess for another.

HybridSearchUseCase now writes, on each search, what it returned (hits, with the 1-based rank of each excerpt), under which conditions (degraded/vector_available), how long it took (latency_ms), who searched (actor_kind/actor_id), and in which session — or in NONE.

Why a TABLE and not just a session event. session_events.session_id is NOT NULL, and a search coming from the RAG tab is a PROJECT one: it has no session. Recording it only as an event would lose exactly the searches in which a human looked at the scores and judged, which are the ones carrying the real signal. It's the same class of problem that forced the embedding metering cut (ADR 0075, token_usage.session_id NOT NULL), and the way out is the same: an own table, with NULLABLE session_id.

pesos frozen in the row is the point. pesosVigentes() copies the values of the moment into the record — the same discipline as the frozen price in metering (ADR 0042) and the image_version in project_containers. Without the copy, the first calibration that touched RAG_SEARCH_WEIGHT_VECTOR would make all the previous measurement start meaning something else, silently — and "did it improve after the change?", the only question telemetry exists to answer, would become impossible to ask.

Recording telemetry NEVER takes down the search, and also doesn't fail SILENTLY. Whoever asks shouldn't lose the answer because the measuring instrument went down; and the repository is explicit about failure that becomes silence (RN-059). So a failing INSERT becomes a log with the origin classified (infra, RN-023) and searchId: null in the response — which isn't the same as "there was no result": it's "there's nothing to attach a vote to", and the screen needs both separate so as not to offer a control the api would refuse (RN-088).

degraded and vector_available are two columns on purpose, and today's redundancy (degraded = !vector_available) is declared in the schema instead of hidden: vector_available is a fact about the PROVIDER — it's what makes medir:rag fail —, and degraded is the word of the CONTRACT with the engine, whose definition may grow.

  • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/hybrid-search.use-case.spec.ts (the row written with rank and weights; the weights being a COPY and not the same object; the tab's search without a session; and the FAILURE CASE — an insert that fails doesn't take down the search and returns searchId: null)

RN-480 — The vote on an excerpt is the only TRUTH signal of the measurement, and it requires the reference the search returned​

Latency and degradation rate say whether the search RAN; only the vote says whether it GOT IT RIGHT. rag_feedback keeps that vote — two values (util/irrelevante) and not a 1-to-5 scale, because a fine scale invites differences of ruler between voters that no aggregation recovers later.

The reference is mandatory, and the two refusals are 400s that TEACH. A searchId that doesn't exist in that project, and a chunkId that wasn't among the hits of that search, are refused before any write. It isn't decorative rigor: the rank of the voted excerpt is what separates two diagnoses that precision@1 confuses — a poor index doesn't return the right excerpt in any position, a wrong weight returns the right excerpt at rank 7. A vote without rank produces a meaningless number, which is worse than no number.

The refusal applies on both paths: through the tab it becomes a 400 on screen; through the agent it becomes an error tool-result the model can fix in the next iteration (RN-061/RN-163), never a crash.

One vote per actor per excerpt per search (unique (search_id, chunk_id, actor_id), with onConflictDoUpdate): changing one's mind overwrites one's own vote. Without the lock, whoever clicked twice would weigh double in precision@k and the metric would start measuring enthusiasm.

The role is viewer, the SAME as search — whoever can read the result is whoever can judge it (RN-102: the minimum is the endpoint's, and voting neither spends nor configures anything). The agent's tool is :direct, never proposed_action: grading an excerpt isn't an external effect, and turning it into an action to approve would fill the queue with noise.

RN-487 — The Arquiteto routes module by module, but only NOMINATES — the Infra elects​

route_modules_to_infra produces ONE list — one item {modulo, imagemCandidata, porque} per module of the current module_map — and it becomes the artifact.module_routing event, with no table: the same design as artifact.module_map/ artifact.project_image/artifact.c4_diagram, the event IS the artifact.

The candidate image goes through the SAME rule as choose_project_image, applied per item. validarDecisaoDeImagem already refuses an image without an explicit tag/digest, latest, and a rationale with fewer than 10 characters — reimplementing that rule per module would create a second version of it to diverge from the first sooner or later. validarRoteamento (domain/architecture/module-routing.ts) delegates, and only adds what is SPECIFIC to the list: empty is refused (it isn't a decision), and a repeated module too (two images for the same module are ambiguous — which one holds?).

A module outside the current module_map is refused naming the VALID modules, the same ruler as AssignStoryModulesUseCase (missingModules): listing only what's wrong would force the model to guess against a map it can't reread; listing the right names ends the search on the first refusal.

With no current module_map, there's no module — refused with 400, never invented. It's the same refusal as create_c4_diagram when the module_map is missing, and for the same reason: there's no module, there's no infra to route. The ArquitetoServer's build_kickoff/1 — the ONLY place from which the model learns the ORDER of the tools — lists route_modules_to_infra as the step that follows create_module_map.

:direct, never proposed_action. Routing has no external effect — it doesn't bring up a container, doesn't change anything outside the event log — and is an INTERNAL architecture decision, of the same caliber as choose_project_image/create_c4_diagram. Putting this in the approval queue would mix a draft the Infra will still review with decisions that already have a real effect.

The Arquiteto nominates, the Infra elects — and this delivery is only the half that nominates. The half that ELECTS among the nominations (or refuses them all) is the Infra Lead's, with its own proposed_action, in a separate PR. What exists here is the auditable list in the event log, before the Infra has a tool to act on it — the same sequencing that already held for the module_map existing before create_c4_diagram needed it.

RN-490 — The RAG accuracy golden-set measures by FILE PATH, in the TOP-5, never by exact chunk or rank 1​

The rag-acertivo gate (docs/gates.yml) measures whether the hybrid search returns the right file for 17 questions composed from real RNs/ADRs of this repository (golden-set, ADR 0123's mold applied to RAG). The criterion of "got it right" has two deliberate decisions, and both avoid measuring the wrong question:

  • File path, never exact chunk. The chunking (1200/150) is precisely one of the parameters this program exists to be able to revise (ADR 0080) — locking the golden-set to the chunk would make ANY chunking adjustment break the 17 cases, even when the right file kept being retrieved.
  • TOP-5, never only the first position. That's how the product uses the result: Chat RAG cites SEVERAL excerpts per response (RagCitationCard, plural), not only the first. Measuring against rank 1 would measure a question the UI doesn't ask. 5, and not the real route's RAG_SEARCH_RESULT_LIMIT (10), so as not to test a looser k than most real searches use.

The criterion is a PURE function (acertouCaminhoEsperado/rankDoCaminhoEsperado), consumed by the seed (seed-golden-set-rag.ts) and tested in isolation — the same discipline as gate-registry.ts: the decision of "this matched" doesn't depend on how the result arrived.

The golden-set runs manually (mix golden_set.rag), never in the regular mix test — the same decision already recorded for the QA golden-set (ADR 0123): without an API LLM secret or new infra, there was no way to run a real Ollama in CI. Excluded by a PERMANENT tag (:golden_set_rag) in test_helper.exs, never by detecting "Ollama reachable" — the same reason as on the QA side: this machine already has Ollama up all the time. The floor is a RATCHET (>=, never >), a count and not a percentage, keyed by the EMBEDDING model (nomic-embed-text, today the only one the product supports) and written only by a human.

Revised by RN-498: "there's no way to run a real Ollama in CI" was true in Stage 2 and stopped being so in Stage 3 (ADR 0138) — a dedicated, scheduled workflow now really runs mix golden_set.rag against a real Ollama in CI. The permanent exclusion in test_helper.exs above STILL holds as is: it protects the regular mix test (and the machine of any developer with Ollama up), never the new workflow, which invokes the tag explicitly, just as was always necessary.

RN-491 — The Infra elects among the Arquiteto's candidates, and the election becomes a NEW version of artifact.project_image​

propose_container_start closes the half RN-487 left declared open: the Infra elects ONE of the imagemCandidata of the Arquiteto's current routing (artifact.module_routing) and proposes bringing up the project's REAL container. The election only has effect because ExecuteContainerStartUseCase REUSES DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase to emit a new version of artifact.project_image with decidedBy: 'infra-lead' — without that the election would be auditable and INERT: the broker composes the container by reading GET .../container-spec, which reads artifact.project_image (RN-105), never artifact.module_routing.

The elected image must be in the candidates list, always — validated BEFORE touching the artifact. Outside the list, the action fails naming the refused image and listing the valid candidates, and neither DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase nor the broker gets called: the Infra elects, never invents.

A new container_start (maintainer, the same caliber as open_infra_pr/ parallelize), deliberately OUTSIDE the block of absolute ceilings of decide.ts — the same reasoning already recorded there for propose_execution_plan/assess_implementability: it's the FIRST time this container really comes up for this election, not exceeding an already authorized ceiling. Unlike open_infra_pr, this action is NOT seeded in INFRA_AUTONOMY_SEEDS — the Infra Lead never applies anything with open_infra_pr (it only proposes a PR a human still merges), but bringing up a container is a real external effect, so it stays require_approval by default, decided case by case through the ApprovalCard. A maintainer CAN configure auto-approval later, and that's why ProposeActionUseCase also executes on the auto_approved path, the same lesson as the comment about parallelize in that file ("without this the action was born, was approved — and nothing came up").

Revised by RN-671 (ADR 0190, 10/01): container_start becomes SEEDED auto_approve on the acceptance of the Infra's handoff, and the Infra Lead's server proposes the first startup on its own when there's routing. The rest of this rule — the candidates list, maintainer, outside the absolute ceilings — remains.

After the broker confirms, the lifecycle transition follows ADR 0081's state machine, never reprovisions needlessly. No row yet, or a row in failed/removed: provisioning (the one that reads the newly decided image and freezes imageVersion) and only then running. A row in stopped: straight to running — the state machine doesn't even allow stopped -> provisioning, and reprovisioning would reemit an image already written in the row. A row already provisioning/running: completes the pending transition or does nothing, relying on the broker's idempotent start (jaEstavaDePe).

Revises RN-485. "Nothing triggers a startup... the only caller that exists today does a READ" stops being true: container_start is the first real caller of ContainerBrokerPort.start, of the five operations ADR 0128/0130 declared. RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase gains its first caller outside tests too. It still holds that NOTHING fires on its own — it's always a proposed_action, decided by a human or by explicit policy.

Dev agents do NOT start working inside the container that comes up here. That stage is a later PR, declared open in CLAUDE.md — the sentence the approval screen shows (apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.ts) stops on purpose before promising that.

RN-492 — The dev agent's terminal command runs INSIDE the real container, when there is one​

Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 gains the FIFTH output (:executar_no_container): a project in execution_mode: container with a REGISTERED running row in project_containers (Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1, a direct read-only read of the table, the same pattern as Engine.Projects.Project). Before this rule, even with a container up (RN-491), EVERY terminal command ran via System.cmd in the engine's process, against the shared folder — the container sat idle.

The command crosses engine → api → broker (POST internal/projects/:projectId/container-exec, ExecutarComandoNoContainerUseCase, ContainerBrokerPort.exec) and runs via docker exec. cwd, when present, is TRANSLATED from the HOST path (inside PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT) to inside /work — the only directory the container sees — swapping the prefix <project_workspaces_root>/ <workspace_dir_name> for /work and preserving the suffix (a dev agent's individual worktree, .worktrees/<agent_id>, included). The worktree itself doesn't change place nor creation mechanism: Workspace.ensure!/4 keeps writing in the SAME physical directory the broker mounts at /work (verified in code: the broker's raizDoProjeto and the engine's PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT resolve the same folder, via workspace_dir_name, RN-109) — the container is just one more observer of it.

REGISTERED running never confirms the container is REALLY up now (RN-486). If it died or was removed from outside between the record and this call, broker.exec fails and becomes a NORMAL failed_result — exit_code nil, a message naming the reason — never a crash, never a silent fallback back to System.cmd outside the container (that would reopen the isolation vector this rule exists to close). mounted never falls into this output: the broker refuses to bring up a container for that mode (ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError).

RN-493 — A terminal inside the real container gains an auto-approval FLOOR, without touching the absolute ceilings​

When containerExecutionActive is true (the same REGISTERED running of RN-492, queried by ProposeActionUseCase only for actionType === 'terminal' in an execution_mode: container project), the INITIAL value of current inside decide() stops being require_approval and becomes auto_approve — a FLOOR, not a new ceiling: the stages that follow (agent_autonomy, permissions.json) can still LOWER that floor exactly as they already lowered the default require_approval (an explicit deny or an ask matching the command win the same way), and the FIVE absolute ceilings of decide.ts (scope, git push/privileged command, protected merge, instruction_patch, parallelism) keep running ON TOP, byte for byte as they were — including when the auto_approve came from the floor, and not from an explicit rule.

The justification is a SECOND boundary, not the absence of the first. The lexical terminal scope (terminalNoEscopo, ADR 0055) keeps running over the SAME HOST paths as always — the cwd/command arriving at decide() are NEVER translated to /work (that translation only happens later, in the engine — RN-492). Inside the real container, a STRONGER boundary is added on top of the lexical one: Docker's mount namespace, which the process physically doesn't cross, plus the /work validation the broker already does (DiretorioForaDoEscopoError). It's defense in depth — the lexical scope isn't replaced, it's redundant.

RN-494 — The image gate (RN-105) applies in the THREE execution modes​

REVISES RN-169 (item 1) and RN-421: the exemption from the RN-105 gate for a mounted/ runner project — "these modes don't bring up their own container, so the Arquiteto's decision will never happen" — is REVOKED. ReadProjectCodeUseCase .portaoDoContainer no longer checks executionMode: the THREE modes now require a decided artifact.project_image (by the Arquiteto, choose_project_image, or by the Infra electing a candidate, container_start — ADR 0133/RN-491) before releasing the seven read routes of the Code tab.

The original exemption confused two questions: "does this project bring up a container on the SERVER?" (no, in mounted/runner, and that doesn't change here) and "does it make sense to require that SOMEONE has decided the project's image before opening code reading?" (yes, in the three modes — the decision is about what the project EXECUTES, not about where the physical container comes up). Keeping the exemption let the Code tab of mounted/runner open without anyone having thought about the project's image; the uniform rule closes that gap.

Accepted cost, spelled out: every EXISTING mounted/runner project without a decided artifact.project_image — including real dogfooding projects like exp001/exp002 — LOSES access to the Code tab the instant this PR is deployed, until the Arquiteto (or the Infra) decides an image for it. That's an OPERATOR ACTION required after deploy, not a transparent fix — that's why the branch is born breaking/, and the version goes up MAJOR.

The lifecycle (project_containers) also stops refusing by mode: RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase no longer answers 400 for mounted/runner — the table can register a row for the three modes, the same provisioning funnel (which already read the image decision, now required for them too). What remains IMPOSSIBLE for mounted/runner is REALLY reaching running: that's applied in a single place, ContainerBrokerPort.start(), which refuses (ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError, a deliberate policy — the broker, on the server, doesn't see the user's folder where the code of mounted/ runner lives) — and ExecuteContainerStartUseCase already handles that refusal as a normal failure (container.start_failed, named reason), never a crash, never silence. In practice, through the normal path (approval of container_start), NO row ever gets born in project_containers for these two modes, because the broker refuses BEFORE any transition is called. Duplicating that mode check in propose-action.use-case.ts or in ExecuteContainerStartUseCase was considered and DISCARDED: the broker already fails loud and named, and the duplicated check would only create a second place to diverge from the first — the same reasoning as the comment on ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError (apps/broker/src/operacoes.ts), which already pointed to this PR.

The web side stops treating mounted/runner as a separate case: ProjectCodeTab asked for the project's mode and opened the shell directly, without even calling GET /projects/:id/container, when the mode wasn't container. That SIMPLIFIED the component — the three modes now follow the same useQuery/states path (loading, error, sem_decisao, decided), with no modoLocal nor conditional enabled per mode.

RN-495 — container_stop/container_remove are born as proposed_action, and only container_remove enters the absolute ceiling​

Closes the gap that the comment on ContainerBrokerPort (ADR 0130) and the CLAUDE.md declared since PR 1.5: stop/remove had a ready HTTP CLIENT (HttpContainerBrokerClient.stop/.remove) and ZERO callers — the global containers page (/containers, RN-496) is the first. The two are NEVER an agent action: only a human clicking "Stop"/"Remove" on a row of the screen proposes them.

container_stop follows container_start's EXACT caliber (RN-491): maintainer, require_approval by default, CAN be configured auto_approve (never seeded) — ExecuteContainerStopUseCase asks the broker to stop and, only when the registered state still said running, registers the running -> stopped transition (container-lifecycle.ts). Already registered stopped/provisioning/failed: the broker is called anyway (it's idempotent — stopping what's no longer running is a no-op on the Docker side), but NO transition is written — inventing one the state machine didn't really describe would be the same defect RN-486 already named for the observed state.

container_remove is the MOST destructive of the three — it discards the container and requires reprovisioning from scratch (container-lifecycle.ts: removed only exits by provisioning again, never "coming back to life") — and that's why it enters the SAME absolute ceiling of decide.ts as git push/privileged command (RN-418): never auto-approvable, neither by agent_autonomy nor by permissions.json, even with "automatic mode" on. The "always allow" gap is closed AT THE SOURCE, by the same mechanism as RN-418: ApproveAlwaysActionUseCase refuses (400) to write the pattern for container_remove — the whole click is refused, and whoever wants to remove approves the instance through the normal flow (POST .../approve). On the web, ApprovalCard.podeSemprePermitir hides the "always allow" button for container_remove, the same ruler that already applies to instruction_patch.

ContainerBrokerPort.remove is docker rm --force — it removes even a running container, in a single call. The state machine has NO direct running -> removed (only running -> stopped/failed, and only FROM THERE to removed): ExecuteContainerRemoveUseCase registers BOTH hops when the registered state still said running (stopped, then removed), reflecting what really happened on the Docker side without widening the state machine with a shortcut that would only exist here.

Neither of the two decides an image — unlike container_start, which reuses DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase to emit a new version of artifact.project_image. stop/remove only ask the broker to act on the container that already exists.

RN-496 — The global containers page asks the broker with a CEILING, and never merges registered with observed​

The same family as RN-486/RN-468, applied to a NEW screen: GET workspaces/:workspaceId/containers (/containers, cross-project) returns one row per workspace project that already has project_containers (ContainersOverviewRepository, THREE batch queries, never one per project — the same spirit as ProjectsSummaryRepository), but asking the broker for the OBSERVED state is a NETWORK call per project, and it doesn't fit in a SQL query.

The ceiling (ADR 0060) is by TWO rulers, not one. First, only provisioning/running rows are ELIGIBLE — a stopped/failed/ removed container doesn't need the daemon's confirmation for the screen to make sense (nobody expects it to be up). Second, among the eligible ones, at most TETO_DE_VERIFICACOES_POR_CARGA (20, revisable) are asked of the broker PER LOAD — in parallel, never in series. What's left out of either ruler carries naoVerificado (fora_do_escopo_da_verificacao | teto_de_verificacoes_atingido), the screen's OWN field — never confused with naoObservado (broker-nao-configurado/broker-sem-resposta/broker-recusou), which is about the broker HAVING BEEN asked and not having answered. A row outside the ceiling has observado/naoObservado/detalheDaObservacao all null: the screen never invents an answer the broker didn't give.

The image read is the FROZEN one, not the current one. imageVersion in project_containers points to the version of artifact.project_image that was current when the row was born — the Arquiteto may have revised the decision AFTERWARDS. The screen resolves the image text by fetching the artifact.project_image event whose version matches imageVersion (decisaoNaVersao, domain/containers/project-container.ts), never the most recent decision — showing the most recent would lie about which image the container that really came up uses. null when that version's event isn't found (never invented).

The pending container proposed_action (if any) travels in the SAME batch read, matched by projectId IN (...) like the other two — it's what lets the screen swap the three action buttons for the inline ApprovalCard without a fourth query per project.

RN-497 — brabo-runner brings up the project's container ON THE USER'S MACHINE, with THEIR Docker​

Closes the half that RN-494 (ADR 0135) left declared: mounted/runner came to REQUIRE a decided image (RN-105's gate applies in the three modes), but still brought up NO container — only execution_mode: container had someone (the broker, apps/broker) capable of really calling Docker. container_start/container_stop/container_remove (RN-491/495) now have a SECOND execution path, branched by the project's executionMode inside ExecuteContainerStartUseCase/ExecuteContainerStopUseCase/ ExecuteContainerRemoveUseCase — never in the action's PROPOSAL nor APPROVAL, which remain mode-agnostic (decide.ts doesn't change).

container goes through the broker, with no change at all. mounted/runner ask the ENGINE (ApiToEngineClient.startContainerViaRunner/ stopContainerViaRunner/removeContainerViaRunner, synchronous like executeTerminalAction) to pass on to the connected RUNNER — the CLI that already keeps the terminal:<projectId> channel (ADR 0103/0104) gains THREE new event pairs, container_start/_result, container_stop/_result, container_remove/_result (apps/runner/src/channel.ts), in the SAME mold as exec/exec_result: Engine.Runners.RunnerRouter dispatches to the channel correlated by ref and stays blocked on receive, the runner calls DockerViaCli.start/stop/remove (@brabo/docker-port, ADR 0128) with the USER'S DOCKER — not the server's — and answers. EngineWeb. ContainerCommandController (routes POST internal/projects/:projectId/ containers/{start,stop,remove}) is the only caller; no other path reaches those three operations on the engine side.

The image that comes up isn't ELECTED again — unlike the container path, which reuses DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase to write a new version of artifact.project_image. The mounted/runner path only READS the CURRENT decision (ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase, the SAME use case that already composes GET .../container-spec for the broker — called directly, without HTTP, because both run in the api's process) and sends it to the runner; without a decided image (RN-105), it fails BEFORE asking the engine.

"No runner connected" is a NORMAL FAILURE, never a generic exception — the same discipline as BrokerIndisponivelError/BrokerRecusouError on the container path. RunnerNaoConectadoError (no runner, or timeout) and RunnerRecusouContainerError (the runner answered and REFUSED — Docker unavailable on the user's machine, invalid specification) are the two classes HttpApiToEngineClient throws; the three use cases catch them and write failed with the reason, never letting them propagate. On the engine side, the response is ALWAYS 200 — sucesso: false in the body, with motivoCodigo ("not_connected"/"timeout") only when the engine DIDN'T EVEN GET to ask the runner (RunnerRouter returned {:error, _}), never an HTTP error status for what is a normal failure of the command.

Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor did NOT gain a new output. The decision "run the command on the host or inside the container this runner brought up" is INTERNAL to the runner — decisao_de_execucao/1 already routes UNCONDITIONALLY every command of a connected runner project to RunnerRouter.exec/4 (RN-423). What changes is only apps/runner/src/index.ts: EstadoDoRunner gains containerAtivo (the NAME of the container THIS runner brought up, or null), and tratarExec now routes to DockerViaCli.exec (via docker exec) when there's an active container, or to the usual path (executarComando directly on the host) when there isn't — the cwd, already validated by validarCwdDentroDaRaiz against the project root, is translated into /work by PREFIX swap (cwdParaContainer, guard.ts), the same reasoning as cwd_para_container/2 on the engine side (RN-492).

guard.ts (containment in $HOME on Linux, RN-434) now also covers the mounted path, with NO new validation. The container's bind-mount IS estado.dir — the same root validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux already validated at the CLI's startup, before any container came up. There's no second check of "valid mount path" because there doesn't need to be: the mount IS the confirmed root, period.

RN-498 — The RAG golden-set runs in real CI, SCHEDULED — and the gate stays warn​

RN-490 recorded the RAG golden-set (ADR 0132) being born as a manual mix golden_set.rag, "never in CI", for the same reason as the QA golden-set (ADR 0123): without an API LLM secret or new infra, there was no way to run a real Ollama on a CI runner. This RN closes that half — only for RAG, never for QA — with a dedicated workflow (.github/workflows/golden-set-rag.yml, schedule + workflow_dispatch) that pulls nomic-embed-text into a real Ollama service (the same pinned version as the rest of the product, today 0.34.4) and really runs mix golden_set.rag.

The difference that makes this tractable for RAG and not for QA: the RAG golden-set only calls the EMBEDDING model — CPU, deterministic, no sampling — never a CHAT model making a judgment, which is what the QA golden-set requires (expensive, it measures something non-deterministic by nature, as ADR 0123 itself records with real rounds varying from 1 to 5 hits out of 6). ubuntu-latest, with no GPU at all, suffices here — it wouldn't suffice for QA. The QA golden-set doesn't change at all with this RN: it remains entirely manual, a TODO(humano) in CLAUDE.md.

severidade: warn (docs/gates.yml) STAYS warn, and the reason changed. It's no longer "there's no CI with an LLM" — it becomes cadence: the workflow is SCHEDULED (nightly + manual trigger), it never runs on pull_request. block would promise a merge lock that doesn't exist — the same reasoning that already held in Stage 2, now applied to the right reason. A regression in search accuracy becomes a trend signal visible within 24h (or immediately, via workflow_dispatch), never a gate that blocks a PR — a trade-off accepted explicitly by the product owner, given the cost of pulling the model and running 17 searches (a few minutes) in every window.

No secret needs to be generated in the workflow. seed-golden-set-rag.ts never defines NODE_ENV, and the four secrets the api would refuse with an example literal in production (RN-114) are only checked when NODE_ENV === 'production' — the script falls into the development branch and uses the dev literals without complaint, unlike docker/smoke.sh, which comes up with NODE_ENV=production on purpose and therefore generates its own with openssl rand.

The permanent exclusion of the :golden_set_rag tag in test_helper.exs (RN-490) doesn't change. It protects the regular mix test — including on the machine of any developer with Ollama up — never the new workflow, which invokes mix golden_set.rag explicitly, just as it was always necessary to run it manually.

Fixed after measuring: the workflow above never ran green once. Five consecutive scheduled runs (09/05 to 09/09/2026) failed, and there were three stacked defects, each hiding the next:

  1. mix golden_set.rag is an alias that calls test, and Mix refuses that outside the :test environment — ** (Mix) "mix test" is running in the "dev" environment —, before running anything. def cli in apps/engine/mix.exs now declares preferred_envs for BOTH golden-set tasks: that's what makes the short command, the only one documented everywhere, work without an environment prefix. Requiring MIX_ENV=test from whoever calls would transfer the fix to all the prose that teaches the command — and to whoever forgot, again.
  2. The job never brought up the api, and the test SKIPS when API_URL doesn't respond (an environment precondition declared in ADR 0132). With item 1 fixed, the job would be green without measuring anything. It now brings up the real api (build, node dist/main.js, waiting for /health) — satisfying the precondition, and never loosening the test, which would be changing the judgment to fit the CI. What does the work is still seed-golden-set-rag.ts, which brings up its own Nest context; the instance exists to answer /health.
  3. The seed died with 409 at the image gate. It created the project as runner precisely to ESCAPE the gate (RN-105), relying on the exemption that RN-169/RN-421 gave to mounted/runner — an exemption revoked by RN-494 (ADR 0135), with the script's comment still citing it. Now the seed CROSSES the gate through the real path: it decides the image via DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase, the same use case as the Arquiteto's choose_project_image, in a consultiva session it opens (the decision event requires session_id, which is NOT NULL) — never a hand-written artifact INSERT, which would make the golden-set measure against a state production doesn't know how to produce.

And the job now requires the golden-set to have MEASURED. The guard is the result line (N/N casos acertaram), which is only printed after the 17 cases run; without it the step fails naming the reason. It's necessary because the {:skip, motivo} the test returns from the BODY is inert — there's no runtime skip in ExUnit, and what you see is Result: 1 passed. That was exactly what happened when measuring: with the seed dying with 409, the test passed. excluded does NOT work as a signal here, unlike what the sibling guard in ci.yml checks: the legitimate output carries over a thousand excluded, which are all the other engine tests, out by the tag.

Measured after the three fixes, on this machine, through the path the job now follows: 17/17 in the top-5, the same as the two manual rounds that recorded the floor.

RN-499 — The Infra's handoff has its OWN actionable card, outside the thread — without widening AGENTES_DE_CHAT​

OfferInfraHandoffUseCase offers the handoff to the Infra Lead (offer-infra-handoff.use-case.ts:43), and until now no screen could accept it. offeredHandoff (SessionPage.tsx) restricts the thread's card to AGENTES_DE_CHAT (RN-136), which doesn't include infra, and acceptHandoff (api-client.ts) had a single consumer — that card, behind that filter. The code's own comment recorded the consequence as accepted: "since Infra is never accepted HERE … in practice, never".

The effect wasn't cosmetic: the handoff stayed offered forever, the Infra Lead was never activated, propose_container_start was never called (RN-491) and no project of any mode ever got to have a container up. The chain "Infra accepts → proposes container_start → approved → running" was unreachable through any screen path.

The filter was NOT widened, and that's the rule. AGENTES_DE_CHAT is right to exclude infra: the engine's agent_command_controller.ex has no message clause for the Infra Lead, and the last clause (unguarded) would treat "infra" as if it were the Criativo — putting infra on the list would make the screen offer a conversation thread that doesn't exist and the composer send a message to the wrong agent. (Since RN-584 the engine refuses by name instead of delivering to the Criativo; the filter remains right for the same reason.) Accepting the Infra is a propositional action, not a conversational one.

The actionable card lives, then, outside the thread: in the fixed strip between the scrolling area and the composer, the same one that hosts the manual handoff (RN-440) and already declares itself the place of handoff actions that "aren't conversation, they're redirection". Three consequences the choice buys: the Infra's handoff.offered stays narrated in the thread as a silent divider (nothing changes in the timeline); no conversational handoff changes shape; and the button doesn't disappear when the offer leaves the 200-event window in a long session — the thread's card would depend on the event being visible, this one doesn't.

The card states the click's consequence, because it isn't obvious: accepting activates the Infra Lead, which takes over provisioning and will propose bringing up the container; the proposal still goes through the usual approval pipeline (container_start, maintainer, never auto-approvable by seed — RN-491). Accepting brings up no container at all.

Closing: the same activeFor(h.toAgent) as the thread's card — a handoff already accepted, or Infra already active in this session by any other path, doesn't reopen the invite. And the click calls the same handleAcceptHandoff, with no second accept path.

  • Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-da-infra.test.tsx — the card appears and accepts with the right ids; disappears with Infra already active; disappears in a non-active session; the thread's silent divider stays there with no thread button; and the non-regression of RN-136: Infra (older) + Dev Lead (newer) pending show BOTH cards, each accepting its own handoff

RN-502 — A dev agent only claims a task with a running container, and the terminal no longer falls outside it​

Two halves of the same rule: without an execution environment, the dev agent doesn't start, and without an execution environment, the command doesn't run anywhere.

The claim guard. Engine.Dev.AgentIo.try_claim/2 — the SINGLE claim point — queries Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1 BEFORE calling claim_task/1. Without a REGISTERED running row in project_containers (RN-243/ADR 0081), the agent falls into :idle, persists, emits dev.blocked_by_container, and doesn't call the api. The guard comes before the claim on purpose: claiming only to give it back right after would leave the task marked and with no live owner, which is the state block_task/4 exists to never produce.

:idle, and not a new status. It's the only state from which a wake still rescues — the guards of handle_info/2 all match it ({:wake, :became_claimable} requires :idle, :rearm requires :idle_tripped, gate_resolved requires a matching task_id, RN-047). An invented :blocked_by_container would be a state from which nothing rescues.

In the ENGINE and not only in the api's activate-execution, because the claim has a path no route covers: REHYDRATION. Engine.Dev.DevRehydrator doesn't cast :work; whoever claims after a restart is DevAgentServer.init/1 → finish_restart_recovery/1 → try_claim/2. A gate only at the HTTP boundary would let every rehydrated agent go back to work without a container.

The wake. A read doesn't notify anyone: an already stopped agent would stay stopped until an unrelated event passed nearby. So arriving at running PUBLISHES — RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase writes the row and the event in the SAME transaction, aggregateType: 'container' (the third aggregate that Engine.Outbox.Drain now drains, alongside session and task), aggregateId = the PROJECT. Engine.Workers.DevAgentWakeWorker delivers {:wake, :became_claimable} to ALL agents of the project (DevAgentState.list_by_project/1 — the container belongs to the project, not to a module). It's the SAME message that already existed, not a new one: its semantics are already "there may be work now", and an own message would require a new handle_info/2 clause in both servers with a guard identical to the one that already exists. Only running publishes; provisioning/stopped/failed/removed release nobody.

The second half: the terminal. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor degraded silently — container without a running container fell into :caminho_de_sempre, that is, System.cmd INSIDE the engine's process, the same one that talks to the database, the api, and all the other projects. ADR 0134 (RN-492) had closed isolation only on the happy path. Now it refuses (:recusar_container_ausente), mirroring the :recusar_nao_verificado/:recusar_runner_desconectado that runner mode already had (RN-423), and as a normal failed_result — never a crash. mounted enters the SAME branch: with a running container it goes through to the broker like container; without it, it refuses. The :caminho_de_sempre catch-all shrinks to what it should always have been on its own — nonexistent project or malformed project_id. No execution mode falls into it.

Declared consequence: a project without a container up stops working, and says why. It's deliberate — it's what the rule exists to do — and that's why it can only come in AFTER the changes that give a container to mounted mode.
