The local agent becomes a USER service, and status does not collapse state (RN-518)​

RN-518 — brabo-runner service install|uninstall|status installs at USER level and never root; uninstall cleans the folder the UNIT records; status answers four states without collapsing any; Windows is a named refusal​

Session 7 of PHASE 28 and point 5 of ADR 0147. Until now the local agent was foreground only: a process ended by SIGINT/SIGTERM, which dies with the terminal and does not come back with the user's session. There was no precedent at all — no mention of systemd, launchd or LaunchAgent in apps/runner/.

User level, ALWAYS — and root is a REFUSAL, not a warning. systemd --user on Linux, LaunchAgent on macOS. This is not a packaging preference: the docblock of apps/runner/src/guard.ts:9-31 declares "the runner runs ON the user's machine, with HIS privileges" as the premise on which the product's three real boundaries rest (authentication, approval pipeline, consent) — and the cwd guard is best-effort in writing, precisely because it is not what holds anything. A system service running as root would break the invariant and leave the best-effort guard as the only thing between an approved command and the machine's disk. That is why install with uid 0 refuses naming the reason, without writing any file and without running any command: installing-and-warning would leave the wrong installation up, and the warning would be read only once.

Windows is OUT OF SCOPE, and the refusal is named. The build matrix already produces the Windows binary (ADR 0112), but a user service there is a third mechanism (OS Services with a user account, or Task Scheduler at logon) — not a variation of the two. The three subcommands answer naming the platform, saying that the decision is declared, and pointing to the path that keeps working (running in the foreground). Never a mute failure, never an "installed" that installed nothing. Any other platform falls into the same refusal.

One unit PER PROJECT, named by the projectId — brabo-runner-<id>.service / dev.brabo.runner.<id> — because the server already enforces one runner per project: a second join on the same terminal:<projectId> is refused by Engine.Runners.Registry. Naming by FOLDER would allow installing two units that can never be up at the same time, and the second would show up as a connection failure instead of an installation error. Installing again, from another folder, overwrites. uninstall and status reach exactly the same unit because they derive the name from the SAME projectId, resolved by the SAME two sources in the same order as the usual CLI (--project, otherwise brabo-runner.config.json), and the folder comes from resolverDir of guard.ts — never a second rule. On Linux the file goes where systemd looks, with its precedence: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user when the variable is set, ~/.config/systemd/user when not — choosing only the second would make the unit be born where the manager never looks, and the failure would show up as "unit file does not exist" on enable, visible but for the wrong reason.

The projectId becomes a FILE NAME, so it is validated here. It comes from two sources that are not the server (a typed flag and a file in the folder), and a --project ../../etc/systemd would write outside the units directory. Only letters, digits, ., - and _, up to 64 characters — a UUID, the real format of every project of the product, passes whole. A runner path and a folder with a double quote or a line break are also a named refusal: a line break in a unit file is directive injection, not an edge case.

A service authenticates with a DEVICE KEY, never with a token. install requires a valid brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json in the folder and refuses without it, ignoring --token/BRABO_ACCOUNT_TOKEN on purpose: writing an account token inside a unit file would leave it on disk, readable by any process of the user and surviving the shell that exported it — and this CLI never wrote a credential to disk (the docblock of auth.ts has a test lock against exactly that). RN-434 runs the same, through the SAME function: a service pointing outside $HOME on Linux is refused, because doing via a unit what the CLI refuses to do via a flag would be getting around the rule through the back door.

Restart=on-abnormal, and never on-failure (in the plist, KeepAlive with Crashed, and never SuccessfulExit). The runner exits with 1 when the join was REFUSED — invalid ticket, another runner on the project, a missing capability (RN-514) — or when it exhausted its own retry ceiling, and both things are "stop and call a human". on-failure would restart a fatal refusal in a loop, which is exactly what the CLI refuses to do on its own. Signal, OOM and watchdog — what on-abnormal covers — are the only failure that restarting fixes. The PATH goes frozen into the unit, with the cost declared in the file itself: both managers give the service a minimal PATH, and the runner calls git (the mirror, RN-516) and docker (ADR 0137); without it the service would come up perfectly and both functions would fail with "not found". It is a snapshot, and it only changes by reinstalling.

The TWO halves of the unit file do NOT have the same syntax, and WorkingDirectory= goes WITHOUT quotes. ExecStart= is parsed with unquoting and word splitting — that is why each argument goes in quotes —, and WorkingDirectory= is not: systemd takes the whole rest of the line as the path. Treating the two as if they were the same cost an entire release: with quotes the value no longer starts with /, the unit is refused at load (Loaded: bad-setting, WorkingDirectory= path is not absolute) and never starts — in both kinds, in no installation at all. The suite was green the whole time, because each assertion asked back for exactly the wrong form: that is why the proof is now made against systemd-analyze --user verify, the real validator, and not against text. What REMAINS to escape is one character, and it is not the space (the line goes whole, so /home/eu/pasta com espaço works literally): it is %, because that directive goes through specifier expansion — /home/dan/50%off becomes /home/dan/50<id-do-os-release>ff with no error at all, and the service comes up in the wrong folder. %% is the way to say a literal %. Reading back accepts both forms, and that is a deliberate debt to whoever already has a broken unit on disk: status and uninstall need to keep reaching its folder. Whoever is in that state fixes it by reinstalling — install overwrites the whole file.

And there is a THIRD syntax in the same file: Environment= (AT-095). It is a LIST of space-separated assignments, with unquoting and C-style escaping, and it also expands specifiers. Written raw — as the XDG_CONFIG_HOME of the MACHINE unit and the PATH of both kinds came out —, Environment=XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/home/dan/50%off com espaco reached the service as /home/dan/50popff: %o expanded and com/espaco discarded by the word splitting. The unit loads, verify approves, the service comes up — and the agent looks for the base and the key in a folder that does not exist, silently. That is why the WHOLE assignment goes in quotes (Environment="VAR=valor"), with \ and " escaped by backslash and % as %%; $ is not escaped there (Environment= does not expand variables). The --dir of ExecStart= had the same class and went along: each argument still goes in quotes, and now \ becomes \\, % becomes %% and $ becomes $$ (the variable substitution of ExecStart=). A line break in PATH/XDG_CONFIG_HOME is REFUSED before writing — in a unit file it is a new directive, not a value. None of this changes the READING back: it only reads the WorkingDirectory=, and neither of the two environment values is read from disk. The proof is the EFFECTIVE VALUE, not verify (which approves the broken form): the very systemd --test --user --unit=<u>, over a temporary units folder, dumps the resolved configuration, and the test compares what systemd UNDERSTOOD with what was written.

An activation that fails does NOT delete the file, and does not say "installed". Writing the unit and activating it are two steps, and the manager may not be there (systemctl out of the PATH, launchd refusing). The file stays — it is what the person needs to finish by hand — and the answer is a third outcome, which names the pending command and the reason. Deleting the file would turn "I could not activate" into "nothing happened", which is false.

uninstall removes the THREE, and the folder comes from the UNIT — never from the cwd. The ADR is explicit: the unit file, the brabo-runner.config.json and the brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json. The last two live in the runner's folder, and the folder that matters is the one that was INSTALLED, not the one from which the person happened to type the command — that is why the WorkingDirectory is read back from the unit file itself, which is the record of what was installed. Without a unit there is no record: the two files are only removed with an explicit --dir, and the message says why. Guessing by the cwd would delete the key of a project that nobody asked to remove. A failing deactivation becomes a warning and the file is removed anyway — a unit the manager no longer recognizes is no reason to leave the file behind.

And uninstall SAYS what it did not do: the key left the disk, not the server. The corresponding public key remains in runner_device_keys, and revoking it is something else (DELETE /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys/:deviceKeyId, ADR 0147 point 6). A "removed" that let the person think they had revoked would be worse than removing nothing. The LaunchAgent log is also not deleted: it is the user's record of what happened, and deleting it was not asked for.

status answers FOUR states, and they do not collapse (RN-088): not installed, installed and running, installed and stopped, and installed and I could not ask. The first answer comes from the DISK — is there a unit file? —, and that is why it stays right on a machine where the manager does not exist; only afterwards is the manager asked. A spawn that failed (binary absent from the PATH) never becomes "the manager said no": they are different answers, separated at the source, and a word this CLI does not know how to interpret also falls into "could not ask" instead of becoming "stopped" by guesswork. Each state has its own sentence and its own exit code (0 / 3 / 4 / 5, with 1 and 2 left out because they already mean generic failure and usage error in this CLI): a single exit(1) for the three "not running" ones would collapse through the code exactly what the sentence separates.

Nothing here is a proposed_action. It is the user running a command on their own machine, about their own service — not an agent asking to act. service is dispatched before lerArgumentos, because none of the three subcommands connects to anything and what matters most (status) needs to work in a folder whose configuration is broken, which is precisely when someone asks.

Device key revocation stops being blind, and reaches the live connection (RN-519..520)​

RN-519 — Nobody revokes what they cannot see: the device key gains a listing for its OWN owner, and the maintainer view stays out by DECISION​

Session 7 of PHASE 28 and point 6 of ADR 0147. Revocation had existed since ADR 0118 (DELETE /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys/:deviceKeyId, developer, 204, idempotent) — and there was no way to see what one revokes.

The real cut was bigger than the docblock said. It declared the absence as "without the maintainer view (list/revoke any user's) that the PAT has". But PersonalAccessTokensController has five routes — @Post(), @Get() and @Delete(':tokenId') for the user themself, plus @Get('all') and @Delete(':tokenId/admin') for maintainer (RN-427) — and the device key one had two. It was not only the maintainer view that was missing: the listing for the OWN owner was missing. An orphan key (tab closed in the middle of the flow of RN-473) was inert, invisible and permanent, with no screen at all on which to revoke it — the gap that CLAUDE.md already declared.

@Get() comes in, developer, in the same format the PAT already has and scoped to the user themself in the repository's WHERE, never in a filter of the use case.

The revoked one STAYS in the list. Same choice as listarDoUsuarioNoProjeto of the PAT: whoever revoked needs to see they revoked, and making the row disappear would make the screen claim the key never existed. revokedAt is what separates the two, and a null lastUsedAt is the sign of the ORPHAN — registered and never used by any runner.

Never the public JWK. It is not a secret, but it serves no purpose here: the list exists to revoke, and for that id, name and the three dates suffice. The private half the api never saw.

The maintainer view stays OUT — now by decision, not by omission. The PAT's two admin routes were born from incident response (RN-427): a dismissed dev with a SHARED secret circulating. A device key is not that animal — the private key never leaves the browser that generated it, so there is no secret in someone else's hands to contain. What the DELETE here gained in exchange was REACH (RN-520), not breadth.

RN-520 — Revoking stops only preventing a NEW ticket and now takes down the LIVE connection; the target is {projeto, usuário} and never {chave}, and taking down never takes down the revocation​

Revised by RN-685 (ADR 0201): the socket ticket now stores WHICH credential requested it, and revoking a key (and a PAT) takes down only the connections opened WITH IT — another runner of the same user, with another key or with a PAT, stays up. The "declared cost" below no longer holds. The {projeto, usuário} pair survives as the target of member removal (RN-615), as that of the LEGACY connection (ticket without a credential) during the rollout, and as plan B when the engine does not know the per-credential route.

The other half of point 6 of ADR 0147. Revoking a device key prevented the NEXT ticket and nothing else: an already connected brabo-runner kept the terminal:<projectId> channel up — executing approved commands, serving PTY, starting containers — with the revoked key, until it dropped on its own.

The one that sends the command is the api; the one that reaches the pid is the engine. The api calls POST /internal/projects/:projectId/runner/disconnect (the same internal HTTP with the usual service token, never a second mechanism), and the engine finds the channel via Engine.Runners.Registry.whereis/1 — the pid it already handed out. The engine does not query the keys table and the api does not talk to the channel; neither of the two does the other's work, the same division as EngineWeb.ContainerCommandController (RN-497).

The precision that exists is {projeto, usuário}, and the one that does not exist is {chave} — by construction, not by taste. Engine.Runners.SocketTicket stores project_id, user_id and kind, and only that; the api requests the ticket with {userId, kind}. The identity of the CREDENTIAL that originated the ticket (the PAT, or the kid of the device key — RN-475) dies in PatAuthGuard and never reaches the socket. Carrying it there would require a new column in runner_socket_tickets, a new field in the internal request and a new assign in connect/3: an auth contract change, outside this delivery.

A DECLARED cost, and named in the code, not only here: a runner of the SAME user connected with a PAT, or with another key of the same project, also drops. It reconnects on its own — the next round requests a new ticket, and the credential that is still valid gets one. Whoever was revoked does not, and that is where the revocation bites. A runner of ANOTHER user on the same project does not drop: the comparison is socket.assigns.user_id, inside the channel process, which is the only one that can read it — and the de_outro_dono outcome goes back to the requester instead of an :ok that does not describe what happened.

It takes down the TRANSPORT, not just the channel process. Stopping only the channel would leave the socket alive and the Phoenix client re-entering the topic forever with an already consumed ticket — silent degradation, exactly the defect ADR 0147 exists not to repeat. EngineWeb.RunnerSocket.id/1 stops being nil and now names the connection (runner_socket:<kind>:<projectId>:<userId>), and the channel uses Phoenix's documented mechanism, Endpoint.broadcast(id, "disconnect", %{}). It is through it that the runner NOTICES the drop: onDisconnected resolves the round, the loop requests a new ticket and the api refuses.

A side effect NEVER takes down the main effect. The DELETE stays 204 and idempotent: engine down, no runner connected or a timeout cannot make the revocation fail nor become 5xx. The call to the engine lives in a try/catch that only LOGS, inside the use case — the SAME rule as rag_searches (RN-479) and mirror_sync_result (RN-517). And the four outcomes are information, not error: sem_runner is the normal case of whoever revokes an orphan key (RN-519), and an UNKNOWN outcome coming from the engine becomes timeout and never derrubado — between asserting that the connection dropped and asserting that maybe not, the safe assertion is the one that does not promise what is not known.

Revoke FIRST, take down afterwards, and the project comes from the revoked ROW, never from the URL: the route's projectId was already ignored in the DELETE, and reading it here would make a divergent projectId take down the runner of a project that has nothing to do with this key.

Extended by RN-574 (ADR 0161): a fourth local refusal reason, sem_broker_na_instalacao, for container/mounted in an installation without a container broker — after "already up" and before "no image decided".

Extended by RN-590 (AT-105): the same reading holds in the mode conversion, in stop/remove and in the Infra Lead's proposal (409 refusal from the api when proposing).

Starting a project's container had one path: the Infra Lead, inside a session, calling its tool. In a real execution of exp004 (runner mode) container_start_via_runner failed due to the defect that RN-508 closed — and there was no way to TRY AGAIN. Five dev agents spent hours emitting dev.blocked_by_container (RN-502), and the only way out was to open a new session and talk to an agent to re-execute a machine operation.

The global containers page (ADR 0136, RN-495) was already the place where a HUMAN decides a container's lifecycle — but it did not even show the project: the rule was "one row per project that already has project_containers", and a start that fails BEFORE recording leaves no row at all. The screen hid exactly the project for which it needed to exist.

The THIRD state has its own name, and it is not stopped. The read model becomes a LEFT JOIN (it was INNER) and registrado becomes null for those that never provisioned — it is not a new value of ContainerLifecycleStatus (stopped is a container that EXISTED and stopped), and it is not "not observed" (which is about the daemon having been asked). The screen prints "never provisioned" and the Observed column says sem_container_registrado, the third reason of naoVerificado — the three do not collapse (RN-088/RN-486).

The list widened; the BUDGET did not. Asking the broker for the observed state is a network call per project, with a ceiling of 20 per load (TETO_DE_VERIFICACOES_POR_CARGA). A project without project_containers has nothing to observe, so it is never eligible and never takes up a slot: in a workspace with hundreds of empty projects, those with a real container stay verified exactly as before. And it remains THREE batch queries, however many projects there are — none inside a loop.

The action branches by execution_mode, with the same rule as the backend (RN-497/RN-503): container and mounted propose container_start (broker, on the server) and runner proposes container_start_via_runner (local agent, on the user's machine). The TWO payloads are different on purpose and are not copied: container_start carries the image ELECTION (image, network, resources), read from the project's current decision at click time; container_start_via_runner has a schema with only rationale (RN-508), because it starts the ALREADY decided image and elects nothing.

The screen does NOT propose what is already known to fail — and says the reason in place of the button. Three refusals, each with its own text, in the order "state of the WORLD before the capability of whoever is looking" (so a viewer still reads "the image remains to be decided", and not only "you cannot"):

  1. no image decided — the gate of RN-105, which holds in all THREE modes since RN-494; without artifact.project_image there is nothing to start;
  2. runner that never had a confirmed folder (null workspaceVerifiedAt, RN-423) — no local agent ever connected, so the action would fail for sure. The same honesty the Infra Lead's tool already practices when refusing LOCALLY before proposing (RN-508);
  3. role below maintainer — the minimum is that of the ENDPOINT (RN-102): both types require maintainer in decide.ts, and the comparison comes from roleAtLeast, never from a hand-written list of roles. What is taken away is the CONTROL, never the INFORMATION (ADR 0064): whoever cannot still sees state, image and resources, and the reason is said ONCE in TEXT — title on a disabled element does not open in Chromium.

And what the screen does NOT know, it declares instead of promising. workspaceVerifiedAt is the record of ONE confirmation and never a heartbeat (RN-468): non-null does not prove a local agent connected NOW, and the api has no presence signal (what knows about now is the Phoenix channel, in the engine). So the runner row offers the button with a written caveat — "if it is not running now, the action fails when approved" — instead of a green dot that would lie.

No ceiling moved. Every proposal on this screen is a proposed_action, always with a HUMAN clicking, never an agent; container_remove stays at the absolute ceiling (RN-418) and decide.ts stays byte for byte. The role read is the WORKSPACE one, and the gap is declared: the effective one is projectRole ?? workspaceRole (RN-471), and fetching project_members per row would be the network N+1 this page exists not to pay — whoever was DEMOTED in a project still sees the button and gets a 403, which is the repairable defect (it ends in a toast), not the invisible one.

RN-539 — assess_implementability triggers the DESIGN threat model in PARALLEL, and only once per story​

The appsec (Engine.Gates.SecOpsAgentServer.run_design/2, RN-360) was born implemented, tested and with no production caller at all: the only mention outside tests was a comment in artifact_schemas.ex. RN-360 itself declared the gap, and docs/fluxo.yml (role appsec, field acionamento) already NAMED the missing trigger — assess_implementability of the Dev Lead, gate implementavel, the same ADR 0090. That was it. run_assessment/2 now calls it via Engine.Gates.Dispatcher.run_appsec_design/2 — the sixth callback of the behaviour, a structural COPY of run_qa_estrategia/3 and swappable in tests for the same reason as its five neighbors (the caller is exercised by a light test, without an Ecto sandbox, and should not start a real GenServer just to prove it ASKED).

In parallel, and the assessment does not wait. The trigger happens on BOTH exits of run_assessment/2 — with a test plan and without — and the outcome of each one stays byte for byte as it was. Making the assessment depend on the threat model would make the implementavel gate depend on TWO asynchronous productions instead of one, and would burn two Dev Lead turns where today one is burned: the :sem_plano branch already returns {:error, ...} asking the model to call again (RN-163), and a second wait stacked on it would multiply the window. The threat model reaches whoever needs it through the path that RN-361 already defined — handoff to arquiteto, dev-lead and infra —, never through this return; the :sem_plano message does not even mention the appsec, because promising the model something it will not receive there is the defect that RN-163 closes.

Since RN-674 there is no more :sem_plano: the assessment comes out on the first call, the appsec trigger accompanies the proposal, and the read of the history serves only the guard below. The appsec stays in DESIGN — the owner's decision that took the test plan out of pre-dev was about QA.

And only once per story. The model is INSTRUCTED to call assess_implementability again while the test plan does not exist: without a guard, each re-call would cost another appsec LLM round and three more handoffs about the SAME story. disparar_appsec_se_preciso/3 only triggers when there is no artifact.threat_model of that storyId in the history. The question here is DOES IT EXIST, not WHICH — the opposite of the test plan, where the most recent wins because a story can be reassessed.

The event log read is one per call: the two questions ("is there already a test plan?", "is there already a threat model?") are answered over the same list. Two list_events/2 in the same invocation would be the traffic amplifier that ADR 0060 refuses, and this path is hot precisely because of the retry. An UNREADABLE history triggers nothing: absence of an answer is not proof of absence of the artifact, and triggering there would reopen the re-call through another door. The invalid args clause also does not trigger — it does not know which story it is.

The flag that turns an agent on has to REACH the process (RN-540)​

RN-540 — A boolean flag read by runtime.exs is mapped in the environment: of the engine service of both composes, with the code's default​

A pause is only reversible if the path to turn it on exists. The pause of the Anamnese and that of the Psicólogo (RN-115, RN-117) were declared reversible in THREE places — the docblock of AnamneseSchedulerWorker.enabled?/0 ("Turning it back on is ANAMNESE_ENABLED=true and restarting the engine"), that of PsychologistWorker.enabled?/0 and the configuration table — and the path did not exist in any environment.

Measured, not a hypothesis. With the dev compose up:

$ docker compose … exec -T engine sh -lc \
    'echo "[$START_ANAMNESE] [$ANAMNESE_ENABLED] [$PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED]"'
[true] [] []

The cause is the layer only Compose has: it does not pass the host environment through to the container. A variable reaches the process if, and only if, it is written in the environment: (or in an env_file) of that service. The engine mapped THIRTEEN Anamnese/Psicólogo variables — all of them cost CEILINGS (ANAMNESE_INTERVAL_SECONDS, ANAMNESE_BUDGET_MICROS, PSYCHOLOGIST_TRIAGE_THRESHOLD, …) — and neither of the two that decide whether the agents run. ANAMNESE_ENABLED=true in .env was inert: apps/engine/config/runtime.exs fell back to the default "false" and both stayed off silently, with no error.

Probable origin of the defect: when the code's default became false (2026-08-10), nobody needed the variable to TURN OFF. Only whoever tries to TURN ON finds out the wire does not exist — and that person, by construction, shows up months later.

The rule. Every BOOLEAN flag that runtime.exs reads — the form System.get_env("X", "true"|"false") == "true" — has to be mapped in the environment: of the engine service of both composes. The cut is that of the booleans and not that of the file's 58 variables because a flag exists precisely to be flipped, and the flip happens through the environment: a flag without a line in the compose is a switch without a wire. A numeric ceiling with a good default (READ_FILE_MAX_BYTES) and a release variable (SECRET_KEY_BASE, POOL_SIZE) are legitimately left out, and that is why the list is DERIVED from runtime.exs instead of maintained by hand.

The default differs per file, and the difference is the decision:

  • in docker/docker-compose.yml (dev) the line repeats the CODE's default. Dev is where the docblocks' promise is exercised, and a divergent default there would make the compose decide product underneath runtime.exs.
  • in docker/docker-compose.prod.yml it is enough to be mapped. That file turns the background agents off on purpose (START_ANAMNESE:-false against the code's true), with the reason written alongside — demanding equality would reject a conscious decision.

This does NOT change any product decision. Both flags remain false by default in both composes: the pause of 2026-08-10 still holds, byte for byte. What came to exist is the switch.

And ANAMNESE_ENABLED=true alone is not enough. START_ANAMNESE (BOOT key, apps/engine/lib/engine/application.ex:82,106-108) decides whether the kickoff/0 that SCHEDULES the periodic tick is called; ANAMNESE_ENABLED (PRODUCT flag) decides whether a NEW round can happen. They are different questions, and the periodic Anamnese requires both at true. The Psicólogo has only the second — its automatic trigger is session closing, not a tick.

deploy/k8s/ is left out, and by decision. The layer that breaks does not exist there: a Deployment/ConfigMap intercepts nothing, and the variable is written where every variable is written. brabo-config has FOUR literals (service addresses and the web's log level), with none of the 13 ceilings nor START_ANAMNESE — the engine runs with the code's defaults, coherently. There is no wireless switch to fix there.

  • Where: docker/docker-compose.yml:406-425 (the four boot keys and the four product flags, in each agent's block); docker/docker-compose.prod.yml:308-315; apps/engine/config/runtime.exs:157,158,162,168,185,229,238,264 (the eight flags); .env.example (the two questions, side by side)
  • Test: scripts/ci/flags-do-engine-no-compose.spec.ts — derives the flags from runtime.exs and fails naming the one missing in either of the two composes, and the one diverging from the code's default in the dev one. No warn: it really fails, in the test-packages job

RN-529 — brabo-runner is born with a local BASE, each project is a subfolder of it, and the base NEVER invalidates --dir​

The local agent had no notion of a base. The only root was --dir, resolved by resolverDir against INIT_CWD ?? process.cwd(); without the flag, the root was the cwd itself. estado.dir is one path, singular — that of the project of that connection —, and there was no constant, variable or field saying where the projects live on that machine. The word "base" only appeared in comments.

The base is LOCAL, and never arrives over the network. It is the broker's design (ADR 0144) applied to the local agent: whoever has the root is whoever executes, and what crosses the network is the relative segment. There is no base field coming from the server, and resolverPastaDoProjetoNaBase refuses an ABSOLUTE segment lexically — never "accepts it and reinterprets".

Two sources, and the flag wins. --base <caminho> on the command line, and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/brabo/runner.json (otherwise ~/.config/brabo/runner.json), which is where the installer (ADR 0150) writes it. The file belongs to the USER and not to a project on purpose: the base is one for N projects, and storing it in brabo-runner.config.json — which is per project, lives INSIDE the project folder and is written by the BROWSER — would give N copies of the same value with N chances of diverging. An environment variable was refused for two reasons: BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE already exists and is the base of mounted projects on the SERVER side (RN-500), the namespace collision that ADR 0141 refused in writing; and under systemd --user/LaunchAgent (RN-518) the environment is the unit's, not that of the shell of whoever installed. The flag alone would not be enough either: the base would go into the ExecStart of each unit, and changing it would require rewriting them all.

--dir keeps meaning exactly what it always meant, and the base does NOT enter its validation. This is the api's prohibition transposed: project-workspaces-root.ts forbids in writing that the base rule go down into caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido, because that predicate runs on every READ and a legacy project outside the base would blow up when read — "the base is a rule of CREATION and CONVERSION; the lexicon is forever" (RN-501). On this side it holds the same: --dir stays validated by validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux + garantirDiretorio (RN-434/RN-435), and being OUTSIDE the base does not invalidate it. Without this the base would be breaking/ with no gain, against the legacy binary of RN-514. The base decides only where a NEW project folder is born.

The guard reuses the rule; a fourth copy is not born. base-guard.ts is the THIRD sibling of guard.ts, next to espelho-guard.ts: it imports semBarraFinal, dentroDoEscopo and realpathMaisProximo — the three helpers that stopped being private precisely for this (RN-516) —, repeats the lexical-then-realpath double pass of validarCwdDentroDaRaiz, and reuses validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux WHOLE to require the base inside $HOME on Linux (a base inside $HOME implies every subfolder inside it, so the two checks keep agreeing). From the loop refusal of espelho-guard.ts it reuses what is rule — dentroDoEscopo, comparison by SEGMENT and never raw startsWith, so /base-outra does not count as inside /base — and not the recusarLaco function, which throws DestinoDeEspelhoInvalidoError and would report a malformed base as a mirror problem. The same lesson as RN-515: one reuses the rule, not the message.

The loop here is ASYMMETRIC, and that is the finding. In the mirror both directions are a defect. Here the project folder INSIDE the base is the NORMAL arrangement — it is literally what "each project is a subfolder of it" means. It is the opposite direction that is a loop: a base inside this project's root (or equal to it) would make every new project be born inside this one, with this one's git and mirror starting to sweep the others. Only that one is refused.

A refusal has a different disposition per SOURCE, and none is silent. An absent base is the NORMAL state (null, the legacy intact). A base from the FLAG that does not pass the guard exits with code 2 — it is an explicit request typed just now and impossible to honor, the same disposition as a refused --dir. A base from the FILE that does not pass is stated on stderr, names what is lost ("it will have nowhere to create the folder of a new project") and the runner continues without a base: taking down a local agent serving a project because of a configuration it does not even use yet would be disproportionate. A file that exists and does not declare base is absence, not refusal — it is configuration WITHOUT a consented base, not broken configuration. And the startup line states the base in BOTH states, because omitting "none" would leave someone looking for why the folder did not appear.

This is BEST-EFFORT, and the TOCTOU caveat is inherited in writing from guard.ts and espelho-guard.ts: a symlink created AFTER the check and BEFORE the mkdir is not covered, nor a link whose target does not exist yet. The security boundary is still authentication + approval pipeline + the consent of whoever ran the CLI.

Nothing here CREATES a folder: the base validation does not require it to exist (what creates it is the installer, and it is the same reasoning as ADR 0142 — validating disk where only the lexicon is knowable would prevent consenting to a base before it exists). The only disk question is the one that is never ambiguous: a path that ALREADY exists and is not a folder will never become one.

The local agent's base gains a consumer: the project folder is born through the channel (RN-532)​

RN-532 — workspace_create creates the folder under the LOCAL base, and what WRITES is still the workspace_confirm that already existed​

RN-529 gave brabo-runner a BASE and validated it, and declared in writing that nothing consumed it. This is the consumer: the workspace_create/workspace_create_result pair, the workspace capability and an own predicate in the engine.

The pair is REQUEST WITH REPLY, and could not be modeled on workspace_confirm. That one is UNIDIRECTIONAL: handle_in("workspace_confirm", …) answers {:noreply, socket} and pushes nothing back. Whoever requests the creation of a folder needs to know whether it appeared, and with what path — so the mold is that of exec/exec_result (despachar_pedido + pending_execs + responder_pedido_pendente/3), the same as the three container pairs. A record of precision, because the name circulated: workspace.verified does not exist in this repository — what exists is the project.workspace_verified event and the column workspace_verified_at.

Only the SEGMENT crosses the network. The base is local and never comes from the server (RN-529); the engine sends projectId and the RELATIVE segment, and it is resolverPastaDoProjetoNaBase — on the runner side, which has the root — that joins them. It is the invariant of ADR 0130/ ADR 0144 applied to the local agent: whoever has the root is whoever executes. An ABSOLUTE segment is refused by LEXICON, never accepted and reinterpreted.

The confirmation REUSES workspace_confirm, and that is what saves an entire front. Having created the folder, the runner pushes the workspace_confirm that has existed since RN-423 — and it is that which writes, through the path already built: channel → engine → internal HTTP → ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase, which revalidates the lexicon, is idempotent and stamps workspace_verified_at. No new write route is born, the engine still does not write the table, and the only path that stamps remains a single one. The ORDER is the mechanism, not aesthetics: the two pushes reach the SAME channel process, in order, and the workspace_confirm handler is synchronous — sending it BEFORE the result is what guarantees the stamp already exists when the requester unblocks from the receive.

The workspace capability enters the vocabulary in the session in which the code enters, on both sides (ADR 0151 point 4). RN-514 had made the opposite bet with espelho — a name on the server without code on the other side — and it only paid off because someone called it in; repeating it would be repeating the silent defect the negotiation exists to prevent.

It is the only one of the four whose declaration depends on the STATE of that execution, and not on the binary's version. The runner only declares it when it has a consented base (capacidadesDoRunner), and it is through that line — and no other — that the server KNOWS a base exists: the engine does not read the user's disk and has no table of bases. Nobody REQUIRES it at join, and that is a decision: requiring it in runner would make every binary without a base stop connecting, which is breaking/ and MAJOR, for a function that project may never use. It is opt-in from the other end — whoever has a base declares it, and only whoever declared receives the message.

Its OWN predicate, and RunnerReadiness stays byte for byte. Engine.Runners.PastaDoProjeto has TWO preconditions — runner connected, base consented — and the ADR literally adopts the refusal that Engine.Runners.Espelho had already written: a shared function with a "skip container" flag is precisely the path by which the third precondition falls BY ACCIDENT for exec in a future refactoring (RN-507/ADR 0145 exists so that it does not fall). And here the third would be worse than unnecessary: it is circular — a runner project only comes to have a REGISTERED running container after the runner itself starts it, and the container starts over the folder this message exists to create.

It also does NOT ask for workspace_verified_at (unlike the mirror: here it is the RESULT, and requiring it would make the message unreachable precisely in the case it was made for) nor the execution_mode (the second source of the same rule — whoever has a consented base is the local agent, and a local agent only exists where it exists).

Where each precondition is answered, and why they are not both in the same place. "Runner connected" belongs to the Registry, and the module answers it on its own. "Base consented" is a property of that CONNECTION: it lives in socket.assigns and never in a table (the rule of ADR 0147), so what answers it is the dispatch — the channel refuses BEFORE pushing and returns motivo: "sem-base" through the SAME ref, in the format the module already expects, exactly as dispatch_exec does with the 126. Never a timeout, which is how the silent defect would show up. The two reasons, the two messages and the order in which they apply live in the module, and nowhere else.

A NAMED error, and five reasons that do not collapse. sem-base, segmento, nao-e-pasta, mkdir and git travel as motivo alongside the erro text — separated on purpose: the text is for a human to read, the reason is for the other side to DECIDE, and collapsing them would force the engine to match a pt-BR substring. Only sem-base becomes its own atom in the engine (:sem_base), because only it has its own fix; the other four are :recusado with the runner's message. The failing init/clone is a named error and never a plan B: a folder without .git would break the dev agent's worktree, the mirror and the user's own versioning in a place far from the cause.

Idempotent, and the three outcomes do not collapse. mkdir -p is already idempotent; what needed a decision was the repository — a folder that is ALREADY a repository comes back as SUCCESS, with the ja-era-repositorio mode, never an init on top (which would lie about what happened) nor a clone (which would fail due to a non-empty folder and turn "it was already ready" into an error). It is the same disposition as ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase, and for the same reason: the message can arrive twice.

estado.dir does NOT change. The folder created is the project's from the SERVER's point of view — and it is workspace_confirm that records it there. The root guard.ts uses to contain an approved command remains that of this execution: changing it at runtime would move a containment boundary because of a network message, and this CLI never does that.

This is NOT a proposed_action, and no ceiling gains an exception. Creating the folder of the project the user just asked for is CONSENTED configuration, not an agent asking to act — the same line the mirror already established (RN-516). Doing it through a terminal command would fall into the scope of ADR 0055 and become a queue of routine approvals, eroding the ceiling that gives the click its meaning.

The Runner mode picker reads the disk of WHOEVER CHOOSES again (RN-533)​

RN-533 — In runner mode the folder browser asks the local agent, and the screen says whose disk it is​

The creation wizard had one folder browser for two modes that read different disks. RN-504 pointed both to the api — right for mounted, whose folder lives under BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, on the SERVER — and declared the price in writing: "for runner the list stops being the disk of the user's machine and becomes the base". That was accepted because "the runner mode leaves project creation in the next PR", which did not happen: the mode is still offered, and the direction of ADR 0151 (point 7) is the opposite. While it lasted, choosing runner and clicking "Browse folder…" browsed a disk that is not that project's — and nothing on the screen said so, so the error would only show up through the list's CONTENT.

The MODE decides the transport, and they are two different questions. mounted stays byte for byte through the api (GET workspaces/:workspaceId/project-folders, hard-scoped to the base — RN-504 intact); runner goes back to fs_list_dir, which always existed on both sides and whose transport in the web never left the repository. It is not a leftover transport that gained a use: it is the question "what is on YOUR machine?", which the api has no way to answer, being asked again of whoever has a way.

The anchor of the runner mode is the EARLY creation of RN-437. The channel ticket is scoped to a real projectId, so the click creates the project before opening the modal — the original purpose of that rule, which RN-504 had left without a consumer. And failing that creation does not open the modal in any transport: falling back to the api would show the SERVER's base under the label of "your machine", exactly the defect this rule closes.

Without a connected local agent, the mode is still offered — and what declares it is the PICKER, not the mode step. RN-513 hides mounted when the base is unknown or absent, and it is right: there the api HAS a signal (GET .../projects-base), and without a base creation ends in a 400 at the end of the wizard, with no fix on the screen. Here neither of the two things holds. There is no runner presence signal in the api — RN-521 already declares that in writing —, so hiding the mode or graying out the button would be deciding "it doesn't have" from "I don't know", the collapse that RN-088/RN-468 forbid; and the mode is not broken without a runner, because the path is confirmed later, by the CLI (RN-423) — what is missing is only the NAVIGATION. So the declaration goes to the only place that actually asks: the picker, at the moment it asks.

The reason is DISCRIMINATED, and the two outcomes do not collapse. MotivoDeFalhaDoAgente is sem-agente (the engine ASSERTS there is no runner connected — a server fact) or sem-resposta (request ceiling, dropped socket, refused ticket — ignorance, and stated as ignorance on the screen). Before this rule what decided was erro?.includes('Nenhum runner conectado') in the COMPONENT — a screen matching a substring of a pt-BR sentence that lives in an .ex of the engine, exactly what RN-532 refuses in writing on the other side ("the text is for a human to read, the reason is for the other side to DECIDE"). The matching remained in one place, the module that owns the channel protocol, and the degradation is named: a sentence rewritten in the engine falls into sem-resposta — the "I don't know" state —, never into "there is an agent". The api transport never fills in motivo, and that is a decision: an api refusal is an api refusal, it has its own message that TEACHES and there is no local agent to install to fix it.

The wait is that of RN-474, REUSED and not rewritten. Both reasons lead to EsperaDoRunner — same three states (esperando/confirmado/ semResposta, which never collapse), same 3-minute CEILING, same wording, same signal (workspaceVerifiedAt CHANGING, never "existing"). It gained an optional callback because here the confirmation has a CONSEQUENCE: the listing that failed is redone on its own, instead of the person having to discover they need to click something. The callback fires ONCE per instance — without the ref, each round of the probe would re-fire it and the caller would enter a loop — and it does not assert "it is up now" (workspaceVerifiedAt never said that, RN-468): that is why whoever receives it REPEATS the request, and if the agent has already dropped again the screen goes back to the same state, honest both times. The wait is ONE per screen: RunnerOnboardingPanel gained mostrarEspera, false only where whoever mounts it already shows its own — two would be two probes, two ceilings and, in the worst case, two sentences disagreeing about the same stamp.

And the picker says WHOSE disk it is, in BOTH origins. The only signal before that was the label of a shortcut ("Projects base" × "Personal folder"), which names a place and not a machine. The api's sentence is not symmetry decoration: without it the runner's would read as an exceptional warning, when it is information both owe.

The backup covers the TWO volumes that are a source of truth, and runs without a cluster (RN-528)​

RN-528 — git_local_repos enters the backup, the destination can be disk, and the compose restore reuses the SAME three validations​

The backup covered one database and ran in one place. Three consequences, and the third is the one that costs code: make test-restore requires kubectl, a cluster and the brabo-backup CronJob in the namespace, and docker-compose.prod.yml had no backup service at all — the image was built by the bake and used only in k8s. Migrating a compose installation had no proven path.

Classify before copying. The easy move would be "back up all the volumes", and it is wrong: of the seven, neo4j_data and project_workspaces are DERIVED, ollama_data is re-obtainable and brabo_projects_base belongs to the user. Copying them gives an impression of coverage without adding recovery. Sources of truth are TWO: pgdata — which was already covered, as a logical dump and never as a copy of the data directory of a running Postgres — and git_local_repos, which no backup covered. A project with the local provider keeps the bare repository in there, and it is NOT rebuildable from Postgres: the event log keeps the narrative, not the git objects. The runbook prose said the opposite ("the real repositories live in GitHub/GitLab") and it is that sentence that explains how the volume went years without coverage — it holds for github/gitlab, and for local there is no upstream at all.

The guarantee of the repos archive is declared, and it is smaller than "snapshot". Nothing is quiesced. What is guaranteed is consistency PER REFERENCE — git writes the objects before moving the ref, and swaps the ref by atomic rename, so a tar that crosses a git push gets the old value or the new one, never half of one. What is NOT guaranteed is a global instant (the tar walks the tree over a period) nor object connectivity (the image has no git, on purpose). And a concurrent gc deleting a packfile becomes a FAILURE and not a partial archive: the status of tar is captured in a file, because in POSIX sh the status of a pipe is that of the last command — without it the incomplete archive would announce itself as good, and a backup that lies is worse than a backup that fails, because only the second becomes an alert. *.lock is left out: restoring an orphan lock produces a repository in which every git refuses to operate.

Disk destination, S3 optional. The five S3 variables stop being mandatory and become what they already were in practice — the configuration of ONE of the destinations. BACKUP_DIR set chooses disk; absent, S3, which is how the k8s CronJob keeps running without a single line of change. The inference (instead of a mandatory destination variable) is what keeps that path intact: an explicit destination would break the CronJob on deploy day, not on commit day. Four prefixes and not two (daily/, weekly/, git-daily/, git-weekly/) because retention is by COUNT: two kinds of archive under one prefix would make "keep 7" mean three and a half backups.

The compose restore changes the wrapper, never the judgment. test-restore-compose.sh triggers a REAL backup through the same image and the same production command, and calls the SAME brabo-restore, with the SAME three validations (table list against the source, count of the critical ones in the backup window, dense continuity of the seq of session_events). deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh stays intact — unifying them would make the compose path depend on kubectl, which is the dependency it exists not to have. And restore.sh still does not touch the SOURCE database, a property that is not negotiated for migration convenience. The step only compose can demand is the third: verifying the repos archive, because in k8s that volume is not even mounted in the pod (skipping is correct) and under compose it is (skipping would be a false green).

Restoring the repos is a SIBLING command, not a phase of the other — they are two artifacts with two judgments, and joining them would make a git failure fail the validation of the event log. It verifies by default and only writes with --restaurar; it refuses to extract over existing repos (the mix of two states raises no error and only shows up in a fetch with the wrong history); and — a finding of the real execution — it refuses BEFORE the tar when the volume does not accept writes, naming --user 0:0. git_local_repos is shared by three images with different uids and carries the owner of whoever mounted it first (measured: 1000:1000, mode 0755) while this image runs as uid 70. When the extraction runs as root, what comes out is handed back to the DIRECTORY's owner and never left as root: otherwise the volume would come back intact and useless, with api and engine unable to write to what was just restored.

Neo4j gets reprojection, not backup. Restoring a possibly old projection next to a Postgres restored at another instant gives two derived states from different moments, with nothing reconciling them. The reprojection was not built here (it is BRB-018): until it exists, a migrated installation is born with an EMPTY graph — known and named degradation, not data loss, because the RAG lives in pgvector and comes in the dump. Since RN-569 it exists (grafo:reprojetar), and the empty graph now lasts until someone runs it.

Provisioning does not converge within the screen's ceilingthe wait STOPS at 3 minutes, declares that this does not prove failure and offers to look again — without firing a second POST (RN-477)
Applying a model to all agents and the api refusing PART of themthe rows that passed stay written and are re-read; the warning says how many out of how many and NAMES those that remained — never "saved" nor "not saved", which would both be lies (RN-476)
INSERT of the RAG search telemetry failsthe search answers anyway, with searchId: null, and the failure becomes a log with origin infra — the measuring instrument does not take down what it measures, and it does not vanish silently either (RN-479)
Vote on a searchId/chunkId that that search did not returna 400 that teaches, nothing recorded — a vote without rank does not distinguish "poor index" from "wrong weights", and a meaningless number is worse than no number (RN-480)
medir:rag over a window in which vector_available was false the whole timefails (exit 1): what was measured is not the hybrid search, it is its lexical half, and calibrating the vector weight against that would be calibrating against another system (RN-479)
route_modules_to_infra called without a current module_map, with an empty list, a repeated module, a module outside the map, or an invalid image (latest/no tag/short rationale)400 naming what is missing or what is wrong — via the agent, an error tool-result the model fixes, never a crash (RN-487)
container_start elects an image outside the candidates of the Arquiteto's current routingthe action becomes failed naming the refused image and listing the valid candidates — neither is the image decided nor is the broker called (RN-491)
Broker refuses or is unavailable when starting the container (BrokerRecusouError/BrokerIndisponivelError)the action becomes failed with the broker's message — never propagates, never stays pending (RN-491)
emit_artifact with type: decision_record missing context/options/choice/consequenceserror tool-result naming the missing key(s) — the model fixes it on the next turn of the loop, never a crash (RN-505)
Terminal/worktree in a runner project verified and connected, but WITHOUT a running containerNAMED refusal (RunnerReadiness), never falls back to the bare host — Docker is a real prerequisite, with no fallback (RN-507)
RunnerGit tries to materialize the worktree without the three preconditions of RN-507raises with a named message BEFORE any exec — never tries blindly and lets the channel timeout explain (RN-507)
Periodic worktree cleanup job finds a runner project without a connected runner or without a running containerSKIPS the project this round, silently — never an error, never stops pruning the other projects (RN-507)
container_start_via_runner proposed for a container/mounted project, or runner without a connected runnerthe Infra Lead REFUSES locally, naming the reason, without calling propose_action even once (RN-508)
container_start_via_runner approved without a decided image (RN-105)the action becomes failed naming the absence of a decision — never calls the engine (RN-508)
Runner connected to a project whose execution_mode requires a capability it did not declare at joinjoin refused naming the capability and telling to update the binary — a fatal refusal, no retry, never silent degradation (RN-514)
Runner that declares a capability THIS server does not knowthe name is ignored and the join passes — a runner newer than the engine connects (RN-514)
exec dispatched to a runner that did not declare the exec capabilityanswers the caller in the same exec_result format, with exitCode 126 and the cause in output — never lets the RunnerRouter wait until the timeout (RN-514)
pty_* relayed to a runner that did not declare the pty capabilitythe message is NOT delivered and the :web receives a named pty_error — never "loading" forever (RN-514)
Mirror destination inside the project's workspacePath, or containing it400 naming the direction of the loop — both are the same refusal, and the comparison is by SEGMENT, so /base-outra does NOT count as inside /base (RN-515)
Mirror destination declared in an execution_mode: container project400 NAMING the reason (the source is a server volume, the local agent does not see it) — never accept and never copy (RN-515)
PUT .../mirror-path without the mirrorPath key in the body400 — omitting would be indistinguishable from asking to CLEAR, and clearing silently is the defect; clearing is an explicit null (RN-515)
brabo-runner service install run as rootnamed refusal, without writing a file or running a command — the service is a user one by design, and a root one would break the premise of the product's three boundaries (RN-518)
brabo-runner service <qualquer> on Windows (or on any platform other than Linux/macOS)refusal naming the platform, saying the decision is declared and pointing to the foreground — never a mute failure, never an "installed" that did not install (RN-518)

"Start" clicked on a project without a decided artifact.project_imagethe button does not even become active: the screen SAYS the image remains to be decided, in text, instead of proposing an action already known to end in failure (RN-521/RN-105)
