The device key gets a screen, and the screen states the reach of revoking (RN-561)​

RN-561 — The Settings tab lists and revokes device keys, marking the KIND — because revoking the MACHINE one takes down the local agent in ALL the owner's projects​

The missing half of RN-519, declared in writing ever since in CLAUDE.md: "what remains open is only the SCREEN: apps/web has nowhere to list nor revoke, so whoever wants to revoke calls the route". Both routes exist — the DELETE since ADR 0118 and the GET since RN-519 —, and no screen used them. This RN is the screen, and it opens no new route: what the listing already returns is enough to draw everything that follows.

Where it lives, and why PROJECT. It takes the Settings tab from 17 to 18 sections and is the 13th in render order (device-keys, group pessoas, right after access-tokens — the neighbor that does the same with PATs); the registry's order is the SAME as the barrel's, because it is what the scroll-spy uses. Project because the endpoint is /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys: an ACCOUNT screen would require a new route, and the scope is about the one that exists.

The KIND shows up, and it is not decoration — it is the reach of the screen's only irreversible action. Since RN-543 the listing marks projeto | maquina, and a MACHINE key (null project_id) serves all the owner's projects and that is why it shows up in the list of ALL of them. Showing it without the mark would make the screen assert it is "this project's key", and whoever clicked revoke would think it takes down the local agent here when it takes it down in all of them — the screen would lie precisely about what can least be wrong. The mark is warning for the machine one and muted for the project one, and never success: green would read as "it's up", which is the arithmetic RN-548 already refused.

The confirmation DEPENDS on the kind, and also states the collateral cost. Revoking opens a dialog with THREE sentences, and the middle one is the one that changes: the machine one names all your projects in runner mode (the loop of RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase over listRunnerModeReachableBy), the project one names its project. A single text for both would lie in one of the halves. The third sentence is the cost RN-520 declared and this delivery does not change: the disconnection target is {projeto, usuário} and never {chave}, so another runner of the same user on the same project also drops — even authenticated by a PAT or another key — and reconnects on its own if its credential is still valid.

Recorded use is NOT an agent up, and the vocabulary is the SAME as RN-548. lastUsedAt is the data class of workspaceVerifiedAt (RN-468): the record of a confirmation, never a heartbeat. The caveat is stated in TEXT in the caption, and the status column talks about REVOCATION ("active"/"revoked", a fact about the row), never about connection — what knows about NOW is still the terminal's channel. Inventing a second vocabulary for the same distinction would be the screen saying the same thing in two ways, and one of the two would age.

Five states, and none becomes the other (RN-088/RN-470). No key ("No device key of yours serves this project"), a REVOKED key (which stays in the list by RN-519's decision — making the row disappear would make the screen assert it never existed, and it gets no button because revoking again, even if idempotent in the api, would suggest an effect that did not remain), NULL lastUsedAt (the ORPHAN key of RN-473: registered by a tab that closed in the middle of the flow and never used by any runner — its own text, and an explanation below the table that only shows up when there is one, because explaining what does not occur is noise), "not loaded yet" and "I could not read". "I don't know" never becomes "it doesn't have".

The role is the ENDPOINT's, and it is the project's EFFECTIVE one. The minimum is developer — what RunnerDeviceKeysController requires on the THREE routes (RN-102) — and the comparison comes from the SAME function RN-548 created (podeLerChavesDeDispositivo, over roleAtLeast), never a second rule and never a hand-written role === 'x' || role === 'y'. What changes in relation to RN-548 is the INPUT: there the panel read the WORKSPACE role and declared the gap, because it mounts in places that do not fetch project_members; here the data is at hand — the section lives in the same tab as MembersSection, with the SAME queryKey, and react-query deduplicates —, so the role is composed as in the use case (projectRole ?? workspaceRole, an OVERLAY in both directions, RN-471) and the gap closes instead of repeating itself. An ABSENT role is not an INSUFFICIENT role: while the member list is in flight the screen says it is verifying, and does not accuse the reader of not reaching developer. Whoever does not reach it still sees the whole section, what a device key is and what revoking the machine one costs — the CONTROL disappears, never the INFORMATION (ADR 0064) —, and the reason is stated ONCE in TEXT (title on a disabled element does not open in Chromium). Since the three routes require the SAME role, whoever does not reach it also does not see the LIST: the screen stops asking what the api would deny, instead of turning a predictable 403 into "I could not read". This is not a security boundary — what refuses is the RolesGuard.

One at a time, and that is why there is no batch outcome. The screen does not offer "revoke all", so the rule of RN-469 — a UI action that becomes N calls is not a transaction, and the screen says so — does not apply: offering the batch would create a partial outcome to narrate for an action nobody asked for. A failure in revocation shows the api's OWN sentence and the row stays in the list.

RN-566 — The Infra Lead refuses container_start by MODE before proposing: the gap of RN-494 closes in the tool that declared it​

propose_container_start proposed blindly. dispatch_container_start/2 assembled the payload and called EngineApiClient.propose_action(...) directly — without a project read between one thing and the other, and with zero occurrences of execution_mode in the whole tool. In a runner project the proposal could only end in failure: since RN-507/ADR 0145 container_start does not serve that mode, because its payload ELECTS a candidate from the Arquiteto's routing (ADR 0131) and in runner there is no routing to elect against — that mode's type is container_start_via_runner.

The rule is not new, and a second one was not born. The sibling tool already refused locally (RN-508) and the /containers page already branched by DESTINATION (RN-521, acaoDeSubidaDoModo): container and mounted come up via the BROKER, runner comes up via the local agent (ADR 0144/RN-503). What this rule does is give the missing tool the SAME rule — one project read (recusa_local_de_subida/2, which returns nil or a reason) and one CLAUSE per tool (recusa_por_modo/3). Two parallel rules would diverge on the first new mode of the enum.

The refusal of container_start is an ALLOWLIST, like the broker's own: container/mounted pass, runner is refused NAMING the sibling tool, and a new mode in the enum is born refused with a message instead of proposed by omission. A nonexistent project also refuses — the same clause for both tools.

The refusal is an INPUT to the loop (RN-163): tool RESULT text, which the model reads and uses to call the right tool. Never agent.error, never end of turn, never proposed_action — the api is not called. And it is not silence: the emit of tool.call now happens BEFORE the refusal in BOTH tools (in the sibling it was inside the branch that proposes), as in the generic dispatch_tool/2 of the same module — a refusal without a trace in the event log is the call vanishing from the human's timeline.

The reads are LOCAL, and that is the decision. Project.get/1 and Engine.Runners.Registry.connected?/1 run in the SAME BEAM process as the Infra Lead; an HTTP call to the api here would put a network call inside the agent's loop. The cost declared in CLAUDE.md — "fixing it would require touching the Infra Lead's prompt/instruction" — was not confirmed: no prompt line changed, and the refusal text is what the model reads as a result.

What this rule does NOT close, and it is half the gap: the blind proposal due to ABSENCE OF IMAGE remains possible in container/mounted. The refusal here is about MODE, and requiring a decided image would invert the order — electing the image is precisely what that proposal DOES (RN-491). /containers checks the THREE things (decided image, mode, confirmed folder) because it has a human clicking; the agent comes to check ONE. GetInfraContextUseCase stays without executionMode — enriching the Infra Lead's context is a separate front. container_stop/container_remove do not come in: they are proposed by the screen, never by an agent (RN-495).

No ceiling changes: container_start remains a real proposed_action, maintainer, never seeded into auto-approval (until RN-671, which seeds it on accepting the Infra handoff), and container_remove stays at the absolute ceiling of git push/privileged command (RN-418).

RN-565 — The signed manifest goes out with what the Release HAS, and does not wait for the platform that never builds​

The signed checksums.txt (RN-524) is the precondition of two other rules: without it, GET /runner-releases/binary refuses with release_sem_manifesto (RN-525) and install.sh refuses itself (RN-526) — on all platforms, including those that attached a binary properly. A manifest that is late is not a late manifest: for whoever installs in that interval, it is an absent manifest.

The measurement, against the three tags that exist. In v4.0.0, v4.0.1 and v5.0.0, the darwin-x64 target (macos-13) spent 24h00m01s in the queue and was cancelled by the Actions ceiling — the SAME number in all three, which says it never gets scheduled. The other four jobs end in at most 4m18s (linux-x64 in v4.0.1, 17:38:28Z → 17:42:44Z). The checksums job had needs: build: the always() guaranteed that it RAN (a cancelled dependency is covered), never WHEN.

The rule: the manifest job does not depend on the matrix. It waits for the Release's ASSETS, not the JOBS — with a ceiling —, and publishes whatever exists, naming in the log what it does not cover. The absence of a target is a foreseen outcome (::notice::), never an error; the absence of the Release remains a named error, because this workflow only ATTACHES and never creates; and no attached binary remains an error, because an empty checksums.txt would assert that the release has no binaries when what happened was the whole matrix failing.

The binaries ceiling is 1200s, and the number is not arbitrary: it is the timeout-minutes: 20 of the build job itself — the most a target with a runner can take after starting. What it deliberately does not cover is queue time, and not covering queue time is the whole point. The loop exits early when all targets arrive, which is the happy path.

Nothing the job DOES changes. It still builds the manifest from the assets (and not from dist-bin/, empty there), signing with keyless cosign and verifying before attaching — RN-524 intact, one manifest and not five signatures. And a target that attaches AFTER the ceiling is not orphaned: the --clobber already existed for that, and redoing the manifest is a workflow_dispatch with the same tag.

What this rule does NOT do: darwin-x64 still does not build. Changing the label, removing the platform or paying for a runner is the owner's decision, and the manifest cannot depend on it — it is precisely because it depended on it that it did not come out.

Measured later, in AT-065 (2026-09-13, by a rehearsal workflow_dispatch): macos-13 is a label without a runner (image retired by GitHub in Dec/2025; 30min in the queue, cancelled, run 34769280227). macos-15-intel schedules in 3–22s and builds, but fails at --self-test-pty because, under Bun, the onData of node-pty does not deliver the child's output (oven-sh/bun#25822, open); the same proof passes under Node on the same runner (run 34770476634). The pending decision stopped being about the runner and became waiting for Bun or removing the platform. The rule above does not change because of that.

Decided on 2026-09-27 (ADR 0174, AT-065): the platform left. The matrix went to FOUR targets, and ALVOS_ESPERADOS followed — it is against it that the absence is declared, and leaving darwin-x64 there would make every manifest announce, forever, a gap that is a decision. The Mac Intel stays with npm install -g @brabo/runner (under Node, where the same proof passes): install.sh says so without trying to download, the GET /runner-releases/binary proxy refuses darwin-x64 with its own 400 pointing to npm, and the browser panel does not even ask for the download. This RN's rule does not change: it keeps holding for any target left without a runner, and scripts/ci/alvos-do-runner.spec.ts fails when the matrix, the api's list, the installer's case and the browser's diverge.

RN-567 — proposed_action.created says WHICH rule decided: the reason of decide() now survives when the action passes​

decide() always returned a pair — policy and reason —, and the reason is written at every return point: insufficient IAM, the container floor (RN-492), agent_autonomy, the lines of permissions.json, the compound command, and each absolute ceiling. But ProposeActionUseCase only kept it in one place: rejectionReason, which initialStatusFor fills in only when the policy denies. On an auto-approval — the outcome that most needs auditing — the event log said "the policy decided" (RN-049) and never which rule. status made auto-approval distinguishable from a click; the reason is the next step.

The rule: the payload of the SESSION event proposed_action.created gains reason, with the string from decide() as is, in all THREE outcomes — auto_approved, pending and denied. No second "structured" rule is born: the string is already the source, and a parallel enum would diverge from it on the first new ceiling. In denied the value is the SAME that becomes rejectionReason.

The outbox does NOT gain the field, and that is a decision. The outbox row proposed_action.created is an api↔engine contract, and no engine consumer reads the reason; widening a contract without a consumer is the cut that ADR 0153 names. The session_event.appended row that AppendSessionEventUseCase writes for the same event carries only eventId/seq/type, so the reason also does not leak through it.

Absent is not "no reason". An event written before this rule does not have the field, and there is no reprocessing nor new column: whoever reads treats an absent reason as "not recorded". Every new event has the field, because Decision.reason is a mandatory string in the type.

Nothing in decide() changes — no ceiling, no verdict, no string. The screen also does not change in this rule: the reason comes to EXIST in the log, and showing it is another delivery. (Since RN-614 the screen shows it on the event's line in the log panel and in the ApprovalCard, through the same sentence.)

What the reason does NOT say, declared: it names the rule, not the scope's ROOT — point 7 of ADR 0055 asked for which root authorized, and escopo: cd dentro da pasta do projeto does not carry the path. (The root started going in the event in its OWN field since RN-609, relative and never absolute.) In the compound command, the reason says all segments hit allow, without saying which pattern matched which segment. And the lines of permissions.json repeat the command's TOKENS in the text (the label of matchAgainstFile) — the same command that already lives in proposed_actions.payload and on the approval card.

RN-568 — The presence of QA, SecOps and the area members in the team panel is decided by the WHOLE session, not by the 200-event window​

The Overview and the Executors tab build the roster with deriveAgentRoster over the session's LAST 200 events (useSessionEvents, latest: true). Two of the presence facts came from that window: gatesEverOpened (qa and secops come in when some pr.gate_changed/infra.gate_changed has already happened) and delegatedSubagents (an area member comes in with a recorded delegation). Both events are among the first of an execution — in a long session they leave the window, and QA, SecOps and qa-automacao vanished from the panel of an execution that kept running. It is the same class of defect that had already been closed for executionActivated, and the workspace summary (RN-090) already aggregated both facts over the whole session (bool_or and selectDistinct in projects-summary.repository.ts) — both screens loaded it and ignored those two fields.

The rule: deriveAgentRoster/rosterFactsFromEvents accept an OPTIONAL agregado (AgregadoDaSessao), and both screens fill it with the summary. Four decisions, each with a reason:

  1. Absent is "I did not read", never "there was none". Without a loaded summary (first paint, error), the fact comes only from the window, exactly as before. An absent read never becomes "QA is not here".
  2. The aggregate ADDS to the window, it does not replace it (logical OR on the gate, union on the delegations). Both facts are MONOTONIC within a session — a gate that opened does not un-open, a recorded delegation does not disappear —, so the window only produces false NEGATIVES, never false positives. An aggregated false that disagrees with a gate SEEN in the window is a late summary (the two reads have their own poll cadences), and cannot hide QA.
  3. It only holds when the summary is of the SAME session the screen reads (latestSessionId === sessionId). The summary aggregates the project's most RECENT session; the Overview reads that same session, but the Executors tab reads the current EXECUTION session (RN-139). An ideation opened afterwards makes the two diverge, and then the aggregate would be of ANOTHER session — the screen goes back to deciding only by the window.
  4. Only PRESENCE changes. rosterFromFacts (the single rule, shared with the dashboard card) stays intact, and each agent's STATUS (gateStatus, subagentStatus) is still read from the window. No new request and the 200 ceiling does not change.

delegatedSubagents came in through the SAME mold because it fits without changing a rule: the delegations table the summary reads and the delegation.* events the window reads are born together in RecordDelegationUseCase (one row, one event, the three outcomes), so the two sets describe the same thing.

executionActivated (AT-130). It is the third fact of the same mold: the Executors tab read it from the summary WITHOUT the guard of item 3, so with a session newer than the execution one the summary (of it) said false and the dev agents vanished — or true, and they appeared without proof. Now it goes in agregado.executionActivated only when latestSessionId === sessionId, and deriveAgentRoster ADDS it (logical OR, monotonic) to the window and to the parameter, which also starts looking at execution.activated in the events. No new field in the API. Tests: ProjectExecutorsTab.test.tsx (summary of ANOTHER session, in both directions). Still open: with a long execution session AND the summary of another session, the event may have left the window and the tab goes back to deciding only by it — it is the cost of the guard, the same as for the other two facts.

RN-569 — The graph is rebuilt from the event log by the SAME translator as the live projector, without touching the outbox, and never comes out as a silent success​

ADR 0152 (decision 4) refused a backup of neo4j_data based on a premise — the graph can be discarded because it can be rebuilt — whose mechanism did not exist: grep for reprojet/reproject in apps/ and scripts/ came back empty, and application/graph-projection/ only had the FORWARD projector. While it did not exist, the graph was not discardable: it was lost.

The rule: apps/api/src/scripts/reprojetar-grafo.ts (pnpm --filter api grafo:reprojetar; node scripts/reprojetar-grafo.js in the image) rebuilds the graph by sweeping the source. Five decisions, each with a reason:

  1. A single translator. The event → node/edge translation LEFT GraphProjector for GraphEventTranslator, and both paths call it — the projector reaches the source through an outbox row, the reprojection through a cursor. Two translators would diverge, and the divergent one would be the one that runs once a year. The projector's injection surface did NOT change (it builds the translator with the dependencies it already received). A test fails a new type in GRAPH_PROJECTABLE_EVENT_TYPES without a translation.
  2. The sources are two, and they are the real ones. handoff.offered, psychologist.hypothesis_proposed and anamnese.profile_updated come from session_events; the Interacao comes from sessions in closed/closed_abnormally, because closing a session is a pure transition and leaves no event in the log. PromptTemplate/PromptVersion do NOT come from the event log and are NOT reprojected — they come back through scripts/dev/seed-prompts.ts.
  3. Idempotent, in batches, and never deletes. Every write is a MERGE on a natural key; running again is the way to resume. session_events is swept in id order (ULID, the primary key), 200 per batch, and --after-event resumes after the printed cursor. With --project, only that project's sessions.
  4. It does not touch the outbox. The live projector keeps its progress in outbox_events.processed_at; the reprojection neither reads nor writes that table, and that is why it runs with the api up without stealing, reopening or marking rows.
  5. Never a silent success. A disabled graph is refused BEFORE reading the log (an empty scope "would pass" with zero projected); a Neo4j that drops midway stops with the last completed event; a nonexistent project is refused without writing anything; and an item with an incoherent payload is counted, named, and the process exits with 1.

What this rule does NOT close: PerfilAnamnese is a snapshot per user + dimension, WITHOUT a project — the last to write wins —, so a round with --project may leave it at that project's value when another wrote later; the full round restores the global last one. There is no time measurement on a large event log (the only real round was the dev compose, 98 events, 2.5 s), and the proof on the local cluster that BRB-018 asks for was not done — it remains open.

RN-570 — The installer brings up the installation only with files the Release signed, checked before asking or writing anything​

RN-549 measured, the first time the installer ran on a clean machine, that the published install.sh brought up nothing on its own: it called docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.install.yml, a path RELATIVE to the directory it ran from, and that file was not a Release asset, did not enter the signed checksums.txt and was not downloaded anywhere. Whoever followed the runbook's one-liner died in "no such file or directory" AFTER the script had written the .env with the secrets. The maintainer decided the way out on 2026-09-13 — a signed asset, and not a clone (ADR 0160).

The rule:

  1. Four files travel with the installer, in the SAME manifest. The installation compose and the three the installation uses by relative path — the postgres/init.sql and the ollama/pull-models.sh that the compose bind-mounts, and the backup/test-restore-compose.sh that the migration (RN-530) executes — are published as brabo-install-* assets by the checksums job and enter the sha256sum that generates the signed checksums.txt. The fourth was not in the E2E's workaround and was found while implementing: in a folder without a checkout the migration would die there. The job checks each manifest line against the file (sha256sum -c --strict) before attaching.
  2. The table has two sides and a guard. The publisher reads scripts/ci/assets-do-instalador.ts; the downloader reads the case of destino_do_asset_do_instalador in install.sh (bash 3.2, without Node). The spec fails the divergence between the two AND derives from the compose every ./… bind-mount that is not in the table — which is exactly how the defect was born.
  3. Verifying comes right after its own origin, and before everything. The installer downloads the four and compares each sha256 against the checksums.txt that verificar_a_si_mesmo already verified (never a second download), by EXACT name equality. The three refusals are distinct — asset not published, manifest that does not cover it, hash that does not match — and all happen with the machine untouched.
  4. It never falls back to the relative path. COMPOSE_DE_INSTALACAO is born EMPTY and only gets an absolute path when the verified copies are put under the installation's folder, at the first instant they are needed (the migration or the startup). Whatever is already there is REPLACED, never read — with rm before the cp, so a symlink does not carry the write outside.

What this rule does NOT close: the end-to-end proof only happens on the first final tag after the merge — install-e2e.yml does not run on PRs (ADR 0150) —, and no already published Release gains the assets: they stay with the old installer and the workaround of running it from inside a checkout at the tag. The adjacency ADR 0160 declared — test-restore-compose.sh called Compose without --env-file, and Compose looks for the .env in the compose's folder — closed in AT-102: the installer passes BRABO_ENV_FILE (--env-file, and not --project-directory, which would also change the project's name and the base of the relative paths) and the installation compose declares the backup_local volume that the backup service references, whose absence refused the whole file with the profile on. Covered by scripts/dev/prova-de-restauracao-env.spec.ts.

RN-572 — The team tree translates every dev.* type the engine emits, and only states work in progress where the panel says trabalhando​

In a real installation (09/14) the dev agents "did not get past started the task". The event log had dev.started followed by dev.blocked_by_container, with the reason spelled out (RN-502). The team tree (timeline-tree.ts) had no translation for the block — what is not in TRADUCAO is discarded —, so the branch stopped at the previous milestone and the present sentence asserted work about a stopped agent. The team panel, on the same execution screen, already said aguardando for the same event (DEV_STATUS_EVENTS, RN-411): two screens, two tables, and only one of them was covered by the comparison with the engine's vocabulary.

The rule, in three parts:

  1. Every dev.* type the engine emits has a decision in the tree — translated in TRADUCAO or declared in TRADUCAO_FORA with the reason (empty today). Omitting stopped being possible: scripts/ci/vocabulario-de-eventos-dev.spec.ts derives the engine's vocabulary through the same extractor as the event inventory and fails, naming the type, whatever is missing; and it also fails a translated dev.* type the engine does not emit. On the first round it found TWO missing (dev.blocked_by_container and dev.error) and ONE extra (dev.rearmed, which the api writes with actor user and which is why it never reached any branch — the tree only hangs milestones of actor agent).
  2. Whether a dev agent's last milestone is work in progress is not decided in the tree. For a dev.* milestone, the branch only stays ACTIVE when the panel gives trabalhando to the same event (statusDoEventoDev, read from DEV_STATUS_EVENTS). aguardando, ocioso, falhou and travado leave the branch stopped — and with them dev.idle, dev.blocked, dev.awaiting_gate, dev.awaiting_approval and dev.idle_tripped, which before also counted as active. A dev.* type the panel did not decide does NOT become active: when in doubt the screen does not assert work.
  3. The container block is its own milestone (espera, color warning, the same as the gate), with the engine's reason as detail — it is what says what to do. And dev.started stops saying "started the task": measured in the engine, it goes out on RECEIVING the order to work, before try_claim (DevAgentServer.handle_cast(:work)); it now says "looking for a task", and what asserts the task is dev.working, which now shows its title.

What this rule does NOT do, and why:

  • container.start_failed does not enter the tree. It is the reason for the block, but the actor is system (action-executor): hanging it on a dev agent's branch would be inventing authorship, and the only other place in the structure, the tronco, IS NOT RENDERED by any consumer (measured: AgentTimelineTree and the Activities section of the Shell only read ramos). The event stays in the chronological log, one click away, and the blocked branch already says, through the reason, that the container needs to be started.

  • The tree's labels stayed in fixed pt-BR in this fix — migrating them was a change to the whole screen. AT-134 did that migration later, and it did NOT touch the rule above: the DECISION per type (whether it becomes a node, which MarcoTipo, which detail) stays in TRADUCAO, in the code, and it is what the spec compares with the engine; only the TEXT left, as a KEY (ChaveDeRotulo) resolved in executors:timelineTree.label.*, with the present sentence in timelineTree.now.* and the origin detail in timelineTree.detail.origin, in both languages (en is the default, RN-425). montarArvore receives the language as an argument (getFixedT), and the two consumers (AgentTimelineTree and the Activities section of the Shell) pass it from useTranslation — switching language rebuilds the tree. A key the table uses without text in one of the two locales fails in timeline-tree.test.ts.

RN-573 — The creation wizard only preselects the mode the installation executes: without a broker, runner is the suggested one and container/mounted stay inert with the reason in text​

In a real installation of v6.1.0 (AT-085), the wizard preselected mounted — install.sh always writes BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, and with a known base RN-513 preselected the mode. But the installation by Release has no container broker (the image is not published, decision 7 of ADR 0150), and container/mounted only start a container through the broker (RN-503). Result: six dev.blocked_by_container and two container.start_failed — nobody works on the project, forever (RN-502).

The rule (ADR 0161):

  1. The api says whether there is a broker, on the route the wizard already reads. GET workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base now returns brokerConfigurado next to projectsBase — the same question ("what mode does this INSTALLATION execute?"), the same minimum (maintainer), no new route. The source is ContainerBrokerPort.configurado(), the same as the read of the observed state. It says BROKER_URL exists, never that the broker answers.
  2. Three states, which do not collapse. Broker confirmed: RN-513 intact. Confirmed absence: container and mounted stay on the screen, inert (the control leaves, the information stays — RN-102), the reason is stated ONCE in text below the cards, and runner is the preselected one. I don't know (loading, failing query, absent field): does not become "it has" — mounted is NOT preselected, the revision of RN-513 — and also does not become "it doesn't have": no card locks and nothing is asserted in text; container stays selected, as before.
  3. The human choice does not point to what does not run. Whoever clicked a mode before the answer arrived, and the answer confirms it does not execute here, falls to runner — the same rule that already knocked mounted down when the base disappears.

What this rule does NOT close: the mode conversion (RN-559) still offers container/mounted in an installation without a broker; the installer does not ask whether to turn the broker on, because its image cannot be obtained by a Release installation (measured — see ADR 0161); and in the development compose, which brings up the broker by default (RN-512) but leaves BROKER_URL empty until someone puts it in .env, the warning shows up — and it is right, because without the variable the api never calls the broker.

RN-574 — /containers refuses before the click the start of container/mounted in an installation without a broker, with its own reason in text​

The same installation of AT-085 allowed approving, through the containers page (RN-521), two container_start that could only end failed with BrokerIndisponivelError. The page already refused locally what it knew would fail — no image, runner without a confirmed folder, role below maintainer — and did not know about this one.

The rule (ADR 0161):

  1. The list says whether there is a broker, on every row. GET workspaces/:workspaceId/containers gains brokerConfigurado per row, with the SAME value in all of them, read ONCE per load — it is the installation's configuration, and swapping the list for an envelope would break the contract.
  2. A fourth refusal reason, sem_broker_na_instalacao, for container and mounted when brokerConfigurado !== true ("I don't know" does not become "it has"). It comes right after "already up" and BEFORE "no image decided": in an installation with nobody to start the container, telling to decide the image would be pointing to the wrong door. The text says what (this installation does not start containers for these two modes), why (no broker, empty BROKER_URL) and what is not affected (runner).
  3. runner never falls into it. What depends on the broker is decided by the SAME branching by destination of acaoDeSubidaDoModo (usaBroker), not by a second rule.

What this rule does NOT close: stop and remove did not get the refusal (without a broker there is no registered container/mounted container up to stop, and the case was not measured), and the Infra Lead still does not know about an absent broker — it refuses by MODE (RN-566), and proposing container_start in an installation without a broker remains possible by the agent.

The container broker in the installation, with consent (RN-575)​

RN-575 — The installer only turns on the container broker with a typed "s", measures the socket's group from inside a container, and writes the four lines together or none​

In an installation by Release, a container or mounted project never executed: what starts the container of those two modes is the broker (ADR 0144), and the installation did not have the service because the image was not published (ADR 0150, decision 7). ADR 0162 publishes the image as the fifth and puts the service in the installation compose, OFF; this rule is what decides when it turns on, because turning it on hands the machine's Docker socket to an installation service.

The rule:

  1. Only a typed "s"/"sim" turns it on. The question comes after the base (the broker's second root derives from it) and before the .env, and SAYS in text what it grants — this machine's Docker socket, and that whoever commands the broker commands Docker — and what contains it. Enter, any other answer and the lack of a terminal leave it off, and the lack of a terminal is STATED, never decided silently. While the answer is not yes, Docker is not touched.
  2. The socket's group is MEASURED, from inside a container, with the broker's own image, no network, read-only rootfs and the socket mounted by --mount type=bind — which refuses a nonexistent source instead of creating a folder on the host, as -v would. It is the gid seen from inside that group_add needs (in Docker Desktop the host's says nothing). A measurement that fails, a path that is not a socket or a gid that is not a number are a named REFUSAL, which teaches to run again answering no — never the compose default's 999.
  3. The four lines go together or none goes: COMPOSE_PROFILES=container-broker, BROKER_URL=http://broker:8090, DOCKER_GID and PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT. A profile without a URL brings up a broker nobody calls; a URL without a profile points the api to a service that does not come up. escrever_env refuses to write the block without the measured gid — a defect of the script, not of the machine. BRABO_BROKER_IMAGE is ALWAYS written, on or not: Compose interpolates the whole file before filtering by profile.
  4. The managed folder's root is COMPUTED and then CHECKED. Before startup, <DockerRootDir>/volumes/brabo_project_workspaces/_data; after, compared with the volume's Mountpoint. Diverging, or the api not reaching the broker over the internal network, becomes a named PENDING item at the end — never a refusal, which would take down an installation that is up because of a step fixed by editing the .env.
  5. The decision shows up in the final summary, in both directions, and the sentence about what the installer does NOT do stops saying that only the Mounted folder stays without a container: container does too.

What this rule does NOT close: the DOCKER_GID and the computed root were not measured on Docker Desktop for macOS, and the tag's E2E runs the interactive half only on Linux. Rootless or remote Docker does not have the socket at /var/run/docker.sock, which is the path the compose mounts, and falls into the refusal of item 2 — turning the broker on there is not offered by another path.

RN-577 — open_adr_pr and open_infra_pr are refused by the agent, before proposing, when the project has no repository​

In a real installation (AT-088, 2026-09-14), a project without a repository — project_repositories, project_git_connections and repo_bootstraps empty — received three open_adr_pr from the Arquiteto and one open_infra_pr from the Infra Lead. The human approved all four, and all four ended failed with "Projeto sem repositório provisionado" (ExecuteAdrPrUseCase, ExecuteInfraPrUseCase). The person approved four actions that could only fail.

It is not an edge, it is the common case. Since RN-541 creating a project does not create a repository, and the repository's trigger is accepting the handoff from the Arquiteto to the Dev Lead (RN-522). The Arquiteto works BEFORE that handoff — so in a new project every open_adr_pr failed by construction.

The rule: both tools ask, BEFORE proposing, whether the project has a repository, and without it they REFUSE with a NAMED reason — what is missing, and when it comes to exist. The proposed_action is not born, and the approval queue does not receive what cannot succeed.

The mold is that of RN-566, with no new rule and without touching the prompt. The refusal is a tool result (RN-163), an input to the loop — never agent.error, never end of turn —, and the model continues the turn reading the reason.

The read is LOCAL, and the predicate is the SAME as the execution's. The engine already read project_repositories directly from Postgres (Engine.Projects.ProjectRepository, the consumers of default_branch/1 and remoto_de_trabalho/1), so there was no HTTP in the agent's loop to measure or justify: the new question, recusa_de_pr_sem_repositorio/2, is the SAME one ProvisionedRepositoryRepository.findByProjectId asks in the two use cases — there is a row for the project. If the two diverged, the tool would let through what the execution refuses, or would refuse what it would accept. Both tools use the SAME function, with the same text.

In the Infra Lead the question comes before the HALT. propose_infra_pr does not propose on the spot: it interrupts the turn so finalize/3 runs the WorkflowsAgent and consolidates into a single PR. Refusing after that (in abrir_pr/3) would have spent a whole LLM loop and recorded two completed delegations for a PR that cannot exist. The refusal happens at the interception, and the turn CONTINUES.

A durable trace in both. AT-048 found that a local refusal left no trace in the event log; RN-566 solved it by emitting the tool.call before the refusal, and here the same holds — in the Arquiteto dispatch_tool/2 already emitted it; in the Infra Lead the interception of propose_infra_pr emitted nothing and now emits, in the refusal branch, with the title and the PATHS (never the files' content). And the WHY goes along: a tool.result with ok: false and erro with the reason — the form the Criativo already uses —, because only the tool.call would say the call existed, not why it did not become a proposal. On the path that proposes nothing changes: its trace remains the proposed_action itself.

The execution use cases keep refusing as before — defense in depth: the agent's refusal is a layer BEFORE, never in its place.

What this rule does NOT decide: WHERE the repository should be born. The refusal text describes the current trigger, and it CHANGED: AT-092 was decided in RN-582 (ADR 0165) — the repository is born on accepting the handoff TO the Arquiteto, before its first turn, with the acceptance to the Dev Lead as a second door. The text changed along with it, as this rule promised: it names the new trigger and, since the Arquiteto only works after that acceptance, says the refusal means a FAILED provisioning (the repository.provision_failed) or a project prior to the rule, with the two ways out. It stopped being the common case; the refusal remains, because those two situations exist. open_infra_pr is also affected in a new project by another path (the Infra Lead is triggered by the Arquiteto's handoff, which can happen before the handoff to the Dev Lead); this rule only makes the proposal not be born, it does not reorder the handoffs.

RN-580 — The conversational agent that comes up over a conversation receives its END, with questions and tools, and the beginning that did not fit is summarized with the number written​

The six conversational agents (Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer and Staff) rebuild the history from the event log in init/1 — on restart and also when they come up in a session that already has a conversation (the PO at the Criativo's handoff). Measured on 09/13 (AT-073, against b61bc49cd), the six had the SAME copy of rehydrate/2, with three defects:

  1. They read the beginning. EngineApiClient.list_events/2 asks for limit=200 without latest, and the internal route — which did not even accept latest — returns the FIRST 200. In a conversation of 201 events the agent woke up without the message it was answering. The screen had already solved this with latest: true and a cut warning (RN-180); the engine had not inherited it.
  2. They rebuilt only chat.message and agent.response. The question asked via a form (chat.structured_question) and the tools called (tool.call/tool.result) disappeared.
  3. They cut silently. And the kickoff reads (PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer) and those of the product_brief rules (Criativo) filtered in memory the same FIRST 200 events of all types: in a long conversation with the Criativo, the brief was born after event 200 and the PO received "(no product brief available)".

The rule:

  1. A single path. Engine.Agents.Reidratacao replaces the six copies; the six servers call historico/3 in init/1.
  2. The tail, with ADR 0060's ceiling. The read is latest=true&limit=200 — the route's MAX_LIMIT, neither more (the api would cut) nor less (it would leave out what it delivers for free). The ceiling did NOT become unlimited.
  3. What comes in. chat.message and agent.response as always (from any agent of the session — it is what the PO inherits from the Criativo); chat.structured_question as the agent's speech, with labels and options; tool.call/tool.result of the agent ITSELF as a text note with the tool, the arguments (cut at 1,500 characters) and the outcome — never as a role: "tool" message, because the event does not keep the call's id and a tool_result without the matching tool_use is refused by the provider. chat.structured_question_answered is left OUT on purpose: the api writes the same answers in a chat.message right after (AnswerStructuredQuestionUseCase reuses SendAgentMessageUseCase), and rehydrating both would duplicate the answer.
  4. The beginning that did not fit is stated, with the number. The seq is gapless and starts at 1, so the number of omitted events is the seq of the tail's first one minus one — SUBTRACTION, without an extra request. When it is greater than zero, the history opens with ONE system message that writes that number and brings the summary of the agent's most recent context compaction (when it was recorded) and the conversation's opening (the first six messages of the first 40 events, cut at 500 characters). Those are two more reads with a ceiling — three in total, and only one when the conversation fits.
  5. context.compacted records the summary from now on — summary, agent and messagesSummarized, next to the usual counts. A conversation compacted before this stays DECLARED ("compacted N time(s) before the summary started to be recorded; that summary was lost"), never rebuilt; the old events do not change.
  6. An unreadable history does not become an empty conversation. If the read fails, the agent receives a system message saying it could not read the history.
  7. Kickoffs and brief refs read BY TYPE, from the tail. The internal route gained types (up to 20, validated; malformed is 400) — a CONTRACT change, additive: without latest/types the response is the one from before. When the read by type hits the ceiling, the kickoff says there may be older items.

Measured per agent: all six changed in rehydration (init/1). In the kickoffs, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead and UX Designer changed; the Criativo changed in the product_brief refs and in the zero-rule guardrail; the Staff has no kickoff (ADR 0088).

What this rule does NOT close: the text the tool returned was not in the log — closed by RN-589, from then on (an old session stays without it). InfraLeadServer (which rehydrates via Reidratacao.historico/3 since AT-150, without its own copy) and DevLeadTools.run_assessment/2 (which reads the TAIL, latest with the same 200 ceiling) also go through the common path; no reader of list_events/2 without latest remains in apps/engine/lib. Rehydration can bring MORE than the live context had (the whole tail, even what had already been compacted); the ContextManager compacts again on the next turn.

RN-578 — The click that triggers an agent turn answers on ACCEPTING, and the refusal stops being silent​

In a real installation of v6.1.0 (2026-09-14), answering the Criativo's questions form took 97.3 s, confirming readiness 97.3 s and confirming architecture ready 51.8 s — each click held by the agent's WHOLE turn, because the conversational's handle_call only answered the engine controller's GenServer.call when the turn's Task ended. A turn above the ceiling (120 s in the Criativo, 180 s in the others) became a 500 on a command that had worked. And the refusal of a second message with a turn in progress ({:error, :turno_em_andamento}) was discarded by the controller, which answered 202: a "Continue" typed during the Arquiteto's kickoff was accepted and never read, with no trace at all.

The rule (ADR 0163, which generalizes ADR 0086):

  1. The acceptance goes out right away. TurnoAssincrono.iniciar/3 answers :ok to the from as soon as the Task comes up — after persisting agent.status: working, never before. It holds for the six conversational agents and for the four user routes that trigger a turn (…/agents/:agent/message and, through it, …/structured-question/:id/answer; …/readiness; …/agents/arquiteto/handoff-infra) and for returning a story (ReturnStoryUseCase). The api's status and body do NOT change (201 { ok: true }): they always meant "accepted"; what changed is when they arrive.
  2. The refusal BEFORE the turn comes up is synchronous and named. The engine answers 409 (turno_em_andamento, aguardando_aprovacao) or 422 (sem_regra_de_negocio) with {error, motivo}, and the api passes on the SAME status with the SAME sentence. turno_em_andamento gets a durable agent.error (origin politica); the other two already had one.
  3. The turn's outcome goes through the channel and the log, never through HTTP. A failure stays a durable agent.error, with the same origin as before.
  4. The screen stops treating "the call resolved" as end of turn. After the acceptance, it follows the end through the channel (agent.done) and, as a safety net, through the log's tail every 4 s: it closes when that agent's most recent persisted agent.status is not working. Without any agent.status of the agent in the window, it does not close — not knowing is not "it ended".
  5. The handoff to the Dev Lead keeps being born AFTER the Infra one. The :offer_dev_handoff that arrives with the Arquiteto's closing turn in progress stays pending and runs when the turn closes — success, failure, crash or cancellation. (Superseded by RN-672: the Arquiteto no longer offers to the Dev Lead, and the pending item ceased to exist.)

What this rule does NOT close: the chat.message the api writes before asking the engine stays in the log when the engine refuses (now explained by the agent.error, before orphaned and mute); an engine restarted in the middle of the turn does not write idle, and the strip stays until "Stop" or a reload; and a message to infra via the composer fell to the Criativo through the final clause of AgentCommandController.message/2 — pre-existing, measured here and closed later by RN-584, which removed the default recipient.

Revised for the MESSAGE by RN-673 (ADR 0191): the user's message that arrives with a turn in progress no longer receives turno_em_andamento — it enters the agent's queue and is read at the end of the turn. The refusal of item 2 still holds for the commands that are not speech (review, readiness, handoff offer).

RN-579 — With the session channel alive, the Session screen swaps the short poll for invalidation and a long fallback; an empty-body response has an ETag​

The installation measured in AT-093 (v6.1.0, 09/14) showed ONE browser making 7,088 requests in 56 minutes — median of 118/min, peak of 263/min — against the 300/min of RATE_LIMIT_USER. Two visible tabs at the peak exceed the ceiling, and the 429 lands in the account owner's browser. Almost everything was a 3–5s poll from the Session screen over data that rarely changes (actions, handoffs and backlog came back 304 99% of the time), while the screen already kept the session:<id> channel with the engine open. The ceiling does NOT change: what drops is the request.

The rule:

  1. The engine announces every confirmed write. The facade Engine.Sessions.EngineApiClient emits event.appended (only type and actorId, never the payload) after the api CONFIRMS append_event, append_event_returning, propose_action (proposed_action.created), create_handoff (handoff.offered) and create_epic/story/task (backlog.*_created). A refused write does not announce. Before, only ArtifactEmitter and the Infra Lead announced, by hand — and they announced even when the api refused the append. Since AT-157, the write the API does on its own also announces — the decision of a human in another tab, a session transition, the chat answered by the api's own model. AppendSessionEventUseCase and SendChatMessageUseCase (the only two points that write to session_events without going through the engine) call SessionChannelNotifier.eventAppended, which asks the engine POST /internal/sessions/:id/event-appended; the engine does the SAME event.appended (only type and actorId). The announcement goes out AFTER the commit of the outermost transaction (aposCommit in DrizzleUnitOfWork): an undone transaction does not announce, and announcing from inside it would make the web fetch before the event exists. A write that came from the engine (an /internal/* route, marked by OrigemEngineMiddleware) is NOT announced again by the api — the facade already announced. It is best effort and is not awaited: a lost announcement never fails the write, and the 15s fallback covers it. It is only those two points: another use case that starts writing to session_events without AppendSessionEventUseCase needs to call the notifier too.
  2. "Channel alive" is a CONFIRMED join. connectSessionHeartbeat marks the session alive on the join's ok and unmarks it on error/close of the channel or the socket and on cleanup. The state is per session and per tab, outside React, because the interval belongs to each OBSERVER and three observers (Shell, SessionPage, ContextAside) read the same events key.
  3. With the channel alive, the poll becomes a fallback. Events, actions, handoffs, backlog and the session itself go from 3–5s to 15s; the budget, from 5s to 30s. intervaloDaSessao is Math.max: whoever already polled slower does not speed up. A dropped channel brings back the short interval RIGHT AWAY — the screen never gets worse than it was.
  4. The announcement's TYPE decides what to invalidate, with a window. Every announcement invalidates the events and the budget; proposed_action.*/action.* also the actions, handoff.* the handoffs, backlog.* the backlog. Each target has a minimum window between two fetches (events 3s, actions/handoffs/backlog 2s, budget 10s): the first goes out right away, the following ones within the window become ONE at its end. Without that, a burst of tool.result would become one fetch per event. The rule of finding C remains, and only for the EVENTS: during a streaming turn they are not anticipated; the actions are.
  5. A hidden tab does not poll. refetchIntervalInBackground: false (TanStack v5's default, now written in OPCOES_PADRAO_DAS_QUERIES) — measured by test, not assumed.
  6. An empty body has a validator. A handler returning null went out with an empty body and WITHOUT an ETag (Express's res.send only generates an ETag with a body), so a 304 was impossible: sessions/:id/budget came back 304 in 0% of the 483 measured calls and execution/session in 22% (the time with active execution). The api writes the empty body's ETag when send goes out without a body — decided on what goes over the wire, not on the handler's value, so that a handler with @Res() that writes later never inherits the empty one's validator. A 304 does NOT reduce the rate limit count (the guard counts before the handler); it reduces bandwidth.
  7. It composes with following the turn through the log's tail (RN-578). The ACCEPTED turn keeps being followed by reading the tail every 4s (acompanharTurnoPeloLog) — it is the net against the lost agent.done, and the channel's announcement can be lost along with it, so the tick does NOT become a 15s fallback. What changes: the event.appended of the FOLLOWED agent's agent.status runs the read RIGHT AWAY (avisoPedeVerificacaoDoTurno), and the turn closes as soon as the log says it closed, without waiting for the tick. An announcement from another agent, of another type, or without a followed turn reads nothing extra. And the 3s poll of events stays PAUSED during streaming (findings 2/7): intervaloDaSessao only holds when the pause does not, and invalidation through the channel respects the same rule of finding C.

Numbers (budget test, one tab on the Session screen, per minute): 123 with the channel down (the behavior from before, intact as a fallback) and 46 with it alive — of which 24 are from the Shell (projects summary and execution session, which do not belong to the session and stay at 5s). Two tabs: 246 → 92. Since RN-632 (AT-278) the PROJECT reads poll at the project pace (15s) and the Executors and Overview tabs go through the SAME criarInvalidadorDoCanal — the measurement with the real screens and two tabs lives there.

What this rule does NOT close: the announcement of the write the api does on its own (item 1, AT-157) is best effort — if the engine is out or the announcement is lost, the screen gets there through the fallback, within 15s (it was 3s); the announcement goes to the engine node that received the call, and the Phoenix PubSub broadcast delivers it to subscribers on any node of the cluster (not measured in a cluster). The roster's working status still depends on the event.appended of the agent.status, which goes out after the api writes it. projects-summary and execution/session (Shell) stay at 5s. During an accepted turn, RN-578's 4s tail read adds up to 15 req/min, only while the turn lasts. It is not a consistency model change (no ADR): the source remains the GET, the channel remains only a trigger — as it already was since Phase 4a —, and what changes is the maximum latency of writes without an announcement.

RN-581 — The conversation in progress holds the session for up to 8h, and the closed session refuses conversation​

In exp001 the heartbeat closed the session 30 seconds after the tab stopped, with the Criativo having just asked — and the event log kept receiving events for four minutes after closed_at. Two defects, one on each side of the closing: none of the pending-work signals of RN-064 saw a conversation waiting for the user (a Criativo that finished its turn is idle, without a handoff, without an action, without dev.*), and nothing — neither the events funnel, nor the conversation use cases, nor the engine — looked at the session's state before writing.

The rule, on the heartbeat side:

  1. A conversation waiting for the user is pending work. It is the FIFTH signal of pending-work: the session's most recent end-of-turn event (agent.response, chat.structured_question or agent.error on the agent's side; chat.message or chat.structured_question_answered on the user's side) is the AGENT's, and the actor is a conversational one. agent.error counts as end of turn on purpose: by RN-059 the agent says in the thread what happened, and the next move is the user's. Speech from someone who does not converse (Psicólogo, dev agent) does not hold.
  2. It is the only signal with a CEILING: 8 hours, counted from the END of the agent's turn (the created_at of that event), not from the last heartbeat. The api returns the instant (aguardandoUsuarioDesde) and the engine applies the ceiling (SESSION_CONVERSATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 28800000). Past it, the session closes closed with its OWN cause, conversation_idle_timeout — not heartbeat_timeout, because whoever reads termination_reason (the Psicólogo, a per-session metric) needs to separate the tab that vanished from the conversation nobody resumed. The TerminationClassifier reads it as :timeout: the api knows six causes in the hypotheses, and opening a seventh would be changing that contract. The ceiling also holds with the tab OPEN (AT-152): the SessionServer has its own clock (:conversation_idle_check, every 5 min — no environment variable, only the test hook :session_conversation_idle_check_ms), independent of the heartbeat — the tab's ping neither resets nor postpones it. On each round it reads the pending item and only CLOSES by ceiling (same cause, conversation_idle_timeout); api down, no pending item or a pending item without an instant only reschedule, because what closes due to api down is still the heartbeat. Before, the ceiling was only checked when the heartbeat expired, and an open tab (ping every ~10s) made it unreachable: an immortal session.
  3. A signal without a ceiling wins. With an offered handoff, a pending action, an agent in a turn or a dev agent working, the instant comes back null and the session stays without a ceiling, as it always did. That is why the signal is the LAST in the list.
  4. A present and unreadable instant is an ERROR, never nil. nil with pending: true is a pending item without a ceiling; a broken format would become an immortal session. As an error, it falls into the api-down path — it closes by heartbeat, saying why.

The rule, on the closed session side:

  1. A closed/closed_abnormally session refuses a CONVERSATION event with a NAMED 409: { message, reason: "sessao_encerrada", status, type }. closing still accepts — the lock is on TERMINAL state.
  2. "Conversation" has two clauses, and both are necessary. The TYPE only exists as conversation (chat.message, chat.structured_question[_answered], agent.status, agent.activated, handoff.offered/accepted, readiness.confirmed, necessity.validated, architecture.readiness_confirmed), OR the ACTOR is a conversational agent (the six plus dev-lead and infra). An ALLOWLIST by type was measured and refused: those who legitimately write to a closed session are the CONSUMERS of the closing — the Psicólogo runs a ToolLoop against it and writes tool.call, agent.response, agent.error; the Anamnese writes its own outcomes —, and they speak the SAME generic vocabulary as the Criativo. The type is the same; who differs is the actor.
  3. The human decision about an action keeps coming in. action.approved/ action.denied and the execution outcomes are not conversation: the action is an item of a DURABLE queue that survives the session, and refusing the decision would leave a pending item impossible to resolve. The normal case does not even get here (a pending action holds the session, signal 2 of RN-064); it only exists when the session died through another door.
  4. The refusal leaves no trace. The state comes from the SAME UPDATE that reserves the seq (with no extra query on the hottest path, under the same row lock as the transition), and the refusal throws inside the transaction: the increment comes back, the seq stays without a hole. The human chat, which writes chat.message without the funnel, has the same lock. The use cases with an effect BEFORE the event refuse before the effect: CreateHandoff before creating the row, AcceptHandoff before marking accepted (which would activate the next agent), ActivateAgent before calling the engine.
  5. The closing STOPS the conversational agents. SessionLifecycleWorker, through which every closing goes (heartbeat, idle conversation, human, crash), stops the session's conversational agents on ALL nodes (Engine.Agents.Conversacionais, via :erpc — the registry is local and the job lands on any replica). The turn in progress is ABANDONED in the terminate/2 of the six servers (TurnoAssincrono.abandonar/1): the task dies without writing or broadcasting anything, because writing would be asking the api for what it refuses. There is no answer to give: since RN-578 (ADR 0163) whoever triggered the turn already received :ok on acceptance. For the same reason the offer_dev_handoff the Arquiteto kept for the turn's closing does NOT run when the closing is the session's — the handoff would be refused (since RN-672 there is nothing to keep anymore: the handoff to the Dev Lead comes from the Infra). The Infra Lead, which runs the turn inside handle_call, is killed if it does not exit within 5s.
  6. The refusal is never silent in the engine. Almost every caller of append_event/3 discards the return; the client logs the 409 sessao_encerrada as a warning, and the return stays the same.
  7. The screen recognizes the 409 by the CODE and says the session closed (AT-154). ehRecusaDeSessaoEncerrada checks status === 409 AND body.reason === "sessao_encerrada" — never the text, and never only the 409, which is also "turn in progress". In the four conversation actions (send a message, answer a structured question, confirm the readiness of the Criativo and of the Arquiteto) the screen shows its own sentence instead of the generic error, redoes the session read (it is the new status that makes the composer disappear) and does NOT lose what was typed: the message goes back to the draft and shows up read-only in place of the composer, and the form's answers stay in the fields. The sentence does not promise "Reopen" — the action does not exist. And the "Close" button stays inert in BOTH terminal states (sessaoEhTerminal, the mirror of isTerminal), not only in closed (AT-155).

What this rule does NOT close: the ceiling is only checked when the HEARTBEAT expires — with the tab open and sending heartbeats, the session stays alive without a ceiling, as always (whoever is looking is not an idle conversation). The stateless human chat's answer to a turn that STARTED with the session open comes in even if it closes midway (the actor is the model, and the spend has already been measured). deploy/k8s/ does not carry SESSION_CONVERSATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, and since AT-153 that is a DECISION written in the engine's Deployment, not a pending item: there nothing intercepts the environment, the absence is the runtime.exs default, and writing the number would make a second copy with no guard against diverging — changing the ceiling there is an env: item in the overlay's engine patch. The THREE composes map it with the code's default (the installation one only since AT-153, and until then the line in an installation's .env was inert), guarded by scripts/ci/teto-ocioso-nos-composes.spec.ts. Since AT-154 the screen handles the 409 with its own sentence (item 11); the screen's other actions that write to a closed session keep showing the api's message.

The closed session can be reopened (RN-649/RN-650)​

RN-649 — A closed/closed_abnormally session reopens to active with the log intact, and the previous closing becomes a new event​

RN-001 said the terminal states have no way out. Since ADR 0183 there is ONE, and only one: the reopening, from closed or closed_abnormally to active, through its own path. The GENERIC transition keeps refusing closed → active with 409, and closing → active remains forbidden through any path.

  1. What comes back is the whole session. The event log is not touched — the conversation, the business rules, the answered questions, the handoff offers and acceptances. A conversational agent stopped at closing comes back through the idempotent start_agent on the first message and rebuilds the history (RN-580). The conversation comes in again because the refusal of RN-581 reads the session's state, which is now active.
  2. The previous closing is not erased. The sessions row loses closed_at and termination_reason; the NEW event session.reopened, in the same seq (RN-002) and with the human actor who reopened, carries {from, to, closedAt, terminationReason}. No event is edited nor renumbered, and the kind does not change (RN-097).
  3. A session with execution does not reopen — 409 sessao_com_execucao. Reopening a session with execution.activated would return it to findActiveExecutionSession (RN-139). The owner's decision, confirmed in ADR 0184.
  4. No deadline. Every closed session is reopenable (the owner's decision, ADR 0184).
  5. The engine is called before the transaction, as in activation: its failure leaves the session closed, with no event. Any non-terminal state is 409 sessao_nao_encerrada.
  6. The closing the reopening undid does not stop the live session. The SessionLifecycleWorker reads the session's status and ignores, with a log, the session.closed/session.closed_abnormally job of a session the api already says is non-terminal.
  7. The Psicólogo's second automatic analysis stays blocked by the alreadyAnalyzed that already existed; manual reprocessing continues. The second graph consolidation extends the window of the same Interacao.

RN-650 — Reopening is developer, through its own route, and the screen only offers the button to whoever reaches the role​

The repository is born on accepting the handoff to the Arquiteto, and execution does not start without it (RN-582)​

RN-582 — Accepting the handoff to the Arquiteto provisions the repository; accepting to the Dev Lead is the second, idempotent door; and execution/activate without a repository is a named 409​

It revises the TRIGGER of RN-522, which fulfilled the promise of RN-541. The mechanism does not change — the same ProvisionRepositoryUseCase, called by the same AcceptHandoffUseCase, always local, with the failure becoming repository.provision_failed and never taking down the acceptance. Structural decision in ADR 0165.

What the real installation showed (AT-092, v6.1.0, 2026-09-14). The Arquiteto proposed open_adr_pr three times before the repository existed; the handoffs to infra and dev-lead were offered together, only the infra one was accepted, and POST /projects/:id/execution/activate answered 201. The tables project_repositories, project_git_connections and repo_bootstraps stayed empty — the project without a repository forever. Two defects: the trigger came AFTER those who need the repository (Arquiteto and Infra Lead write to it before the Dev Lead), and the only trigger was SKIPPABLE (activating execution does not require accepting to the Dev Lead).

1. The trigger is accepting the handoff to arquiteto. The Arquiteto is only activated by an accepted handoff addressed to it (canActivateAgent), and that handoff is born from the PO (offer_handoff(to_agent: "arquiteto")) or from the user (manual handoff) — both doors go through the same acceptance. Provisioning runs BEFORE activateAgent: the Arquiteto wakes up in a project that already has somewhere to write. Consequence: the Infra Lead, activated by a handoff FROM the Arquiteto, never again wakes up without a repository.

2. Accepting to dev-lead keeps provisioning, as a SECOND DOOR. It is the way out for a project that went through the Arquiteto before this rule (the exp001 of AT-092: Arquiteto accepted, Dev Lead offered) and the natural resumption of a provisioning that failed at the acceptance to the Arquiteto. With the created repository already up, the second call creates nothing — no repository, no session, no bootstrap row, no branch, no commit —, and that is proven by BOTH doors in sequence against the real Postgres and LocalGitProvider.

3. execution/activate without a repository is REFUSED with 409, right after the module_map check and BEFORE any effect (persisted budget, permissions.json, session, engine, event). The sentence is chosen by the state of the project's handoffs, read by HandoffRepository.findByProject (from all sessions — the handoff to the Arquiteto lives in the PO's): handoff to the Arquiteto offered → accept it; otherwise to the Dev Lead offered → accept it; otherwise one of the two already accepted → provisioning left no repository, see the repository.provision_failed and use the provisioning page (/projects/:id/provisioning?provider=local); otherwise → no handoff to the Arquiteto was accepted. A handoff offered to ANOTHER agent never becomes an acceptance instruction (accepting the Infra provisions nothing). An ADOPTED repository counts as a repository. Refusing and not provisioning here is a decision: provisioning inside activation would hide a git effect, and the agents before it would remain without a repository.

4. The screen removes the control and states the reason once, in text (the rule of RN-102 and ADR 0064). In the Execution section of the Overview, with GET .../git/repository answering a CONFIRMED null, "Activate execution" stays inert in place, the text says where the repository is born, and there is a link to provision. On the card of the handoff to the Dev Lead, inside the session, the "Activate execution" shortcut leaves and the card says that accepting that handoff provisions the repository. Loading or with an error, nothing locks — "I don't know" does not become "it doesn't have", and the backend refuses anyway. Accepting a handoff invalidates the repository query, because the acceptance may have created it.

The technical session does not displace the working one (AT-131). The session the provisioning opens (repo_bootstraps.session_id, named git-bootstrap) is born in the MIDDLE of the Arquiteto's phase, and choosing "the most recent" only by createdAt put it in place of the working session until the next one was born (ADR 0165 left that declared). Now the two reads by createdAt of the workspace summary (latestSessionId and the cut of the unread ones) order by "is a bootstrap session" BEFORE createdAt, and the Overview (useLatestSession) does the same. The technical one is only the most recent when it is the ONLY one — in the manual provisioning flow it is in it that the project starts. The api reads the marker through repo_bootstraps; the web only has the session's NAME, and renaming it makes the two diverge (the Overview then treats the summary as being of another session and does not use it). The criterion does not change what ADR 0165 decided (where the repository is born), which is why there is no new ADR.

Revised by RN-592 (AT-183): the web stopped reading the NAME — the session listing returns the technical marker, through the same link in repo_bootstraps, and renaming the session no longer makes the two diverge.

The activation refusal does not tell to accept a handoff from a closed session (RN-581, AT-131). Accepting a handoff in a terminal session is 409 sessao_encerrada, checked BEFORE the handoff becomes accepted — so nothing is half provisioned. The refusal sentence now queries the state of the session of each offered handoff: only the one living in an OPEN session becomes "accept it"; if the only offered one is in a closed session, the sentence says so and points to the provisioning page. A session not found counts as open ("I don't know" does not become "closed"). The events provisioning writes do not fall under RN-581: the actor is system and the destination is the freshly created git-bootstrap session. What remains NOT covered: the Overview and the handoff card in the session read the state of the repository, not that of each session, and did not change.

RN-584 — The chat message has no default recipient: each conversing agent has its own clause, and the rest is a named refusal​

The last clause of EngineWeb.AgentCommandController.message/2 did not look at the agent: it matched ANY name the clauses above had not caught and delivered the message to the Criativo. A message written to infra was read by another agent, the click answered 202, and the Criativo answered in the thread — nothing broke, and nobody saw. Found as an adjacency of RN-578 (AT-089) and fixed here (AT-098).

The measurement, before the fix (the three sides, on dev at 72ee8cdcf):

DestinationDoes the screen offer it?Does the api accept it?Did the engine have a clause?
criativoyes (composer: the creative session's fallback and AGENTES_DE_CHAT)yesNO — it was the final clause, without a guard
po, arquiteto, dev-lead, ux-designer, staffyes (AGENTES_DE_CHAT, the most recent agent.activated)yesyes, one each
infranot in the composer (out of AGENTES_DE_CHAT since the 9-fix finding and RN-499)yesno — it fell to the Criativo
any other name in the roster (qa, subagents, secops, psicologo…)only through the structured questions form, which answers the ACTOR who asked (agent={event.actor.id}); today only Criativo and PO askyesno — it fell to the Criativo
unknown name, or nonenoyes (the api does not validate the agent; only the sessionId becomes a checked URL segment, RN-128)no — it fell to the Criativo

The rule:

  1. Each conversing agent has its OWN clause, the Criativo included ("agent" => "criativo"). The final clause stopped existing as a delivery: it is a REFUSAL.
  2. A name without a clause is a NAMED 422, {error, motivo} in the mold of RN-578: agente_sem_conversa, with a sentence that names the agent and says the message was recorded and no agent read it. The api passes on the 422 as UnprocessableEntityException with the SAME sentence (the postComandoDeTurno of RN-578, without new code), and the screen shows it through the mensagemDaRecusaDoAgente that already existed. Without "agent" in the body it is agente_ausente, and a conversing agent without text is mensagem_sem_texto — three reasons, because "does not converse" said to one who converses would be a lie.
  3. infra has its OWN refusal, with a sentence that says what it does: it works by proposal (the infra PR, starting the container), and what asks for a decision shows up in Approvals. It is not missing code, it is the same reading as RN-499 — the Infra Lead is propositional. And the user_message/2 that InfraLeadServer still exports does not serve for a clause: it runs the WHOLE turn inside handle_call (up to 180 s), without the acceptance of ADR 0163 and without "Stop" (via_for/2 does not know it). Wiring it would give back to the click the wait RN-578 removed.
  4. "Stop" also does not guess. cancel/2 without "agent" stopped the Criativo's turn; it becomes 422 agente_ausente. The api always sends the agent on both routes, so those two refusals only reach a broken caller.
  5. The screen keeps not offering infra in the composer — no UI change: AGENTES_DE_CHAT already excluded it, and what changed is that, if one day someone puts it there, the engine refuses with a name instead of delivering to another, and the CI guard fails it first.

Since RN-617 (ADR 0175), items 3 and 5 no longer hold: the Infra Lead's turn migrated to TurnoAssincrono, and only then did it gain its own message/2 clause, the "Stop"'s via_for/2 and the place in AGENTES_DE_CHAT. Its agente_sem_conversa refusal left; the underlying rule of this RN — no default recipient, every name without a clause refused with a name — is the same.

The guard that closes the class lives in scripts/ci/destinos-do-composer.spec.ts, because the destination is born in TypeScript and the clause lives in Elixir — neither of the two suites reads the other language. It DERIVES the destinations from the source (AGENTES_DE_CHAT, the agentParaEnviar = '…' literals of SessionPage.tsx and the roster's AgentKey) and requires: its own conversing clause and the "Stop"'s via_for/2 for each composer destination; no clause without a fixed agent in the head that delivers to an agent; the last clause of message/2 being a refusal; infra out of the composer and with its own refusal; and @agentes_de_conversa equal to the set of clauses that converse. Five mutations measured, all killed (the old catch-all back, infra in AGENTES_DE_CHAT, the Criativo's clause renamed, the Staff's via_for removed, the infra clause renamed).

What this rule does NOT close, declared:

  • Whether the Infra Lead comes to converse through the composer was a product decision, without an owner — taken in RN-617 (AT-141): yes. Giving it a clause requires, first, migrating its turn to TurnoAssincrono (the acceptance and the turno_em_andamento refusal of RN-578) and registering it in "Stop"; and requires deciding what a conversation does with an agent whose contract is to propose. Its user_message/2 stays exported and without a caller.

  • The chat.message written by the api before the refusal stays in the log — and since RN-587 the engine writes the refusal's agent.error next to it, so the thread explains itself.

  • The api does not validate the agent. Refusing there, before writing, would require a second list of who converses on the TypeScript side — and diverging it from the clauses is the defect this rule closes. What decides is whoever has the clauses (decision kept in RN-587).
