RN-624 — The api detects the author's language from their own messages and ASKS; only the confirmed one becomes a preference​

RN-618 left the "confirmed detected" step ready and empty. Maintainer decision (AT-168 answers 4, 6 and 7): detect, ASK whether the language is right, and the confirmed one becomes the default — per person, global, with the question on the screen where the language is already shown and corrected.

  1. The yardstick is ONE, and lives in the api. The heuristic of AT-080, measured by AT-160 (contrastive markers of pt/es/en, the stripping of code, log, quotation, URL and identifier), moved from scripts/idioma/ to apps/api/src/domain/iam/heuristica-de-idioma.ts, and the instrument REEXPORTS it from there — what the product runs is what the instrument measures. The rule of WHAT counts as evidence (only actor user; in the form, only the answers, and the echo with the agent's labels skipped) is also a single one, evidenciasDoAutor, used by the real-corpus extraction and by the detection. Local, no LLM, no new dependency.
  2. The sample comes from the event log, the hysteresis is recomputed. Detection reads the person's 11 most recent pieces of evidence across ALL sessions (the window of 10 plus the one the hysteresis recomputes) and decides when the TWO last evaluations of the sample point to the same language (idiomaConcordante). No detection state is stored: the evaluation of the previous message is recomputed with the window that ended at it. The read is served by a PARTIAL index (session_events_evidencia_de_idioma_idx, actor user and the two evidence types): measured with 200 thousand events, 0.056 ms through the index against 13.5 ms for the scan without it.
  3. The thresholds are PROVISIONAL. PARAMETROS_PROVISORIOS are the candidates of AT-080 with ONE difference, the minimum evidence of 10 words and not 20 — in the SYNTHETIC corpus, at 10 the coverage of decidable cases goes from 42.2% to 58.9% with the same three errors (all in a language outside the three). List at080; threshold 0.8, margin 0.3, sample 10 messages / 2,000 characters, hysteresis 2. The synthetic corpus was written by the same hand that wrote the heuristic: none of these numbers is calibrated, and the owner recalibrates them with the real corpus (pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:medir --real), changing the object, which is the only place the api reads them from.
  4. When it asks. GET .../sessions/:sessionId/response-language returns detectionQuestion with the language to ask about, or null. It does not ask when: the detection does not agree (short text, "ok", code, log, mixed); the effective one comes from an EXPLICIT choice — session override or Account —, because confirming would record a step BELOW them and the reply would not change; the detected one is already the effective one, compared by SUBTAG (pt does not diverge from pt-BR — the heuristic only knows the language); or the person already declined that language.
  5. Detection never changes anything on its own. Only POST /users/me/preferences/detected-language writes: confirm writes the pair detected_language + detected_language_confirmed_at (the CHECK of RN-618) and deletes the old decline of the same language — and it is 409 deteccao_mudou, without writing, when the messages no longer point to the language (the column says "detected" and cannot hold what the heuristic did not detect); decline writes the decline to detected_language_declines (one row per person and language, with the date), and THAT language is not asked about again. What is stored is the language and the person's decision — never country, nationality or proficiency.
  6. Where the question appears. In a small card anchored just below the language indicator of the session bar (RN-620): "Detectamos que você escreve em espanhol (es) — usar espanhol (es) nas respostas?", with "Usar", "Não" and "Agora não". No modal, without covering the composer; "Agora não" only hides it on this screen, without writing, and the question comes back on the next read. Sending a message (or answering a form) rereads the indicator, because the new message is the evidence that can make the question appear.
  7. Failure never blocks anything. Detection runs on the language READ, and not inside SendAgentMessageUseCase: the evidence is already in the event log, the question survives a page reload and appears in any session, and sending the message does not go through it — it gains no latency and has no way to fail because of it. On the read, any failure (database, heuristic) becomes a warning and detectionQuestion: null; the language keeps being shown.
  8. Cost: CPU measured on the synthetic corpus, on this machine — 11.6 µs to clean and classify a message, 110 µs per detection (11 messages, two evaluations), plus the indexed read of item 2. Zero tokens.

What this rule does NOT close, declared: the heuristic knows three languages, and the language list is open — Galician and French can become es/pt (the synthetic errors), and under this rule the cost is a wrong question, which the person declines. A message in Spanish in a Portuguese window leaves the sample undetermined while it is in it (no question, no change). And the heuristic file cannot have import: the instrument runs it by type stripping, and scripts/idioma/ has its own tsconfig without verbatimModuleSyntax to accept the exports of a CommonJS module.

RN-625 — The loop asks the Jev which tool, and the user's model sees only the menu that remains; the Jev restricts and never decides​

Maintainer decision (AT-236, 2026-09-28) and, on the criterion, of 2026-09-29: before each chat call of an agent, the api asks the Jev (typesafe/jev-1.13, OpenRouter's Decisions API) which tool fits the step, and the chat provider receives only the menu that the P3 policy derives from that answer. The mechanism is in ADR 0179; the adoption decision, with the numbers, too.

  1. When. Only with the turn model's provider equal to openrouter, with two or more tools in the request, with an agent in the turn (except the Anamnese and the compaction summarizer), without catalogoCompleto requested by the engine and with the workspace switched on (workspaces.tool_router_enabled, on by default, PUT workspaces/:workspaceId/tool-router, owner). Any condition fails: no call, no event. With a provider ≠ openrouter the workspace is not even read. The key is the workspace holder's, the same as the chat's (RN-058).
  2. The policy is P3 and it only restricts. Menu = {Jev's choice, previous tool of the SAME execution}. The Jev's responder_sem_ferramenta, or no previous tool in the step's catalog, leaves the WHOLE catalog. There is no tool_choice (the model can still reply in text) and there is no confidence threshold in v1: the confidence is recorded and it is up to AT-239 to propose one. Adoption criterion: 80%, owner decision of 2026-09-29 — Jev top-1 73% (66–79), P3 menu coverage 91% (85.1–94), top-2 90%; coverage is the CEILING of end-to-end accuracy (62%–91% in replay), and the real validation is AT-239.
  3. The state is what the product has before the step, cut from the messages the engine already sends, without a database read: agente = the agentId; contexto = the beginning (1,500 characters) of the system message that the ToolLoop puts in front (apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tool_loop.ex:98, system_msg, assembled by system_prompt/1 at :316); pedido = the last user message — in execution agents the initial message of the loop (apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/dev_agent_server.ex:484, initial_message/2, or the correction one at :523), in conversational ones the person's utterance; and passos_recentes = the last 6 tool calls after that message, one entry per call, argument and result cut at 500 characters — the result comes from the tool message the loop appends (tool_loop.ex:293, concluir_despacho/5, with toolCallId). The current execution is "after the last user" because ctx.messages restarts at each ToolLoop.run. Ceiling of 8 thousand tokens; exceeded, fallback estado_grande.
  4. The turn never fails because of the Jev. HTTP error, timeout (2,000 ms, TOOL_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS), network error, unexpected JSON, choice outside the options, large state and collision with the reserved name: the provider receives the whole catalog and the event carries motivoDaQueda and origemDaQueda (infra, modelo or codigo — RN-059), never silent.
  5. The policy does not change. The Jev does not approve, does not deny and does not choose a model. A chosen tool that requires approval still requires it; a call to a tool outside the menu is dispatched as always and the event only records foraDoCardapio. The iteration ceiling is the same as before (the call to the Jev is not an iteration).
  6. Per-step record. The engine writes tool_router.decided, in the EngineApiClient facade for all agents, with menu before and after, choice, confidence, second option, aplicado, fallback, latency, real cost and foraDoCardapio. The api writes ONE token_usage row for the Jev: actor = the agent itself (the spend goes into the area budget, ADR 0110), modelName = typesafe/jev-1.13, modelId null, estimated = false, costMicros = the usage.cost of the response, IMPLIED price per million (cost ÷ tokens) with price_implicit = true — keeps tokens × price = cost of RN-044 without inventing a catalog price. Without usage.cost in the response there is no row. The budget gate is not reconsulted between the Jev and the chat.
  7. Getting out of the dead end. Restricted menu and the model replies without calling a tool (not even in recoverable text), with no provider error: the facade repeats the step ONCE with catalogoCompleto: true, which skips the Jev. In the stream, only if nothing was written to the person. It asks for more tools, never one the agent did not have.

What this rule does NOT close, declared: the screen (showing that the step was routed, with the confidence, and the "choosing tool" strip through the tool_routing_started frame) belongs to apps/web; the gain is AT-239's; a timeout that OpenRouter billed without returning usage.cost does not enter token_usage; the endpoint is ALPHA and the manual smoke (jev-tool-router.smoke.spec.ts, ceiling US$ 0.05) is what flags the change.

Deciding in the chat, where the owner is (RN-626)​

RN-626 — The session chat decides what the agents proposed in another session, shows the turn that was in progress and proposes the merge — without changing any ceiling​

The real use of 2026-09-29 measured the cost of the owner talking in one session and the dev agents proposing in another: their approvals never appeared where he was, 45 of 173 clicks on "Sempre permitir" came back 409 (the card was still clickable after the action had already left pending), and reopening the session with a turn in progress gave back a free composer and the 409. The four fixes are SCREEN fixes — the api, the engine and every ceiling stay as they are.

  1. The card goes inert and says the api's sentence (AT-256). ApprovalCard holds the buttons while the decision is in flight (the double click was a certain 409) and, when the call returns a promise that rejects, shows the sentence the api sent ON the card — never a generic toast. A 409 (the action is no longer pending) leaves the buttons inert with the reason in text until the list swaps the card for the outcome line. The caller returns the promise and refetches the list EVEN on refusal (finally): it is ONE invalidation per click, no new poll, and the invalidation uses the channel and budget of RN-579.
  2. Reopening the session resumes the turn from the log (AT-268). The screen's turn state is local useState and was lost on leaving. On the first read of the events of an active session, turnoEmCursoNoLog looks at the most recent persisted agent.status of each agent (the same read as turnoTerminouNoLog, from RN-578); whatever is working reopens the strip and locks the composer through the same entry points as an accepted turn (iniciarTurnoDoAgente + acompanharTurnoPeloLog), and the read of the log tail closes it. It runs ONCE per mounted session (a recurring effect would rearm the strip with the old working still in the cache). The working left by an engine restart is closed by a new event at boot (RN-586), so what remains is a live turn. It does not queue messages: a message with a turn in progress is still refused with a named 409 — the queue is a pending decision of the owner (AT-267).
  3. Pending items of OTHER sessions of the project appear in the chat (AT-265). PendenciasDeOutrasSessoes reads GET /projects/:id/actions?status=pending (the same endpoint as the PRs tab and the "needs you" panel) and draws the ones that were NOT born in this session — this session's are already decided by the thread. It is a SHORTCUT and never a substitute (RN-467): the SAME ApprovalCard, the same endpoints, with the sessionId the action itself carries; onActivateAutoMode stays out (it is policy, not decision). The two queues — approvals and PR merges — have their OWN title and count and are never summed, and each row states the originating session. The drawing has a ceiling of 20 cards, and the excess is stated ("Mostrando N de M"): a declared cut, as in RN-180. The poll is the session's (5 s with the channel down, the 15 s fallback with it live — intervaloDaSessao), because the session channel does not announce another session's writes.
  4. "Mergear" on the card of the open PR (AT-266). Under the card of an executed pr_open, and only when the action.pr_open event carries the PR id and there is no live git_merge (pending, approved or auto-approved) for it, the button PROPOSES the git_merge through the same endpoint as the PRs tab (actor user, in this session). The proposal appears in the thread as the usual card, with Aprovar/Negar: the confirmation is the same and belongs to the human — merge into a protected branch remains unconditional require_approval (RN-418), without auto-approval, without "sempre permitir", without auto mode. The dedupe and the api's refusals (PR already merged, merge already proposed — RN-663) reach the owner as the api's sentence; a pending gate is not a refusal, it is a text notice next to the button.
  5. The role is the ENDPOINT's, and the gap is declared. Deciding an action and proposing an action require developer (actions.controller.ts); the screen uses roleAtLeast over the WORKSPACE role, because the Session does not fetch project_members — the same single gap of RN-471, declared here and not closed. Whoever does not reach it SEES the pending item and the button, with the controls inert and the reason in text (bloqueio of ApprovalCard): what is taken away is the control, never the information.

What this rule does NOT close, declared: (a) "Mergear" does not propose AND approve in a single click — it is two clicks, the proposal and the confirmation, on purpose; (b) resuming the turn reads the window of events already loaded, and an agent.status outside it is not seen (not knowing is not "is working"); (c) the list of pending items from other sessions has the ceiling of 20 cards, and the rest stays in the Aprovações tab; (d) architecture pending items and the Psicólogo's hypotheses still have NO inline decision (there is no ApprovalCard for them).

RN-629 — The QA Lead treats the subagent that SUSPENDS again on resumption the same way as the first time, and a result it does not know becomes a named block​

qa-automacao runs several commands and each one may ask for human approval. The QaLeadServer already stopped the area when run/5 returned {:awaiting, _} (finding AB, ADR 0052), but the RESUMPTION (retomar/3, when the decision arrives) returned the result of a loop that could suspend ANOTHER time — and that second {:awaiting, _} went into the list of collected results as if it were a verdict. On consolidating, registrar_resultado/5 had no clause for it and the GenServer crashed (FunctionClauseError, measured on 29/09/2026: 06:55:01 and 07:00:10), leaving the three delivered tasks in awaiting_qa forever, with no verdict and no named outcome.

  1. A single place decides what to do with a subagent's result (tratar_resultado/6), whether it comes from run/5 or from retomar/3. {:awaiting, _} keeps the in-flight state (keyed by the new action), keeps the gate_states row in in_progress with the subagent and STOPS the area: no verdict, without blocking the task, without recording the delegation. The resumer is the same {:action_settled, _} of Engine.Dev.Wake (ADR 0086), as many times as needed.
  2. A result the lead does not know never crashes nor vanishes (RN-059): it becomes {:blocked, …} with origin codigo (a clause is missing here, it is not infra, model or policy), which registrar_resultado/5 records as a failed delegation and QaLead.consolidar/1 turns into a block of the task with the origin.

Declared, not resolved: an engine restart with the lead suspended loses the Wake subscription (accepted gap of ADR 0086); the GateRescuer restarts the whole area (ADR 0067), it does not resume the ctx. This rule does not change ADR 0090 (the moment of QA-strategy) nor the subagent's iteration ceiling.

RN-630 — Who is active in the session is read from the WHOLE session, not from the last 200 events​

"Who is active" and "who receives the composer" came from the agent.activated seen in the 200-event window (latest: true). In a long session the activations of the Arquiteto and the Infra left the window; handoff offers addressed to them went back to looking acceptable and the "hi" went to the last agent that still appeared. It is the defect class of RN-180 (a silent ceiling makes the screen assert about what it did not read), already closed for the presence of QA/SecOps in RN-568.

The rule: the project summary (RN-090) returns roster.activatedAgents — the agents with at least one agent.activated in the most recent session, one per agent, the most recently activated (by seq) first. Four decisions:

  1. The source is still the event log. No derived column, no index and no migration: the field enters the SAME per-session scan that already computes executionActivated/gatesEverOpened (array_agg ... filter), so the number of database round trips of the summary does not change (the constant-count spec still holds). The reserved migration 0066 was not used.
  2. No new HTTP per poll. The field travels in the summary the screens already read (RN-579).
  3. The client ADDS it to the window and only trusts it with the summary of the SAME session (latestSessionId === sessionId), as in RN-568: activation is monotonic (an activated agent does not deactivate), so the window only gives false negatives. A summary of another session does not count; with no summary, the window decides alone.
  4. The api says what happened, not who receives. The explicit, visible recipient in the chat (AT-251) and acceptance by handoffId (AT-253) consume this field in the web and are NOT part of this rule.

Declared gap: this round only delivers the api CONTRACT. apps/web (session-readiness.ts, session-handoffs.ts) keeps reading the window until AT-251/AT-253 start consuming roster.activatedAgents.

Closed in RN-631 (AT-251): the composer recipient and the handoff offers of the Session screen ADD roster.activatedAgents to the window, with the same-session guard. criativoActive/arquitetoActive (session-readiness.ts) still read only the window.

RN-627 — The project container runs as the folder's owner, measured by the api​

Under --cap-drop ALL the container's root lacks CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and cannot write to the project folder, which belongs to the operator's uid: npm install gave EACCES for every dev agent (AT-247, ADR 0180).

  1. The api measures, the broker composes. container-spec returns usuarioDaPasta (stat of the folder for the container/mounted modes; null if the folder is not reached, if the owner is root or if the project is runner). The broker copies it into spec.usuario and the adapter emits --user uid:gid and --env HOME=/tmp.
  2. It never comes from the requester. start has no body and the exec body ignores extra fields; exec inherits the container's user.
  3. The broker revalidates. Integers in 1..2^31-1; 0 is refused naming usuario.uid/usuario.gid (root is the absent one, "as always").
  4. It does not loosen containment: --cap-drop ALL, one bind, a two-valued network and five operations remain. An already created container only changes when recreated.

RN-628 — The executed merge closes the PR's task: done, once only​

The QA/SecOps gate ends in awaiting_user and nothing else touched the task's status: in the real use of 09/29 pr-6 was merged three times and the tasks stayed in in_review (AT-275).

After the merge, never in its place. git_merge is still unconditional require_approval (RN-418); the rule runs INSIDE ExecuteGitActionUseCase, in the transaction that records the merge result, and only when the provider returned state: 'merged' (an open PR, or a merge that failed, does not touch the task).

When it moves, it writes ONE immutable backlog.task_status_changed event (cause: 'pr_merged', pullRequestId, actionId), append-only, with no UPDATE on an events table. No migration.

RN-640 — The neutral palette closes the contrast debt, and UI color only comes from a token​

The dark theme stops being petrol blue and becomes neutral black with a soft terracotta accent; the light one becomes the neutral of the same family (ADR 0181). The mechanism of RN-184 does not change — the pairs are measured in both themes, with the same floor —; what changes is what is demanded:

  1. The dark theme's debt became a floor. The five pairs that RN-184 left locked by number (3.89 / 3.10 / 3.88 / 3.88 / 4.41) pass 4.5:1 in both themes, and the test rejects whoever brings them back down — it no longer "records". The final value came from MEASUREMENT: the draft's --text-muted (#71717a) repeated the debt and was refused (#86868f in dark, #696972 in light), and muted stays BELOW --text-secondary on the three surfaces, which the test also demands.
  2. Text over a solid brand/state background passes AA. The dark theme's --on-accent is the neutral black (5.61:1 over the accent, 7.25:1 on hover, 7.65:1 over --success, 5.24:1 over --danger); the "known exception" of the primary button ceases to exist, and the accent's hue stays terracotta (10°–30°) in both themes.
  3. UI color only comes from a token. Whatever paints through a runtime library (Mermaid, xterm, minimap) reads the active theme's token and, without it, falls back to the default of TOKENS_PADRAO — a copy of :root that the test checks against design/tokens.css. Agent color is always var(--token); the three agents without a semantic one have --agent-* per theme, measured at 3:1. And no CSS module uses a var(--x) that nobody declares.

RN-642 — "Sempre permitir" approves and records the pattern in the SAME transaction; a click on an already approved action is a named success​

In the real use of 09/29, 45 of 173 clicks on "Sempre permitir" returned 409 (AT-310): the pattern was recorded BEFORE approving, and an action that had already left pending (double click, the same pending item in two panels, another tab) threw 409 with the pattern ALREADY recorded and WITHOUT the permission.granted event.

  1. Same transaction, after the transition. ApproveActionUseCase accepts an aoAprovar that runs INSIDE the decision's transaction, after assertTransition passes and before execution; it is through it that the pattern (permissions.json/allow or agent_autonomy, RN-509) and the permission.granted are recorded. "Approve first, record later" in separate transactions was refused: it would trade the defect for an approved (and even executed) action with the pattern failing afterwards. agent_autonomy and the event are atomic with the decision; permissions.json is a file and does not enter a transaction — it is only written after the transition is valid, and failing to write it undoes the approval. What remains, declared, is the window of the COMMIT failing after the file was written.
  2. The event goes with the recording, and only with it. A pattern that already exists is not rewritten nor narrated again (padraoGravado: false).
  3. An already approved action is a named success. If the transition is refused because the action is already approved/auto_approved/executed/failed, the response is 201 with desfecho: 'ja_aprovada' (the normal path returns 'aprovada'), without executing again, recording the pattern only if it is missing — with the event. An invalid transition coming from EXECUTION, after the decision has been confirmed, does NOT become ja_aprovada: it propagates as always.
  4. A DENIED action is still 409, named (reason: 'acao_ja_recusada'), without recording pattern or event: freeing forever what someone just denied is not idempotency.
  5. Ceilings intact. git push/PR/deploy, sudo/doas (motivoDeRecusaSempreAprovar, RN-418) and container_remove are still refused with 400 BEFORE any state read — including with the action already approved. The pattern is still the action's EXACT one (generalization by verb is AT-257, outside here).
  6. The ceiling TYPES too (AT-320). Measured in the audit of 09/30: the api only refused the git push TYPED in the terminal; the TYPED git_push passed and recorded GitPush() in allow (or module autonomy), and the ApprovalCard offered the button. TIPOS_SEM_SEMPRE_PERMITIR is the SINGLE list — git_push, pr_open, git_merge (whole: the GitMerge() pattern would apply to every target), container_remove, instruction_patch, parallelize, raise_max_parallel — and motivoDeRecusaDoSempreAprovar judges terminal by the command and the rest by type. The refusal is 400 with reason: 'teto_do_sempre_permitir' and actionType. The web hides the button through the copy in apps/web/src/lib/sempre-permitir.ts, checked against the api's by test; a terminal command keeps the button (repeating the parser on screen would be a second yardstick) and receives the api's refusal. When it was born, it did NOT change decide() nor the seeding; since RN-689 both change — git_push/pr_open are in the decide() ceiling and activation seeds only git_commit —, and the pattern the click would record for them would be inert.

RN-631 — The chat recipient is chosen and visible, and the handoff offer is matched by handoffId​

The composer message's recipient was DERIVED: "the most recent agent.activated within the 200-event window" (finding 9-fix). It was a default recipient on the SCREEN side — the defect class that RN-584 closed in the engine — and it was INVISIBLE: the composer did not say who the message went to, and accepting a handoff on this screen changed nothing beyond the log. In the real use of 09/29 the session had handoff.accepted to the Infra and then to the Arquiteto, and the user's "hi" was answered by the Arquiteto without the screen saying so. And the acceptance card matched the offer to the event by the ACTOR/toAgent pair (e.actor.id === offeredHandoff.fromAgent), although handoff.offered has carried handoffId from the start (AT-251).

The rule:

  1. The OPTIONS are the agents that converse (AGENTES_DE_CHAT) and that are already in the session: agent.activated in the window, roster.activatedAgents from the project summary (RN-630, the WHOLE session, only with the summary of the SAME session, in the mold of RN-568) or an ACCEPTED handoff (the list of handoffs has no window). The last two terms are RN-180: the agent does not vanish from the selector because the activation left the 200 events. In the creative session the Criativo is an option before being activated, because the first message activates it (finding 3).

  2. The recipient is what the person CHOSE — in the composer's "Para" selector, or by accepting a handoff ON THIS screen (the gesture of calling that agent; a failed acceptance changes nothing). Nothing in the log chooses for them: an acceptance made in another tab or through another path only adds an option.

  3. A SINGLE option is the recipient, and the composer names it before sending. It is not a default in the sense of RN-584 — there is no other agent the message could go to.

  4. Two or more options and no valid choice: no recipient. The "Enviar" (and Enter) is locked and the screen says in TEXT that a choice is needed — never "the most recent". Zero options is the session chat without an agent (SSE), and the screen says so too. Revised by RN-682: zero options also locks sending — the consultative session without an agent asks for an agent, and SSE to the raw model is no longer called by the screen.

  5. The choice is remembered per session in localStorage — a convenience for the viewer (without storage the screen just asks for the choice again), never product state.

  6. "Parar" stops the agent OF THE TURN (turnoAgentRef, streamingAgent, statusAgent), and only in its absence the recipient: changing the selector in the middle of another agent's turn must not stop the wrong one. The model shown in the topbar follows the recipient.

  7. The offer is matched by the payload's handoffId, never by the actor: each handoff.offered is the card of its own offer, with no pair to confuse nor a "most recent" to choose. Offers to an already activated agent (window OR roster.activatedAgents) do not become acceptable again.

  8. Every pending offer is actionable, and none hides another (AT-253). The card picked ONE offer (handoffs.find, the oldest pending), and the MANUAL handoff (ADR 0109, RN-441) — recorded with the PERSON as actor, and therefore never matched by the actor — had no "Aceitar" and hid the following offers. Now every pending offer to an agent that converses (except the Infra's, which has its own card, RN-499) has the button on its event; two pending ones to the SAME agent give a single button, the most recent one's, and accepting it removes the other through activeFor. The manual handoff pill says "Handoff manual" instead of the person's id.

  9. "Already in the session" is read from window-LESS sources scoped to the REQUESTED session (review of PR #759). The summary's roster.activatedAgents belongs to the project's MOST RECENT session, and activating execution CREATES a new session that becomes that one: the chat session lost the whole source and went back to depending on the 200 window. The sum now has THREE sources — the summary, only when it is this session's; the handoffs of THIS session (whoever received an accepted one and whoever OFFERED one, who was in it); and the per-agent spend of THIS session (GET .../token-usage, aggregated without a window: an agent with a row there ran a turn, and only an activated agent runs a turn). Each source only fixes false negatives, and spend is proof of PRESENCE, never of absence. Declared gap: an agent activated by a direct start, without a handoff, that never ran a turn, in a session that is no longer the most recent, still depends on the window — and whoever has a role below developer (the minimum of the spend route) lacks the third source. Closing it requires the activation aggregate PER SESSION in the api; it was not done here.

  10. A pending offer whose event left the window gets a button in the fixed strip above the composer (review of PR #759). The actionable card belongs to the handoff.offered, and the list of handoffs has no window: in a long session the offer stayed offered and without a button anywhere. The criterion is the CUT, not absence — the offer is older than the oldest event in the window (a just-created offer whose event has not arrived yet does not flash in the strip), and an empty window does not assert a cut. The strip has only the acceptance; the "Ativar execução" shortcut of the Dev Lead card stays in the thread.

The guard of RN-584 (scripts/ci/destinos-do-composer.spec.ts) now reads DESTINATARIO_DA_SESSAO_CRIATIVA instead of the literal from SessionPage.tsx: every destination the composer can give still has its own clause in the engine. No api or engine change.

RN-633 — The manual handoff does not declare readiness, and "already active" for the offer is the project's​

Two reads of the Session screen left the handoff stale (AT-293, AT-294):

  1. The MANUAL handoff does not hide "Estou pronto para produzir" nor "Confirmar arquitetura pronta" (AT-293). prontidaoJaDeclarada and arquiteturaJaDeclarada only asked "is there a handoff leaving the Criativo/Arquiteto?", and the manual handoff (ADR 0109, RN-441) records as fromAgent the LAST activated agent (request-manual-handoff.use-case.ts): requesting a manual handoff to the Staff with the Criativo active hid the readiness button with no readiness at all declared.   2. An offer to an agent already ACTIVE in another session of the project is not actionable (AT-294). "Active" was the SESSION's: after "Ativar execução", the Dev Lead runs in the execution session, and the offer to him in the chat session still had "Aceitar". RN-632 — A PROJECT read polls at the project pace, and every screen that listens to the session channel invalidates through the SAME window​

The real use of 09/29 hit the user's 300 req/min ceiling (RN-579) with two tabs open: 192 × 429 at 07:14, 106 of them on GET /projects/:id/sessions and 20 on GET /projects/:id, and three approve_always clicks refused in the middle (AT-278). RN-579 had put the SESSION screen reads under the channel; the PROJECT ones and the other screens that listen to the channel were left out. The ceiling does NOT change: what drops is the request.

The rule:

  1. A project read that no channel announces polls at 15s (INTERVALO_DO_PROJETO_MS), UNCONDITIONALLY. The session:<id> channel only announces writes of its own session; the project's session list and the rail counters (approvals of the most recent session, pending merges of the project, stories to promote, architecture pending items, hypotheses) change by writes of ANY session — there is no notice to wait for, so the mechanism is a long poll, in the same fallback that RN-579 already accepts for the session. It applies to useProjectSessions/useLatestSession (they were 5s), to the five counters of the ProjectPage frame and to the architecture of the Executores tab. The tab that shows the data as its SUBJECT (Backlog, Arquitetura, PRs) keeps its own poll, and the fastest observer dictates the key's pace. Whoever writes in this tab still invalidates the key immediately.
  2. Whoever only needs the data on click does not poll. Each row of /containers reads its project's most recent session to PROPOSE stop/remove/start; at a 5s poll it was 12 req/min PER PROJECT — nine projects, 108/min from that page alone, the number that matches the 106 in the log. useLatestSession(projectId, false): mount and window focus are enough.
  3. Every screen that listens to the channel goes through criarInvalidadorDoCanal. The Executores and Visão geral tabs invalidated the events on EVERY event.appended, with no window: a dev agent in a burst (10 notices/s) made 630 event GETs per minute in the Executores tab alone. Now both use the SAME invalidator as the Session screen (window per target, the TYPE decides the target), and get as a bonus what was missing: the dev agent's action proposal invalidates the actions immediately, instead of waiting for the 15s fallback. The Visão geral requests the backlog on every notice (the blocked tasks come from it) through the extras parameter, with the same window.
  4. Waiting for the runner stops when it is over. EsperaDoRunner only stopped the GET /projects/:id probe (3s) at the CEILING; once the connection was confirmed, the ceiling's effect exited early and the probe kept going forever — 20 req/min while the panel was on screen, and, being the fastest observer of ['project', id], dragging the page's whole key. Now it stops at the ceiling OR on confirmation.

Numbers (duas-abas.orcamento.test.tsx, the real screens — Shell, SessionPage, ProjectPage on the Executores tab, ContainersPage — over a fetch that counts per route; each tab measured alone, because two tabs are two JS contexts, and summed; req/min, dev → this rule):

ScenarioBeforeAfter
session chat + Executores, live channel70 + 138 = 20870 + 72 = 142
same, dev agent in a burst (10 notices/s)70 + 764 = 83470 + 97 = 167
same, channel that never connects155 + 186 = 341155 + 120 = 275
/containers with 9 projects132 (108 from /sessions)24

What this rule does NOT close: with the channel DOWN in both tabs, 275/min is still close to the ceiling — the Session screen goes back to the usual 3s (RN-579: never worse than it was), and 25 req/min of slack vanish with a burst of clicks. The Shell keeps polling projects-summary and execution/session at 5s and, in the chat tab, the events of the EXECUTION session at 3s (the tab does not have its channel) — 44 of the 70 req/min of the chat tab. A session list created in another tab shows up here within 15s (it was 5s). The incident's number was MATCHED, not reproduced: the log did not say which tabs were open, and the reading that /containers was in one of them is inference from 106 ≈ 9 × 12.

RN-635 — One pending handoff offer per target in the project; the one that stops being valid becomes superseded​

handoffs only recorded offered/accepted, with no expiry, supersession or dedupe: a double click on "architecture ready" gave 2× Infra and 2× Dev Lead, and an offer to an already active agent stayed actionable forever (AT-291, ADR 0182).

  1. At most ONE offered per (project, target). decidirOferta decides: with no pending one, it creates; pending in the SAME session and with no new artifact (the new one is null or equal), it returns the existing one (desfecho: ja_oferecido, no row nor event); any other case creates the new one and replaces the pending one (substituiu_oferta) — returning the old one would lose the new artifact, or leave the requester with nothing to accept in the session they are in.
  2. Whoever replaces records. The row becomes superseded and a handoff.superseded event is born (handoffId, toAgent, motivo, substitutaId) in the session of the OLD offer, actor system, even with the session closed. The original handoff.offered is not touched.
  3. Serialized per target. CreateHandoffUseCase runs in a transaction with pg_advisory_xact_lock of the (project, target) pair: two tabs arriving together produce ONE row. Duplicates from before converge on the next offer or activation, with an event; the migration rewrites no row.
  4. An already active agent receives no offer: 409 reason: agente_ja_ativo, without row or event. Active = agent.activated in a NON-terminal session of the project. The message is the text the model reads: offer_handoff passes it on verbatim, and FalhaDeTurno.origem/1 classifies it as politica.
  5. Activating supersedes. ActivateAgentUseCase (acceptance and direct activation) and ActivateExecutionUseCase (per dev-<modulo>) supersede, after activating, every pending offer to the agent in any session of the project; the accepted one is not touched, and a refused activation supersedes nothing.
  6. "Architecture ready" is idempotent. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase does not trigger the target (infra, dev-lead) that already has a pending offer or is active; with both like that, it neither records nor calls the engine (desfecho: ja_oferecido, jaAtendidos with each one's reason).

RN-644 — The thread cuts by MESSAGE, never splits an exchange and collapses the history in the order it happened​

The visual survey of Round 29 (finding X3, AT-319) measured three defects in the thread cut of RN-177, all in the same function: (1) the "last 5" counted entries, and the handoff, approval and story cards counted as one message each — in a short conversation, the first question and the first answer went to the collapsed history; (2) the cut fell where the count said, possibly leaving the question collapsed and the answer open; (3) the history was grouped by origin, in the order of the origins, and the "LLM" group came before "Usuário" — expanded, the Criativo's answer appeared ABOVE the question that generated it.

The rule, in the thread (the log panel does NOT change — there the axis is the layer):

  1. The cut counts MESSAGES: chat.message, agent.response and chat.structured_question (TimelineEntry.mensagem). Cards and dividers do not count; those that come after the cut stay open with the messages around them. A per-agent collapse (RN-138) and a "Passos do turno" are still ONE entry, and count as one message.
  2. The cut never splits a turn (RN-172): it backs up to the opening of the turn of the message that marked it, so the question always stays together with the answer. That is why the open ones may exceed five — never an exchange in half. The prologue (turn 0) has no opening and does not back up; if backing up reaches the start, there is no history.
  3. The history is ONE block, in chronological order, and DECLARES the cut (RN-180): the title says what the cut counts ("Antes das últimas 5 mensagens") and the trailing separates what stayed inside ("2 mensagens · 2 outras entradas"). The "LLM" label leaves the thread along with the per-origin groups.

What was lost, declared: reopening only what the user said, without reopening the rest, was the reason for the per-origin groups in the thread. It does not survive chronological order — the log panel keeps offering that cut.

RN-637 — The screen reads the TAIL of the session's actions, and the old pending one comes back with it​

GET /projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/actions ordered by ascending seq with a ceiling of 200, and usePendingActions never paginated: from the 201st action of a session on — which a real execution easily reaches, a dev agent proposes dozens of commands per task — the NEW pending one was outside the only page read and vanished from the thread, the Executores and Aprovações (AT-296), precisely when someone was waiting for it.

The rule:

  1. The route accepts latest=true and status=pending. latest brings the limit actions with the highest seq, returned in ASCENDING order and without nextCursor, ignoring afterSeq — the same contract as the events' latest (ADR 0021). status only accepts pending (another value is 400, without querying); combined with latest, it brings the newest pending ones without the decided ones taking up the window. Without the two parameters the contract is the previous one.
  2. The screen asks two questions, and the second only when needed. buscarAcoesDaSessao reads the tail (200); only if it comes back FULL does it also request the pending ones and merge by id, in ascending seq. An old pending one that the tail pushed out is still a decision to be made and does not vanish for having waited too long. The short session — the common case — still costs ONE request, and a failing read of pending ones brings the query down (the screen says it failed, never pretends an empty queue — RN-088).

What this rule does NOT close: with more than 200 PENDING ones in a session, the oldest beyond them stay out (the ceiling is the same limit); and what the thread shows as DECIDED is still the tail — an old decided action, outside the 200 newest, does not appear in the thread. Pending items of the WHOLE project are another read (RN-638).

RN-638 — Whoever asks "what awaits a decision" reads the PROJECT's queue, never the most recent session​

The rail's Aprovações counter, the "needs you" panel (RN-467), the Aprovações tab, the Visão geral roster and the Código tab read the pending ones from useLatestSession — the session CREATED last —, which is only the execution one by coincidence. An ideation or a chat opened after the execution zeroed the counter and hid from the roster the dev agents waiting for a decision (AT-297). And the block of pending items from other sessions in the chat (RN-626) only existed in an active session, while the container_start that the Infra Lead proposes in the CHAT unblocks the dev.blocked_by_container that appears in the EXECUTION (AT-298).

The rule:

  1. The queue is the project's. Those screens read useProjectPendingActions (GET /projects/:projectId/actions?status=pending, in any session), all through the SAME key ['project-pending-actions', projectId, undefined] — at the project pace of RN-632, and at 3s only in the Aprovações tab, which has it as its subject. The ProjectPage frame takes the PR counter (git_merge) from the SAME read, instead of a second query. The queues stay separate, each with its own badge — nothing is summed (RN-467).
  2. Each card decides through the session the action ITSELF carries. In the Aprovações tab, approve, deny, "sempre permitir" and the batch call the endpoint with action.sessionId, and invalidate the project queue by prefix and the actions of the action's session. The tab's PR and gate blocks read events and actions of the current EXECUTION session (RN-139), and only without it of the most recent one.
  3. Pending items from other sessions appear in any state. The chat block also shows in closed and technical sessions — deciding is about the action of the OTHER session, not conversation in this one (RN-581 keeps refusing conversation) —, and the Executores tab gets the SAME block for the execution session: the chat's container_start becomes visible where the block appears.
  4. The proposal arrives through the channel, without waiting for the poll. Every proposed_action.*/action.* notice from any session channel a screen listens to also invalidates the project queue (pendenciasDoProjeto in criarInvalidadorDoCanal, 2s window), and dev.blocked_by_container too — the proposal that unblocks it is born in another session, whose channel nobody there listens to (AT-299). No poll went up.
  5. The block fits in the column and shows all of them (AT-318). At the width of the thread and the composer (780px), collapsible, with the PRESENCE of each queue in the header — "Aprovações 3 · Merges de PR 1", each with its own number, never the sum (RN-467) — visible even when collapsed. Cards are born with the detail CLOSED (detalheRecolhido in ApprovalCard): open, they covered ~60% of the thread and left one card in view out of three. The origin label shows ONCE per session, with the time of the oldest — per card, it repeated between one card and the next. The ceiling of 20 cards and the declared cut (RN-180) remain.

What this rule does NOT close: the notice only arrives where there is a screen listening to a session channel (Sessão; Visão geral, the most recent session; Executores, the execution one). In a tab without a channel (Aprovações, PRs, Backlog…) or for a proposal made in a session whose channel no open screen listens to, the counter arrives through the project poll, within 15s; opening a session channel in the frame would change the session lifecycle (the channel is RN-064's heartbeat) and was left out. The Aprovações counter still counts the pending git_merge, as before — the panel dedupes it into the PR queue. The gap of the WORKSPACE role in place of the effective one (RN-471) applies to the new Executores block as it does to the chat's.

RN-646 — A block and an inert control state the reason of WHOEVER is on screen: the PRs tab speaks of the PR list, and Parar/Remover without a container say there is no container​

Two screens showed a correct state with the text of another place (AT-323, AT-324 — findings P1 and K1/K2 of the visual survey of Round 29).

A row with a running container gets no text at all.

The long reason for the missing broker. The text that names BROKER_URL was nine lines long and tripled the height of the table row. RN-648 — The sidebar, the Dashboard card and the artifacts panel do not contradict each other: each empty state says WHICH session it read, and counter and list count in the same unit​

Three screens asserted "nothing" next to a screen that showed something (AT-325 — findings S2/D2/X6 of the visual survey of AT-290). Reproduction with the real engine was not possible in this environment (egress blocks repo.hex.pm and Alpine, and no image compiles); the three contradictions were MEASURED in the code and proven by tests that fail before the fix. The Dashboard one was born, in the survey, from a 500 of the engine stub in the workspace summary — but the text that turned it into "no activity" is the web's, and with the real engine any summary failure would produce the same.

The sidebar read the EXECUTION session, and only it. The Atividades block (RN-198) requested the events of the current execution session (useActiveExecutionSession). In a project with only conversation sessions it is null, the list came back empty, and the sidebar said "Nenhum agente entrou em ação ainda" next to a Visão geral with the Criativo waiting. Now: with a current execution, the sidebar keeps reading IT (the dev agents and the -2 instances are what the grouping of RN-198 exists to show, and the queryKey is the Executores tab's); WITHOUT execution, it reads the SAME session as the Visão geral and the Dashboard card — the most recent working one (useLatestSession, the rule of sessaoMaisRecente). The states that collapsed into the same text separate (RN-470): loading (nothing is asserted), error (its own text), project without a session ("Este projeto ainda não tem sessão."), and the session read without an agent, with the text NAMING which one ("…na sessão de execução…" / "…na sessão mais recente…"). The session list is only requested without execution, and with the freshness of a project cycle (frescorMs in useProjectSessions): when the sidebar enables it the project frame has already brought it, and the request budget of RN-632/RN-645 does not grow.

The Dashboard card had one text for four states. "Sem atividade ainda" came out with the workspace summary LOADING, with it FAILED (the survey's case: the summary responded 500 and the card of a project with sixteen events said there were none), with the project WITHOUT a session and with the most recent session empty. Now there are four texts: "carregando atividade…", "atividade indisponível", "Nenhuma sessão ainda" and "Sem atividade na sessão mais recente ainda". The row still reads the most recent working session (latestSessionId), the same as the Visão geral and the sidebar without execution — the api did not change.

"Artefatos gerados 3" over a single group "PO 1". The section header counted the backlog TREE (epic, story and task: 3) and the per-agent group counted only the ROOTS (1). Both now count in the same unit — each item carries quantos (1, plus the descendants when it is a backlog root), the header is the sum of the items and each group is the sum of its own, so the sum of the groups IS the header, by construction. And the section's empty state says what it counts ("Nenhuma PR nem item de backlog nesta sessão ainda.") instead of the generic "Nada ainda.", which next to a brief or a rule of the same session seemed to deny they existed — the section's scope (PR and backlog, RN-159) does not change.

RN-639 — What changes per token does not re-render the screen, and what follows the bootstrap polls at 3 s and stops at the end​

Three screens did work nobody saw (AT-301/AT-302). The Session screen re-rendered ENTIRELY on every token of a turn — the in-progress text lived in the state of the hook it called. The provisioning and adoption screens polled the bootstrap status and the technical session's events at 1 s, and the events never stopped, even with the repository ready. And /status hit forever a service that did not respond.

  1. The in-progress text lives in an external store. The consultative chat text and the turn's activity strip stay in a per-session store (criarStoreDoStreaming), subscribed via useSyncExternalStore only by the two components that draw them — the thread bubble and the strip. The page subscribes to ONE boolean question (has the turn shown content yet?), which is what the "thinking" timer (RN-131) needs and which changes once per turn. The strip's reducer is the same; what changed is who holds the state.
  2. The bootstrap is followed at 3 s. Status and events, on both screens.
  3. And it stops at the end. Status and events stop when the bootstrap converges (provisioned) and when the query errors (pollQueParaNoErro). FAILURE (provision_failed) is terminal in adoption and NOT in provisioning: there "Tentar novamente" triggers a new bootstrap and the screen needs to see its progress (RN-477).
  4. /status stops on error. A service that responds — including with 5xx, which becomes status: 'error' in a resolved body — continues every 5 s. A service that does not respond stops being asked by timer; window focus and remount ask again, and the first success resumes the pace.

RN-643 — Below 768px the sidebar becomes a drawer and the project rail becomes a horizontal bar; the page never scrolls sideways​

The visual audit of Round 29 (AT-290, finding S1) measured that the product had no mobile layout after login: at 390px the sidebar (264px) and the project rail (180px) remained FIXED, adding up to 444px of frame, and the content was left with 0 to 126px or overflowed to the right. Configurações reached 114 truncated texts (validacao-visual.js).

The rule:

  1. One cut, one source. The breakpoint is CONSULTA_MOVEL ((max-width: 767px)), read by useLayoutMovel. Whoever switches layout reads that hook and applies the mobile design through a CLASS; the CSS modules have no @media of their own for it. That way what the JS decides and what the CSS draws do not diverge at a boundary pixel, and the component test (jsdom, without CSS) proves the same cut the browser applies. Without matchMedia the layout is the DESKTOP one: mobile only applies when the query asserts it.
  2. The sidebar becomes a drawer. A bar at the top carries the menu button (aria-expanded, aria-controls) and the brand. The drawer is a modal dialog (role="dialog", aria-modal): on opening, focus enters it; Tab does not leave; Esc, the X and the backdrop close it and return focus to the menu button. It also closes on following any link inside it (the project tabs only change ?tab=) and when the route changes from outside. In the drawer the sidebar always appears EXPANDED, and the "Recolher menu" button disappears: manual collapse (RN-195) is a desktop preference, it stays recorded and applies again when the window crosses the cut back.
  3. The project rail becomes a horizontal bar. They are the same 12 leaves, in the same order, with the group headers inline and aria-orientation="horizontal". The arrows that move are left and right, and the active tab is scrolled into the visible strip. The bar scrolls INSIDE; the page does not scroll sideways. The project body becomes a column (the bar above the panel), and the Visão geral stacks the team and the activity instead of keeping the 360px rail beside them.

Measured (390×844, dark theme, api seed, validacao-visual.js injected): the document's scrollWidth = 390 on all authenticated screens (dashboard, the 12 tabs, /containers, /account), and <main> with the whole 390px. In Configurações, texto-cortado dropped from 114 to 33. The rest is component text (tables and section labels), a matter of typography and space, not of frame. The fora-da-viewport left over in Visão geral and Aprovações are tabs of the horizontal bar beyond the edge, where internal scrolling reaches them.

Revised by ADR 0211 (AT-404): item 3 no longer applies — the project rail left, and with it the horizontal bar. On the phone the project tabs live in the DRAWER (item 2), with the groups, the active one and the counters; choosing one closes the drawer. The project body no longer becomes a column: only the paddings shrink.

What this rule does NOT close: the Código tab keeps the 48px rail of CodeShell and the editor in columns; it was not designed for the phone. The Session screen inherits the new frame, but the top bar and the thread still have findings X1–X3 of the audit. The duplication of tab navigation (drawer and bar) closed in ADR 0211.

RN-645 — Configuration is not fetched again on every mount, does not poll, and the Configurações tab has three frame strips, not four​

The visual survey of Round 29 (finding G1, AT-321) went through the Configurações sections in ~40s and the project's whole page turned into "Limite de requisições excedido" — the 300 req/min ceiling is the USER's (RN-579). The script RELOADED the page per section, and one load of the tab cost 55 requests. Measured with the real screens, the defect had three parts, and none of them calls for raising the ceiling:

The rule:

  1. CONFIGURATION data is valid for one minute (FRESCOR_DA_CONFIGURACAO_MS). With TanStack's staleTime: 0, every observer that MOUNTS after the first one refetches. The sections only mount after the project arrives, so GET /projects/:id, GET /projects/:id/git/repository and GET /workspaces went out TWICE on every load; and switching tabs and coming back remounted the 19 sections and redid 31 fetches. Configuration only changes by MUTATION, and every mutation of the tab invalidates its own key — invalidating ignores staleTime, so whoever saves sees the new value immediately. What the minute delays is a change made by ANOTHER person, which still arrives on window focus and on the next mount after the minute. Operational state stays out (container lifecycle, spend per agent and per key, device keys with lastUsedAt, bootstrap plan): there the question is "what is up now".
  2. Configuration does not poll. The proficiency profile and the instruction version history polled at 15s — 8 req/min against the ceiling for two lists that only change through their own section (which invalidates) or through an approved patch.
  3. The summary LIES DOWN above the sections, at any width. As a sticky column next to them it was the fourth vertical strip (sidebar 264 + rail 180 + summary 208): at 1440px ~740px of content remained and the models table cut the agent name at 79px and the model's at 91px (finding G2). The column had no way to pay its own price even on a wide monitor, because .body has a ceiling of 1040px (ADR 0078). Laid down, it gives the 208px back to the sections; the price is what the narrow window already paid — one loses the "where am I" STUCK to the screen, not the navigation. No token changed.

Numbers (configuracoes.orcamento.test.tsx, Shell + ProjectPage on the Configurações tab over a fetch that counts per route; dev → this rule):

ScenarioBeforeAfter
tab load (2.5s)5350
one minute idle on the tab7668
Configurações → Visão geral → back (configuration fetches)310
tab load, with the resolved bindings in a BATCH (RN-654, AT-334)4930

The "After" of the first three rows were measured on the same base as the "Before"; integrated into dev with RN-638 (the frame reads the project queue only once), the load stood at 49 and the minute at 64. The fourth row is RN-654, measured on dev at 94e5dc721d: the 20 bindings resolved per key became ONE read, and the test holds the load at 30 and the minute at 64.

What this rule does NOT close: until RN-654, 20 of the load's requests were the RESOLVED binding of each agent (17) and of each area (3), one route per key (GET projects/:projectId/agent-bindings/:agentSlug) — that part closed with the BATCH route. RELOADING the page per section, as the survey script did, still costs 30 per load (~10 loads per minute before the ceiling); navigating through the summary INSIDE the tab remounts nothing and costs zero. The 68 of the minute all come from the FRAME (the Shell polls projects-summary and execution/session at 5s and the execution session's events at 3s), common to every tab — the same gap that RN-632 declares.

RN-654 — The resolved bindings of all agents and areas come in a single read​

RN-645 measured 49 requests on loading the Configurações tab, and 20 of them were the RESOLVED binding of each agent (17) and of each area (3), one route per key. Three sections read those keys — models per agent, models per area and best models per capability —, and the 300 req/min ceiling is the USER's (RN-579).

The rule:

  1. GET projects/:projectId/model-bindings/resolved?agents=…&areas=… returns { agents: [{ key, binding }], areas: [{ key, binding }] }, in the requested order and without repetition. Each binding is EXACTLY what the individual route would respond for that key (GET .../agent-bindings/:slug, GET .../area-bindings/:key): the same cascade workspace › projeto › área › agente without a session, the same origins the screen turns into a chain (RN-470), the Criativo inheritance, and null when no level has a model. There is no new cascade: the use case calls ResolveModelBindingUseCase key by key, with the input the individual route would pass.
  2. The minimum role is that of the individual read routes, viewer. Whoever does not reach the project gets the SAME 403.
  3. The read is contained (ADR 0060): the keys come in a comma-separated list, with the slug alphabet (lowercase, digits, -, _), and are at most 64 combined (TETO_DE_CHAVES_NO_LOTE). A malformed key or a batch above the ceiling is 400 naming the reason, never a key silently discarded — the response would assert about fewer keys than the screen requested.
  4. The web reads the batch through ONE queryKey (['model-bindings-resolved', projectId]), served by one request to the three Configurações sections and, since AT-339, also to the Visão geral and the Executores tab (useBindingsDosAgentes): the roster agents the catalog knows come from that SAME key — the cache one tab warmed serves the other without a request —, and those the catalog does not know (the dev-<modulo>) come from ONE extra batch read, under the same prefix and in slices of the same ceiling. Every write of an agent or area binding rereads the whole batch by that PREFIX, which reaches both reads; no per-agent key is left to invalidate. The failure of these reads leaves the agent card without a model — "I don't know", never an asserted model — and does not fall back to the per-agent route.
  5. The batch failure does not become "no model". With a single read, the failure is of all keys at once: the section states the reason ONCE, with the api's sentence and the action to reread, and each row says "não lido" in place of the chain. While the batch does not respond, the row says "lendo…". "Sem modelo em nenhum nível" stays reserved for the null the api asserted.

Numbers: the tab load dropped from 49 to 30 requests (configuracoes.orcamento.test.tsx, on dev at 94e5dc721d); the idle minute stays at 64, all from the frame. In AT-339, the Executores tab load dropped from 29 to 27 and the Visão geral's from 33 to 31 (duas-abas.orcamento.test.tsx, with the base roster of three agents — with team and modules, the drop is one per card), and going from Configurações to the Visão geral stopped fetching any binding (before, 3).

What this rule does NOT close: the per-key routes still exist in the api (no screen reads them anymore). A dev-<modulo> whose key exceeds 64 characters would be refused by the batch format, and the read of the extras would fail entirely — not measured on a real project, and declared.

RN-651 — On the phone, the Session panel is a drawer, the bar wraps, and the table becomes cards​

The "after" visual audit of Round 29 (docs/explanation/auditoria-visual-rodada-29.md, findings N1 and N3 to N8) measured, at 390px, what RN-643 had not reached: in the Session the "Contexto da sessão" panel kept ~320px and left ~70px to the thread (one word per line), and the bar pushed "Iniciar ideação" and "Encerrar" past the edge; in /containers seven fractional columns overlapped the headers and cut the actions; in "Modelos por agente" the agent name had 6px and the selector 0px; /status scrolled sideways (413px); the Dashboard search became "Bus"; the session name in the Criativo's list had 0px; and the mobile rail left the active tab cut off, with no sign that it scrolled.

The rule (the cut is the same useLayoutMovel of RN-643, and the design comes through a CLASS or attribute that the component sets, never through @media):

  1. The Session context panel is born CLOSED on the phone and opens as a DRAWER over the thread, from the right: a modal dialog with the panel's name, focus on the X on opening, Esc, X and backdrop close it and return focus to whoever opened it. On desktop it is born open next to the thread, as always. Crossing the cut goes back to the new side's default — a panel open on desktop does not reappear squeezing the thread on the phone. The exception is navigation that COMES to the panel (highlightEvent, the Psicólogo's evidence chip): then it is born open on the phone too.
  2. The Session bar wraps, never cuts. Exit, state, title and the panel toggle stay on the first line; type, settings, "Iniciar ideação" and "Encerrar" go down, and go down again if needed. What the bar shows is still decided by its width (RN-620 item 6).
  3. Every Table becomes a stack of cards on the phone. Each row is a card and each cell carries the column label next to the value; the header disappears. A column without a label, or marked largaNoMovel (a selector, a block of actions), takes the card's width with the label on top.
  4. The page does not scroll sideways, and what identifies the row does not vanish. /status scrolls the table inside its own wrapper; the Dashboard search gets a full line; the session list row wraps with the name on top, whole.
  5. The mobile rail follows the active tab and says it scrolls. The active one is brought into the strip on mount, on switch, when the rail's CONTENT changes (the counters arrive later and widen the earlier tabs) and when the fonts finish loading — never on every render, otherwise whoever scrolled the strip by hand would be pulled back. The edge that hides tabs fades (data-rola-inicio/data-rola-fim).

Measured (390×844, both themes, native api with the seed, validacao-visual.js injected): scrollWidth 390 on all seven screens; zero texto-cortado on the Dashboard, the Criativo's list, the Session (with and without the drawer), /containers and /status; in Configurações the 33 dropped to zero, and the rail's active tab stayed whole within the strip on the three tabs measured.

What this rule does NOT close: in the minimal bar "Encerrar" still has only the icon and the accessible name (RN-620 decides that by the bar's width). The panel toggle moves up to the title line only in PAINTING (order): the Tab order follows the DOM's. The fora-da-viewport that the checker still reports in Configurações and Aprovações are decorative icons with position: absolute inside controls below the fold, not something cut off.

The author of each utterance in the thread is the event's actor (RN-652)​

RN-652 — chat.message is drawn under the event's ACTOR — person, agent or unknown —, never under whoever is viewing the screen​

Until now every chat.message came out with the name and avatar of whoever was logged in: in a shared session, another person's utterance appeared with YOUR name, and an agent's with your e-mail (finding N2 of the visual audit of Round 29, hidden while the thread grouped the history by origin). The author now comes from the event's actor, which the api records with the sender's id (SendAgentMessageUseCase, SendChatMessageUseCase) and which the generic append-event route accepts of any kind. The outcomes do not collapse:

  1. The viewer (actor.id equal to the token's sub; without it, by the e-mail of the member row) — the name or e-mail of the member row, otherwise the session's e-mail, and only in the absence of both "Você".
  2. Another person the screen can name — their name, otherwise the e-mail, from TWO reads composed into a single list (comporMembros), the PROJECT one before the WORKSPACE one: GET projects/:id/members (minimum viewer), under the SAME queryKey as the Configurações tab, and since AT-335 GET workspaces/:id/members (RN-655), of the PROJECT's workspace. Whoever has both rows appears once, through the project one — the same order as the role overlay (RN-471).

Another person the screen CANNOT name — "Outro membro": without a project or workspace row (someone who left the workspace and still has utterances in the log), or both reads failed or have not arrived yet. The read that fails does not erase the other, and neither of them breaks the thread. Until AT-335 this was the declared GAP of whoever joins only through the workspace role, which had no read route; the route was born by owner decision.
  4. Agent — nomeDoAgente and the agent's avatar/color, like agent.response.
  5. Unknown actor (absent, without id, system or a kind outside person/agent) — "Autor desconhecido", never "Você".

The backlog.story_promotion_returned narration, which had the same defect (the viewer's name over whoever returned the story), goes through the same function. The composer's OPTIMISTIC message keeps the viewer's e-mail — it is always theirs.

Reading the workspace members (RN-655)​

RN-655 — GET workspaces/:id/members is viewer, and returns only id, name, e-mail and role​

The session thread (RN-652) only named whoever had a row in project_members; whoever joins the project only through the WORKSPACE role became "Outro membro", because there was no route that read the workspace members (owner decision, AT-335). It is viewer, that of the neighbouring reads (GET workspaces/:id, .../projects) and that of GET projects/:id/members, which it completes — whoever opens a session needs to know who spoke in it, and a workspace viewer already sees every project of the workspace.

The response has the SAME shape as the project read — userId, name, email, role (the WORKSPACE role) — and nothing else: no createdAt, no account state. A nonexistent workspace is 404, and a non-member is refused by the RolesGuard (403). There is still no workspace members SCREEN: the read exists to name, and the write routes remain API-only.

The policy reason on each Aprovações card (RN-656)​

RN-656 — The session events read filters by actionId, and each card of the Aprovações tab reads its own reason through it​

The action does not keep the policy reason: it lives in proposed_action.created (RN-567, RN-609). The Aprovações tab reads the PROJECT queue (RN-638) and the log of ONE session, so since AT-333 it said in a single note how many actions were left without a reason (RN-614). Owner decision (AT-336): each card shows its OWN.

What was measured. The two options for the card were an actionId filter on the events read or a route that read the event by action. The filter is the smaller: it reuses the route (GET .../sessions/:sessionId/events, viewer), the DTO and the use case, and the action already carries the sessionId of the session that proposed it. No index or migration is born: the predicate on payload->>'actionId' runs INSIDE the session, which the unique index (session_id, seq) already narrows. A PROJECT read by actionId would require a new route to find the session the card already knows.

The rule in the api. actionId returns only the events whose payload.actionId is that action, in the requested session — it never crosses sessions. It combines with the other parameters and limit counts only the matching ones; seq stops being contiguous in the page, so whoever filters does NOT derive omitted ones by subtraction (RN-180). Empty is 400: a filter that vanishes with the wrong string would return the whole log to whoever asked for an action's reason.

The rule on the screen. useDecisoesDaPolitica: an action whose event is in the log the tab ALREADY loaded uses that one, without a request; the others read by action, in their session, with staleTime: Infinity — an event is immutable, so each action costs ONE read while the cache lives and the queue polls without repeating any. Nothing is requested while the tab is still loading its own log. A read that responds WITHOUT the event gives the "motivo não registrado" sentence (never silent); only the read that FAILS leaves the card silent, and that one, and only that one, is what the top note counts ("de N das M ações abaixo"). Since AT-340 the cards of the pending items from OTHER sessions in the chat (RN-626, PendenciasDeOutrasSessoes, also in the Executores tab) go through the SAME hook and the SAME cache: every action there is from another session, so none is covered by the screen's log and each one reads by action — only the DRAWN ones, within the block's card ceiling, and one the Aprovações tab already read costs nothing there (and vice versa). A read that fails also silences the card and is stated once, at the top of the block. The "needs you" panel does NOT use this path: it reads no log and opening it does not trigger a query, so the card there stays silent, as RN-614 already said — a decision, not a gap. No ceiling changes.

RN-660 — The PO's handoff to the Arquiteto is accepted by the SYSTEM when the backlog is covered and the repository is local and without credentials​

The po → arquiteto offer that the engine creates (POST /internal/sessions/:id/handoffs) is accepted without a click, in the same request and AFTER the offer's transaction, when the four conditions hold (decidirAceiteAutomatico, pure):

  1. the offer is offered;
  2. the backlog is covered: the project has at least ONE business rule (artifact.business_rule) and NONE without a story that cites it in businessRuleIds — the SAME computeCoverage as the Backlog tab and the PO's read (RN-164). Zero rules is not covered;
  3. the repository is local and without credentials: the project has no repository (the acceptance provisions local) or has a local one, and has no git connection (OAuth) in project_git_connections;
  4. whoever opened the session still has developer in the project (effective role, RN-471) — the minimum of the human acceptance route.

The acceptor is still AcceptHandoffUseCase: the repository is born there, before activateAgent (RN-582, ADR 0165), on behalf of whoever opened the session. The acceptance is auditable: handoff.accepted and agent.activated come out with the SYSTEM actor handoff-auto-accept, and handoff.accepted carries automatico: true, emNomeDe and the criterio (regras, cobertas, repositorio). A condition that fails records nothing — the offer stays with the usual button, and the response to the engine says the reason (regras_sem_historia, repositorio_nao_local, credencial_de_git_no_projeto…). A failure AFTER deciding "yes" does not bubble up: it becomes the handoff.auto_accept_failed event (origin infra) and the thread shows it. With the acceptance done, the offer_handoff tool tells the PO that the Arquiteto has already been activated. A remote repository or one with credentials still asks for the click, and the manual handoff (ADR 0109) too.

It is accepted only when ALL hold (decidirAceiteImplicitoDoPo): the offer is criativo → po, offered, of THIS session, and carries as artifact the product_brief born AFTER the most recent marked readiness.confirmed. The 400 for "not offered" is not a failure: someone decided the offer through another path in the interval, and that is already in the log. The screen hands the composer recipient to the PO on the click (the gesture of calling him, RN-631); until he joins, the choice does not count and the Criativo keeps receiving. No ceiling moves: accepting the PO does not provision a repository (only the Arquiteto and the Dev Lead, RN-582), does not merge nor push.

The dev agent's PR targets dev, and the gate judges that PR's diff (RN-664)​

RN-664 — The agents' work is born from dev, their PR targets dev, and the gate judges the diff against dev — the three together​

The product's branch policy has work born from dev (the bootstrap creates dev and qa from main, RN-582), but until now nobody pointed the agents at it: the dev agent's pr_open carried no targetBranch and the api filled in repo.defaultBranch (main); the Arquiteto's ADR PR was born from main and targeted main; the project's working tree opened default_branch; the gate computed the diff against it; and the QA context said "Repositório · branch main" (AT-250, item A4 of the real use of 09/29). Every agent PR skipped the dev → qa → main pipeline.

Owner decision (09/30): the THREE now use dev, together — changing only one would leave the gate judging a diff that is not the PR's. The WORKING branch is dev and it is NOT the provider's default_branch (which remains the one promotion reaches last and is still read where it is the question):

  • the project's working tree opens dev (ensure_remoto/2 ignores the remote's default_branch to choose the base), and each dev agent's worktree is born from dev EXPLICITLY, not from HEAD — a workspace initialized before this rule is stuck on default_branch (the ready mark prevents re-initializing) and gets the local dev from origin/dev, without a new fetch;
  • the dev agent's pr_open carries targetBranch: "dev" in the payload, and the api, without the field (an action proposed before), fills in dev and no longer the defaultBranch; the ADR PR is born from dev and targets dev;
  • the gate's diff is dev...HEAD, and the project context line says "Repositório · branch de trabalho dev".

Repository WITHOUT dev (adopted without bootstrap, or a bootstrap that did not reach create_dev_branch): there is NO fallback to default_branch — it would be the agent working and the gate judging over a base that is not the PR's. Each point fails NAMED, through the behavior it already had for a missing branch, with one new exception: the working tree refused nothing and created an EMPTY LOCAL dev (the path of the bare that never received a push), marked ready and never re-initialized again. Now that path only applies to a remote WITHOUT any branch; with branches and without origin/dev, initialization raises with the named message (mensagem_sem_branch_de_trabalho/1, "o repositório do projeto não tem a branch dev… crie a branch… e tente de novo") and .git is undone (AT-112), so the next attempt, with dev created, initializes normally. The worktree refuses with the same message when there is neither dev nor origin/dev; the diff fails with git's error naming the revision; the provider refuses the PR (and the creation of the ADR branch) naming the ref. infra (open_infra_pr) did NOT change: it still is born from and targets defaultBranch.

The value lives in TWO places, on purpose, one per language, and they change together: BRANCH_DE_TRABALHO in the api and branch_de_trabalho/0 in the engine.
