The Infra Lead does not announce a start it did not make (RN-668)​

RN-668 — What the Infra Lead's turn announces about starting the container is decided by the code, not by the model's text​

It is RN-163 ("nothing is announced that the code will not execute") applied to the Infra Lead. In the real use of 09/29 (session be70, seq 282) he wrote that he would start the container "in parallel" to the infra PR, and no start tool.call came afterwards (AT-264). There were two causes in the code, and both close here:

  1. The response's whole batch is dispatched before the turn ends. An accepted propose_infra_pr ends the turn without a new trip to the model — it is the only point where the CODE cuts the loop with the model wanting to continue —, but it stopped dispatching in the MIDDLE of the batch: a propose_container_start (or container_start_via_runner) requested in the SAME response, after the PR, vanished without tool.call, without tool.result and without notice. Now it is the Dev Lead's form (propose_execution_plan): all calls of the response run, and only afterwards does the accepted PR end the turn. A second propose_infra_pr in the same response is refused with a reason (tool.call + tool.result with ok: false) — only the first consolidates with Workflows.
  2. The turn's closing says, with a SERVER sentence, when the start was NOT proposed — the form of the Criativo's consolidated outcome (encerrar/2). The decision is by what the loop executed (was any start proposal ACCEPTED by the api in this turn?), never by what the model wrote; its text is not read. It speaks in two cases: the turn ended through the PR and no start was proposed; or a start was attempted, refused, and no accepted proposal came afterwards. A turn that never touched the start (a question, a gate correction) gets no sentence at all, and neither does a container already REGISTERED running/provisioning (the same local read as recusa_ja_de_pe/2, without HTTP).

The kickoff and the description of propose_infra_pr now say what the code does: the start comes BEFORE the PR or in the SAME response, because the PR ends the turn. That is help for the model, not the guarantee — the guarantee is the closing of item 2.

Nothing here starts a container or proposes a start, with the refusals by mode and state intact (RN-566/RN-610). Since RN-671 (AT-260) the first start is a SERVER step in the kickoff, marked by the SAME registrar_subida: in the common case it was proposed and the closing of item 2 has nothing to say; it still speaks when the server's start was refused (or DENIED by the policy, which since then counts as a refusal) and when it was not up to the server (no routing, runner) and the model did not propose it.

RN-669 — The path scope compares against the REAL execution folder: /work and the container's /tmp when it is up​

The scope ceiling of ADR 0055 compared every command with the project folder on the HOST, including when the command runs INSIDE the container (RN-492/RN-502). In the real use of 09/29, the 37 "scope" requests were /work/... and /tmp compared with /home/<usuario>/projetos-brabo/<projeto> (AT-258).

With a REGISTERED running container in a container or mounted project, the scope root is /work — the mount point, where the folder and the project's .worktrees live — plus the container's OWN /tmp. The cwd arrives as a host path and is translated to /work by the same engine rule (cwd_para_container/2): the root becomes /work, what is under it becomes /work/..., what is outside stays as it came and remains outside. In mounted the translation is bijective. Without a container, the root is still the project folder on the host, and the host's /tmp stays OUTSIDE.

It applies to whoever is not on autopilot (the specific terminal rule): the autopilot does not go through the scope (RN-603, kept by RN-670). projectScopeRoot does not change nor merge with permissionsFilePath (RN-478); the auto-approval FLOOR remains only for container mode (RN-493). runner stays out, on purpose: the api does not know whether the runner will route to the container or to the host (RN-558). A command argument with a HOST path now counts as outside when there is a container — the engine translates only the cwd, and inside the container that path does not exist.

RN-670 — Auto mode is the AUTOPILOT, and "Sempre permitir" does not switch it off​

Owner decision of 10/01 (ADR 0189): RN-603 is NOT revoked. Now the specific auto_approve under the wildcard auto_approve resolves as the WILDCARD. A specific one that says something else (require_approval, deny) still wins, and with the toggle back in manual the specific one recorded by the click applies alone again, with the scope. The click still records the specific one; what decides whether it already exists is the especifica field of the resolution, never the resolved mode.

The screen says what the autopilot unlocks and what it does not, with ONE list in the three places where the mode is switched on: the Executores batch card (RN-661, open), the ApprovalCard and the toggle of the agent card (collapsed). The "does not unlock" is the text RN-661 already had, reused.

RN-675 — "Sempre permitir" records VERB + SUBCOMMAND, one pattern per command segment​

Owner decision of 10/01 (AT-257, which closes AT-170 — point 6 of ADR 0055, the unit of generalization; ADR 0189). Until now the click recorded the WHOLE command, byte for byte (Terminal(<comando>)): the next command was almost never the same — 173 clicks in the real use of 09/29 —, and the compound became ONE pattern whose content only matched the FIRST segment, so cd src && npm test only freed cd src.

Now each SEGMENT of the command (the same cut as decide(): &&, ||, ;, |, &) becomes a pattern, and the unit is:

  • the verb alone (ls) → the verb;
  • verb + word (npm test, git status, mix test, npx vitest) → both. A "word" starts with a letter, without /, ., =, glob or flag; an argument that looks like a word (cd src) stays as a subcommand — the NARROW side of the doubt, because telling the two apart would require a list of verbs, which is the space that findings Z/AD say does not converge;
  • verb + argument that is not a word (cat src/x.ts, cd ../lib) → the verb;
  • verb + FLAG (ls -la src, git -C /x status) → the EXACT segment: the form with a flag is where verb and invocation diverge, and generalizing there would be choosing a form from within the code;
  • a unit that is a PREFIX of an RN-418 ceiling (git remote, gh pr) → the EXACT segment; and if even the exact one is a prefix (git alone), no pattern for that segment.

Matching is still the usual one (token prefix), a click on a command with an external or privileged effect is still refused whole beforehand (motivoDeRecusaDoSempreAprovar, 400 teto_do_sempre_permitir), the decide() ceiling runs after the file, and the path scope still limits WHERE outside the autopilot (RN-669). Whoever can record is whoever already could (the endpoint's role, unchanged); the precedence with auto mode is that of RN-670. A module dev agent's "Sempre permitir" still goes to agent_autonomy (RN-509), without a pattern. Only the patterns that are MISSING are recorded and narrated; permission.granted carries patterns (the recorded list) and pattern (the same list joined by comma, for the timeline).

RN-663 — PR merge refuses the already merged PR and the repeated proposal; a pending gate is only a notice​

The real use of 09/29 measured both holes: pr-6 had THREE git_merge executed, and pr-4 was merged with the task in awaiting_qa. The api did not dedupe git_merge per PR (only the screen did, and only in the same list), and LocalGitProvider returned the already merged PR without error — the executor recorded a second executed for the same merge.

  1. Proposal. A git_merge of a PR that a previous execution already merged (executed with state: 'merged') is 409 pr_ja_mergeado; with a LIVE proposal of the same PR (pending, approved or auto_approved), 409 merge_ja_proposto. In both, nothing is created. Denied or failed do not count: whoever denied or saw it fail can try again. The comparison is by the payload's pullRequestId, across the whole project (any session).
  2. Approval. Approving a pending git_merge whose PR ANOTHER proposal already merged is 409 pr_ja_mergeado, before any effect, and the action stays pending for whoever sees it to deny. A merely LIVE sibling does not prevent deciding this one.
  3. Provider. LocalGitProvider refuses to merge an already merged PR with GitPullRequestAlreadyMergedError, and the target does not move — aligned with GitHub, which refuses the repeated merge.
  4. A pending gate is a NOTICE, never a refusal (owner decision, 09/30). The PRs tab and the chat's "Mergear" say in TEXT which gate is missing (qa-verificada with awaiting_qa or a gate not yet opened, secops-segura with awaiting_secops), and the button and the card stay active. awaiting_user, a done task and a PR without a task give no notice. The "blocked gate" (task blocked) stays as it was.
  5. No ceiling moves. Merge into a protected branch remains unconditional, human require_approval (RN-418, decide.ts): this rule only prevents proposing or approving when there is nothing to merge. Declared: two simultaneous proposals of the same PR are not serialized (there is no per-PR lock), and it is rule 2 that holds the second one.

RN-671 — The Infra starts the container on handoff acceptance: the server proposes, and the seeded autonomy approves​

Owner decision on 10/01 (ADR 0190), revising the "never seeded" of RN-491. In the real use of 09/29 the Infra announced the start "in parallel" and did not propose it; the container only started through /containers (AT-260).

  1. The seed. Accepting the handoff addressed to infra records, besides open_infra_pr: auto_approve and terminal: deny, the autonomy container_start: auto_approve. Only that one among the container ones: container_start_via_runner and container_stop remain never seeded, and container_remove remains in the absolute ceiling (RN-495).
  2. The trigger is the SERVER's. In the Infra Lead's kickoff, BEFORE the first trip to the model, if there is a current routing (artifact.module_routing roteado, with a candidate) and a container/mounted project, the server proposes container_start through the SAME path as the propose_container_start tool: the local refusals by mode and state (RN-566, RN-610), then propose_action, where the api refuses without a broker (RN-591), resolves the autonomy and, auto-approved, executes the start, electing the image through DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase with decidedBy: 'infra-lead' (RN-491). runner has no server step: it goes through container_start_via_runner, proposed by the model and decided by a human.
  3. The election is deterministic. The candidate with the most modules; on a tie, the routing's first. Network none, default resources, and a rationale that says it was the server. (Revised by RN-683: the resources are omitted and the api starts with the minimum derived from the module_map, not with the default.)
  4. The trail says who called. Durable tool.call (with origem: "servidor") and tool.result, and no tool message in the model's history; the kickoff says in text what HAS ALREADY happened (returned status, or the refusal reason).
  5. The closing of RN-668 stays true. The server's start marks the turn as the tool's would: proposed, the closing says nothing; refused, it says it was refused. A proposal DENIED by the policy (status denied, like a session opened by someone who is not maintainer) counts as a refusal, in both origins.

No ceiling moves: the minimum role stays maintainer (the effective one of whoever opened the session), a deny in permissions.json still wins, and /containers does not change (it proposes as a human, and agent autonomy does not apply to it). Declared: the card's manual/auto toggle writes the wildcard, and the specific rule wins — putting the Infra in "manual" does not switch off this seed.

RN-672 — The handoff to the Dev Lead comes from the Infra, and only with the project container running​

In the real use of 09/29 both were born from the same confirmation (session be70, seq 252/254).

OfferInfraHandoffUseCase has one target (infra); the engine port's offerDevHandoff, the route POST /internal/sessions/:id/agent/offer-dev-handoff and the Arquiteto's :offer_dev_handoff/handoff_dev_pendente ceased to exist. ja_oferecido now means "the Infra already had an offer or was active".
  2. The one who offers the Dev Lead is the Infra Lead's server, through create_handoff_if_absent/5 (infra → dev-lead, ADR 0182): a pending offer in any session of the project comes back as is, and an already active Dev Lead (409 agente_ja_ativo) is not a failure. It is not a tool: the model does not decide when the Dev Lead comes in.
  3. Only with the container REGISTERED running (the local read of ProjectContainerLifecycle). The question is asked at two moments: at the end of every Infra turn (concluir) — the common case, because the server's start on acceptance (RN-671) runs inside the kickoff — and when the outbox's container.running arrives outside a turn (later approval, /containers, container_start_via_runner): Engine.Outbox.Drain now also enqueues Engine.Workers.InfraOfereceDevLeadWorker, which notifies the project's Infra Lead through PubSub.
  4. A failure that is not "already handled" is a durable agent.error with origin (RN-116), without bringing the turn down; the end of the Infra's next turn tries again.

What stays as it was: the second repository door on acceptance to the Dev Lead (RN-582) — the acceptance is the same, only who offers changed — and the execution activation chained to the acceptance (RN-161). Declared: the outbox notice is at-most-once, like Engine.Dev.Wake; without an Infra Lead up at that instant, the offer waits for the end of its next turn.

The test plan is born after the dev's delivery (RN-674, ADR 0192)​

RN-683 — The Infra starts the container with the SMALLEST eligible resource, derived from what the Arquiteto declares per module in the module_map​

Owner decision on 10/01 (ADR 0199, AT-261). Until now omitted resources became RECURSOS_PADRAO (2 cpus, 4096 MiB, 512 pids) and the server's start on acceptance (RN-671) always omitted it: every container was born at the default, with no notion of minimum.

  1. Each module declares its own. The module_map gains resources (cpus, memoryMb, pidsLimit) per module — what THAT module needs alone in the container. The create_module_map tool asks for it; the api accepts it absent and refuses with 400, on map creation: a HALF declaration (all three or none), a non-positive value or one above the ceiling, and a SUM across modules above the ceiling. The field lives in the artifact's JSON, without a migration.
  2. The minimum is the SUM, field by field. A project has ONE container (project_id UNIQUE in project_containers) and the modules run in it at the same time; the maximum across modules would undersize the container whenever two were up.
  3. A module without a declaration: floor at today's default. No number is invented. If there is a module without a declaration, the minimum is the larger of the sum of the declared ones and RECURSOS_PADRAO, field by field, and the rationale NAMES who did not declare. With no declaration at all (every map prior to this rule), and without a current module_map, the minimum is exactly today's default.
  4. The container_start execution resolves field by field. Omitted becomes the minimum (the server's start sends everything omitted); below the minimum is a named failed, without recording an image decision or starting; above is valid up to the ceiling, which does not change. The rationale of the recorded artifact.project_image gains "Recursos mínimos (RN-683): …" with the summed modules and the map version.
  5. A single yardstick. The api derives; the engine sums nothing and the server's start says in the rationale that the resources are the derived minimum.

Out, declared: choose_project_image (the Arquiteto decides the image and its resources) and container_start_via_runner (starts the already decided image) do not change; the refusal below the minimum happens on execution, not on proposing.

RN-674 — The QA-strategy writes the plan over the DELIVERED code, at the start of the qa-verificada cycle, and implementavel is judged without it​

In the real use of 09/29 the PRE-DEV test plan (RN-341) ended twice in toolloop.limit_reached 8/8 without emit_plano_de_teste: the loop read docs, empty RAG and folders until concluding that "the code does not exist yet". The owner decided (10/01) for option (b): the plan is born AFTER delivery. ADR 0192 revises 0090 on that point, and the rule has four parts:

  1. The plan is the first step of the review cycle. The QaLeadServer's run_area/3 obtains the delivery's plan BEFORE the subspecialties (plano_de_teste_da_entrega/5): it finds again in the session tail (rehydration ceiling, RN-580) the artifact.plano_de_teste of the SAME taskId — the correction round does not pay for another loop —, and otherwise runs QaEstrategiaAgent.run/6 with the dev's worktree as workspace_root, the task's business rules and the list of files the delivery touched (git diff dev...HEAD, up to 40 names). A diff that fails becomes text ("não consegui listar: motivo"), never an empty list.
  2. The plan is INPUT, never a verdict. It reaches the Automação at the END of its message, for the step of finding which test covers each rule; the verdict yardstick does not change (one coverageMatrix row per story rule, approved only with a green suite and every rule covered) and the external contract remains ONE qa_verdict per cycle. A plan that FAILS does not hold the review: the QA-strategy records agent.error with origin (RN-059) and the Automação receives the usual message, byte for byte.
  3. implementavel is judged over the story and the module_map. run_assessment/2 neither reads nor triggers a plan: it proposes the verdict on the FIRST call, over what the Dev Lead's kickoff already gives it, with payload storyId/parecer/justificativa. Gate, owner, severity warn and human approval do not change; only the entrada ([story-ready, module_map]). The appsec (RN-539) keeps triggering there, in design.
  4. The ceiling stays 8. "qa-estrategia" gets no clause in Iteracoes.tipo/1; what changed was the input. The agent now runs under the task_budget_micros that the subspecialties share (RN-036).

run_design/3, Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 and QaEstrategiaContext were removed, and artifact.plano_de_teste now requires taskId. Declared and not decided here: whether the plan's executable criteria should become MANDATORY rows of the coverageMatrix (and therefore fail a delivery).

Credentialed git runs on the runner's host (RN-676)​

RN-676 — With an active container, RunnerGit's credentialed git fetch runs on the runner's HOST, marked by the engine; the code stays in the container​

Owner decision (10/01), recorded in ADR 0193: a CREDENTIALED git operation runs on the runner's HOST, and the code runs in the container. It closes the half that RN-558 left open — the authenticated fetch in runner mode with the container up, which is the common path, always ended in the named refusal.

  1. The engine marks, and only at one point. RunnerGit.fetch!/3 dispatches the credentialed fetch through RunnerRouter.exec_git_credenciado/5, which puts gitCredenciado: true in the exec payload and requires a non-empty env by guard. The dev agent's terminal command goes through RunnerRouter.exec/4 and never carries the mark. Without credentials (provider local), the fetch goes without the mark.
  2. The runner runs on the host only with the CONJUNCTION: the literal mark true and a non-empty env. Then the command goes to executarComando (the env merged over process.env), even with an active container. The folder is the same: estado.dir is the bind-mount of /work.
  3. env without the mark does not get the host. With an active container, that pair stays REFUSED with the RN-558 mark and origin politica. Today no engine caller produces it; in practice it comes from a brabo-runner older than ADR 0193, which does not read the mark — and the engine's message says to update it. The mark without env changes nothing either: the command goes to the container.
  4. No containment changes: DockerPort.exec remains without env (ADR 0130), and RunnerReadiness (RN-507) stays byte for byte — the mark decides WHERE the runner executes, never WHETHER the engine dispatches.
  5. The log never carries the name or value of an env variable: the refusal gives the count, and the host path's log adds only [git credenciado, no host].

RN-673 — A message that arrives with a turn in progress enters a queue persisted in the log and is read at the end of the turn, N messages in a single turn​

Until now a message that reached a conversational agent in the middle of a turn was 409 turno_em_andamento (RN-578): recorded as chat.message (the api records before talking to the engine) and never read. The real use of 09/29 measured three in a single session — PO, Infra Lead and Dev Lead. Owner decision (10/01), for the SEVEN conversational agents through the same path:

  1. Queue, not refusal. With a turn in progress, the message enters the agent's queue (TurnoAssincrono.receber_mensagem/4), the agent records chat.message_queued (mensagemId, texto, idioma, posicao) and the click gets 202 with {entrega: "enfileirada", posicao}. Without a turn, the turn starts right away, as always (entrega: "lida"). The api route also returns the mensagemId — the id of the chat.message.
  2. N messages = 1 turn. At the END of the turn (finalizar/1, never suspender/1) the pending ones become ONE turn, in order of arrival, in a single text (FilaDeMensagens.texto_do_turno/1: one is itself; several, numbered), and the agent records chat.message_delivered with the ids. Delivery is a message to itself, after the server's closing (the Infra Lead's gate correction and the Arquiteto's handoff come first). A message that arrives between the end of the turn and the delivery goes to the END of the queue, and the queue is delivered right away.
  3. Ceiling of 10 pending per agent and session. The 11th is 409 fila_de_mensagens_cheia, with a durable agent.error of origin politica — it is recorded and will not be read.
  4. Cancel. POST …/agents/:agent/messages/:messageId/cancel (developer, the message route's minimum): only the SENDER (403 mensagem_de_outra_pessoa), only in a session that accepts conversation (RN-581). Whether it is still in the queue is decided by the agent's process, which serializes the race with the delivery: 409 mensagem_fora_da_fila when it was already read or cancelled. The engine records chat.message_cancelled on behalf of whoever cancelled; with the agent down, it records directly (the queue is the log).
  5. Persisted in the log, never in a table. Pending = queued and neither delivered nor cancelled — the same derivation in the engine and on the screen. The init/1 of the seven rebuilds the queue and schedules delivery; RN-580 removes from the history the cancelled one and the agent's own pending one; at boot, after closing the orphan turn (RN-586), the agent with a pending queue is woken up. The interrupted turn is still never redone.
  6. A turn suspended on approval (Dev Lead, RN-284) keeps refusing with aguardando_aprovacao — with no foreseeable end, queuing would promise a reading with no date. A queue that already existed waits for the resumption to finish.
  7. The screen. With a turn in progress the composer no longer locks for a message to an agent: the button becomes "Pôr na fila" and the message does not arm a new turn. In the thread, "na fila de " with Cancelar for the author, and "cancelada" struck through. The chat without an agent still locks.

The turno_em_andamento refusal remains for what is not speech: the PO's story review, the Criativo's readiness, the Arquiteto's handoff offer.

RN-677 — Accepting the Dev Lead only brings him in to plan; APPROVING his plan is what activates execution​

Revises RN-161 (owner decision, 10/01): accepting the handoff to the Dev Lead no longer chains POST .../execution/activate, for EVERY role. The explicit "Ativar execução" shortcut of the card (RN-137) and the Visão Geral one remain — they are a click of their own, not the acceptance.

The real use of 09/29 measured the inversion: execution was activated on handoff acceptance at 06:45:01 — the web chained the activation for maintainer/owner (session-acoes-de-handoff.ts, RN-161) —, and the Dev Lead's plan, proposed at 06:47:47, stayed pending and was never used. The plan had no consumer: propose_execution_plan had no execution pipeline and, approved, stayed approved forever. Measured on dev before changing: the acceptance backend (AcceptHandoffUseCase) NEVER emitted execution.activated; the only emitter is ActivateExecutionUseCase, called only by the execution/activate route.

The rule:

  1. Accepting the Dev Lead only activates him to plan. handleAcceptHandoff accepts and nothing more; AcceptHandoffUseCase does not change — it keeps provisioning the repository as the idempotent second door (RN-582).
  2. Approving propose_execution_plan ACTIVATES execution. The action gained an executor in the api, ExecuteExecutionPlanUseCase, called by manual approval (ApproveActionUseCase) and by auto-approval (ProposeActionUseCase — the type is not in the absolute ceilings of decide.ts, so it CAN be configured auto-approvable). It records the tasks' module (RN-678) and calls the SAME ActivateExecutionUseCase as the button — no second yardstick: the 409 without a repository (RN-582), the 409 for execution.activated in a consultative session (RN-097) and the idempotent reactivation through findActiveExecutionSession stay there, untouched.
  3. Whoever activates is whoever APPROVED (decidedBy); on auto-approval, whoever opened the session — against whom decide() resolved the role. Both require maintainer, the same minimum as execution/activate, so resolving the effective role of the dev agents' git_* (the execution session's createdBy) does not change owner.
  4. The Dev Lead's session does NOT close (it is not passed as originSessionId, RN-135): it is there that he resumes the suspended turn and narrates the outcome.
  5. The outcome is named and durable. The action ends executed with { sessaoDeExecucao, modulos, tarefasAtribuidas } or failed with the motivo (the api's sentence, e.g. the 409 without a repository), plus the execution.plan_applied/execution.plan_failed event in the timeline. The Dev Lead reads the real outcome on resuming ("execução ATIVADA na sessão …" or "a ativação falhou: …"), never "plano registrado". Failing does not undo the approval: the human's decision is already recorded.

RN-678 — The task belongs to a module, assigned by the Dev Lead in the plan, and only that module's dev picks it up​

In the real use of 09/29 dev-input-keyboard picked up "Implementar loop de queda automática da peça" and dev-board-engine picked up "Mapear teclas…": the task had no module, the story had several, and claimNext let any dev of any module of the story pick up any of its tasks (s.module_ids ? $1).

The rule:

  1. The task has a module — tasks.module, nullable text (migration 0068_modulo_da_tarefa). The one who assigns it is the Dev Lead, in the execution plan: propose_execution_plan gained tarefas: [{ taskId, modulo }], and his kickoff lists the pending tasks of the PROJECT backlog with the task_id and the story's modules.
  2. The valid set is the current module_map. The api reads the plan (lerPlanoDeExecucao, a pure function) on PROPOSAL and refuses with 400 plano_de_execucao_invalido, without creating the action, when: the plan has no tarefas; a task has no taskId or is without a module; the module (of the task or of the plan) is outside the module_map; the task appears twice; or it does not exist in this project. The sentence names the task, the module and the valid modules, and goes back to the Dev Lead as a tool error (loop input, RN-163), for him to fix.
  3. Approval rereads the plan against the module_map of that moment (it may have changed): a refusal becomes failed without recording anything and without activating. Passing, the modules are recorded BEFORE the activation, so that no freshly started dev agent looks for an ownerless task.
  4. Only that module's dev picks it up. claimNext and countClaimableByModule use the SAME predicate (daTarefaDoModulo): a task with a module belongs to whoever has that module, and nobody else — the story's module_ids no longer decide. A task without a module is only claimable when the story has ONE module only, and it is the dev's: it is the only case in which "that module's dev" is not ambiguous, and it is the path of whoever activated through the Visão Geral without a plan. A task without a module of a story with several waits for the next plan.

Left out, declared: a task created AFTER the plan is born without a module (the PO does not assign); the task.became_claimable notice is still routed by the STORY's modules (waking one extra dev picks up nothing, it only costs a query); and the plan's per-module agentes stays informative — activation starts one dev per module of the module_map, as before, and extra parallelism still goes through parallelize (RN-083).

The Anamnese switched back on: eligible subject and profile fact (RN-680)​

RN-680 — The Anamnese does not run without an eligible subject, and the hypothesis the person themselves accepted becomes a fact of their profile in the graph and enters the context of the agents that talk with them​

Owner decision on 10/01 (AT-277): switch the Anamnese back on with fixes. In the real use of 09/29 it ran six times and all six ended in anamnese.run_skipped ("no eligible member"), written by the MODEL after a paid call (8,933 micros), and the three accepted hypotheses stayed in the queue with no destination. See ADR 0196.

  1. Without an eligible subject, the round does not run. A subject is an EFFECTIVE member of the project (projectRole ?? workspaceRole, the yardstick of RN-471), outside the opt-out, with OWN interaction in what the round shows the model — an event of theirs with actor_kind: "user" in the window, or a decision of theirs. The guard comes BEFORE triage and not even the queued hypothesis gets past it. Without a subject: no LLM call and no RAG search; the reason goes NAMED to the engine log (sem_sujeito_elegivel, with nenhum_membro or nenhuma_interacao_propria and the numbers) and, in a manually requested round, also to the event log (anamnese.run_skipped with causa: "sem_sujeito_elegivel"). Through the tick it is only a log — it would be a notice every 15 minutes per project. The prompt now lists only the subjects.
  2. A project member is the EFFECTIVE one. Creating a project does not write project_members, and the Anamnese read only that table — the workspace owner was never a member. The Anamnese's three use cases now read listEffectiveMembers; listMembers remains only project_members.
  3. A hypothesis ACCEPTED by the person THEMSELVES becomes a profile fact. The psychologist.hypothesis_accepted carries projectId, sujeito (the author of the analyzed session), hipotese, sugestao and fatoDoPerfil, and the GraphEventTranslator — the same one as the projector and grafo:reprojetar — translates it into (:FatoDoPerfil {hypothesisId}), linked to the person (SOBRE) and to the project (NO_PROJETO). fatoDoPerfil is only true when the one who accepted is the subject: a fact about a person is never born from someone else's click, and the payload says why (motivoSemFato). A declined one is only recorded, as before. Acceptances recorded before this RN lack the fields and do not become facts.
  4. The fact enters the context of the agents that talk with the person. The author's message to a conversational agent carries THEIR facts in this project — read by QueryUserContextUseCase, scoped to the project, the 5 most recent, with the total beside them and the cut stated —, and the engine puts them in the turn as an EPHEMERAL system message, through the same path as the language (RN-622): never in the history, before the language guidance, with a ceiling of 2,000 characters. Graph down becomes a log, and the turn goes on without the facts. A turn without an author receives no facts.
  5. Switched back on. ANAMNESE_ENABLED returns to default true in runtime.exs and in the three composes; START_ANAMNESE does not change (the production one stays false, an already declared divergence). The Psicólogo stays paused.

RN-682 — The consultative session without an agent asks for an agent: the composer does not send without a recipient, and the chat route refuses by name​

Until now, a message in a consultative session without an agent went to the SSE of POST .../chat (SendChatMessageUseCase), which sends to the bound model only the current text — no history, no system prompt, no tool — and records the answer with the MODEL NAME as actor. Measured in the real use of 09/29: session 5d66 answered "I have no access to previous conversations". The owner's decision (10/01) is that, without an active agent, the consultative session asks to choose an agent — the same yardstick as RN-584 (no default recipient) reaching the last case that still had one: the raw model.

The measurement, before the fix: the chat route had ONE client, the screen (handleSend, only when there was no recipient — which, since RN-631, only happened in the consultative session without an agent: the creative one always has the Criativo as an option). The curl the seed prints is a development hint, in a creative session. The use case has a SECOND legitimate consumer: the provider smokes (*-provider.smoke.spec.ts) use it directly as an end-to-end instrument (credential → call → metering) in a session without an agent. That is why the api's refusal lives in the ROUTE, and the use case does not change.

The rule:

  1. The screen does not send without a recipient. "Enviar" and Enter are locked with zero options, as they already were with two and no choice; the SSE branch left handleSend.
  2. The recipient line SHOWS who can be called. Without an option, the manual handoff selector (RN-440) moves into it — "Para", the list, and "Chamar" —, and the selector above disappears so there is not the same choice in two places. The list is the agents that converse (AGENTES_DE_CHAT, those the engine matches with their own clause) and that the manual handoff reaches, minus whoever already joined and minus the Criativo: the consultative session promises in its invitation that he does not join, because opening the ideation is what the creative one does (RN-097). Chamar offers the handoff; accepting it in the thread makes the agent the recipient (RN-631).
  3. The api refuses the same case for any client. POST .../chat in a consultative session in which no agent.activated was recorded is 422 {reason: "destinatario_ausente"}, with the sentence that points to .../agents/:agent/message, BEFORE any effect: nothing is recorded and no model is called. The refusal goes out as an HTTP response and not as an error frame inside a 200 stream — the handler returns Promise<Observable>, and the rejection before the SSE header becomes the normal response.

What this rule does NOT close, declared:

  • The route still answers through the raw model outside that case: in a creative session without an agent (the seed's curl) and in a consultative one WITH an agent, for whoever calls it by hand. The screen calls it in neither; the owner's decision was about the consultative session without an agent, and closing the whole route is a separate decision.

RN-684 — The contract between modules is a versioned artifact of the Arquiteto, and the dev agent reads it through the tool, never in another dev's worktree​

Owner decision (10/01), recorded in ADR 0200. In the real use of 09/29, dev-board-engine spent 5 of its 24 tool steps reading other modules' worktrees to discover their interface: the module_map says who depends on whom, never what a module exposes. It applies RN-164 to the dev agents.

  1. The artifact is artifact.module_contracts, without a table, like module_routing and c4_diagram: the current one is the highest version, with ties broken by seq. Each declaration carries the WHOLE list and REPLACES the previous one; changing a contract is a new version by the Arquiteto.
  2. Per module, only what it EXPOSES: {modulo, expoe: [{tipo, assinatura, descricao}]}, tipo in funcao | rota | evento | dado, assinatura mandatory (up to 300 characters), from 1 to 40 items. What it CONSUMES is the dependsOn of the current module_map, derived on read — never retyped.
  3. The api refuses with 400 and the whole reason (which goes back to the model, RN-061): empty list, repeated module, module outside the current module_map (listing the valid ones) or no module_map, empty expoe or above 40, unknown tipo, empty assinatura or above 300. Nothing is recorded.
  4. An artifact SEPARATE from the module_map, never a field of it: revising one does not reissue the other.
  5. The dev reads through listar_contratos_de_modulos, :direct, in the Engine.Dev.Tools registry: project scope by the route, NO parameter, the dev's module coming from ctx.module. It shows in full its own and those it consumes; those that consume it and the rest, by name only; a ceiling of 120 items with the cut stated. A contract of a module that left the map is STATED, never attributed.
  6. The dev's kickoff says where to read another module's interface, and that it is not in another dev agent's worktree. Without a contract for a shown module, the tool says to implement from what the story and the task say and, if an interface is missing, report_blocked naming the module — never rereading the worktree.

RN-685 — Revoking a credential brings down only the connections opened WITH IT: the socket ticket keeps the credential, and the target stops being {project, user}​

Revises RN-520. Until now, revoking a device key brought down the runner's live connection by the {project, user} pair, because the credential's identity died in PatAuthGuard: a runner of the SAME user connected with a PAT or with another key went down too, and the MACHINE key (RN-543) multiplied that per project. Revoking a PAT brought down nothing.

The ticket keeps WHICH credential requested it. runner_socket_tickets (an engine table) gains credential_kind (device_key | pat) and credential_id (the kid, which is the record's id — RN-475 —, or the PAT's id), both NULLABLE: the terminal ticket belongs to the web tab and has no device credential, and a runner one issued by an older api arrives without it. The PatAuthGuard annotates the credential AFTER authorizing (request.credencialDeDispositivo), the runner ticket carries it to the engine and the terminal one never does; an incomplete pair or an unknown kind becomes ABSENT, never an invented credential.

The socket keeps the credential, and its id too. connect/3 sets assigns.credencial, and the id becomes runner_socket:<kind>:<projectId>:<userId>:<espécie>:<id> when it exists — the disconnect the channel broadcasts to its own id reaches only that credential.

Revoking ONE credential:

  1. voids its PENDING tickets — a request made seconds before the revocation does not get in after it (consumed_at, the same "already used" state, no new state);
  2. asks EVERY runner in the cluster whether it was born from this credential — only the channel knows —, and only those born from it go down. The machine key is ONE request, and goes down in every project where it opened a connection, including one the api would not list;
  3. responds with a TALLY (derrubados, legados, intocados, semResposta, ticketsAnulados) — zero brought down is the normal case for an orphan key (RN-519).

It applies to the three revocations: the key one (per project and through the Account, RN-611) and the two PAT ones (the owner's, RN-426, and the maintainer's, RN-427). It revokes FIRST, brings down afterwards, and bringing down is still a side effect that only LOGS — the DELETE stays 204 and idempotent.

What already went down still goes down (the prohibition of AT-013). The LEGACY connection — a ticket without a credential — of the same owner, in one of the projects that a KEY revocation sends as scope (the row's, or the machine's candidates), goes down by the pair as before; the PAT gains no legacy scope, because it brought down nothing. And if the engine does not know the per-credential route (404 from an older engine), the key revocation falls back to the pair, disconnectRunnerOfUser, project by project.

The {project, user} pair remains, with another owner: it is the target of member removal (RN-615), which removes the PERSON, with whatever credential.

The screen states the precision (RN-561): the revoke confirmation — device keys in Configurações and machine keys in the Account — replaces "outro runner seu também cai" with "só cai o que se conectou com ESTA chave". The label changes, not the behavior.

RN-688 — The runner binary reads the PTY with its own reader under Bun, and the self-test proves the SECOND read​

Under Bun (the bun build --compile binary, ADR 0112), the tty.ReadStream with which node-pty reads the PTY's master side is an fs.ReadStream, and the first read with no data from the non-blocking fd RAISES as EAGAIN: the stream destroys itself, closes the fd, and no onData arrives after that (oven-sh/bun#25822). The binary's interactive terminal stopped after the first chunk of output on all THREE Unix platforms; Linux passed the proof only because the first read already brought the echo and the answer together.

The rule: under Bun and outside Windows, node-pty's spawn runs with the tty.ReadStream swapped for its own reader that reads the SAME fd with fs.read and, on EAGAIN, WAITS and retries (from 4 ms, doubling up to 32 ms, back to the minimum on every piece of data); EIO or zero bytes is the end. The swap applies only DURING the spawn and is restored even when it throws; under Node the module comes back INTACT. The fd and the child process remain the real ones — nothing simulates output. And --self-test-pty makes TWO rounds, the second after a pause with nothing to read: it is the pause that forces the read through an EAGAIN, and it is through it that the old reader fails on Linux too. When it fails, the self-test says why (chunks, the child's output, a probe on a second PTY and the stream's events) — the verdict does not change.

It was the probe that measured Windows: there the read side is ConPTY's named pipe, opened by node-pty as a net.Socket, without an fd the reader could take over, and the pipe ends after the first chunk — which is why win32-x64 left the matrix (ADR 0187) instead of getting a workaround.

The runner flow through the browser is retired (RN-687, ADR 0203)​

RN-687 — The runner panel sends to the installer; the browser does not generate a key, does not download a binary and does not write a folder​

The flow of ADR 0118 (RN-464..466) was RETIRED by owner decision (10/01, BRB-031): it was the only installation path that ended in a manual chmod +x, and install.sh already does its three things on the right side — it downloads the binary checked against the signed checksums.txt and installs it with install -m 0755 (RN-531), and creates the key ON THE MACHINE and registers it (RN-547, RN-551, RN-552).

The rule:

  1. The RunnerOnboardingPanel shows the installer command (curl -fsSLO …/install.sh && bash install.sh, the SAME sentence as the runbook and install.sh, RN-526), copyable, with what it does stated in text, the caveat that it serves the installation's machine, and the EsperaDoRunner (RN-474) below. The command in the web is a COPY, and the copy is checked against the installer's constant.
  2. Once an active key that serves the project is recognized — machine (RN-548) or project (AT-107) —, the installer block LEAVES and the gesture is checking the service. The manual command with a PAT (--token) always stays in the <details>, named as the path for ANOTHER machine.
  3. There is no button to configure a folder, to download files, nor a platform selector, and the web no longer calls Web Crypto, File System Access nor the binary proxy. runner-bootstrap.ts was removed entirely.
  4. The api no longer has POST /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys. It was left without a caller. GET and DELETE stay (list and revoke); the internal machine route (POST /internal/machine-device-keys) stays.
  5. An ALREADY registered project key remains valid and revocable: nothing in the database changes, PatAuthGuard keeps accepting it (RN-465) and the CLI keeps reading the configured folder (RN-466). A runner configured through the browser before ADR 0203 does not break.

Left out, declared: an installation with a TEAM loses the PAT-less path to pair a second machine (the machine key route is 409 with two or more people), and now uses the manual command; GET /runner-releases/binary is left without a production consumer and was NOT removed — that is a separate decision.

The RN-418 ceiling also applies through the typed door (RN-689)​

RN-689 — Typed git_push and pr_open are never auto-approvable: the RN-418 ceiling applies to the command AND to the action​

Revised by RN-713 (AT-385, 10/02): auto mode (the wildcard in auto_approve) now unlocks git_push and pr_open.

Revises RN-418, by owner decision (10/01). Until now decide()'s external-effect ceiling only looked at actionType === 'terminal': a TYPED git push became require_approval, and the message said to use the typed action git_push — which, with the minimum role (maintainer) met, was born auto_approved through ANY of the three stages: the "*" wildcard of auto mode (RN-153, the autopilot of RN-670), a specific agent_autonomy rule (execution activation seeded git_push/pr_open as auto_approve for each dev-<modulo>) or an allow in permissions.json. Measured in decide.spec.ts before the fix: the six cases (two types × three stages) came out auto_approve.

The rule: git_push and pr_open enter the block of absolute ceilings — if the verdict up to that point is auto_approve, it becomes unconditional require_approval, with the named reason ("teto de efeito externo (RN-418): … nunca é auto-aprovável"), which goes in proposed_action.created. deny has already returned before and still wins; the ORIGIN of the autonomy does not matter. The "sempre permitir" of both was already refused at the source (RN-642, TIPOS_SEM_SEMPRE_PERMITIR), and that is the half that keeps the ceiling from being decorative.

The seeding follows along: DEV_AUTO_GIT_ACTIONS becomes only git_commit — on activation and on parallelization acceptance. Seeding push and PR would be recording an autonomy that decide() never honors, the screen promising what does not happen (the argument of RN-642). Already recorded rows stay in the database, inert. The dev agent follows the path of RN-050: commit executed, push and PR pending, agent in awaiting_approval holding the worktree until task.pr_settled; only then does the gate open.

Left OUT, on purpose: git_merge (its own protected-branch ceiling); git_commit (stays on the machine, RN-670); open_adr_pr and open_infra_pr (they open a real PR on the provider, but the owner's decision does not cover them — open_infra_pr is seeded auto_approve on the Infra's acceptance, RN-671); the bootstrap actions (git_repo_create/git_branch_create/git_branch_protect, which do not go through decide()); and deploy, which is not a proposed_action type — it only exists as a target of the terminal command's message.

RN-690 — The assistant keeps the response's toolCalls: the tool result does not reach the provider orphaned​

The conversational agents with their own loop (Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer, Staff and Infra Lead) kept in the history the assistant's message WITHOUT the response's toolCalls and, right after, the role: "tool" message with the toolCallId. On the wire, the provider received a result that answered no call and discarded it: the model never saw what the tool returned and repeated the same call up to the loop ceiling (measured in v7.0.0: the PO called listar_regras_de_negocio 12 of 12 times in two turns).

The assistant's message now carries the response's NATIVE toolCalls when there are any — the same format the ToolLoop already kept and that the ContextManager groups on compaction —, assembled in a single place. RN-698 — The turn's text becomes ONE answer, and the iteration ceiling appears in the thread​

With tools, the model writes in pieces — a stretch before the call, another on the next round, often continuing the same sentence. Each round became its own agent.response, and the thread collapses the earlier ones into "Passos do turno": on show stayed only the last piece (" histórias e tarefas que cubram tudo.", starting with a space). The transport lost nothing — the api's final frame carries the whole text of the ROUND —; what was split was the TURN. In the seven conversational agents, the text of a round with a tool is accumulated in the turn's process and recorded in a single agent.response only when the turn closes (no tool, ceiling, failure, Dev Lead suspension, Infra PR). A piece that starts or ends with a space goes in as it came; two pieces stuck together become paragraphs.

The conversational agents' toolloop.limit_reached (RN-166) now becomes a line in the thread, in the failure bubble, origin modelo, stating the ceiling ("parou no teto de N passos sem terminar o turno"); without the number in the payload the line says ?.

The turn's agent.response carries modelName (RN-146) in EVERY outcome, not only in the tool-less closing: when the turn closes without a final call that brings it (it delivered an ask_structured_questions form, exhausted the ceiling, failed), the model of the last accumulated round applies. With no LLM call having returned a model, the field stays nil — never an invented model (AT-384; the Infra Lead records modelName in no outcome and stays out).

Revision (owner decision, 10/03, AT-395): only the turn's closing in the bubble. In real use (loja-teste-2, 10/02) the single answer joined the text of ALL the rounds ("Vou registrar… Excelente! Registrei…", two summaries in a row in the PO). The turn's agent.response is still ONE, but content now is only the CLOSING — the text of the last round that wrote something (a turn that ends in a form, with no text in the last round, keeps the previous one) — and the text of the earlier rounds goes, in order, in the passos field, absent when there are none. Nothing vanishes: the thread draws each step as narration of the same turn+author before the closing, and the "Passos do turno" collapse that already existed folds them, closed by default; the steps do not count in the thread's message cut (RN-644). The rehydration (RN-580) returns passos BEFORE content, in the same assistant, so the model does not lose what it said mid-turn. It applies to the seven conversational agents (the Infra Lead too, without modelName). No ceiling of its own for passos: the accumulation was already recorded whole before the revision.

The installer offers the local models, and does not mistake dev for an installation (RN-691, RN-692)​

RN-691 — install.sh ASKS whether to switch on the local models (profile llm), measures the Ollama port before writing, and composes ONE COMPOSE_PROFILES line​

Measured in a real installation of v7.0.0 (AT-351): every business rule recorded backlog.semantic_duplicate_check_skipped with getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN ollama, because the installation from a Release starts without the llm profile and the installer never asked; switching it on by hand hit address already in use on 11434, the port of a NATIVE Ollama on the host.

The rule: after the broker question (RN-575), the installer states the COST (disk for the image and for the models the ollama-model-loader downloads, RAM with a model loaded) and what is LOST without it (the semantic duplicate check of RN-681 and a local model for the agents), and only a typed "s" switches it on; without a terminal it stays off SAYING so. Switching on MEASURES the host port before writing anything — 11434, or the first free one up to 11443, through bash's own /dev/tcp (3.2 included) — and the whole range being taken is a NAMED refusal, with nothing written, never an address already in use on startup. The .env gets OLLAMA_PORT and the llm profile; the consented profiles go out in a SINGLE COMPOSE_PROFILES line (container-broker,llm), because two lines do not add up — the last one would win and the broker would silently vanish.

Left OUT, declared: the session stating ONCE that the semantic check was skipped (api side, another front); and the tag's E2E answers NO (switching on would download GBs of models), so startup with the llm profile is not proven end to end.

RN-715 — A merge conflict returns the task to the owning dev agent, and the gates judge again​

  • Rule: when the approved merge of a PR is refused due to a conflict with dev (GitMergeConflictError, RN-704), each task of the PR that is in_review goes back to in_progress with gate_status reset (the old QA/SecOps verdicts do not apply to the branch that is going to change), records backlog.task_status_changed with cause: merge_conflict and puts task.merge_conflict in the outbox, with the agent that proposed the pr_open (the OWNER), the PR and the conflicting files. The engine delivers it to the owner through Engine.Dev.Wake; if free, he READOPTS the PR's branch (WorktreeManager.adopt/3, the same garantir_base, without losing the commits) and runs the CORRECTION loop with the reason in the text: bring in origin/dev through git fetch/git merge, resolve the files, run the suite. On report_done he proposes commit and push through the usual path (the current approval policy decides) and the gate RESTARTS from QA (open_gate + QA), without a new pr_open — the PR is the same branch. No new task state: in_progress with the cause in the event.
  • Named outcomes: owner without a row in dev_agent_states — the task is BLOCKED (conflito de merge sem dev agent para resolvê-lo, origin infra); owner with the breaker open (idle_tripped) — blocked, origin politica; the branch does not come back (adopt fails) — blocked, origin infra. A busy owner (working/awaiting_gate/awaiting_approval) gets the conflict again in 30 s. The merge refusal (RN-705) does not depend on any of this: the action is already failed, with the reason, before the engine acts. A task that is no longer in_review (repeated merge) is not reopened nor wakes anyone, and a PR opened by a human has no owner to wake.
  • Measurement (AT-383, 10/02, loja-teste): #6 ended failed due to a conflict in package.json, and the task stayed in_review with nobody to resolve it.

RN-704 — The local repository's merge is a real merge, and a conflict is a named refusal​

  • Rule: the local provider's mergePullRequest fast-forwards only when the target is an ancestor of the source; with the two diverged, it builds a merge commit with both parents (git merge-tree --write-tree + commit-tree, without a worktree, message Merge pull request #N from <branch>, identity Brabo Bot). The target ref is moved by update-ref with the expected old value, so a concurrent merge fails instead of overwriting. A conflict throws GitMergeConflictError with the conflicting files: the ref stays intact, the PR stays open, the git_merge action ends failed with the reason in action.failed, and over HTTP the error is 409 merge_conflict.

RN-707 — The SecOps gate's semgrep has a writable $HOME, and the output-less failure is named​

  • Rule: in the production and installation composes, the engine's tmpfs /home/engine is born owned by the image's user (/home/engine:uid=1000,gid=1000,mode=0700). SemgrepDetector.Live distinguishes exit 1 with JSON (findings) from exit 0/1 with empty stdout, which becomes {:error, {:sem_saida, exit_code}} instead of :invalid_output. The gate's verdict does NOT change: a scanner that did not run is still "skipped" in the verdict's summary.
  • Measurement (AT-380): inside brabo-engine-1 (production image, read_only: true), the tmpfs /home/engine was born root 2755; the gate's semgrep scan exited 1 with empty stdout and PermissionError: '/home/engine/.semgrep' on stderr, and the parser called that :invalid_output. With the tmpfs uid=1000 the same command returns the JSON (exit 0). Kubernetes did not have the defect (fsGroup: 1000 on the emptyDir).

RN-714 — SAST that did not run leaves the SecOps gate pending, never approved​

  • Rule: when the SecOps gate's semgrep does not run — missing binary, invalid output (:invalid_output), :sem_saida, exception or time ceiling —, no verdict is recorded: the PR stays in awaiting_secops, the gate stays PENDING and blocking, and the PR does not reach the user as approved by SecOps. The reason goes to the thread as an agent.error of origin infra ("SAST não rodou: — … reexecute o gate depois de corrigir"). The external contract does not change: the usual two verdicts remain (approved/changes_requested), one per gate. A missing gitleaks is still only "skipped" in the summary.
  • Re-run: the cycle stays in_progress in gate_states, and the GateRescuer re-runs it at engine boot and after the staleness threshold (gate_rescue_stale_after_seconds, 15 min). There is no re-run gate button on screen.
  • No repetition (AT-386): a rescue that finds the SAME reason again does not record another agent.error: if the SecOps's last event for that task (agent.error or artifact.secops_verdict, read by type, tail with a ceiling) is already this error with the same reason, only the server's Logger line remains. A different reason, a verdict in between or a failing read record again; the agent.error now carries taskId.
  • Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/secops_agent_server.ex:116 (run_secops), apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/secops_agent_server.ex:144 (sast_nao_rodou), apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/secops_agent_server.ex:194 (erro_ja_registrado?)

One cache key, one question (RN-718)​

RN-718 — Whoever writes a session's actions into the cache makes the SAME read as the thread​

['session-actions', projectId, sessionId] is ONE TanStack Query cache entry, and the Sessões tab wrote into it the result of another question: the FIRST ascending page (listActions({ limit: 200 }), without latest), while the Session thread reads the tail of the 200 newest plus the pending ones it pushed out (RN-637). The two screens swapped each other's cut — after opening the tab, the thread could draw the session's 200 OLDEST actions, the defect RN-637 closed, reopened through the cache door (AT-365).

The rule: key and function go together, in consultaDasAcoesDaSessao (apps/web/src/lib/acoes-da-sessao.ts). Whoever READS a session's actions to put them in the cache uses that pair — usePendingActions and the per-session summary of the Sessões tab. A key of its own for the tab was considered and discarded: it would stop the cache swap, but keep the tab summarizing the wrong cut. With the same read, the summary gains — a long session's new pending one now counts in "aguardando". Whoever only INVALIDATES the key (decision on the approval screens, the live channel) still writes the list by hand: invalidating writes no data.

  • Where: apps/web/src/lib/acoes-da-sessao.ts:76 (chaveDasAcoesDaSessao), :80 (consultaDasAcoesDaSessao); apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts:432 (usePendingActions); apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSessionsTab.tsx:270 (acoesPorSessao)
  • Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSessionsTab.test.tsx (describe "a leitura de ações é a mesma do fio": with the thread having written the tail, mounting the tab leaves tail + pending in the cache and no call without latest — fails on the old code, which wrote the 200 oldest; and the pending one pushed out of the tail counts in "aguardando")
  • Declared gap: the card of an action whose proposed_action.created left the 200-event window still JUMPS to the top of the thread (ordemDaAcaoNaTimeline degrades to createdAt and anchors at 0.5) — locked as current behavior in apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.acao-fora-da-janela.test.tsx, whose fix is a separate decision. The same test proves that the decided card does not ask for a decision again: what seemed to "come back" in AT-365 was ANOTHER action.

RN-723 — The Infra inherits the network the Arquiteto declared for the project​

Owner decision on 10/02 (ADR 0208), revising the literal none network of the start on acceptance of RN-671. The Infra's election uses the network of the most recent artifact.project_image emitted by the Arquiteto (actor_id: "arquiteto", any session of the project), read locally by the engine; without a decision of his, or with a value outside none/egress, it stays none. RN-720 — The PO completes the story that already exists, and does not offer the handoff to the Arquiteto with an uncovered rule​

Context: in the real use of loja-teste-2 (10/02) the PO created twelve stories without a linked rule, read in listar_regras_de_negocio that seven of the eight rules were WITHOUT coverage, wrote that it had no tool to edit a story and called offer_handoff to the Arquiteto anyway — asserting in the thread that coverage was complete and that the system would accept on its own. The automatic acceptance of RN-660 did not happen (the criterion did not hold), and the story it recreated triggered the semantic duplicate notice (RN-681).

The rule:

  1. The PO has complete_story: it completes an EXISTING draft story of the project — the given business_rule_ids are ADDED to those already linked (completing never unlinks a rule; an id that is not an artifact.business_rule is 400), given non-empty lists replace the current ones and omitted ones stay. A story that is not draft is 409; from another project, 404. After writing, promotion follows the SAME criterion as create_story (isPromotable; auto goes to ready, manual sets proposedReady), and the write records backlog.story_completed.
  2. The PO's offer_handoff to the Arquiteto is REFUSED, without creating an offer, while there is a rule without a story or an incomplete draft story (without proposedReady) — and the result lists both, with id and title, and says to complete with complete_story. Coverage is the api's (computeCoverage, the same as the automatic acceptance), never a second count in the engine; a read failure does not become a refusal. The other agents and targets do not go through the check.
  3. When the PO's business_rule emit_artifact comes back with the similarity notice (status: warned), the result adds that the rule seems to ALTER an existing one and that it should ask the user (ask_structured_questions) which one holds before going on (AT-389: the user said "taxa fixa de R$ 10", the Criativo recorded "R$ 10 por pedido" and the PO emitted "R$ 10 por torrefador"). The already recorded rule is not undone; the notice stays a notice.

The PO's kickoff says all three things.

The Anamnese does not pay twice for the same window, and gate rescue does not restart a cycle that waits for someone (RN-722)​

RN-722 — The Anamnese closes the window it evaluated and only runs with new interaction; gate rescue asks about the task, respects the pending human decision and parks the old cycle​

  • Rule (Anamnese): (1) a round that EVALUATED the window and ended without a profile (skip_proficiency) records anamnese_runs with zero profiles, and the next one starts at window_to — revising the clause of RN-680/the moduledoc "a round that does not conclude does not record": a round that FAILS (ceiling, budget, provider) still does not record, and one that never reaches the LLM (no subject, triage, daily ceiling) closes nothing; (2) the events the Anamnese itself writes (anamnese.* and every event of actor agent/anamnese) and those of actor system stay out of the window and of the triage count; (3) owner decision of 10/02: a subject is whoever has at least 5 NEW own interactions (events of actor_kind: "user" plus decisions, in the window that already starts at the end of the last attempt) — revising the "at least ONE" of RN-680 —, and the project has at most 4 paid rounds per UTC day (concluded, failed or run_skipped written by the model; the no-subject skip does not count). Below either of the two, no LLM or RAG call; the reason goes to the log and, only in a manually requested round, to anamnese.run_skipped (causa: "teto_diario" or "sem_sujeito_elegivel").
  • Rule (gate rescue, revises RN-140): the GateRescuer (a) considers alive the cycle whose TASK is in flight in the lead, by asking it ({:em_voo?, task_id}), and no longer the project's process — an idle lead does not hold the rescue; a lead too busy to answer counts as alive; (b) does not restart a cycle whose session has a PENDING proposed_action from a gate actor (qa*, secops*, appsec) — it only logs; (c) owner decision of 10/02: a cycle stalled for more than 2 h since its LAST ACTIVITY (updated_at) is PARKED (parked_at) with gate.rescue_parked in the session log (task, gate, age, reason), is resumed neither at boot nor on the tick, and resuming requires a human gesture (GateRescuer.retomar_estacionado/3).

RN-725 — Text with a literal escape is decoded, and the argument refusal says what arrived​

Context: in TP-01 (10/03, Claude Haiku 4.5) the PO recorded story titles with the LITERAL unicode escape (código): the normalization of RN-719 only decoded array/object fields. Recreated with the right title, the stories went through the duplicate refusal (RN-720/RN-081), which did not match the escaped one with the normal one. And the "exige X" refusals did not say what had arrived: the PO spent 28+ steps (48% of the test's cost) up to the ceiling, and complete_story replied "ainda faltam RF, DoD, DoR ou business_rule_ids" without saying which.

The rule:

  1. At the same point as RN-719, a string with a LITERAL \uXXXX (surrogate pair included) is decoded, and with it \n, \t, \" and \\ of the SAME string. A string without \uXXXX comes back byte for byte — code in a content with a literal "\n" does not change. This revises RN-719's "a string field is never touched" only in this case.
  2. The EXACT duplicate of a story (api) and of a rule (engine) compares the title with the escape decoded, before the usual case folding and NFD.
  3. A tool refusal that says "exige X" gains, at the same point, the KEYS that arrived (names, never values), or that a string/list arrived instead of an object. emit_artifact with a key missing in the payload states the missing keys and the received ones, instead of {:missing_keys, …}.
  4. complete_story names exactly what is missing (falta: business_rule_ids), by the same yardstick as the api's missingForReady, read from the returned story.

The same recognition makes FalhaDeTurno.origem/1 return infra for the credit final frame (it applies to the gate agents, like QA). The session counts dev.credit_exhausted as pending work, like dev.idle_tripped. Since RN-730 the 402 arrives with its own code (insufficient_credit) and it is that which decides; recognition by text remained only as a safety net.

RN-732 — The turn's text goes through the same escape yardstick as the arguments​

  • Rule: the text the model writes in a conversational agent's turn — the content (closing) and each passos of agent.response — goes through the SAME decodificar_escapes/1 of RN-725 before being recorded: a literal ã becomes ã. One yardstick only, without a copy, and with the same limit: it only acts when there is a literal \uXXXX, so text without escapes — including code with a literal "\n" in a fenced block — comes back byte for byte. RN-734 — The OpenAI-compatible path ALWAYS sends the output ceiling​

  • Rule: every chat call through the /chat/completions dialect (the providers born from OpenAICompatibleProvider, OpenRouter included) carries the output ceiling field — max_tokens or max_completion_tokens, according to maxTokensField — even when the caller does not set maxTokens. Without a setting, the value is MAX_TOKENS_PADRAO (4096), the SAME DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS as anthropic-provider.ts, so the agent has the same ceiling in both dialects. The reason is the credit RESERVATION: without the field, OpenRouter reserves per call the model's MAXIMUM output and refuses with 402 ("would exceed your available credits given your current in-flight requests") with a balance that would cover the real call. Today no caller (engine → llm-turn) sets maxTokens, so the default applies to all agents. An answer cut by the ceiling (finish_reason: "length") is read and narrated since RN-737 (RN-698 narrates the ITERATION ceiling, not the token one). RN-741 — Reasoning has its own budget and does not eat the visible output​

RN-757 — The auto-approved terminal waits for the command, and the command ceiling is 2 min​

  • Rule: the terminal action the api auto-approves is EXECUTED inside the same propose_action request (api → engine /internal/actions/execute → api container-exec → broker), and the engine waits for that request for TERMINAL_ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS + 120 s — not for the Req default of 15 s. The command ceiling (TERMINAL_ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS) goes from 15 s to 120 s in the three composes and in runtime.exs. The chain becomes broker (T) < api → broker (T + up to 45 s, RN-604) < engine → container-exec (T + 90 s) < engine → propose_action (T + 120 s), and with T = 120 s the outer hop (240 s) stays below the 300 s of headers of Node's fetch. If the wait still overflows, the model receives NAMED text — the ceiling in seconds, that the process may keep running and the suggestion of nohup … & with a log —, never a raw %Req.TransportError{reason: :timeout}. Asynchronous/streaming exec was considered and not done: the smallest change that makes a common npm install fit is the ceiling.
  • Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/engine_api_client.ex:1919 (opcoes_do_propose_action) and apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/hooks/action_pipeline.ex:80 (resultado_de_teto_do_terminal)

RN-758 — The Jev's cut never removes the agent's obligation tool​

RN-760 — The dev agent's next task starts from its last not-yet-merged branch​

What was left uncommitted in the worktree is preserved first, as in RN-743; the pointer recorded by block_task/4 is not overwritten. When the previous branch is already an ancestor of the local dev (merged), the next one starts from dev, which already contains it. WHEN the queue moves does not change: the next task is still claimed at the end of the gates, before the user's merge (owner decision). Declared: a squash merge on a remote does not leave the branch an ancestor of dev, so the next one keeps starting from it; the pointer still lives only in memory, and in runner mode the merge check does not run.

RN-761 — An installed dependency does not enter the repository: base .gitignore, a commit that excludes it and a gate that flags it​

  • Rule: three layers, with the SAME list of directories (node_modules, deps, _build, .venv, venv, __pycache__, vendor, target):
    1. the repository bootstrap (the three providers and adoption) gets the commit_gitignore step, which commits a base .gitignore to main BEFORE dev is born, so every working branch inherits it. It is the single point because it is through it that EVERY created or adopted repository passes, before any agent writes; the Infra through the module_map would arrive after the dev's first commit and only in the projects that go through it. The step only CREATES the file: an already existing .gitignore, even a different one, is the user's and does not enter the plan;
    2. the dev agent's commit (git_commit) and the commit that preserves the worktree on blocking (RN-743) stage everything EXCEPT those directories, at any depth (pathspec :(exclude,glob)), even without a .gitignore;
    3. the SecOps gate flags, as a finding (changes_requested), a directory from the list that appears in the PR's diff, with the file count. The two copies of the list (api and engine) are checked by test. Declared: a dependency file ALREADY tracked before this rule is not removed by the commit (the exclusion does not stage removal); an already bootstrapped project only gets the .gitignore if the bootstrap runs again; in runner mode the commit runs through the same GitExecutor and the same exclusion applies where the engine runs git.

RN-763 — Closing the execution session stops the dev agents and the gates, and "Parar execução" in the Executores tab​

For each dev with a task in progress (working, awaiting_approval or awaiting_gate), the worktree's work becomes a commit on the task's branch (RN-743) and the task is BLOCKED with reason "sessão de execução encerrada", origin politica, and the diagnosis saying where the work was left — it goes back to the queue when a human releases it, never lost. The session's gate_states rows are removed, so the GateRescuer does not reopen a cycle of the closed session. The Executores tab gets "Parar execução" (role developer, that of closing a session), whose mechanism is the SAME closing (closing → closed), without a new state; the confirmation says before the click what remains: the tasks in progress (with the count), the open PRs, the pending approvals and that the session does not reopen. Declared: a dev agent's pending action stays pending; an open PR stays open; a session with execution.activated does not reopen (RN-650), so resuming means activating execution in a new session; the confirmation's task count comes from the tab's event window. The confirmation on the session bar's "Encerrar" belongs to another activity (AT-452).

RN-779 — The worktree of the (re)claimed task starts from the CURRENT dev and integrates it​

  • Rule: before creating a task's worktree (first time or resumed), the engine runs git fetch origin in the project's working tree (serialized per project) — it is on the remote that PRs are merged, and the local dev only moved at the checkout of initialization. The tip of dev is origin/dev when the local one fell behind. The task is born: (1) from the previous task's unmerged branch (RN-760), (2) from its OWN branch when it has work that dev does not contain — the task resumed in a new process, which lost the in-memory pointer (RN-743) —, or (3) from the current tip of dev. In cases (1) and (2) the worktree INTEGRATES the tip of dev (merge --no-ff, identity <agente>[bot]) before the first step. A conflict in that integration is a NAMED refusal ("conflito ao integrar a dev atual", with the files), the merge is aborted, the source branch stays intact and the task blocks with its own reason and origin codigo. A failing fetch blocks the task with git's reason, never falls back to the old dev. Readoption after a merge conflict (RN-715) does not integrate on its own. Measured in TP-01: AT-447 FIRED on the 1st claim (reflog: Created from feature/task-b3cc92b8); what lost the base was the reclaim, which reset the branch to the LOCAL dev stuck at the infra merge (Reset to dev). Declared: in runner mode none of this runs (the git is the user's machine's).
  • Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/worktree_manager.ex:151 (atualizar_remoto), :195 (add_worktree), :227 (ponta_do_trabalho), :225 (retomada), :300 (integrar_trabalho)

RN-780 — A reasoning-only answer cut by the ceiling is a cut, not giving up​

The round is retried ONCE, without the empty answer in the history and counting an iteration — the iteration ceiling and the task budget still apply. If it repeats, the loop stops marking corte_pelo_teto, and the dev agent blocks the task with the reason "resposta só de raciocínio, cortada pelo teto" and origin modelo, instead of "parou sem concluir nem reportar bloqueio". A tool call in between resets the retry. Declared: the engine receives from the api truncated and usage.outputTokens, but NOT the reasoningTokens (they stay only in token_usage), so an empty answer that hits the ceiling without finish_reason: length is not recognized.

RN-787 — The gate counts the PR's diff against the origin's dev, and the QA verdict records a list​

RN-778 — The orphan dev agent closes through a new event at boot​

  • Rule: at boot, for each non-terminal session, the dev agent whose last dev.* in the session is a waiting one (dev.working, dev.blocked, dev.idle_tripped and the others GetSessionPendingWorkUseCase counts) and that has NO row in dev_agent_states IN THIS session gets a dev.error with origin infra (reason: dev_agent_sem_processo) followed by dev.idle, which takes it out of the pending work yardstick (RN-064). It is the mold of RN-586 for the dev.* vocabulary: it never re-executes, never rewrites an event, and the durable row is the proof of ownership — with it the DevRehydrator restarts the agent, and closing it would be killing a healthy agent. It does not touch the task: a blocked task or one with a PR waiting for the merge keeps holding the current execution session through RN-776 (AT-457), which has a human owner.

RN-807 — An exec that exceeds the ceiling comes back as an overflow, and the command dies inside the container​

  • Rule: the overflow of the DockerPort's exec ceiling is decided by the CLOCK (elapsed ≥ ceiling) besides killed, because the docker exec client catches the SIGTERM of execFile's timeout and exits with code 0 — measured: sleep 30; echo FIM under a 3s ceiling came back erro: null, stdout: "", and the adapter returned exitCode: 0. An agent command that exceeded the 120s came back "exit 0", and QA approved a suite that hangs. The overflow now returns exitCode: -1, timedOut: true and the timeout mark. And killing the client does not kill the command: exec wraps the command (which stays as ONE argument, intact) in an sh that records its own PID — group and session leader, because the runtime does setsid on every docker exec — in the container's /tmp; on overflow the adapter kills the GROUP by that PID (SIGKILL), in an internal call, without a new operation on the port (ADR 0130). Measured and refused: busybox's timeout inside the sh -c — the watcher dies with the client and the sleep survives. If killing fails (/tmp not writable, for example), the mark says the process may have survived.
  • Where: packages/docker-port/src/docker-cli.ts:269 (estourouOTeto), packages/docker-port/src/docker-cli.ts:455 (matarExecEstourado)

RN-823 — The gate cycle the engine restart killed is resumed at boot, and the thread says so​

  • Rule: at engine BOOT, a RECENT in_progress row of gate_states (below gate_rescue_stale_after_seconds, 15 min, and therefore invisible to the tick) with no live process ON THIS node nor on the OTHER nodes of the cluster is an orphan of the restart, not a slow cycle: the boot resumes it right away (Dispatcher.run_qa/run_secops), without waiting for the threshold. "Alive" is the yardstick of RN-722 (the task in flight in the lead), also asked of the other nodes through :erpc.multicall — a node that does not answer counts as ALIVE, the yardstick of TurnoOrfao (RN-586). The usual guards apply: a pending action of a gate actor does not restart, and an absent dev owner only deletes the row. Before redispatching, the boot records gate.interrupted in the session log (taskId, gate, ultimaAtividadeEm, retomadoEm), and the thread shows it as a notice, in both languages. The periodic tick does NOT change: outside boot, a recent row is a cycle in flight. Declared residue: a node that has not yet joined the cluster at the moment of boot is not asked, and the worst outcome is the usual one (duplicated and cheap work; the second verdict is refused by the api).

Measured: an unless-stopped container stopped with docker stop stays exited with RestartCount=0.
