Only the observed state unlocks: without an observation, or observed running, the record still holds. The api already accepted it: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase with a running row transitions nothing (ADR 0081's state machine does not change) and the broker does docker start on the stopped container.

RN-833 — Every web Phoenix socket gets disposed of, and the replaced one does not act​

  • Rule: every web Phoenix socket is born through criarSocket and dies through descartar(), which does disconnect() and removes the three listeners that the phoenix@1.8.9 constructor registers on window (pagehide, pageshow, visibilitychange) — disconnect() alone left them, and the visibilitychange reopened the old socket. In the session channel each conectar() is a GENERATION: the previous one is disposed of (leave, descartar() and ITS ping) before the new one is born, and every callback of an old generation is a no-op — the onClose of a replaced socket does not schedule a reconnection, does not clear the current one's ping and does not mark the live channel dead. The live channel (RN-579) is a COUNT of connections per session, not a boolean. The neutralization of auto-reconnect (RN-108) stays mandatory in the type of criarSocket.

RN-847 — A merged PR keeps stating the files it changed​

  • Rule: extension of RN-844. Now the merge records in the PR's store the merge base and the source tip at the moment of the merge (mergedBaseSha/mergedHeadSha), and the merged PR's diff is mergedBaseSha...mergedHeadSha. A PR merged before those fields falls back to the target's merge commit (first parent) whose second parent is the source tip; one merged by fast-forward without the fields cannot be reconstructed and stays empty (declared gap). GitHub and GitLab already return the merged PR's diff through the platform itself. On screen, the context summary is reread on the SAME triggers that reread the PR list (RN-841): the channel's prs target (with its 2 s window, no extra fetch) and the change of the backlog signature, by prefix ['session-context-summary', projectId].

RN-858 — An agent's open question is a durable record, and only the session author answers it​

  • Rule: the doubt an agent leaves for the user becomes the artifact.open_question event (append-only, in the log of the session where it is born) with {questionId (uuid), pergunta (até 500), sugestao (até 300, opcional), afeta: {regras, historias, tarefas}, autor, sessionId} — the events funnel refuses with 400 a payload outside that shape, whether it comes from the engine or the api. POST .../open-questions/:questionId/answer with {resposta} or {aceitarSugestao: true} is only accepted from the AUTHOR of the originating session (403 so_o_autor_da_sessao); already answered is 409 pergunta_ja_respondida, a question from another project is 404 and an empty answer (or a suggestion that does not exist) is 400. Answering records, in one transaction, an artifact.decision_record with the user as actor (context = the question, choice = the answer, consequences = what it affects, plus questionId and afeta) and the open_question.answered, notifies the session channel (through the funnel, RN-579) and asks the engine to resume the PARKED QA gate of each affected task (the RN-724 path) — best effort: a gate that was not parked or an engine that is down does not undo the answer. RN-862 — The open question on the engine side: tool, verdict and decision in the context​

RN-906 — The API refuses network none when a module's stack downloads dependencies​

RN-908 — The PO kickoff asks for the backlog in batches, after reading, by layer​

  • Rule: the PO kickoff tells the model, in this order: read listar_regras_de_negocio and listar_backlog in the same response, with no write alongside; then all epics in one response; then all stories, using the epic_id returned; then all tasks, using the story_id returned. Never recreate an epic that already exists, and at most about 10 tool calls per response. Measured reason: without the batch request, nemotron makes 1 tool per response and qwen makes 3; with it, 9 each (parallel_tool_calls changed nothing). Reading first is what stops qwen from creating epics without reading the backlog. It does not change the @max_iterations ceiling (RN-166).

The credential is mandatory. The provider capabilities are false (only listModels and streaming, required by the contract, are true) until a smoke with a key proves the rest (ADR 0041). Model prices are not discovered: they enter by manual curation and, by the owner's decision, a subscription model records the equivalent API's public price, not zero. The provider sends x-9router-token-saver: off on every call, so 9Router does not compress the tool_result.

RN-912 — The area model is a box on the lead's line, under "Models per agent"​

  • Rule: the "Area model" section no longer exists. The area default (RN-102, the area scope of RN-470) is linked by a box only on the lead's line of each area (dev-lead, qa, infra): "Apply to the whole X area (lead + subagents)". The area binding is one value per area and does not store the source agent, so a box on every line would have two competing for the value. Checked ⇔ the lead's effective value comes from the area (origin: 'area'), read from the batch of RN-654, with no new query. Checking writes the area with the lead's effective value and the lead's routing criterion (PUT .../area-bindings/:area) and THEN deletes the lead's own binding (DELETE .../agent-bindings/:lead; copying it would leave it behind, RN-102). These are two calls and the outcome is per step (RN-469): if the area refuses (including the 422 of RN-040) nothing changed and the toast carries the API's phrase; if the area was written and the DELETE fails, the screen says the area default was written and the lead's own model was not removed (a 404 on the DELETE counts as already removed). Unchecking deletes the area (DELETE .../area-bindings/:area) and writes nothing to the lead; a 404 becomes "already inherited". With the box checked, the lead's selector and routing criterion write the AREA. An agent with its own binding overrides the area (RN-470) and does NOT follow: the screen lists, in plural, the known subagents in that situation (declared scope, RN-180; the dynamic dev-<modulo> ones are not included and the screen says so) and does not delete their decision. The "apply to all" (RN-476) writes its own binding to the 17 and, for that reason, takes the subagents off the area default; its notice says so. Role: the box and, while checked, the lead's selector require maintainer (the minimum of the area endpoint, RN-102), compared by roleAtLeast; below that they stay inert and the reason is said ONCE in text in the section legend (ADR 0064). The other lines remain at developer. The box is born disabled if the lead has no effective value to copy, and it says the reason in text on the box itself (AT-601, key modelsSection.areaBox.needsModel). Revises the UI of RN-040, RN-102 and RN-470; the cascade, the scope and the endpoints do not change (no ADR).
